 Phenotypic heterogeneity in stress tolerance among isogenic bacterial cells fundamentally impacts the efficiency and robustness of microbial bioprocesses while fostering persistent infections, yet its underlying regulatory mechanisms remain elusive. Here, by integrating single-cell RNA-sequencing with microfluidic time-lapse tracking, we discovered small heat shock protein Hsp20 as a central regulator of acid-tolerance heterogeneity. Strikingly, contrary to its canonical role as a holdase to prevent protein aggregation, Hsp20 actively promotes the formation of protective protein aggregates that sequester transcription and metabolic proteins to inactivate gene transcription and metabolism. Hsp20-promoted aggregates drive cells into varying depths of dormancy, regulating the trade-off between stress tolerance and post-stress recovery of single cells. Hsp20 enhances cellular tolerance at the expense of recovery capacity, an aspect that has rarely been systematically reported. Moreover, Hsp20-regulated protection extends broadly to heat, oxidative, and bile salt stresses, revealing a generalizable strategy for stress adaptation. Our work broadens the roles of small heat shock proteins in cytoplasmic protective aggregation during the microbial stress response and provides a mechanistic link between transcriptional noise and phenotypic heterogeneity. It offers a new theoretical basis for understanding the survival strategies of prokaryotes and for precision control in microbial industry and epidemic control.

title: ZCCHC7 Phase Separation Drives Oncogenic Alternative Splicing and Is Targetable by Olaparib in Colorectal Cancer
abstract:
In colorectal cancer (CRC), the protein ZCCHC7 drives tumor growth and chemoresistance by forming liquid-like condensates that dysregulate RNA splicing. Disrupting ZCCHC7 condensate formation with the existing drug olaparib reverses the detrimental splicing alterations and enhances chemosensitivity. This drug-repurposing approach provides a readily available therapeutic strategy with promising translational potential for CRC.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Alternative splicing (AS) is a hallmark of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet targeting splicing regulators remains challenging due to toxicity and poor selectivity. We identified ZCCHC7 as a critical splicing regulator via integrated analyses of GEO datasets, proteome microarrays, mass spectrometry, and RNA-seq/RIP-seq. ZCCHC7 was highly expressed, correlated with poor prognosis, and promoted CRC proliferation and chemoresistance. In vivo efficacy was confirmed in AOM/DSS and Apc min/+  models. Mechanistically, IDR1 drives liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) of ZCCHC7, forming condensates that enrich SRPK1 and its substrate SRSF1, leading to SRPK1-dependent SRSF1 phosphorylation and exon 3 retention in PTPMT1. This favors the oncogenic long isoform (PTPMT1-L) over the short isoform (PTPMT1-S). Molecular docking identified olaparib (OLA) as a direct LLPS inhibitor binding to IDR1. By disrupting ZCCHC7-SRSF1 interaction, OLA reversed PTPMT1 splicing toward the short isoform and synergized with 5-fluorouracil in PDX models. In this preliminary observation, olaparib plus capecitabine achieved a near-partial response (30% tumor reduction) and durable stable disease with manageable toxicity in two heavily pretreated patients with pMMR/MSS CRC. In conclusion, our findings suggest that ZCCHC7 drives oncogenic splicing in CRC through LLPS, and repurposing OLA as a first-in-class LLPS inhibitor targeting ZCCHC7 may be a promising strategy to overcome chemoresistance.

title: Geometrically Decoupled Magnetization of Microparticles via Programmed Chaining of Internal Magnetic Nanoparticles
abstract:
A scalable lithographic platform is introduced to independently program microparticle geometry and magnetic anisotropy through field‐directed assembly of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (SPION) chains. By varying the assembly field and SPION loading, fabrication conditions influence internal chain morphology and the resulting magnetic torque response. This approach establishes a fabrication–structure–property relationship, enabling the design of magnetically programmable microparticles with diverse geometries and magnetic properties.








ABSTRACT
Magnetically responsive microparticles are increasingly used as building blocks for microrobotics, active matter, and directed self‐assembly, yet conventional fabrication methods often couple magnetic orientation with particle geometry, limiting independent optimization of structural and magnetic properties. Here, we present a scalable photolithographic fabrication strategy that decouples microparticle geometry from the magnetic easy axis through field‐directed assembly of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (SPION) chains within a photoresist matrix. The approach enables fabrication of arbitrary two‐dimensional microparticles with independently programmable magnetic anisotropy over wafer‐scale areas using accessible materials and equipment. By varying the assembly field and SPION loading, we influence features of nanoparticle chain morphology, including chain length, alignment, and aspect ratio. Vector vibrating sample magnetometry reveals that these structural differences produce tunable magnetic torque, while a model based on magnetic energy minimization relates the programmed chain structures to the magnetic responses of microparticles. Together, these results establish a fabrication‐structure‐property relationship linking fabrication conditions to chain morphology, magnetic anisotropy, and particle torque. Beyond enabling programmable magnetic behavior, this microfabrication approach expands the design space for magnetically responsive microparticles by allowing particle geometry and magnetic function to be engineered independently, providing a foundation for future studies in programmable self‐assembly, active matter, and responsive materials.

title: Spatial Engineering of Posterior Signaling Centers in Cerebral Organoids via Controlled Morphogen Exposure Within Hydrogels
abstract:
We present a spatially engineered hydrogel platform that drives localized formation of posterior signaling centers in cortical organoids through stiffness‐controlled layers that preferentially deliver morphogens to one side of the organoid. This work paves the way for an accessible method to reliably generate spatially controlled expression of cell populations within a single organoid.








ABSTRACT
Cerebral cortex organoids are powerful in vitro models that recapitulate key features of human development. However, conventional methods produce cortical organoids with spontaneous, spatially disorganized cortical regions due to limited control over morphogen distribution within local environments. Here, we present a spatially engineered hydrogel platform that drives localized formation of posterior signaling centers in cortical organoids through controlled, localized exposure to morphogens. Using a combination of bulk photopolymerization, thermal crosslinking, and digital light processing (DLP) approaches, we fabricated hydrogels with stiffness‐controlled layers that preferentially deliver morphogens to one side of the organoid, selectively inducing the expression of posterior markers on the exposed face. We further validated this platform by delivering fluorescently tagged dextran, used as molecular weight‐matched model morphogens, to visualize spatiotemporal delivery dynamics at the organoid interface. As a proof of principle, we also demonstrated that DLP fabrication enables the printing of dual morphogen hubs, serving as a model for establishing two opposing gradients within a single organoid. Together, this hydrogel platform enables systematic spatial patterning of cell populations in organoids, more faithfully recapitulating the spatial organization and cellular diversity of native tissues and advancing higher‐fidelity models for studying human development and disease.

title: Catalytic Upcycling of Automotive Shredder Residue Plastics Into Naphtha‐Range Hydrocarbons Through Direct Reuse of Spent FCC Catalysts
abstract:
Automotive shredder residue plastics and spent FCC catalyst are combined in a catalytic upcycling process that converts waste plastics into naphtha‐range hydrocarbons. Reusing the refinery catalyst supports the direct treatment of heterogeneous automotive plastics and integrates two industrial waste streams within a single conversion route for more resource‐efficient production of circular hydrocarbon feedstocks.








ABSTRACT
Automotive shredder residue (ASR) plastics are difficult to recycle because of their heterogeneous composition, including mixed polymers, additives, fillers, and inorganic impurities. Spent fluid catalytic cracking (FCC) catalysts are continuously discharged from refineries, although they retain residual acidity and accessible pore structures. Here, ASR‐derived plastics are converted into naphtha‐range hydrocarbons by reusing a spent FCC catalyst. Naphtha yields reach 55.8% from an ASR‐derived polypropylene‐rich feedstock at 350°C and 65.3% from unsorted ASR plastics at 400°C. Comparative studies using HY zeolites and other zeolite frameworks show that catalytic cracking cannot be explained by Brønsted acid site density alone, but instead depends on acid‐site accessibility and framework‐dependent pore architecture. During five reaction–regeneration cycles, the spent FCC catalyst maintains stable naphtha yields of 56.2%–58.0%. In a waste‐PP‐to‐naphtha benchmark analysis, techno‐economic analysis shows that the spent FCC catalyst process achieves a naphtha minimum selling price of $1.58 per gasoline gallon equivalent (GGE), lower than $1.66/GGE for the HY(60) process, while life‐cycle assessment indicates a normalized global warming potential of −26% relative to conventional fossil‐derived naphtha. These results demonstrate that direct reuse of spent FCC catalysts provides a practical strategy for converting difficult‐to‐recycle ASR plastics into naphtha‐range hydrocarbons while reducing reliance on freshly synthesized catalysts.

title: Biomimetic PLGA/PHE@RBCMKTP Nanoparticles Enable Targeted Delivery of an MAO Inhibitor for the Treatment of Kidney Stone Disease
abstract:
Biomimetic PPR KTP  nanoparticles preferentially accumulate in the kidney and enhance renal delivery of phenelzine. Treatment reduces renal MAO activity and is associated with decreased oxidative stress, inflammation, apoptosis, and calcium oxalate crystal deposition. These findings support PPR KTP  nanoparticles as a potential kidney-directed therapeutic strategy for calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Calcium oxalate (CaOx) nephrolithiasis is common, yet its pathogenesis is incompletely understood and mechanism-based therapies remain limited. This study investigates amine metabolism in nephrolithiasis and evaluates monoamine oxidase (MAO) as a therapeutic target. Mendelian randomization, targeted metabolomics, transcriptomics, and CaOx models reveal altered amine metabolism, increased tubular MAO expression, and oxidative stress. Pharmacological MAO inhibition, tubular  Maob  deletion, and tubular MAO-B overexpression provide complementary functional evidence linking MAO-associated oxidative stress to renal crystal accumulation. Systemic phenelzine (PHE) reduces crystal burden but is associated with neurobehavioral alterations. A biomimetic nanoplatform, PPR KTP -NPs, combines PHE-loaded poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) cores with red blood cell membrane (RBCM) coating and a kidney-targeting peptide (KTP). These nanoparticles enhance renal accumulation and proximal tubular uptake. In vivo, PPR KTP -NPs reduce MAO activity, oxidative stress, and inflammatory mediators; attenuate CaOx deposition and tubular injury; and improve renal function. No overt neurobehavioral abnormalities or systemic toxicity are observed under the tested conditions. Time-resolved pharmacokinetic analyses show increased renal and decreased brain PHE exposure. These findings link altered amine metabolism to CaOx nephrolithiasis and support kidney-targeted MAO inhibition as a potential therapy.

title: Targeting the Microglial ApoE‐C1q Axis Modulates Synaptic Pruning Homeostasis to Ameliorate Traumatic Brain Injury‐Induced Cognitive Impairment
abstract:
Li et al. demonstrate that the microglial ApoE-C1q axis modulates synaptic pruning homeostasis after TBI. ApoE directly binds C1q to restrain excessive complement-mediated synapse elimination;  Apoe  deficiency unleashes C1q-driven microglial hyperactivation and pathological synaptic pruning, exacerbating TBI-induced cognitive impairment. Targeting this axis preserves synaptic integrity and ameliorates neurological dysfunction, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for TBI.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Traumatic brain injury (TBI)-induced cognitive impairment is tightly linked to pathological synaptic loss, and the underlying mechanisms, particularly the role of apolipoprotein E (ApoE) in microglia-mediated synaptic pruning, remain incompletely elucidated. Using single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq), we found time-dependent upregulation of  Apoe  in microglia derived from the perilesional areas of TBI mice, with its functions significantly enriched in synaptic pruning. Spatial transcriptomics (ST) further verified aggravated synaptic loss and abnormal complement activation in  Apoe -knockout mice.  Apoe  deficiency facilitated excessive microglial activation, thus worsening TBI-related nerve tissue damage, synaptic loss, and cognitive dysfunction. Mechanistically, ApoE binds complement C1q (C1q) with high affinity, and  Apoe  deletion unleashes C1q-dependent excessive synaptic pruning and severe damage to synaptic ultrastructure. In  Apoe -knockout mice, intervention with the ApoE mimetic COG1410, C1q-neutralizing antibody or PLX3397 could effectively ameliorate these pathological changes. In summary, the ApoE-C1q signaling axis exerts a key regulatory effect on TBI-induced synaptic loss and subsequent cognitive decline, which provides a promising therapeutic target for TBI treatment.

title: Timed Transcription Factor Programming Directs Human Pluripotent Stem Cell‐Derived Hematopoietic Progenitor Cells Toward Functional Natural Killer Cells
abstract:
Six transcription factors were identified through scRNA-seq analysis. These were delivered via lentivirus in the order  NFIL3  →  EOMES  →  TOX2 , and combined with pulsed IL-2WT stimulation. This strategy synergistically activates the proliferation and differentiation capabilities of NK cells, allowing hematopoietic stem cells to differentiate into functional, cytotoxic NK cells in just 2 weeks.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Using single-cell RNA sequencing, we analyze the transcriptional profiles from hematopoietic progenitor cells to mature natural killer (NK) cell. This analysis uncovers stage-specific networks centered on nuclear factors, interleukin 3 regulated gene ( NFIL3 ), TOX high mobility group box family member 2 gene ( TOX2 ), and eomesodermin gene ( EOMES ), revealing a multi-factor regulatory landscape that single-factor approaches cannot capture. These findings indicate that coordinated transcriptional factor (TF) activity, rather than isolated regulators, is essential for establishing NK cell identity. We further identify cytokine signaling, specifically IL-2 receptor bias, as a key bottleneck limiting hPSC-derived NK differentiation. Continuous exposure to wild-type IL-2 preferentially activates high-affinity IL-2Rαβγ on regulatory T-like populations, diverting cells away from NK program and restricting IL-2Rβγ-mediated maturation. To overcome this constraint, we develop a temporally tuned IL-2 delivery strategy that aligns cytokine availability with endogenous TF activation. Early high dose of IL-2 promotes proliferation and NK specification, while its withdrawal upon induction of  NFIL3 ,  EOMES , and  TOX2  supports transcriptionally driven maturation and prevents IL-2-induced exhaustion. Taken together, these findings establish a mechanistically informed framework that integrates temporal cytokine control with intrinsic TF networks to enhance the efficiency and functional output of hPSC-derived NK cells.

title: SparseKG‐Flow: A Virtual Cell Generative Architecture Unifying Structural Causal Models and Knowledge Graph Priors for Single‐Cell Drug Perturbation Prediction
abstract:
SparseKG‐Flow combines sparse representation, molecular knowledge graphs, and flow modeling to predict how single cells respond to unseen drugs. It accurately forecasts drug effects, explains key biological pathways, and helps prioritize promising therapies for cancer cells.








ABSTRACT
Predicting single‐cell responses to new drugs is essential for mechanism‐aware virtual cell modeling, yet existing models often fail on unseen drugs or cell types by relying on memorized correlations rather than transferable mechanisms. SparseKG‐Flow addresses this out‐of‐distribution (OOD) challenge as a generative architecture integrating three inductive biases: a sparse drug‐effect encoder with Gumbel–Softmax gating, a heterogeneous graph adapter for drug–target–pathway knowledge, and a mechanism‐guided residual flow decoder. On Tahoe‐100M, it achieves Pearson r$r$ of 0.942 and 0.920 under Test‐NewDrug and Test‐NewCell settings, respectively, outperforming the next‐best baseline by 16.6% and 14.8%. It also reduces Δexpression$\Delta{\rm expression}$ error by 89.0% and 91.7%, respectively, and more than doubles held‐out‐drug top‐gene recovery (Overlap@50 = 0.210). Frozen‐model evaluation on high‐grade serous ovarian cancer patient data provides preliminary evidence of transfer beyond the Tahoe‐100M panel. Ablations confirm all components aid OOD generalization, with the molecular knowledge adapter contributing the most. SparseKG‐Flow further reorganizes pharmacological priors into interpretable, task‐trained representations and highlights Abemaciclib, Capmatinib, and Gemcitabine in A549 analysis. It thus serves as both an accurate perturbation predictor and a mechanism‐grounded virtual cell platform for therapeutic prioritization.

title: Beyond Decoupling: A Three‐Level Framework for High‐ICE Hard Carbon Anodes in Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract:
Sodium‐ion batteries are promising for grid‐scale energy storage, yet hard carbon anodes show low initial Coulombic efficiency. This review organizes reported strategies into a three‐level framework coupling structural regulation, decoupling mechanisms, and tolerance to irreversible sodium loss. It distills engineering principles and validation indicators, offering a roadmap for the rational design of high‐efficiency hard carbon anodes in practical sodium‐ion batteries.








ABSTRACT
Low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE) of hard carbon anodes constrains the first‐cycle energy efficiency and gravimetric energy density of sodium‐ion full cells. Existing reviews typically classify ICE‐improvement strategies into intrinsic structural regulation, surface/interface engineering, and presodiation compensation. This work recasts structural regulation and active‐sodium compensation into a structure‐coupling, decoupling‐tolerance framework that links reversible sodium storage and irreversible sodium loss through structural features, ion accessibility, and interfacial reaction conditions. A given local structure exhibits distinct sodium occupancy, charge distribution, and interfacial reactivity across potential, electrolyte composition, and cycling stage, so its reversibility is governed jointly by local free energy and kinetic accessibility; however, insufficient causal validation limits the framework's predictive power. This review systematically examines three irreversible sodium‐loss pathways, SEI formation, intrinsic defect trapping, and open‐pore side reactions, analyzes their multiscale coupling, and discusses the efficacy boundaries of the three strategy families. A three‐level framework is proposed, comprising bulk competition, interface reaction, and system optimization, built on a competitive sodium‐storage‐site model, an interface‐stability regulation model, and a multi‐objective collaborative optimization model. Combined with standardized evaluation, full‐cell validation, and a data‐driven platform, a progressive validation path establishes quantifiable, testable, and iterative design language for hard‐carbon ICE research.

title: Mitochondrial Protein Quality Control as a Hierarchical Defense System in Health and Disease
abstract:
This Review conceptualizes mitochondrial protein quality control as a hierarchical defense system comprising four interconnected functional tiers rather than fixed spatial compartments or a strictly sequential pathway. It explores how mitochondrial protein import surveillance, intramitochondrial proteostasis, mitochondrial dynamics and selective recycling, and mitochondria–nucleus stress signaling cooperate to maintain cellular homeostasis. Furthermore, it highlights how these initially protective responses may become maladaptive under persistent stress, contributing to ageing, neurodegeneration, and metabolic diseases.








ABSTRACT
Mitochondria sustain energy production, metabolism and cellular stress responses, yet their function depends on the continuous delivery and maintenance of many proteins. Most mitochondrial proteins are made outside the organelle and must enter the correct compartment, fold and assemble before becoming functional. Defects at any of these steps can threaten both mitochondrial and cellular health. This Review organizes mitochondrial protein quality control (MpQC) into four interconnected functional tiers: (1) monitoring proteins before and during mitochondrial import; (2) folding and removal of damaged proteins inside mitochondria; (3) remodeling and selective recycling of mitochondrial components or entire organelles; and (4) communication of mitochondrial stress to broader cellular response pathways. These tiers interact rather than forming a fixed sequence, and their effects depend on stress intensity, duration and tissue context. We distinguish established pathways from emerging or debated mechanisms and examine how initially protective responses may become harmful under persistent stress. Finally, we consider their relevance to ageing, neurodegeneration and metabolic disease, and highlight unresolved questions for future research.

title: Intratumoral Klebsiella pneumoniae Activates TLR4/NF‐κB/IL‐1β Signaling in Microglia/Macrophage‐Like Cells to Drive Calcification in Spinal Meningiomas
abstract:
Single-cell RNA sequencing maps the cellular ecosystem and calcification-linked remodeling in human spinal meningiomas. Multi-modal analyses identify intratumoral  Klebsiella pneumoniae  enriched in calcified lesions. Its LPS activates microglia/macrophage-like cells TLR4-NF-κB signaling to trigger IL-1β secretion that promotes meningioma calcification, exposing this microbial-mediated pathogenic calcification axis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Pathological calcification complicates surgical resection and increases postoperative risks of spinal meningiomas. Conventional mechanisms, including microenvironmental pH shift-induced calcium precipitation and tumor cell intrinsic osteogenic reprogramming, fail to explain the consistent LPS-enriched pro-inflammatory microenvironment in calcified clinical specimens, leaving the key upstream driver of calcification unclarified. To resolve this mechanistic gap, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing on five spinal meningiomas (3 calcified vs. 2 non-calcified), identifying calcification-specific microenvironmental remodeling. Further multi-modal verification confirmed differential enrichment of intratumoral  Klebsiella pneumoniae  in calcified lesions. In vitro and in vivo functional assays validated that  Klebsiella pneumoniae  LPS activates the microglia/macrophage-like cell TLR4/NF-κB axis to trigger IL-1β release and drive tumor calcification. This work establishes a novel microbiota-immunity-calcification axis for spinal meningioma pathological mineralization. Targeting TLR4 or IL‑1β may offer a viable strategy to mitigate pathological calcification, reduce surgical difficulty, and improve long-term postoperative outcomes for patients with spinal meningiomas.

title: Spatial Synchronization and Determinants of Multidimensional Biodiversity and Endemism Across Multiple Taxa in China
abstract:
Integrating taxonomic, phylogenetic, and genetic dimensions across terrestrial taxa in China, this study reveals strong plant–insect spatial congruence but weaker vertebrate congruence, while contemporary climate primarily structures taxonomic and phylogenetic patterns and genetic facets remain more weakly explained.








ABSTRACT
Understanding the spatial alignment of multidimensional biodiversity across taxonomic groups is a central challenge for conservation. It remains unclear whether the spatial synchronization of taxonomic, genetic, and phylogenetic diversity, alongside their respective endemism patterns, exhibits a unified spatial structure across terrestrial taxa in China. Here, we presented a national‐scale assessment using occurrence data for 2105 terrestrial vertebrates, 15 963 vascular plants, and 28 894 insects, with phylogenetic and genetic analyses based on data‐matched subsets. We revealed strong spatial coupling between vascular plants and insects, contrasting with weaker congruence in terrestrial vertebrates. Across taxa, taxonomic diversity (TD), phylogenetic diversity (PD), weighted endemism (WE), and phylogenetic endemism (PE) were generally more spatially congruent than genetic diversity (GD) and genetic endemism (GE). In widespread‐species analyses, energy, water availability, and climatic seasonality were the primary determinants of TD and PD, whereas human activity showed relatively small independent contributions. Notably, several previously unrecognized complementary hotspots were identified, including the Tianmu Mountains, the Middle–Lower Yangtze Plain Mountains, the Taihangshan–Lvliangshan and Nuluerhushan–Heishan Mountain Systems, which warrant further assessment of conservation coverage. These findings indicate that vertebrate‐ or taxonomic‐diversity‐based conservation alone may not adequately protect plant and insect biodiversity, supporting multidimensional and taxon‐specific conservation planning in China.

title: An Evolutionarily Conserved prrx1–wwp2 Enhancer Axis Regulates Osteogenic Differentiation in Tendon‐associated Progenitors
abstract:
Cross-species analyses identify a functionally conserved  prrx1–wwp2  enhancer regulatory axis associated with tendon ossification. In zebrafish, this axis links  prrx1 + tendon-associated progenitors to osteogenic differentiation and intermuscular bone formation. Its conserved regulatory features in human primary tendon stem/progenitor cells (hTSPCs) provide molecular insight into shared mechanisms underlying physiological tendon ossification in teleosts and pathological heterotopic ossification in mammals.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Tendon ossification (THO) occurs in distinct physiological and pathological contexts across vertebrates. In some teleosts, myoseptal tendon ossification is a physiological process that generates intermuscular bones (IBs), whereas tendon ossification in mammals typically occurs in pathological contexts. Whether these contexts share conserved mechanisms remains unclear. Here, we used time-resolved scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq analyses to investigate the cellular and regulatory basis of tendon ossification in zebrafish. We identify  prrx1 + progenitors within myosepta as a tendon-associated progenitor population that is spatially and transcriptionally associated with osteogenic differentiation during IB formation, and reconstruct a gene regulatory network associated with this process. Cross-species integration reveals conserved cellular and molecular features of THO-associated cell populations between zebrafish and mammals. Functional perturbation analyses reveal that disruption of  prrx1  impairs osteogenic differentiation in zebrafish and human tendon-associated progenitor cells. Integration of genome-wide association studies with cross-species scRNA-seq data identifies  wwp2  as a conserved regulator associated with this osteogenic program. Further cis-regulatory analyses uncover a functionally conserved  wwp2  enhancer associated with  prrx1 -mediated regulation of  wwp2  expression. Together, these findings support an evolutionarily conserved  prrx1-wwp2  enhancer axis underlying osteogenic differentiation and provide insight into shared molecular features between physiological tendon ossification in zebrafish and pathological heterotopic ossification in mammals.

title: PFAS‐Free Localized High‐Concentration Gel Polymer Electrolytes for Ambient Temperature Li‐Metal Batteries
abstract:
Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)-free localized high-concentration gel polymer electrolyte (LHC-GPE) is designed using  in-situ  polymerization, deploying non-fluorinated toluene diluent, and methacrylate monomers. The LHC-GPE balances ion aggregation and transport, showing long room-temperature cycling (≈ 90% retention over 200 cycles) in LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2  (NMC-811)||Li cells at charge-discharge rate of C/3, 3 mAh·cm −2  area capacity, and 25°C.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Impregnating localized high-concentration liquid electrolytes into in situ polymerized matrices to form localized high-concentration gel polymer electrolytes (LHC-GPEs) is emerging as a commercially viable alternative to both conventional liquid electrolytes and solid polymer electrolytes for room-temperature Li-metal batteries. However, LHC-GPEs often rely on fluorinated diluents and polymeric components to achieve compatibility with high-voltage cathode materials. Herein, we investigate perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)-free LHC-GPEs based on toluene as a non-fluorinated diluent and non-fluorinated polymeric matrices. Their physico-chemical properties are elucidated through experimental characterization and molecular dynamics simulations. We then studied electrochemical performance in Li||Li and LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2  (NMC-811)||Li cells under practically relevant conditions, including a C/3 charge-discharge rate, cycling at 25°C, and NMC-811 areal loading of 3 mAh·cm −2 . The optimized LHC-GPE formulation delivers a capacity retention of ≈ 90% over 200 cycles (with 500 µm thick lithium metal anode, LMA) or 100 cycles (with 20 µm thick LMA on 8 µm thin Cu current collector). Interestingly, the LHC-GPE exhibited a longer cycle life than cells with similar liquid electrolyte composition, demonstrating the utility of the gel polymer electrolyte approach. This study demonstrates the suitability of environmentally friendly LHC-GPEs for Li-metal batteries, enabled by the use of fluorine-free diluents and polymer-based components.

title: Medium‐Entropy O3‐Type Layered Oxide as a High‐Performance and Air‐Stable Cathode Material for Sodium‐Ion Batteries: Investigation of Sn Doping to Enhance Cycling Stability
abstract:
Sn doping stabilizes O3-type sodium cathodes, suppressing phase transitions and enhancing cycling, rate capability, and air/moisture stability, achieving 83% retention after 500 cycles and 261.9 Wh kg −1  in full cells.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 O3-type layered oxides are attractive cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) but suffer from rapid capacity decay due to severe phase transitions and air/moisture sensitivity. Herein, NaLi 0.05 Ni 0.3 Mn 0.5−x Cu 0.1 Mg 0.05 Sn x O 2  was synthesized via spray drying. Sn incorporation induced strong Sn─O bonding and enlarged interlayer spacing, improving structural stability and electrochemical kinetics, building upon the medium-entropy stabilization already conferred by the multi-element base composition. The optimized NaLi 0.05 Ni 0.3 Mn 0.47 Cu 0.1 Mg 0.05 Sn 0.03 O 2  (x = 0.03; Sn0.03) delivered a reversible capacity of 142 mAh g −1  (at 0.1 C), 83% capacity retention after 500 cycles at 1 C, and excellent rate capability (98 mAh g −1  at 30 C). Operando synchrotron x-ray diffraction and x-ray absorption spectroscopy confirmed that Sn doping suppresses the O3 to P’3 phase transition, effectively mitigating lattice distortion and enhancing cycling performance. The reversible redox reactions of Ni 2+ /Ni 4+  and Cu 2+ /Cu 3+  compensated the charge, while electrochemically inactive Mn 4+  and Sn 4+  stabilized the structure. Sn doping improved structural integrity, maintaining electrochemical performance after water immersion and air exposure. A Sn0.03//hard carbon full cell exhibited a competitively high energy density of 261.9 Wh kg −1 . Density functional theory calculations corroborated delayed phase transitions and enhanced air/moisture stability. These findings establish Sn0.03 as a potential cathode candidate for practical SIB applications.

title: A‐Site Vacancies and Cu‐Doping in Lanthanum‐Based Perovskite Anodes for Selective H2O2 Oxidation to O2: A Descriptor‐Based Approach
abstract:
Electronic structure tuning of La-based perovskites through lanthanum vacancies, surface O-truncation, and Cu substitution enhances H 2 O 2  oxidation on perovskite oxides. Volcano correlations based on ΔG OOH  and a three-electronic-descriptor MLR model uncover key activity descriptors and identify La 0.8 Co 0.91 Cu 0.09 O 3-τ  as the most promising HPOR catalyst through computational screening.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The electrochemical oxidation of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) to oxygen (O 2 ) is crucial for controlling reactive oxygen species and for the durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. Herein, density functional theory (DFT) calculations were used to study the hydrogen peroxide oxidation reaction (HPOR) on LaMO 3  (M═Co, Mn, Fe, Ni) for eighteen lanthanum-based perovskites, such as A-site vacancy, oxygen-layer-truncated, and Cu-substituted LaM 1-x Cu x O 3-τ  structures. Electronic descriptor analysis revealed that defect engineering decreases d-orbital occupancy up to the Fermi level(O e ) while increasing the d-orbital density of states at the Fermi level(D π (E F )) compared to the pristine surface, thereby enhancing catalytic activity. AIMD simulations reveal the structural stability. The Co1 site in La 0.8 Co 0.91 Cu 0.09 O 3-τ  showed the highest HPOR activity, with an overpotential of 0.49 V after DFT+U correction. The OOH adsorption free energy (ΔG OOH ) showed a volcano-type correlation with catalytic activity (R 2  > 0.84; RMSE = 0.12). The electronic descriptor dxz_fermi has a good correlation with ΔG OOH  (R 2  = 0.73). The MLR model with three electronic descriptors gave R 2  = 0.85 and cross-validation Q 2  = 0.80, which allowed for efficient screening of electrocatalysts. The results provide design principles for advanced peroxide-oxidation electrocatalysts.

title: Aluminum‐Ion Modulated Electrochromism in Hexagonal Sodium Tungsten Bronze NaxWO3 Films: Ultrahigh Cycling Stability and Integrated Zinc‐Based Smart Window Devices
abstract:
The electrochromic (EC) effect of the Na 
    x 
 WO 3  film has been achieved in AlCl 3  aqueous solution. Initial optical modulation is maintained at 95.6% after 1000 coloration/bleaching cycles. A Zn-based Na 
    x 
 WO 3  EC device with multifunctionality has been developed to save energy. Two functional demonstrations of LED lighting and model house temperature regulation have been successfully fulfilled.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Electrochromic devices have attracted significant interest in the area of smart windows because of their capabilities of saving energy, changing colors, and regulating solar irradiance inside buildings. Low cost, multifunctionality, and excellent cycling stability are crucial for the widespread application of electrochromic devices. Here, nano sodium tungsten bronze Na 
    x 
 WO 3  with a hexagonal phase has been synthesized to study the electrochromic properties of Na 
    x 
 WO 3  film. The coloration and bleaching of the film are achieved by Al 3+  ion insertion and extraction, respectively. Its initial optical modulation can be maintained at 95.6% after 1000 coloration/bleaching cycles. Subsequently, a Zn-based Na 
    x 
 WO 3  electrochromic device by using Na 
    x 
 WO 3  film as the cathode has been assembled. It possesses an optical modulation of 41.5% and a coloring efficiency of 78.3 cm 2  C −1  at 750 nm. The device demonstrates excellent cycling stability, achieving an areal capacitance of 68.4 mF cm − 
 2  at a current density of 0.3 mA cm − 
 2 , along with an areal energy density of 8.1 µWh cm − 
 2  at an areal power density of 154.2 µW cm − 
 2 . Two functional demonstrations of LED lighting and model house temperature regulation based on the Zn-based Na 
    x 
 WO 3  device have been provided to display its application potential in multifunctional smart windows.

title: The Critical Behavior of Brain Activity Across Mammalian Species
abstract:
Comparative analysis using critical whole‐brain models across more than a hundred mammalian species reveals that larger brains support richer state and synchronization repertoires, as well as heightened sensitivity to perturbations, independent of shared evolutionary history. These findings indicate that evolutionary expansions in brain size and connectome topology systematically scale up functional capacity, driven fundamentally by critical dynamics.








ABSTRACT
This study investigates the functional implications of anatomical brain connectivity across 103 mammalian species, spanning 12 taxonomic orders and brain volumes over four orders of magnitude. It asks whether functional brain activity can be inferred from anatomy alone using whole‐brain models. For each connectome, we construct a brain model composed of binary units interacting through structural connections, assuming brain activity operates near a critical point between order and disorder. We focus on two functional measures at criticality: the diversity of network states and susceptibility to external input, as functions of brain volume, known to shape mammalian connectome topology, spatial constraints, and network information. The results indicate that larger brains support richer dynamical repertoires and stronger responses to perturbations, persisting when controlling for shared evolutionary history. Furthermore, long‐range connections are crucial for maintaining both the diversity of network states and the susceptibility to external input, and their contribution is stronger in larger brains. Finally, stochastic oscillation models show that the repertoire of synchronization patterns scales with brain size, supporting the view that larger connectomes enhance functional complexity. Our results suggest that evolutionary increases in brain size and associated connectome topology changes are accompanied by greater functional capacity driven by critical dynamics.

title: Lattice Distortion‐Modulated Sonocatalysis and Arachidonic Acid Metabolism for Enhanced Ferroptosis‐Driven Tumor Therapy
abstract:
This work presents a lattice distortion-engineered sonocatalytic electronic modulator based on Fe-Ti 3 O 5  that integrates electronic modulation with AA metabolism reprogramming to amplify ferroptosis. Fe incorporation induces lattice distortion and electronic redistribution, facilitating ultrasound-triggered interfacial electron transfer and boosting ROS generation. Moreover, Fe-Ti 3 O 5  exerts peroxidase-like and catalase-like activity, thus synergizing oxidative damage. Multi-omics analyses reveal Fe-Ti 3 O 5  under ultrasound activates AA metabolism and stabilizes ACSL4 through deubiquitination, thereby sensitizing tumor cells to ferroptosis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), the predominant subtype of kidney cancer, features excessive lipid accumulation, rendering tumor cells tolerant to oxidative stress and limiting the efficacy of ferroptosis therapy. Although arachidonic acid (AA) metabolism is a central regulator of ferroptotic vulnerability, its therapeutic activation remains challenging because insufficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) fail to sustain lipid peroxidation and metabolic remodeling within tumors. Here, we present a lattice distortion engineered sonocatalytic electronic modulator based on Fe-doped Ti 3 O 5  that couples electronic structure regulation with AA metabolism reprogramming to amplify ferroptosis. Fe incorporation induces lattice distortion and electronic redistribution, generating defect associated active sites and impurity energy levels, facilitating ultrasound (US) triggered interfacial electron transfer and substantially boosting ROS generation. Moreover, Fe-Ti 3 O 5  exerts peroxidase‑like and catalase‑like activity, thus synergizing oxidative damage. Fe-Ti 3 O 5  with US irradiation enhances AA metabolism, which in turn sensitizes tumor cells to ferroptosis. Furthermore, Fe-Ti 3 O 5  with US irradiation activates deubiquitination pathway that stabilizes acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), establishing a positive feedback axis linking sonocatalytic ROS production, AA metabolic reprogramming, and ferroptosis amplification. Moreover, US -activated Fe-Ti 3 O 5  significantly inhibits tumor growth in both subcutaneous and orthotopic ccRCC models.

title: Intermetallic‐Reinforced Yolk–Shell Architecture for Long‐Life, High‐Rate Silicon Anodes
abstract:
Spatially programmed titanate and graphene oxide nanosheets transform into a multifunctional shell around a porous Si/SiO x  yolk. The internal cavity buffers alloying strain, Ti 5 Si 3  reinforces the outer framework, and reduced graphene oxide sustains electron transport. By decoupling silicon expansion from the electrolyte-facing surface, this architecture enables rapid charge storage, 3500-cycle durability, and stable full-cell performance.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Managing Si expansion without sacrificing charge transport remains a key challenge in high-energy lithium-ion batteries. In this study, lepidocrocite-type titanate and graphene oxide nanosheets are used as reactive, spatially programmed precursors to construct a yolk–shell composite comprising a porous Si/SiO 
    x 
  yolk confined within a Ti 5 Si 3 –reduced graphene oxide (rGO) shell (PSiO@TSG-YS). Layer-by-layer assembly, controlled core etching, and magnesiothermic conversion collectively create an internal expansion reservoir, a mechanically reinforcing Ti 5 Si 3  framework, and an electronically percolating rGO network. Microscopy, diffraction, Ti K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy, and solid-state  29 Si magic-angle-spinning nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy verify Ti 5 Si 3  formation and Ti–Si coordination. The resulting architecture limits electrode swelling to 10.9% after 100 cycles and maintains low polarization and diffusion impedance during prolonged cycling. PSiO@TSG-YS retains 70.5% of its second-cycle capacity after 3500 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 . An NCM811||PSiO@TSG-YS full cell retains 86.1% of its initial capacity after 250 cycles at 1 C. Reactive nanosheet-to-intermetallic conversion thus integrates geometric buffering, interfacial stabilization, and electronic percolation in high-capacity alloying electrodes.

title: NDR2 Deficiency in Senescent Macrophages Drives Endplate Sclerosis via THBS1‐Dependent Chondrocyte Dysfunction
abstract:
NDR2-deficient senescent macrophages modulate THBS1 transcription and secretion through suppression of the AKT/ERK-Sp1 signaling axis. Secreted THBS1 subsequently binds to and activates its receptors, thereby disrupting the anabolic-catabolic balance and driving microenvironmental remodeling within the cartilage endplate. Overall, this study systematically elucidates how senescent macrophages disrupt endplate homeostasis, offering novel immune-based therapeutic strategies for intervertebral disc degeneration.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Endplate degeneration is a pivotal initiator of lumbar spine degenerative disorders and is closely linked to immunosenescence, particularly macrophage senescence. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we observed that senescent macrophages accumulate in degenerative endplate tissues and are characterized by downregulated NDR2 expression. In aged mice and transplantation models, NDR2-deficient macrophages accelerate endplate sclerosis. Conditional knockout of NDR2 in macrophages (Lysm 
    Cre 
 ; NDR2 
    f/f 
 ) triggers spontaneous endplate sclerosis and exacerbates lumbar spine instability (LSI)-induced pathology, whereas chondrocyte-specific knockout (Aggrecan 
    CreERT2 
 ; NDR2 
    f/f 
 ) not, highlighting the macrophage-specific role of NDR2. Mechanistically, thrombospondin-1 (THBS1) is identified as the critical mediator linking senescent macrophages to chondrocyte dysfunction in the endplate. NDR2 regulates THBS1 transcription and secretion via the AKT/ERK-Sp1 axis, and secreted THBS1 binds its receptors to orchestrate chondrocyte fate and endplate microenvironment remodeling. Notably, THBS1 knockout (Lysm 
    Cre 
 ; NDR2 
    f/f 
 ; THBS1 
    f/f 
 ) rescues the endplate sclerosis phenotype caused by NDR2 deficiency. Our study systematically elucidates how senescent macrophages disrupt endplate homeostasis, offering novel immune-based therapeutic strategies for intervertebral disc degeneration.

title: Cooperative Lewis Acid/Photoredox Catalysis for the Construction of Chiral Bicyclo[2.1.1]Hexanes
abstract:
We report a synergistic Lewis acid/photoredox strategy for the enantioselective synthesis of highly strained bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHs) using an acyl imidazole auxiliary. The system lowers the reduction potential of bicyclobutanes, yielding controlled radical intermediates and avoiding carbocation side pathways. The protocol delivers >25 enantioenriched BCH products in up to 98% yield and 99.5:0.5 er.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHs) are increasingly valued as bioisosteres of  ortho - and  meta -substituted benzenes, yet catalytic enantioselective access to these scaffolds remains challenging. Here we describe a cooperative Lewis acid/photoredox catalytic strategy that enables enantioselective strain-release construction of BCHs through [2σ + 2π] annulation of BCBs with activated alkenes. A coordinating acyl imidazole auxiliary facilitated binding of the BCB substrate to a chiral lanthanide catalyst, thereby lowering the reduction potential of the BCB and organizing the substrate within a well-defined chiral environment. UV-visible spectroscopy and  1 H NMR experiments prove the interaction between BCB and the Lewis acid. Electrochemical measurements support Lewis acid-induced redox modulation, and radical trapping experiments are consistent with a strain-release radical pathway that minimizes carbocation-mediated side reactions. The DFT computation elucidated that the major enantiomer-forming transition state avoids destabilizing non-bonding interactions. The reaction provides more than 25 enantioenriched BCH products in up to 98% yield and 99.5:0.5 er. These findings highlight the utility of cooperative Lewis acid and photoredox catalysis for controlling both reactivity and stereoselectivity in highly strained systems.

title: HspBp1 Promotes Tau Pathology and Cognitive Impairments by Inhibiting STUB1(CHIP)‐Mediated Tau Ubiquitination
abstract:
In hippocampal neurons, the co‐chaperone HspBp1 rises with age and emerges as a hidden driver of Tau pathology in Alzheimer's disease. By destabilizing the E3 ligase STUB1, it disrupts Tau ubiquitination and clearance, fueling tauopathy, synaptic degeneration, and cognitive decline. Restoring STUB1 reverses these deficits, highlighting the HspBp1–STUB1 axis as a promising therapeutic target.








ABSTRACT
Tau pathology is a core neuropathological hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD), increasing evidence indicates that disruption of protein quality control contributes to Tau accumulation. However, the upstream modulators that impair Tau clearance are poorly defined. Heat shock protein 70‐binding protein 1 (HspBp1), a co‐chaperone of the E3 ubiquitin ligase STUB1 (CHIP), has been implicated in proteostasis regulation, but its role in Tau pathology remains unknown. We found that HspBp1 was selectively expressed in hippocampal neurons and markedly upregulated in the hippocampus of aged AD mice. Neuron‐specific overexpression of HspBp1 exacerbated Tau and Tau hyperphosphorylation, synaptic and dendritic degeneration and cognitive impairments, whereas HspBp1 downregulation significantly attenuated Tau‐induced neuropathology and cognitive deficits. Mechanistically, HspBp1 reduced STUB1 levels and disrupted STUB1–Tau interactions, leading to decreased Tau ubiquitination and impaired proteasomal degradation. Consequently, Tau accumulated and underwent pathological hyperphosphorylation. Importantly, restoration of STUB1 expression largely abolished HspBp1‐induced Tau accumulation, synaptic dysfunction and cognitive deficits. Meanwhile, upregulation of STUB1 improves Tau pathology and cognitive impairments in P301S mice. These findings support HspBp1 as an age‐associated modulator that promotes Tau pathology by suppressing STUB1‐mediated Tau ubiquitination and degradation. Targeting the HspBp1–STUB1 axis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy for AD.

title: The Peripheral Endoplasmic Reticulum is a High‐Capacity Calcium Conduit for Coccolithophore Calcification
abstract:
Intracellular coccolith formation requires massive calcium flux while cytosolic Ca 2 
 +  must remain low. A calcium-rich peripheral endoplasmic reticulum connects the plasma membrane to the coccolith vesicle network, providing a direct calcium-transport route from seawater to the calcification site. This architecture supports high-capacity Ca 2 
 +  transport while bypassing the cytoplasm.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Coccolithophores, unicellular marine microalgae, dominate global geochemical cycles through the formation of calcium carbonate scales called coccoliths. This intracellular process requires high-capacity transport of calcium ions, which is challenging for any eukaryotic organism that needs to maintain very low calcium concentration in the cytoplasm. Currently, the mechanisms of calcium uptake and transport for calcification remain debated. Here, using multiple cryogenic imaging and spectroscopic techniques, we demonstrate that the peripheral endoplasmic reticulum (pER) of  Chrysotila carterae  (formerly  Pleurochrysis carterae ) serves as a concentrated reservoir, with local concentrations reaching 25 m m . In addition, structural analyses show direct physical contact between branches of the pER and the Golgi-derived coccolith vesicle system, as well as the presence of distinctive granules in the pER. The results show that the pER facilitates intracellular calcium transport and storage, ensuring a sustained supply for intracellular biomineralization while avoiding cytotoxicity. This mechanism of calcium transport that bypasses the cytoplasm may represent a common pathway for mineralizing cells.

title: Evolutionary Crosslinking‐Driven 3D Printing of Silicone Elastomers
abstract:
This review establishes a five‐step framework for silicone elastomer 3D printing based on evolutionary crosslinking, linking thermal‐field construction, printing‐strategy selection, extrusion, material response, and print‐quality assessment. The framework provides a systematic methodology for processing thermally curable materials and regulating crosslinking evolution through thermal control during printing.








ABSTRACT
Flexible functional systems require materials that combine mechanical compliance, structural stability, and long‐term reliability. Silicone elastomers satisfy these requirements through their low modulus, large recoverable deformation, environmental stability, and chemically crosslinked networks. Among them, platinum‐catalyzed addition‐cure silicones are particularly attractive because of their low curing shrinkage, uniform networks, and stable properties. However, increasing structural complexity and functional integration challenge conventional mold‐based fabrication and motivate additive manufacturing of complex silicone architectures. A central challenge in silicone 3D printing is to move beyond tailoring materials for printability toward designing printing processes around their intrinsic material behavior, thereby enabling precise control over both geometry and properties. Unlike thermoplastics or photocurable elastomers, addition‐cure silicones undergo continuous, time‐ and temperature‐dependent crosslinking after mixing, leading to concurrent evolution of crosslinking state, rheology, and mechanical stability during shaping. This Review defines this process as evolutionary crosslinking and introduces “crosslinking‐in‐shaping” to describe manufacturing in which structure generation is intrinsically coupled with crosslinking evolution. This Review establishes a five‐step framework for extrusion‐based silicone additive manufacturing, reorganizing existing studies from a manufacturing‐science perspective. The framework is also applicable to other thermosetting material systems governed by irreversible crosslinking and thermal regulation.

title: Molecularly Encoded Bioactivity in Designer Amino‐Acid Hydrogels for Regenerative Medicine
abstract:
This work presents a designer amino‐acid hydrogel platform with molecularly encoded bioactivities for regenerative medicine. Designed biocompatible, infection‐resistant hydrogels capable of potential wound healing, bone regeneration, and drug delivery. These findings establish molecularly engineered non‐peptidic poly(amino acids) as effective building blocks for versatile soft material designs.








ABSTRACT
Peptidic poly(amino acids) dominate amino‐acid‐based biomaterials but are constrained by stringent synthetic conditions, high costs, limited chemical tunability, and restricted scalability. Non‐peptidic poly(amino acids), particularly derived from engineered amino‐acid vinyl monomers, offer simpler, cheaper, and more modular alternatives. Yet, their molecular properties and functional potential remain largely unexplored. This work proposes a designer amino‐acid hydrogel platform with molecularly encoded bioactivities for regenerative medicine. Methacrylated L‐histidine, L‐lysine, and L‐arginine, selected through molecular screening of antimicrobial and antioxidant performance, and cytocompatibility, are copolymerized with gelatin methacryloyl to fabricate biomimetic amino‐acid hydrogels (HLAGels) via UV curing. Functionalities of amino‐acid moieties impart covalently integrated antimicrobial, reactive oxygen species‐scavenging, and hemostatic capacities. The hybrid hydrogel network affords adaptive material‐tissue mechanics and self‐healing behavior, favoring wound healing. HLAGels provide driving forces for robust mineralization in simulated body fluid and for growth‐factor‐free osteochondral differentiation of human adipose‐derived mesenchymal stem cells. As drug carriers, HLAGels enable controlled release of dexamethasone. Lastly, an in vivo rat model reveals their biocompatible nature and potential for tissue remodeling. These findings establish molecularly engineered non‐peptidic poly(amino acids) as effective building blocks for soft material design, offering an adaptable strategy for regenerative medicine.

title: No evidence of genome-wide selection against sensetranscription starts in human introns
abstract: RNA polymerase II often starts transcription inside genes, usually at elements that initiate in both directions. An intragenic start pointing in the gene's direction (a sense start) makes RNA that passes the gene's splice sites and polyadenylation signals and may interfere with the gene. Introns may therefore have lost sequences that start sense transcription. In PRO-cap data from K562 and HCT116 cells, the sense start at intronic elements, measured against the antisense start, is a fifth to a third weaker than at intergenic elements of similar read depth. Sequence models that have never seen an element's chromosome predict 30-42% of this bias from local DNA, except models trained on K562 applied to HCT116. However, introns as a whole show little or no depletion of predicted sense starts, and among 76,215 human genomes, variants predicted to create sense starts are not kept rarer than those creating antisense starts. In both cell lines, and in K562 GRO-cap data, strong measured start sites are rarer on the gene strand, mainly near the 5'' end of active genes. Thus, weaker sense starts appear to be a feature of individual active elements, partly predictable from their sequence, and we find no sign that selection has removed such sequences from introns.

title: Transcription starting inside human introns is widespread but mostly yields short-lived RNA
abstract: Background: Thousands of annotated long non-coding RNAs lie inside introns of protein-coding genes, on the host's strand, but whether they are independent genes or pieces of host transcripts is usually unknown. An independent gene needs its own start site. Results: We mapped transcription starts inside introns, using nascent capped RNA from two human cell lines. The approach detected the start sites of 94% of clearly expressed protein-coding genes nested in introns and confirmed 1,346 and 3,061 intronic start sites, almost all unannotated. Most are cell-type-specific, carrying active chromatin marks and motifs of the cell's key transcription factors. Many initiate as strongly as the hosts' alternative promoters but rarely sustain transcription: after a synchronised restart of transcription, their nascent RNA fades within a few kilobases, their short transcripts are partly degraded by the nuclear exosome, and the sequence downstream rarely has the early splice-donor site that protects promoter transcripts. Per initiation event, they leave about as little stable RNA as start sites between genes, so host transcription does not explain their low output. Expressed intronic RNAs on the host's strand more often lack their own start site than those on the opposite strand. Conclusions: Transcription starting inside human introns is widespread but mostly yields short-lived RNA. Many intronic long non-coding RNAs on the host's strand are therefore likely to be pieces of host transcripts rather than independent genes, which matters for their annotation. All intronic start sites in both cell lines, with every measure used here, are provided as a resource.

title: A noise-corrected metric for evaluating spatial transcriptomics predicted from histology
abstract: Deep learning methods that predict spatial transcriptomics from histology offer scalable molecular profiling of clinical cohorts. However, conventional correlation metrics overstate prediction quality across whole sections by crediting models for recognizing broad tissue regions, and understate fine-scale prediction quality because sampling noise dominates sparse RNA counts. To resolve this, we introduce the reproducible-signal correlation (RSC) metric. RSC randomly splits RNA counts into two halves to separate reproducible signal from sampling noise across spatial scales and within tissue regions or cell classes. Across 12 spot-level and three single-cell methods, RSC revealed that most models capture broad tissue patterns but largely miss differences between neighboring spots or cells, which whole-section correlation overlooks. Within malignant cells, RSC distinguished methods that genuinely capture part of the cell-to-cell heterogeneity from those whose scores across all cells were inflated by cell-type composition. Guided by RSC, we designed a pairwise difference loss between neighboring spots that improved fine-scale predictions on average across 11 models. RSC thus provides a foundation for benchmarking predictions, guiding model design and determining which spatial analyses histology can support.

title: VenusPheno: Transfer-Guided Task Grouping for Multi-Task Bacterial Phenotype Prediction
abstract: Understanding how genomic information gives rise to bacterial phenotypes is a fundamental problem in biology. Genome-level prediction requires models that integrate information from thousands of proteins, while related phenotypes may share genomic signals. However, not all phenotype tasks benefit from being learned together, and suitable task groups can be difficult to define from biological knowledge alone. We present VenusPheno, a framework that combines multiple-instance learning over pretrained ProtT5 protein embeddings with transfer-guided multi-task learning. An attention-based Set Transformer aggregates the proteins in each genome into a genome-level representation. We evaluate VenusPheno on 14 binary phenotype tasks from 12,178 bacterial genomes using genus-disjoint splits. Under single-task training, VenusPheno outperforms computational, conventional machine-learning, and deep-learning baselines in terms of mean balanced accuracy. We then use leave-one-task-out analysis to estimate directed transfer relationship between phenotypes, revealing both beneficial and detrimental interactions. Grouping tasks based on these transfer relationships further improves mean balanced accuracy over independent training and joint training of all tasks. Although inferred without biological priors, the resulting groups are consistent with biologically plausible relationships among phenotypes. VenusPheno therefore combines accurate phenotype prediction with a data-driven strategy for determining which tasks should be learned together. The PyTorch implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/YJinling/VenusPheno.

title: Genome-guided vs transcriptome-guided mapping: systematic evaluation of RNA-seq quantification bias for tandemly duplicated genes in model and crop plants
abstract: Accurate quantification of RNA-seq data is fundamental to modern plant biology. The choice of mapping strategy and aligner critically determines expression quantification accuracy and shapes the quality of downstream biological analyses. However, a pervasive yet often underappreciated challenge is the accurate quantification of genes located within tandemly duplicated arrays. Here, we selected six representative plant species (Arabidopsis thaliana and five important crops), and compared RNA-seq analysis results generated from two mapping strategies (genome-guided and transcriptome-guided) using three widely used aligners (TopHat2, HISAT2, and STAR). Our results reveal pervasive alignment errors in genome-guided strategies, arising primarily from misaligned reads spanning tandem gene duplicates, a gene class that plays important roles in plant defense and stress responses, detoxification, and secondary metabolism. TopHat2 with the transcriptome-guided strategy yielded the most accurate alignments, whereas transcriptome-guided HISAT2 and STAR corrected most, but not all, of the errors. Transcriptome-guided mapping also demonstrates superior performance over the genome-guided approach on simulated RNA-seq benchmark datasets. Moreover, in functional enrichment analysis, the transcriptome-guided strategy outperformed the genome-guided one in retrieving gene sets biologically relevant to the processes under study. Overall, this study provides a systematic evaluation of how mapping strategies and software selections affect RNA-seq quantification for tandem gene duplicates, and offers a valuable reference for standardizing plant RNA-seq analytical workflows, particularly for studies investigating biology processes regulated by tandem gene duplicates.

title: Population genomics of the Anopheles farauti complex reveals a distinct regime of malaria vector evolution in the southwest Pacific
abstract: Abstract: The southwest Pacific has one of the highest per-capita malaria burdens outside Africa, yet how its malaria mosquitoes evolve is largely unknown. In African vectors, insecticide resistance evolves rapidly in large, connected populations carrying abundant standing variation. Southwest Pacific vectors show little to no biochemical resistance despite decades of insecticide-based control. We analyse 495 genomes from six taxa of the Anopheles farauti complex, which includes the region's major vectors. The complex radiated rapidly in the late Pleistocene concomitant to the peopling of Near Oceania. Thereafter, post-glacial sea-level rise and climate change fragmented its populations into recently colonised island isolates. Successive environmental and colonisation bottlenecks left a legacy of extraordinary inbreeding, most marked in island populations of the coastal specialist An. farauti sensu stricto, where sustained low effective population size has allowed deleterious alleles to be purged effectively; the inland generalists An. hinesorum and An. oreios retain more variation. After five decades of chemical control we recover a single resistance sweep, at Gste2, alongside recent selection at species-specific chemosensory gene repertoires. Severe inbreeding and the loss of standing variation have not prevented ecological success, challenging assumptions about how much variation and connectivity a vector population needs to thrive. This work establishes the first genomic foundation for this major vector system of endemic species through a biogeographically diverse region of the world.

title: BRIDGE: Backbone Representation for Inverse-folding-Driven Generalizable RNA Encoding
abstract: RNA recognizes small molecules and proteins through their three dimensional structures, but sparse functional annotations limit task specific learning of transferable structural features. We present BRIDGE, an inverse-folding encoder pretrained on 2,501 RNA chain records from experimental structures. Each nucleotide is represented by its phosphorus atom and five ribose atoms (P, C1', C2', C3', C4', O4'). Base coordinates are not encoder inputs. From these atoms, the encoder is trained to predict nucleotide identity, solvent accessible surface area (SASA) and base geometry. With matched readouts, frozen BRIDGE representations reach a three-model ensemble pooled average precision (AP) of 0.627 for external ligand-binding site prediction and 0.647 for RNA-protein interface prediction, compared with 0.503 and 0.516 for frozen, randomly initialized encoders. Under the evaluated full-adaptation recipes, pretrained initialization reaches AP 0.703 for ligand binding and 0.641 for protein interfaces, versus 0.635 and 0.623 for training from scratch. Sequence-only pretraining, without SASA or base-geometry targets, also transfers to both tasks. Whether the base-geometry objectives add further value depends on the task and adaptation mode. In decoy ranking and apo/holo evaluations, transfer depends on the readout and the test set, and small target panels and downstream training overlap in the apo/holo evaluation limit broader conclusions. These results support inverse-folding pretraining as a route to transferable RNA structural representations that do not require observed base coordinates at inference.

title: Alternative splicing edits intrinsically disordered regions across human protein isoforms
abstract: Intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) lack a stable three-dimensional structure, yet they mediate many of the interactions and regulatory functions of proteins. Alternative splicing produces multiple protein isoforms from a single gene, and because individual exons can encode all or part of an IDR, splicing has the potential to add, remove or reshape disordered regions. However, it remains unclear whether splicing preferentially acts on disordered sequence in all kinds of proteins, how it changes an IDR from one isoform to another, and how this relationship arose during evolution. Here, we map predicted disorder onto the coding exons and genomic codons of human protein isoforms, which allows any two isoforms of a gene to be compared directly, and analyze this map across protein classes and families. We find that alternatively spliced exons are more disordered than constitutive exons in every class of protein, from transcription factors to metabolic enzymes, and that splicing usually changes IDRs at their ends, adding or removing disordered segments as modular units rather than cutting through them. The disordered sequence that splicing varies is compositionally distinct from the disorder that all isoforms share. Notably, the apparent loss of disorder over gene evolution reflects differences between protein families rather than change within them, whereas exons whose splice sites are conserved in few mammals encode more disorder than the other exons of the same gene, with a composition resembling that of young genes. Our results suggest that alternative splicing treats intrinsic disorder as a modular, evolvable layer of protein architecture, and that exons with poorly conserved splice sites may be one route by which disordered sequence enters proteins.

title: A modular decomposition framework of the CHO transcriptome reveals lineage, genomic, and process-responsive cell states
abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) transcriptomic studies have generated diverse datasets across parental lineages, cell-line development histories, and culture conditions. However, the transcriptional programs underlying this heterogeneity remain difficult to compare and interpret across studies. Here, we asked whether heterogeneous CHO transcriptomes could be organized into reproducible and biologically interpretable transcriptional modules. To address this, we assembled a discovery compendium of 778 quality-controlled RNA-seq samples spanning multiple parental lineages, engineered cell backgrounds, culture conditions, and perturbations, and applied robust multi-run independent component analysis, resulting in 105 independently modulated gene sets, termed iModulons. To accommodate mammalian regulatory and genomic complexity, we interpreted these modules by integrating gene function, activity-metadata associations, promoter motifs, genomic localization, and RNA-biotype composition. The iModulons captured lineage-associated variation, chromosomal enrichment, and responses to temperature downshift and antiviral stimulation, together with an ATF4-associated amino-acid-stress program. Projection of 377 independent samples onto the discovery-derived iModulons reproduced selected lineage- and process-associated activity patterns and captured a glutamine-deprivation response not represented in the discovery compendium, supporting the transferability of these modules across datasets. When the compendium was expanded to 1,155 samples and ICA was repeated de novo, 89 of the 105 discovery iModulons were preserved among 148 expanded modules, while an additional CHO-DXB11-associated transcriptional pattern emerged. To our knowledge, this study represents the first application of the iModulon framework to a mammalian cell system, establishing a transferable and expandable set of transcriptional coordinates for comparing CHO cell states across heterogeneous datasets and prioritizing programs relevant to cell-line and bioprocess engineering.

title: Evolutionary rescue of rare human genetic disorders in yeast models
abstract: Several thousand human disease-associated genes have clear yeast orthologs, making yeast an ideal model system for advancing a basic understanding of human disease. We used CRISPR-Cas9 editing to generate 51 yeast strains with 11 human disease-associated variants, focusing on human disease genes involved in protein glycosylation, ribosome maturation, mitochondrial function, and RNA regulation. We find that most of these alleles recapitulate as fitness defects in yeast. To enrich for suppressors, we evolved these populations for 1,000 generations and performed whole genome sequencing. We identified both known and previously unknown suppressor mutations. For example, we identify mutations in DPM1 and RPS9B that compensate for disease phenotypes of ALG7 and SDO1, respectively. Reconstructed strains harboring evolved suppressor mutations and the original disease alleles demonstrate that these suppressors rescue fitness and may compensate for defects in molecular function. By exerting continuous selective pressure over thousands of generations, experimental evolution allows us to select for suppressor mutations, including those with modest fitness effects or occurring at lower frequencies, which are underrepresented in traditional genetic screens. Our results map local genetic interaction networks centered around disease-associated alleles, providing greater insights into disease phenotypes and informing potential targeted therapies for disease management in patients with rare disorders.

title: Differential gene expression profiling of lumbar disc degeneration in the RuDDS cohort
abstract: Lumbar disc degeneration disease (LDDD) is a major structural cause of low back pain, one of the leading causes of disability worldwide, and has no disease-modifying treatment. We performed RNA sequencing of 72 intraoperative intervertebral disc samples from the Russian disc degeneration study (RuDDS) cohort, comparing severe (Pfirrmann grades IV-V) with moderate (grade III) degeneration. We identified 731 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; 347 upregulated and 384 downregulated in severely degenerated discs) in the 57 samples that passed quality control. Upregulated DEGs were enriched for extracellular matrix organisation, ossification, and TGF-beta; and Hippo signalling, whereas downregulated DEGs were enriched for immune and inflammatory processes. We identified five differentially active transcription factors, including the TGF-beta; effectors SMAD3 and SMAD4 and the osteogenic regulator DLX5. Of the five, only DLX5 was also a DEG. DEGs were enriched for LDDD-associated genes from Open Targets (odds ratio = 1.68, P = 3.37 * 10-6). Connectivity mapping against the LINCS L1000 database showed that histone deacetylase inhibitors and glucocorticoids reverse the signature of severe degeneration. Together, these results point to TGF-beta-driven fibrotic and osteogenic remodelling as the dominant transcriptional feature of severe disc degeneration, and prioritise candidate genes and compounds for functional validation.

title: Benchmarking sample mispairing detection tools in complex cancer datasets
abstract: Sample mispairs are common and potentially costly mistakes, and therefore checking for sample mispairing is a crucial quality-control step in multimodal genomic studies. This study presents an independent benchmark of sample mispairing detection tools in multimodal transcriptomic cancer datasets. In pseudobulk experiments with known sample pairings, four tools achieved near-perfect F1 scores across datasets. In real-data experiments, three tools performed particularly well, and sample mispairs were identified in three of five datasets. Finally, a high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma dataset is reconstructed: resolving mispairs between two bulk RNA-sequencing modalities, resolving mispairs between pooled single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data, and reestablishing the connection between the transcriptomic data and patient metadata using genetic ancestry inference.

title: Functional interrogation of osteoarthritis-associated regulatory variants and effector genes.
abstract: Background: Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci associated with osteoarthritis (OA); however, the regulatory variants and effector genes underlying most associations remain unresolved. Results: We used complementary functional genomic approaches in chondrocytes to resolve prioritized OA risk loci. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) in primary human chondrocytes identified allele-specific regulatory activity at variants across multiple loci, two of which were independently validated using low-throughput reporter assays. In parallel, integration of OA GWAS signals with chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac CUT&Tag, and chromatin conformation data prioritised candidate regulatory elements for CRISPR based perturbation. CRISPR activation and interference supported functional regulatory relationships between OA risk regions and Pappalysin 1 (PAPPA) and Sprouty RTK signaling antagonist 4 (SPRY4) as target genes. At the 9q33 locus, multiple independent lines of evidence converged on rs1895062, which resides in an accessible region that loops to the PAPPA promoter. The OA risk G allele at rs1895062 results in higher regulatory activity by MPRA and low throughput reporter assay. Activation of this region by CRISPR increases PAPPA gene expression and induces widespread transcriptional changes involving extracellular matrix remodelling and other OA-relevant pathways. Conclusion: Integrating genetic association, genomic and epigenomic data, and functional perturbation in disease-relevant cells can resolve the regulatory mechanisms underlying OA risk loci. Using this multi-faceted approach, we provide convergent functional evidence for rs1895062 as a likely causal variant that controls PAPPA gene expression and OA risk.

title: Tuning evolutionary information in MSAs shapes protein generation and folding
abstract: Protein multiple sequence alignments are widely regarded as fixed artifacts of homologue retrieval. An alignment's row composition shapes the evolutionary context that is supplied to a protein model. In this study, we tested whether tuning row composition would steer protein generation and structure prediction outcomes. We tuned lower-tail alignment information by controlling row selection within a reference protein-projected coordinate frame. We paired each information-targeted alignment with a matched-depth random-row control alignment. Across a cohort of 45 diverse proteins, row coherence among the retained homologues is predictive of structural confidence readouts and generated sequence novelty. The strongest row-coherence states occur near an empirical lower-tail information reference point of 1 bit/site. Below this reference point, generated de novo sequences demonstrate more eager exploration, higher decoder uncertainty, and reduced structural confidence at mutated positions. Across an independent structure-prediction benchmark, controlling the fraction of low-information positions demonstrated that intermediate fractions of low-information positions were associated with improved structure prediction within a confidence-gated subset. These findings evince that evolutionary information in protein alignments can be tuned to shape protein generation and structure prediction results.

title: To sort or to hash? Revisiting k-mer counting
abstract: Motivation: Counting k-mers in large genomic datasets is a foundational primitive in bioinformatics, supporting applications such as genome assembly, variant discovery, metagenomic profiling, and sequence database indexing. As sequencing throughput grows, k-mer counting is routinely applied to collections of hundreds to thousands of files. Even a modest per-file speedup compounds into hours of saved computation across such collections. Methods: Sorting and hashing are the two main ways of counting k-mers, and practice has largely settled on the former, of which KMC3 (Kokot et al., 2017) is the most refined expression. We reconsider this choice and analyze both approaches using a cost model that charges computation and memory transfers together.
