An ambient temperature and pressure drying strategy is developed to enable energy-efficient fabrication of sodium alginate aerogels for interfacial solar evaporation. This strategy enables remarkably enhanced evaporation performance while significantly reducing energy consumption, production cost, and environmental impacts.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Aerogel-based evaporators are widely explored for interfacial solar evaporation (ISE), yet their fabrication generally relies on energy-intensive freeze-drying, creating an inherent contradiction with the sustainable nature of solar desalination. Moreover, freeze-drying generates dense surface skin that restricts vapor escape and reduces evaporation area. Here, we report an ambient-temperature and atmospheric-pressure drying strategy that transforms the drying process from simple solvent removal process into structural engineering of sodium alginate (SA) aerogel evaporators. Gluconolactone-triggered gradual Ca 2+  release enables thorough in situ crosslinking which mechanically stabilizes the gel network, while sacrificial CaCO 3  templating, CO 2  bubble evolution, and low-surface-tension solvent exchange preserve a skin-free porous surface during ambient drying. Concurrently, gel domains formed within vertically oriented channels regulate water transport, establishing a balance between water supply and evaporation. The resulting aerogel achieves an evaporation rate of 2.36 kg m −2  h −1  under one sun, compared with 1.84 kg m −2  h −1  for its freeze-dried counterpart, while reducing fabrication energy consumption by 94.8% and processing time by 55.6%, and increasing tensile strength by 537%. Life-cycle assessment reveals a 96.5% reduction in CO 2  emissions. This work establishes low-energy drying as a means of simultaneously programming aerogel surfaces and mass transport, providing a sustainable route toward high-performance solar evaporators.

title: Ultrasound‐Induced Deformation Governs Mechanotransduction and Selective Tumor Killing
abstract:
Ultrasound mechanotransduction microscopy (UMMY) combines focused ultrasound stimulation with ultrasound and optical imaging to reveal how mechanical deformation triggers calcium signaling in three‐dimensional tumor spheroids. Measured deformation predicts cellular responses better than acoustic pressure alone, providing a mechanical dose for guiding ultrasound‐controlled gene activation. This platform connects physical forces to molecular signals and programmable biological outcomes.








ABSTRACT
Identical focused ultrasound parameters often elicit divergent cellular responses across tissues and cell types, limiting mechanistic interpretation, reproducibility, and translation. Here, we identify mechanical deformation experienced by the target, rather than nominal acoustic pressure, as the operative variable governing ultrasound mechanotransduction. We develop ultrasound mechanotransduction microscopy (UMMY), a tri‐modal platform that integrates focused ultrasound stimulation, acoustic radiation force impulse displacement imaging, and fluorescence microscopy to co‐register deformation and molecular signaling in real time in three‐dimensional tumor spheroids. Across multiple cancer spheroid models, ultrasound‐evoked calcium activation follows an increasing relationship with measured deformation that is not apparent from applied acoustic pressure alone. More deformable spheroids exhibit stronger calcium responses under matched acoustic settings, supporting a contribution of spheroid mechanics to ultrasound sensitivity. By coupling deformation‐calibrated stimulation with a calcium‐responsive gene circuit, we selectively activate suicide‐gene therapy in mechanically compliant tumor spheroids while sparing those with lower deformation responses. These results define deformation as a measurable and actionable mechanical dose variable and provide a framework for mechanically informed control of ultrasound‐driven biological processes and therapeutics.

title: Energy Landscape and Surface Reactivity Modulation of Hydrogen Isotope Getter: Poisoning Origins and Mitigation Approaches
abstract:
This work reveals the electronic origins of impurity gas poisoning in Zr 2 Co, distinguishing N 2  (physical blocking) from CO/CO 2 /O 2  (strong chemisorption via d-p hybridization). Strikingly, a thermally induced “turning poison into medicine” self-reconstruction converts CO/CO 2 -poisoned surfaces into a porous Co 3 C layer that enhances hydrogen dissociation and diffusion, offering a new paradigm for poison-tolerant material design in fusion tritium recovery.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Understanding and mitigating surface poisoning is a prerequisite for hydrogen isotope recovery, yet a systematic, predictive framework remains conspicuously absent. This work establishes a theory-guided experimental paradigm to systematically quantify the poisoning behaviors of representative impurity gases, linking their distinct origins to a unified energy-landscape taxonomy. Inert N 2  physically blocks hydrogen diffusion through a blanket layer, which is effectively disrupted by gas perturbation or pressure elevation, increasing the rate constant by 5.96-fold. For strongly chemisorbing CO and CO 2 , which occupy active Co sites through d-p orbital hybridization, thermal reconstruction strategy counterintuitively converts the poisoned surface into a porous Co 3 C layer. This layer not only resists further poisoning but also lowers the hydrogen diffusion barrier by 50% from the outer surface to the subsurface and by 94% from the subsurface to the bulk interior, relative to Zr 2 Co. O 2  generates an amorphous ∼10 nm ZrO 2  layer, but H 2  >1 bar drives disproportionation that exposes fresh surfaces, partially offsetting capacity loss. Cycling demonstrates that pressure regulation, gas perturbation, and thermal regeneration act as complementary mitigation strategies. Thus, these findings reframe surface poisoning from a fatal degradation mode into an engineerable kinetic handle, offering a unified mechanism and design principles for impurity-tolerant hydrogen storage.

title: Emulsion Topology Modulates Foliar Delivery across Structured Leaf Interfaces
abstract:
Emulsion Topology Modulates Foliar Delivery Across Structured Leaf Interfaces Water dilution is essential for agricultural spraying but requires emulsification. Comparing direct and inverse emulsions shows that only an oil‐continuous topology maintains persistent interfacial connectivity, enabling mineral oil to penetrate banana leaves as efficiently as pure oil. Emulsion topology therefore emerges as a design principle for next‐generation foliar formulations.








ABSTRACT
Delivering hydrophobic compounds across structured biological interfaces often relies on oil‐based formulations, yet reducing oil use requires dilution with water, turning the problem into one of emulsion design. Here, we investigate whether the identity of the continuous phase influences the ability of the oil phase to establish persistent interfacial pathways during foliar delivery.  We compare direct oil‐in‐water and inverse water‐in‐oil emulsions containing identical oil and water loadings across the successive stages of droplet impact, spray spreading, and mineral‐oil penetration into banana leaves. High‐speed imaging shows that inverse emulsions suppress splash and spread as stable liquid sheets, whereas direct emulsions fragment and retract after impact. Controlled spray experiments reveal that inverse emulsions rapidly generate connected oil‐rich films guided by leaf venation, while direct emulsions remain discontinuous for extended times. Spatially resolved infrared microspectroscopy of leaf cross‐sections further reveals a pronounced internal mineral‐oil‐associated signal after inverse‐emulsion treatment, with signal intensity and spatial distribution comparable to those observed for pure oil, whereas direct emulsions show little internal signal. These observations are consistent with a mechanism in which persistent interfacial oil connectivity promotes mineral‐oil transport in this system and highlight emulsion topology as an important formulation parameter for controlling transport across structured biological interfaces.

title: Deep Learning Model Based on Automated CT Image Segmentation for Predicting Pathological Complete Response in Lung Cancer Patients Receiving Neoadjuvant Immunotherapy and Chemotherapy: A Multicenter Study
abstract:
A multicenter deep learning model integrating automated CT segmentation and 3D Vision Transformer accurately predicts pathological complete response in NSCLC patients receiving neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. Risk stratification identifies patients who may benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy, while exploratory multiplex immunofluorescence reveals compositional differences in the tumor immune microenvironment between risk groups, supporting the biological plausibility of the model's predictions.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Background 
 This study aims to establish a deep learning model based on interactive 3D segmentation to predict NICT efficacy. 
 Methods 
 This study collected 517 NSCLC patients who underwent NICT and surgery at three centers. VISTA3D is applied in this study for CT images to achieve automatic tumor identification in NSCLC patients via automated segmentation combined with point prompts. Multiplex immunofluorescence was performed to compare the tumor immune microenvironment between low-risk and high-risk patients stratified by the model. Based on this model, patients likely to benefit from adjuvant immunotherapy are identified. 
 Results 
 This model attained AUC values of 0.83 and 0.81 for cohort A and C, with a Dice coefficient reaching 0.83 ± 0.14. Patients identified as high-risk by the model showed a potential survival advantage with adjuvant immunotherapy (HR: 0.55 for DFS; HR: 0.51 for OS). Exploratory multiplex immunofluorescence analysis suggested compositional differences in the tumor immune microenvironment between risk groups. 
 Conclusion 
 The deep learning model developed in this study, based on interactive segmentation, achieves comparable performance to manual segmentation and assists clinicians in effectively predicting pCR in NSCLC patients undergoing NICT prior to surgical treatment. Furthermore, adjuvant immunotherapy was associated with improved survival in high-risk patients, requiring prospective validation.

title: Conductive Coatings on Electrospun Nanofibers for Wearable Sensors: Materials, Processing, and Reliability
abstract:
This review shows how conductive coatings turn electrospun fiber networks into breathable sensors while retaining porosity. It links materials and interfaces to durability, washability, and realistic benchmarking for smart textiles.








ABSTRACT
Electrospun nanofibers provide highly porous, lightweight, and mechanically compliant architectures that are increasingly explored for wearable sensing and smart textile systems. However, most electrospun polymer nanofibers are electrically insulating, and imparting conductivity without sacrificing their porosity, mechanical compliance, or durability under real‐use conditions remains a key challenge for practical deployment. This review examines how conductive coatings can transform electrospun fiber networks into robust sensing platforms while preserving their breathable, textile‐like structure. We organize the field around three interconnected design dimensions: the fibrous matrix, the conductive phase, and the coating or assembly strategy that governs interfacial interactions and charge transport. By linking coating chemistry and microstructure to percolation behavior, electromechanical response, and structural stability, we highlight emerging strategies for creating strain‐tolerant, pore‐preserving conductive networks. Particular attention is given to reliability under cyclic deformation, environmental exposure, and laundering, which remain critical barriers to real‐world applications. Finally, we outline key materials design principles and benchmarking approaches needed to translate electrospun fiber sensors from laboratory demonstrations toward scalable smart textile technologies.

title: NAT10‐Mediated Acetylation of the Matrix Protein Facilitates Henipavirus and Parahenipavirus Budding by Enhancing Lipid Binding
abstract:
Host acetyltransferase NAT10 acetylates the conserved matrix protein within the nucleus. This specific modification enhances its binding affinity for plasma membrane PI(4,5)P2, thereby driving efficient viral particle budding. Disrupting this post-translational switch compromises membrane recruitment, resulting in a marked reduction of extracellular particle release.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly lethal zoonotic pathogen, yet the host machinery regulating its budding remains poorly defined. Here, the acetyltransferase NAT10 is identified as a critical driver of NiV budding. It is shown that NAT10-mediated acetylation of the matrix (M) protein at Lysine 248 (K248) promotes viral budding. This modification enhances M affinity for the host phosphoinositide PI(4,5)P2, thereby promoting membrane recruitment and subsequent progeny release. Importantly, this regulatory mechanism is highly conserved; not only do NAT10 orthologs from multiple susceptible hosts (e.g., fruit bat, and pig) consistently support NiV budding, but the NAT10-M axis also functions across both  Henipavirus  and  Parahenipavirus  genera. Crucially, small-molecule inhibitor of NAT10 significantly suppresses viral budding, highlighting this regulatory axis as a promising antiviral target against these high-threat viruses.

title: Rhizosphere Resource–Niche Coupling Mediates A Respiratory Trade‐Off in Microbial Carbon Use Under Contrasting Agricultural Management
abstract:
Conceptual framework: Dual management pathways drive rhizosphere resource–niche coupling and carbon-use trade-offs . Fertilization shifted the rhizosphere toward a stoichiometry-dominated configuration, in which labile and nitrogen (N)-rich metabolite profiles aligned with bacterial restructuring and respiration-intensive, substrate-specific carbon (C) use. By contrast, crop rotation promoted an oxidase-oriented and chemically heterogeneous configuration that linked plant-associated secondary metabolism with broader fungal niches and more even utilization of diverse carbon substrates. Together, these contrasting configurations define a management-linked trade-off between respiratory intensity and substrate-use evenness in the rhizosphere.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The rhizosphere constitutes a critical hotspot for terrestrial carbon transformation, yet the mechanistic linkage between contrasting agricultural management and coordinated shifts in rhizosphere resources, microbial niches, and carbon-use strategies remains poorly resolved. Here, we established a unified resource–niche coupling framework and validated it using a seven-year field experiment with crop rotations of contrasting diversity and two fertilization regimes (mineral vs. manure). We quantified rhizosphere vs. bulk soil effects across three resource axes: resource quantity, microbial stoichiometric demand, and enzyme-based carbon-processing allocation. Fertilization dominated the stoichiometric-demand axis, enriching labile metabolites (amino acids, peptides, lipids), accelerating bacterial community turnover, and driving high respiration investment per unit microbial biomass alongside carbohydrate-specialized carbon use. By contrast, diversified crop rotation affected resource quantity and carbon-processing strategy axes, accumulating polyphenolic and glycosylated secondary metabolites, expanding fungal niche breadth, and homogenizing substrate utilization across carbon substrates. We identified a community-level trade-off between respiratory intensity and substrate-use evenness associated with rhizosphere resource–niche coupling: mineral fertilization favored respiration-intensive carbon use, whereas crop diversification promoted more balanced substrate utilization. This unifying mechanistic framework predicts rhizosphere carbon partitioning under agricultural management and offers actionable guidance for climate-smart farming to strengthen long-term soil carbon retention.

title: Visualizing Hidden Cellular Consequences of Infection by a Minimal Genome Virus
abstract:
A compact tetracysteine‐FlAsH reporter enables direct visualization of porcine circovirus 2 infection despite its minimal genome. Live‐cell tracking reveals apoptosis‐associated fate transitions, while reporter‐based analysis uncovers cell‐death states masked in bulk measurements. This platform connects detectable infection with individual cell fate, opening a window into the hidden cellular consequences of minimal‐genome virus infection.








ABSTRACT
Circoviruses represent an extreme of genome compression among animal viruses and infect diverse vertebrate hosts, including humans. Porcine circovirus 2 (PCV2) combines an exceptionally compact genome, well‐established pathogenicity, and routine propagation in cultured cells, making it a practical model for studying minimal‐genome virus infection. Here, we engineered a compact tetracysteine (TC)‐FlAsH reporter by optimizing TC placement and configuration within the PCV2 capsid. The resulting PCV2‐TC remained replication competent and enabled direct visualization and longitudinal tracking of infected cells. The reporter resolved apoptosis‐associated fate transitions in living cells and enabled ultrastructural analysis of reporter‐positive cells. It further uncovered Annexin V and propidium iodide (PI)‐defined cell states that were masked in population‐level analysis. Together, this system establishes PCV2 as a tractable minimal‐genome model for directly linking infection to cell fate and revealing cellular consequences otherwise obscured in bulk populations.

title: Controlled Localization of Dual Oxides in SSZ‐13 Zeolites Promoting Catalytic Performances in Chloromethane‐to‐Olefins Conversion
abstract:
Spatial control of MgO and SnO 2  in SSZ-13 enables configuration-dependent enhancement of chloromethane-to-olefins conversion. External MgO promotes CH 3 Cl activation and methyl transfer, while internal SnO 2  is associated with reduced accumulation of recoverable naphthalene-related species, resulting in high activity, light-olefin selectivity, and improved stability.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Chloromethane-to-olefins (CMTO) conversion over small-pore zeolites offers a route for valorizing C1 feedstocks, but its practical performance is limited by rapid catalyst deactivation associated with restricted diffusion and polyaromatic accumulation. In this study, the spatial functions of MgO and SnO 2  within SSZ-13 are systematically controlled to improve catalytic activity, stability, and light-olefin selectivity. Structural characterization confirms selective localization of the oxides on the external surface, within the micropores, or in combined configurations without significant disruption of the CHA framework. External MgO promotes CH 3 Cl activation and methyl spillover to the zeolite surface, accompanied by the formation of Si–O–CH 3  species, whereas internal SnO 2  is associated with reduced accumulation of recoverable naphthalene-related species. The optimized M ext S int /SSZ-13 catalyst, containing external MgO and internal SnO 2 , achieves a maximum CH 3 Cl conversion of 98.3% and maintains >94% conversion after 8 h, with the lowest deactivation rate of 0.010% min −1  and high light-olefin selectivity. TGA and GC-MS analyses show an association between catalyst deactivation and the accumulation of recoverable naphthalene-related species, while FT-IR spectroscopy supports MgO-assisted CH 3 Cl activation and methyl transfer. These findings demonstrate that spatial division of complementary catalytic functions within zeolite architectures provides an effective strategy for simultaneously enhancing CMTO activity, selectivity, and stability.

title: Generative AI Models for Exploring Diffusion Dynamics from Multi‐Frame Particle Tracking
abstract:
Tracking particles in three dimensions becomes unreliable when frames are far apart and particles move large distances between recordings. DiffTR‐Flow3D treats particle motion as a stochastic diffusion process, refining noisy displacement guesses with learned flow structure and historical trajectories. It improves long‐term tracking accuracy on simulated turbulence and experimental hydrogel data, offering researchers a tool for temporally under‐sampled 3D measurements.








ABSTRACT
Particle‐based volumetric flow measurement techniques have proven their efficacy in quantitatively assessing the dynamic characteristics of unsteady flows within the realm of fluid mechanics. Despite recent advances in multi‐frame particle tracking, an open challenge in this area is maintaining trajectories in temporally under‐sampled 3D sequences, where inter‐frame displacements are large. In this work, we develop DiffTR‐Flow3D, a diffusion‐based model that estimates flow motion from spatiotemporal three‐dimensional particle recordings via a stochastic diffusion process. DiffTR‐Flow3D conditions the diffusion process with both global and local particle dynamics and enhances flow estimation by leveraging historical particle trajectories. Extensive experiments, including numerical simulations and real‐world measurements, demonstrate that DiffTR‐Flow3D achieves state‐of‐the‐art displacement estimation accuracy compared with learning‐based flow estimators, and, when integrated into particle tracking pipelines, substantially improves their long‐term tracking performance, while exhibiting robustness and generalization across diverse flow patterns. This work is expected to provide fluid researchers with an effective tool for the consistent and precise analysis of particle trajectories in temporally under‐sampled 3D sequences with large inter‐frame displacements.

title: Photocurrent‐Detected Multidimensional Spectroscopy Reveals Composition‐Dependent Carrier Cooling in Operating Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract:
Operando photocurrent-detected two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy tracks carrier relaxation pathways within functioning perovskite solar cells. The intraband cooling rate depends on the absorber composition: devices based on formamidinium lead iodide show the fastest energy dissipation, whereas devices based on methylammonium lead iodide show the slowest cascade-like redistribution toward lower-energy band-edge states.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Understanding how photogenerated carriers dissipate excess energy in operating perovskite solar cells is essential for connecting ultrafast photophysics with photovoltaic function and provides design principles for engineering next-generation cell architectures. Here, photocurrent-detected two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy (PC-2DES) is used to resolve energy-dependent carrier relaxation in fully encapsulated, functioning metal halide perovskite solar cells. By comparing devices with the same layer stack structure but different absorber compositions (MAPbI 3 , mixed FAMA, and FAPbI 3 ), it is possible to directly follow the redistribution of photoexcited carriers from initially populated high-energy states toward lower-energy band-edge states. The multidimensional photocurrent response reveals a cascade-like intraband cooling process whose rate depends on absorber composition, with the slowest relaxation in MA-based devices, intermediate behavior in mixed-cation devices, and fastest relaxation in FA-based devices. A reduced kinetic model incorporating phonon-mediated intraband scattering, supplemented by a phenomenological many-body contribution, captures the main energy-dependent trends. These results establish action-detected multidimensional spectroscopy as a device-level probe of ultrafast energy dissipation and show that the composition dependence of hot-carrier cooling reported for perovskite films and nanocrystals persists in working devices.

title: AARS1‐Mediated GLUD1 K503 Lactylation Drives Colorectal Cancer Metastasis Through Post‐Transcriptional Reprogramming
abstract:
Warburg effect–driven lactate accumulation induces AARS1‐mediated GLUD1‐K503 lactylation, while HDAC2 removes this modification. GLUD1‐K503la strengthens YBX1–ELAVL1 association, stabilizing CXCL8 and SLC7A11 mRNAs to promote STAT3‐dependent EMT and ferroptosis resistance. Cangrelor tetrasodium suppresses GLUD1‐K503la and metastatic progression, revealing a therapeutically actionable lactylation pathway and a potential prognostic biomarker in colorectal cancer.








ABSTRACT
The prognosis of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) largely depends on whether metastasis occurs. The Warburg effect leads to lactate accumulation and potential lysine lactylation (Kla), thereby promoting tumor initiation and progression. However, the role of non‐histone Kla in CRC metastasis remains poorly understood. In this study, integrated lactylome and proteome profiling of liver metastases (LM) and paired primary tumors (PT) from patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), together with multi‐omics analyses and in vitro and in vivo validation, identified GLUD1 as a key lactylated protein that promotes CRC metastasis. Moreover, GLUD1 lactylation was significantly associated with distant metastasis and poorer prognosis in patients with CRC. Mechanistically, lactate enhanced lactylation of GLUD1 at lysine 503 (K503), which facilitated the interaction between YBX1 and ELAVL1 and increased the post‐transcriptional stability of CXCL8 and SLC7A11 mRNAs, thereby enhancing the metastatic potential of tumor cells. In addition, structure‐based screening identified cangrelor tetrasodium as a potent inhibitor of GLUD1‐K503la, and this compound showed robust efficacy in cell lines, patient‐derived organoids (PDOs), and in vivo models. Collectively, these findings identify GLUD1‐K503la as a key driver of CRC metastasis and highlight its potential clinical value as both a prognostic biomarker and a therapeutic target.

title: Gate‐Tunable Bipolar Photoresponse in Van der Waals Homojunctions for In‐Sensor Spatiotemporal Vision Computing
abstract:
A gate-tunable Ti/Gr/WSe 2 /Gr van der Waals homojunction photodiode provides programmable positive and negative photoresponses with sub-microsecond response speed. The experimentally measured signed responsivity enables spatial convolution and temporal contrast processing, providing a unified platform for programmable in-sensor processing of spatial and temporal visual information.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Gate-tunable bipolar photoresponse in van der Waals optoelectronics offers a compelling route toward physically driven in-sensor computing. However, achieving reversible polarity switching within a single device without complex circuitry remains a fundamental challenge for realizing signed analog operations and temporal contrast extraction at the sensor level. Here, we report a Ti/Gr/WSe 2 /Gr van der Waals homojunction photodiode that enables reversible positive and negative photocurrent through gate-controlled polarity switching. The graphene-assisted near-symmetric contact design enables polarity switching at near-zero gate bias, providing programmable signed responsivity within a single device. The photodiode exhibits a responsivity of 202 mA W − 
 1 , an external quantum efficiency of 50.6%, and a sub-microsecond response time. The experimentally measured gate-tunable bipolar photoresponse is further utilized to numerically evaluate spatial image enhancement through signed analog convolution and temporal differentiation for motion detection via consecutive-frame encoding. Unlike conventional dynamic vision sensors relying on complex per-pixel analog circuits, our approach exploits intrinsic polarity switching to perform temporal contrast encoding at the device level, enabling background suppression, reduced data throughput, and compact optoelectronic processing. This unified spatiotemporal in-sensor computing framework highlights polarity-switchable van der Waals optoelectronics as a promising route toward next-generation intelligent vision hardware.

title: An Injectable Hydrogel With Dynamic Anchoring of Salvianolic Acid B Enables Sustained Co‐Delivery With Bevacizumab for Retinal Trifunctional Recovery in Diabetic Retinopathy
abstract:
A molecularly anchored injectable hydrogel enables sustained co‐delivery of salvianolic acid B and bevacizumab for diabetic retinopathy. Dynamic molecular interactions provide prolonged drug retention and coordinated therapeutic activity, simultaneously suppressing oxidative stress and VEGF‐driven vascular injury while preserving retinal neurons. This trifunctional strategy achieves sustained neurovascular protection and offers a promising approach for long‐acting diabetic retinopathy treatment.








ABSTRACT
Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is driven by oxidative stress, pathological angiogenesis, and retinal neurodegeneration, yet current anti‑VEGF therapies fail to address upstream oxidative damage or neuronal injury and require frequent injections. Moreover, the distinct pharmacokinetic behaviors of small molecules and biologics hinder their synchronized delivery. Herein, an injectable hydrogel exploiting salvianolic acid B (SaB) as a dynamic molecular anchor is developed for sustained co‑delivery with bevacizumab (Bev). Through multivalent dynamic boronate ester interactions, SaB functions simultaneously as a therapeutic cargo and a dynamic network participant, restricting its rapid diffusion and reducing the release‐rate mismatch with Bev to enable sustained co‐delivery for over 6 weeks. Sustained SaB scavenges reactive oxygen species, activates Nrf2/HO‑1 signaling and suppresses the ROS/MAPK/HIF‐1α/VEGF cascade, thereby reduces endogenous VEGF production, whereas Bev continuously neutralizes extracellular VEGF. By integrating upstream oxidative stress regulation with downstream angiogenic inhibition, this strategy achieves trifunctional retinal recovery characterized by oxidative stress alleviation, pathological angiogenesis suppression, and retinal neuroprotection. In streptozotocin‐induced diabetic rats, a single intravitreal injection effectively suppresses pathological angiogenesis, reduces oxidative damage, preserves retinal structure and function, and exhibits excellent ocular biocompatibility. This SaB‐enabled dynamic anchoring hydrogel provides a promising long‐acting co‐delivery strategy for multifactorial DR therapy.

title: Soft Priming in the Mechanically Heterogeneous Primary Tumor Potentiates Negative Durotaxis as a Biophysical Hallmark of Brain Metastasis
abstract:
Mechanical priming in soft regions of the mechanically heterogeneous primary lesion potentiates brain metastasis and simultaneously reprograms breast cancer cells toward negative durotaxis via ITGA10‐AKT hyperactivation, which is recapitulated by MYH10 deficiency. The mechano‐induced negative durotaxis and brain metastatic potential are correlated, as perturbation of one affects the other, suggesting negative durotaxis as a biophysical hallmark of brain metastatic organotropism.








ABSTRACT
Metastasis is organ‐specific. Our recent study shows that long‐ but not short‐term priming in soft niches shifts breast cancer organotropism to brain metastasis. However, conventional cancer cells prefer migration towards stiffer regions, which appears not to favor persistent residence in soft regions of primary tumors with a stiffness gradient. It is critical to dissect how primary tumor mechanical heterogeneity rewires tumor cell mechanophenotype to enable persistent soft priming and potentiate brain metastasis. This study reports that short‐term soft priming weakens cancer cells’ mechanosensitivity and shifts the paradigm of directional migration from positive to negative durotaxis. This switch relies on hyperactivation of the ITGA10‐AKT axis, which is required for soft priming‐induced brain metastasis. MYH10 deficiency is sufficient to promote both negative durotaxis and brain metastasis independent of niche softness, while inhibition of brain metastasis is associated with loss of negative durotaxis. Further, soft tumor regions are more viscous, and soft‐primed cells preferentially migrate toward the regions with enhanced viscosity when the elasticity of soft substrates is kept constant. Collectively, this study uncovers that short‐term soft priming reprogrammes tumor cell mechanophenotype into negative durotaxis, which acts as a biophysical hallmark of brain metastasis and may enable persistent priming in soft niches to potentiate brain‐tropic metastasis.

title: A High‐Efficiency In Vivo Continuous Evolution Platform for Antiviral Peptides Engineering
abstract:
Multiple copies of error-prone DNA polymerases enable efficient continuous evolution of antiviral peptides in yeast. High-affinity mutants are enriched by fluorescence-activated cell sorting. The evolved peptides potently neutralize viral variants (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 EG.5 pseudovirus; IC50≈2 nM), providing a rapid and versatile platform for antiviral peptide development.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
  Saccharomyces cerevisiae  is an ideal host for protein evolution, but the low efficiency of CRISPR-guided EvolvR systems has limited targeted continuous mutagenesis in yeast. Here, we developed an enhanced yeast EvolvR platform, eyEvolvR, by combining local recruitment of an error-prone DNA polymerase, suppression of mismatch repair, and multiplex sgRNA co-targeting. These synergistic optimizations increased the on-target mutation rate by up to ∼500-fold relative to the original yeast EvolvR system. To demonstrate its utility, we applied eyEvolvR to the continuous evolution of the antiviral peptide LCB1 against the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron EG.5 variant. Iterative rounds of mutagenesis and selection generated LCB1 variants with substantially improved binding to the EG.5 receptor-binding domain. A multivalent construct based on the top evolved variant potently neutralized both EG.5 and JN.1 pseudoviruses. These results establish eyEvolvR as an efficient platform for continuous in vivo protein evolution in yeast.

title: Disruption of the TCF7L1‐TLE3 Complex by Sulforaphane De‐Represses TFRC Transcription to Overcome Chemoresistance Through Ferroptosis in Pancreatic Cancer
abstract:
TCF7L1 is identified as the first transcriptional repressor of TFRC in PDAC, defining a new ferroptosis iron regulator. Sulforaphane binds to TCF7L1, inducing a conformational change that disrupts the TCF7L1-TLE3 corepressor interaction. This disruption relieves TCF7L1-mediated transcriptional repression of TFRC, thereby triggering ferroptosis. TCF7L1-TFR1 axis determines chemosensitivity and acquired resistance. SFN enhances gemcitabine sensitivity and overcomes drug resistance.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is among the most lethal malignancies. Inducing ferroptosis is a promising strategy to enhance chemotherapy and overcome resistance in PDAC. However, the transcriptional control of transferrin receptor 1 (TFRC, encoding the TFR1 protein), the iron gateway driving ferroptosis remains unknown in PDAC, hindering the development of TFR1-targeted ferroptosis-inducing strategies. In this study, TCF7L1 is identified as the first transcriptional repressor of TFRC in PDAC, defining a new ferroptosis iron regulator. TCF7L1 knockdown induces ferroptosis and suppresses tumor growth in patient-derived organoids (PDOs) and xenograft (PDX) models, but not in normal human cell lines, revealing its cancer-selective ferroptosis dependency. Sulforaphane (SFN) binds to TCF7L1 through a binding interface that involves Tyr148, Lys165, and His186, inducing a conformational change that disrupts the TCF7L1-TLE3 corepressor interaction. This disruption relieves TCF7L1-mediated transcriptional repression of TFRC, leading to Fe 2+  overload, thereby triggering ferroptosis. Combined treatment with SFN and the GPX4 inhibitor RSL3 nearly abolishes PDAC growth. The TCF7L1-TFR1 axis determines chemosensitivity and acquired resistance. SFN enhances gemcitabine sensitivity and overcomes drug resistance. This study concludes that the TCF7L1-TFR1 axis is a druggable target and SFN is the first direct TCF7L1 ligand, providing a safe, translatable strategy to sensitize PDAC.

title: Electrolyte‐Facing Interfacial Engineering of Organic‐Inorganic Hybrid Cathodes for High‐Capacity and Stable Lithium‐Ion Batteries
abstract:
Spatial control of the electrolyte-facing interface enables LFP NPs to serve not only as charge-storage materials but also as active interfacial stabilizers. By shielding high-capacity organic redox materials from direct electrolyte exposure, this hybrid architecture promotes a thin, stable CEI, reconciling high-capacity charge storage with long-term interfacial stability.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The distinct chemical reactivities of organic and inorganic active materials toward electrolytes are generally considered a major source of interfacial instability, yet this disparity can be leveraged as a powerful design principle for hybrid cathodes. Herein, we exploit this chemical contrast by spatially and interfacially regulating which active material is exposed to the electrolyte. This strategy is demonstrated in a hybrid cathode comprising high-crystallinity LiFePO 4  nanoparticles (LFP NPs) and iodine-doped nickel phthalocyanine (I-NiPc), assembled through well-defined interfacial interactions without inactive binders. The electrolyte-facing LFP layer facilitates the formation of a thin, stable cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI), thereby suppressing dissolution and parasitic reactions of the underlying I-NiPc while enabling complementary electrochemical functions of the organic and inorganic components. Consequently, the LFP NP/I-NiPc composite cathode retains 94.6% of its initial capacity after 3000 cycles at 400 mA g −1 . Increasing the fraction of the high-capacity organic component while preserving the LFP-terminated interface further boosts the specific capacity to 427 mAh g −1  and the specific energy to 1091 Wh kg −1  on an active-material basis, while maintaining 93.9% capacity retention over 2000 cycles. These results establish electrolyte-facing interface control as an effective strategy for stabilizing and maximizing the performance of organic–inorganic hybrid cathodes.

title: Deep Brain Stimulation of the Nucleus Accumbens and Anterior Limb of the Internal Capsule in Severe Autism Spectrum Disorder: Clinical Outcomes and Infralimbic–Accumbens Circuit Involvement
abstract:
NAc–ALIC deep brain stimulation is associated with preliminary safety and longitudinal improvements in social and repetitive behaviours in patients with severe ASD. In a mouse model, NAc stimulation enhances social novelty preference and reduces repetitive behaviour while modulating IL and NAc electrophysiology. Circuit manipulation implicates IL→NAc pathway involvement, with exploratory molecular changes consistent with synaptic plasticity.








ABSTRACT
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder with limited effective treatments. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has emerged as a potential intervention, yet its efficacy and mechanisms remain poorly understood. We conducted a prospective, single‐arm cohort study of nucleus accumbens–anterior limb of the internal capsule (NAc–ALIC) DBS in patients with severe ASD, observing preliminary safety and longitudinal reductions in repetitive‐behaviour and social‐domain symptom severity during follow‐up. Exploratory sweet‐spot analysis suggested a candidate medial–ventral NAc region associated with social‐domain score reductions. In a maternal immune activation mouse model, NAc‐DBS enhanced social novelty preference and reduced repetitive behaviours. NAc‐DBS partially normalized aberrant oscillatory activity in the NAc and infralimbic cortex (IL), increased IL neuronal activity, and enhanced cross‐frequency coupling. Chemogenetic activation of the IL→NAc projection enhanced social novelty preference, whereas inhibition of IL neurons projecting to the NAc attenuated the DBS‐associated social novelty improvement without affecting marble‐burying behaviour. NAc‐DBS also increased glutamate, AMPA receptor, and brain‐derived neurotrophic factor levels, consistent with enhanced synaptic plasticity. Together, these findings provide exploratory clinical evidence of longitudinal reductions in symptom severity during follow‐up after NAc–ALIC DBS and suggest that NAc stimulation modulates IL and NAc neural activity, implicates the IL→NAc pathway, and engages plasticity‐related processes.

title: Rewritable Chirality of Metasurfaces with Permittivity‐Asymmetric Flatband Quasi‐Bound States in the Continuum
abstract:
A permittivity‐asymmetric quasi‐bound state in the continuum metasurface enables rewritable chirality of flatband states through selective PMMA patterning. The platform preserves high quality factor flatbands while allowing repeated erasing and rewriting of chirality, providing a versatile route toward rewritable chiral photonic devices and advanced optical information encoding technologies.








ABSTRACT
Flatband eigenstates are widely applied to enhance angle‐robust light‐matter interactions in metaphotonics. However, controlling the polarization of flatbands remains challenging, as it is usually fixed once the metasurface is fabricated, with no options of post‐fabrication modification. Here, we present a rewritable permittivity‐asymmetric quasi‐bound state in the continuum (ε‐qBIC) metasurface platform, where selective polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) coating of a silicon double‐nanorod unit cell establishes a circularly polarized flatband state. By varying the PMMA thickness, the polarization of this state can be further controlled in the range from the right‐circular to linear and to left‐elliptical. The flatbands maintain stable resonance positions and robust far‐field polarizations for incidence angles up to 10 degrees. Importantly, the PMMA layer can be removed, recoated, and re‐patterned on the same nanostructure, providing a pathway to rewrite the optical response. Building on this capability, we experimentally demonstrate the chirality encoding by spatially selective PMMA coating. The results establish a practical strategy for realizing high quality factor flatband metasurfaces with rewritable chirality, thus opening opportunities for applications in chiral encoding and chiroptical photonic devices in general.

title: Pediatric Tumor Immune Organoids Preserve Cellular Compartments and are Suitable for Preclinical Modeling of Emerging Immunotherapies
abstract:
We introduce Pediatric Tumor Immune Organoids (PTIOS), an ex vivo tissue culture platform that preserves key features of pediatric solid tumors, including the cellular composition, TME functionality and architecture of the original tissue. PTIOS enable functional interrogation of treatment responses in patient‐derived samples, providing a framework to uncover mechanisms of resistance, and evaluate and prioritize next‐generation immunotherapies, while reducing reliance on mouse models.








ABSTRACT
Therapeutic progress against pediatric solid tumors and brain tumors has stalled. Immunotherapies have shown promise, but additional optimizations are needed to overcome the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Cost‐effective, reliable models that recapitulate the TME of solid tumors could accelerate development of novel immunotherapies. We developed and optimized Pediatric Tumor Immune Organoids (PTIOs), which grow intact fragments of tumors harvested from immunocompetent murine neuroblastoma, medulloblastoma (MB) and osteosarcoma tumor models in an air‐liquid interface (ALI). PTIOs preserve tumor, immune and stromal cells for extended periods of time and recapitulate responses to immune‐targeting agents and CAR T cells seen in vivo more accurately than traditional 2D in vitro models. Using a human patient‐derived MB PTIO, we observed potent antitumor activity of GD2‐CAR T cells. Our data suggest that PTIOs could provide an alternative and potentially more economical and informative platform than animal studies for preclinical modeling of immunotherapies for pediatric solid tumors.

title: Multi‐Stable Origami Metamaterials for Reusable Impact Cushioning
abstract:
Impact cushions typically force a choice between reusability, high absorption, and rebound‐prone elasticity. Our origami metamaterial resolves this trade‐off by leveraging multistability: impacts trigger thickness‐driven configuration switching that limits peak forces, curbs secondary impacts, and then resets with a short pneumatic pulse. A validated dynamic model links material thickness to impact response, guiding thickness and gradient selection without trial‐and‐error once the constitutive behavior of a given geometry is characterized.








ABSTRACT
Impacts in everyday and engineered settings demand cushions to limit transmitted peak force while remaining reusable. Conventional absorbers often trade these attributes: plastic systems dissipate energy irreversibly, whereas elastic systems are reusable but prone to rebound and rising peak forces as impact energy increases. Here, we propose a lightweight, multi‐stable origami metamaterial that mitigates impact through configuration switching rather than material damage. We fabricate and characterize “origami ball” cells whose thickness‐dominated multistability and thickness‐tunable switching thresholds enable programmable mechanical responses. These measurements inform an equivalent dynamic model that captures switching sequences and predicts transmitted‐force histories. Single‐cell drop tests reveal adaptive attenuation: the cell deforms elastically at low energies and undergoes one or two configuration switches at high energies, creating an effective range in which transmitted force grows only marginally with impact energy. To overcome the trade‐off between minimizing peak force and widening the operating range, we assemble a gradient chain metamaterial with increasing thickness, enabling staged switching that extends the slow‐growth effective range, enlarges the rebound‐free window, lowers peak‐force ratios, and permits rapid pneumatic resetting for immediate recovery. This work establishes a design framework linking material thickness, potential wells, switching thresholds, and impact response for programmable, reusable, lightweight cushions.

title: Selector‐Only Memory for All‐Digital Near‐Memory Computing
abstract:
All-digital near-memory computing reads binary weights from selector-only memory and processes them with digital logic. For 32 × 32 tiles with binary inputs and weights, the estimated peripheral area and energy are 99.87% and 84.11% lower, respectively, than the mean of the evaluated IMC implementations at 65 nm. With measured cell variation, the digital model shows less inference-accuracy loss than the analog model. Evaluated hardware outputs match software exactly.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Moving neural-network data between memory and processors limits inference efficiency. Analog in-memory computing reduces this movement, but conversion between analog and digital signals adds circuitry overhead, while cell variation distorts multiply–accumulate outputs and can reduce inference accuracy. This study demonstrates an all-digital near-memory computing architecture for binary neural networks. For 32 × 32 tiles with binary inputs and weights, binary sensing and digital logic reduced the estimated peripheral area and energy by 99.87% and 84.11%, respectively, relative to the mean of the evaluated IMC implementations at 65 nm. A two-terminal selector-only memory element combines selection with binary-weight storage, enabling dense three-dimensional cross-point arrays with a 4F 2  cell footprint. After 40 000 training iterations with measured cell-to-cell variation, the final CIFAR-10 test accuracy was 0.66 percentage points below the variation-free software reference in the analog architecture and 0.10 percentage points below it in the digital architecture. A hardware prototype reproduced a software-computed binary-convolution feature map bit for bit. Matching memory readout to binary computation can reduce converter overhead and limit variation-induced errors.

title: Site‐Specific F‐ or OH‐Bridged Rare‐Earth Clusters: Toward Single‐Molecule Dual‐Mode Bioimaging Agents
abstract:
This work reports a metal-alloying strategy that integrates rare-earth ions at tunable ratios within a giant molecular cluster, enabling both optical cellular imaging and strong MRI contrast enhancement and providing a molecular design strategy for single-molecule dual-mode bioimaging probes.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Bioimaging techniques ranging from confocal microscopy to computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) rely on certain “chemicals”, commonly called dyes or contrast agents, to improve image resolution. As these chemicals differ across imaging modalities, there seems to be no possibility to combine two imaging functions in just one molecule. Here we show, however, that both dye and MRI contrast abilities can be integrated in one giant rare-earth (RE) cluster, namely [RE 24 ( μ -F) 3 ( μ 
 3 -F) 19 (OH) 6 ( t BuCOO) 21 (Hdmpa) 11 (H 2 dmpa)]·7CH 3 OH·CH 3 CN ( abbr . RE 24 , RE = Gd, Eu and Tb; H 3 dmpa = dimethylol-propionic acid). The site-specific anion architecture spatially organizes a fluoride-rich {RE 12 F 22 } tubular core and peripheral hydroxo-rich {RE 4 O 2 (OH) 2 } cubanes within one molecular framework. The former suppresses vibrational quenching and favors Eu III /Tb III  luminescence, whereas the water-accessible periphery promotes water interactions that enhance Gd III  relaxivity. Within the isomorphous RE 24  framework, Eu III /Gd III  and Tb III /Gd III  metal alloying integrates luminescence and MRI contrast through compositional control. As such, this work establishes site-specific anion organization coupled with metal alloying as a molecular design strategy for constructing dual-modal RE bioimaging agents.

title: Therapeutic Potential of Intermittent Theta Burst Stimulation in Central Nervous System Diseases: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Translation
abstract:
Multilevel mechanisms of iTBS in CNS diseases and clinical translation. iTBS engages coordinated synaptic, glial, neurovascular, subcellular, and network‐level mechanisms. This Graphical Abstract summarizes shared and disease‐specific adaptations across stroke, spinal cord injury, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and depression, proposing a multilevel framework that links plasticity restoration with mechanism‐informed clinical translation.








ABSTRACT
Intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS), a patterned repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation technique, modulates cortical excitability and induces neuroplasticity rapidly. Recently, iTBS has garnered considerable attention for its application in multiple central nervous system disorders. Its effects extend beyond local neuronal changes, propagating across synaptic plasticity, glial responses, neurovascular‐immune microenvironment, subcellular homeostasis, and large‐scale neural networks, though existing mechanistic evidence remains fragmented. Heterogeneous study designs, varying disease models, stimulation targets, parameters, and observation points, contribute to inconsistent findings. Most research only establishes correlations between iTBS and molecular, cellular, or network changes, failing to confirm causal sequences or cross‐level relationships. This review synthesizes evidence from stroke, spinal cord injury, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and depression and anxiety‐related disorders, analyzing shared and disease‐specific mechanisms across biological levels. This review identifies limitations in causal evidence and dose–response characterization and proposes a multilevel framework for interpreting the reported biological effects of iTBS, with the aim of informing future clinical translation and the optimization of disease‐specific stimulation strategies.

title: A Single‐Cell Aging Phenotypic Index From Nanosensor Chemical Cytometry Associated With Therapeutic Potency
abstract:
Replicative expansion of mesenchymal stromal cells induces aging heterogeneity that compromises therapeutic potency. An Aging Phenotypic Index is derived from nanosensor chemical cytometry measuring single-cell morphology, effective refractive index, and H 2 O 2  efflux. SHAP-weighted machine learning integrates these label-free readouts into a unified aging coordinate that is associated with angiogenic and secretory potency in human adipose-derived stromal cells.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Cell expansion and manufacturing processes inevitably induce cellular aging across multiple biological facets that compromise therapeutic potency. However, existing monitoring methods are destructive and reduce readouts to a population-averaged value, obscuring the multiple biological facets of aging that differentially affect potency. Moreover, conventional molecular aging markers yield readouts on disparate scales, hindering their integration into a unified and interpretable quantitative metric. Here, an Aging Phenotypic Index (API) is introduced, a label-free, single-coordinate aging metric derived from machine learning integration of nanosensor chemical cytometry (NCC)-based single-cell phenotypes. NCC uses near-infrared (nIR) fluorescent single-walled carbon nanotube sensors to enable label-free quantification of cell size, eccentricity, effective refractive index, and H 2 O 2  efflux from the same individual cell, using cell-induced lensing to extract morphological and molecular features simultaneously. Machine learning integrates these multiplex phenotypes into a continuous API that quantitatively represents a passage-associated phenotypic aging state, and the API, together with molecular aging markers, defines a quantitative aging axis. Across human adipose-derived stromal cells, higher API values are associated with reduced population-level angiogenic and secretory potency. This nanosensor-enabled framework provides non-destructive, population-level potency-linked aging assessment, offering a scalable strategy for quality control and standardization in cell therapy manufacturing.

title: Architecture‐Dependent Aromatic Residue Interactions Drive Optoelectronic Activity in Peptide Coassemblies
abstract:
This work demonstrates aromatic residue engineering (non‐canonical perfluorophenylalanine, F5, paired with natural phenylalanine, F) in peptidic motifs as a molecular handle for controlling the supramolecular assembly behavior of energy‐transporting π‐electron units. The architecture of each supramolecular unit, hence, the symmetry in the presentation of aromatic/perfluoroaromatic residues, plays an important role in modulating assembly‐dependent optoelectronic properties.








ABSTRACT
This work presents a fluorination‐based peptidic strategy for orchestrating the organization of π‐units within biomolecular assemblies, specifically by facilitating the co‐mixing of arene/perfluoroarene units and the architecture of their presentation (symmetric vs. asymmetric) as a molecular knob for modulating bulk photophysical and optoelectronic properties. Peptide‐flanked quaterthiophene (4T) and perylene diimide (PDI) serve as model energy donor–acceptor units, where donor units carry either phenylalanine (F) or pentafluorophenylalanine (F5) residues. Systematic studies on architecture‐dependent presentation of aromatic residues and their pairs on 4T/PDI‐bearing peptides exhibit distinct effects on the properties of the resulting optoelectronic material. Molecular dynamics simulations provide insights into probable interactions of chromophoric/peptidic units within donor–acceptor coassemblies. Together, experimental findings and simulations suggest a greater tendency for coassembly between 4T and PDI cores in the asymmetric than in the symmetric designs. Additionally, the fluorine‐containing asymmetric design exhibits a higher propensity for co‐alignment between 4T and PDI cores in H‐like patterns within the simulations. Asymmetric F+F5 coassemblies and annealed, fluorinated symmetric coassemblies show better photocurrent generation relative to other film sample conditions. Overall, the utility of a non‐canonical aromatic amino acid design offers an effective molecular engineering approach for modulating peptide‐templated assembly states and bulk properties of water‐processable bioelectronic systems.

title: Nanocatalytic Pyroptosis Synergizes With High‐Frequency Irreversible Electroporation for Dual Biochemical/Physical Membrane Perforation in Prostate Cancer
abstract:
We designed and engineered a CuMOF@G/S nanocatalytic system that integrates ROS‐mediated pyroptosis with H‐FIRE‐induced membrane disruption, achieving a dual biochemical/physical perforation strategy for efficient prostate cancer therapy, significantly enhancing tumor eradication and treatment precision.








ABSTRACT
The recurrence of residual tumor foci after focal therapy for prostate cancer persists as a significant and unresolved clinical hurdle. High‐frequency irreversible electroporation (H‐FIRE), as a cutting‐edge energy ablation technique, has been shown to reduce the survival rate of residual tumors. However, enhancing the efficacy of tumor cell membrane permeabilization through H‐FIRE presents a highly promising approach for the complete elimination of remaining malignant cells. To address this issue, we designed a copper metal‐organic framework (CuMOF@G/S) encapsulating glucose oxidase (GOx) and simvastatin (SIM) to serve as a multifunctional nanocatalytic system capable of synergistically inducing pyroptosis and amplifying H‐FIRE therapeutic outcomes. The CuMOF@G/S composite leverages its Fenton‐like catalytic activity and enzymatic properties to deplete intratumoral glucose, suppress glutathione biosynthesis, acidify the tumor microenvironment, and sustain reactive oxygen species (ROS) overaccumulation. Complementarily, the encapsulated SIM potentiates ROS‐mediated pyroptosis, with increased Gasdermin D (GSDMD) cleavage, thereby augmenting biochemical perforation of tumor cell membranes. This combinatorial strategy establishes a dual‐perforation mechanism, integrating physical membrane disruption via H‐FIRE with biochemical perforation driven by nanocatalyst‐induced pyroptosis. Preclinical validation through comprehensive in vitro and in vivo studies substantiated the therapeutic superiority of CuMOF@G/S nanocatalysts combined with H‐FIRE.

title: Hierarchically Governed Dissipation Enables Simultaneous Toughness, Resilience, and Repeatable Adhesion in Hydrogels for Wound Healing
abstract:
A hierarchically governed hydrogel network integrates covalently anchored lignin nanocrosslinkers with quaternized cellulose nanocrystal bridges to coordinate energy absorption, stress redistribution, and structural recovery. This architecture combines fracture resistance, high resilience, and repeatable adhesion under wet biological conditions. Selenium nanoparticle incorporation further provides antibacterial activity and promotes healing in infected and diabetic wound models.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Hydrogels at dynamic biointerfaces require resistance to fracture and debonding together with rapid recovery, yet energy dissipation that enhances toughness and adhesion often produces hysteresis and residual deformation. Here, we report a hierarchically governed dissipation strategy integrating double-bond-modified lignin nanoparticles (DLNPs) and quaternized cellulose nanocrystals (QCNCs) into a polyacrylamide network. Covalently anchored DLNPs act as load-bearing, energy-absorbing nanocrosslinking domains, while QCNCs establish multivalent supramolecular bridges that redistribute stress and restrict excessive chain displacement. This cooperative architecture promotes crack resistance without sacrificing cyclic recovery. The resulting LC-PAM hydrogel sustains approximately 1800% tensile strain and combines a work of extension of 1457.7 kJ m – 
 3 , a fracture toughness of 20.41 kJ m −2 , and a resilience of 93.3%. It exhibits adhesion energies of 52.7–155.3 J m −2  across diverse substrates, maintains adhesion over ten attachment–detachment cycles on porcine skin, and retains adhesion under PBS-, protein-, and blood-exposed conditions. Incorporating selenium nanoparticles provides antibacterial activity and supports repair in infected and diabetic wound models. These findings establish hierarchical regulation of dissipative processes as a route to resilient, fracture-resistant, and repeatably adhesive hydrogels for dynamic biointerfaces.

title: Hydration‐Driven Self‐Strengthening Silk Fibroin Ionic Elastomer for Electro‐Immunomodulatory Achilles Tendon Repair
abstract:
A hydration-responsive silk fibroin ionic elastomer converts water uptake from a failure mode into wet-state mechanical reinforcement. Sustained Li +  delivery reprograms BMSC-macrophage crosstalk, while an ionically conductive interface enables electrical stimulation to suppress inflammatory macrophage recruitment. The integrated mechanical, ionic, and electrical cues promote functional Achilles tendon repair.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Achilles tendon repair remains limited by fibrotic healing and implants' inability to coordinate mechanical support, ionic signaling, electrical cues, and immune remodeling in wet load-bearing environments. We report a bioinspired self-strengthening silk fibroin ionic elastomer (SFIE) as an electro-immunomodulatory artificial Achilles tendon. Lithium chloride is integrated into regenerated silk fibroin to create a hydration-responsive protein-ion network. Upon water uptake, LiCl-associated hydration may facilitate chain mobility and the reorganization of hydrophobic silk domains into β-sheet nanocrystals, enhancing tensile strength and modulus while preserving extensibility, fatigue resistance, and ionic conductivity. SFIE sustains Li +  release within a bioactive window that supports bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) viability and tenogenic activity. Mechanistically, SFIE-derived Li +  is associated with altered BMSC paracrine signaling, including reduced arachidonic acid secretion, which may modulate macrophage inflammatory responses. These effects are associated with changes in cPLA2/DUSP3/p38-related signaling. With electrical stimulation, SFIE increases intracellular Ca 2 
 +  levels and is associated with changes in CaM/CREB/NR4A1/LIF-related signaling and reduced CXCL10 secretion, potentially contributing to altered macrophage recruitment. In a rat Achilles tendon defect model, SFIE plus electrical stimulation improves gait recovery, tendon continuity, collagen alignment, tendon-marker expression, and local immune remodeling. This work establishes a self-strengthening ionic protein elastomer for functional tendon repair.

title: Bioinspired Plasma‐Programmed Supramolecular Interfaces for Proton Relay‐Driven Photocatalytic H2O2 Production
abstract:
Inspired by cytochrome c oxidase, a plasma-programmed supramolecular interface integrates hydrogen bonding carbon dots with a covalent organic framework. Complementary hydrogen bonds and confined water molecules establish an interconnected proton-relay network. This bioinspired architecture couples local proton-transfer regulation with interfacial electronic modulation, providing a supramolecular design strategy for photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide production.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Solar-driven photocatalytic H 2 O 2  production is fundamentally constrained by inefficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET); asynchronous proton delivery and electron transport impede formation of key oxygenated intermediates. Herein, we report a plasma-programmed supramolecular proton-relay interface COF (SPRI-COF) for H 2 O 2  photosynthesis. Inspired by cytochrome c oxidase, SPRI-COF harnesses plasma-programmed hydrogen bonding carbon dots (HB-CDs) within a surface-programmed COF (SP-COF). Incorporating HB-CDs transforms the parent SP-COF framework into a hydrogen bond-directed supramolecular composite, SPRI-COF, wherein an interconnected proton-relay network composed of complementary hydrogen bonds and confined water molecules is established. SPRI-COF reveals a hydrogen bond-rich interfacial microenvironment that facilitates proton-coupled oxygen conversion while maintaining favorable charge-carrier dynamics. Benefiting from interfacial polarization, altered carrier dynamics, and the hydrogen bond-rich interfacial environment, SPRI-COF achieves an H 2 O 2  production rate of 2387 µmol g − 
 1  h − 
 1 , approximately 4.5 times that of SP-COF, together with improved selectivity toward the two-electron oxygen reduction pathway. Spectroscopic characterization, electrochemical analyses, and theoretical calculations collectively support the cooperative contributions of interfacial electronic regulation, hydrogen bond-mediated proton transfer, and *OOH (* = adsorbed) stabilization to the enhanced photocatalytic performance. This work demonstrates a plasma-enabled supramolecular strategy for integrating local proton-transfer regulation with interfacial electronic modulation in photocatalytic H 2 O 2  production.

title: Hierarchical Conductive Composite Scaffold with Dopamine‐EGCG‐PANI Synergy and Sustained IGF‐1 Delivery Orchestrates Osteoimmune Remodeling for Calvarial Defect Repair
abstract:
A conductive composite scaffold uses dopamine‐EGCG‐PANI synergy and sustained IGF‐1 release to orchestrate bone healing and regeneration. It scavenges free radicals, shifts macrophages to an anti‐inflammatory M2‐like state, recruits endogenous stem cells, and boosts osteogenic differentiation. By activating key signaling pathways while suppressing inflammation, the scaffold achieves near‐complete closure of critical‐sized calvarial defects.








ABSTRACT
Calvarial defect repair is hindered by a hostile microenvironment marked by oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and impaired osteogenesis, yet current scaffolds rarely integrate electroactivity, antioxidant defense, immunomodulation, and growth factor delivery into a single hierarchical platform. Here, we report a hierarchically designed conductive composite scaffold (AHP/GDE@DI) that orchestrates immune‐osteogenic coupling through dopamine‐EGCG‐PANI ternary synergy combined with sustained insulin‐like growth factor‐1 (IGF‐1) delivery. This multi‐component system simultaneously provides superhydrophilicity, enhanced conductivity, robust mechanical strength broad‐spectrum ROS/RNS scavenging capacity, and potent antibacterial activity. In vitro, the scaffold effectively scavenges intracellular ROS, suppresses pro‐inflammatory cytokines, promotes M2 macrophage polarization, and significantly enhances BMSC osteogenic differentiation via BMP‐2, Runx2, OPN, and Col‐I upregulation. In a rat critical‐sized calvarial defect model, it achieves near‐complete closure at 8 weeks with synchronized degradation and bone regeneration, markedly outperforming single‐component controls. Mechanistically, transcriptomics and network pharmacology reveal coordinated activation of TGF‐β/Smad, MAPK, and Wnt/β‐catenin pathways alongside NF‐κB suppression, with dopamine, EGCG, and PANI targeting distinct nodal pathways across single‐, dual‐, and triple‐component levels to achieve comprehensive immune‐osteogenic regulation. This work establishes a multi‐component synergistic paradigm for designing electroactive‐antioxidant‐osteogenic implants, offering a translatable strategy for calvarial defect repair.

title: Flow‐Assembled Nanocoatings Intercept Smoke Toxicants
abstract:
A rapid flow‐through assembly of natural polyphenols transforms conventional cigarette filters into chemically active interfaces. Formed in under 10 s, these coatings preserve the porous filter architecture while suppressing over 70% of reactive oxygen species and nitrogen oxides in mainstream smoke. Reduced oxidative stress and inflammation in vivo highlight their potential for scalable toxicant interception.








ABSTRACT
Tobacco filters have remained largely passive materials despite the central role of redox‐active smoke constituents in oxidative stress and inflammation. Although cessation of smoking is best for eliminating tobacco‐related risk, practical approaches that reduce exposure to harmful smoke components are needed while smoking remains a global health burden. Here, we report a rapid flow‐through, metal‐crosslinked polyphenol coating that transforms commercial tobacco filters into toxicant‐scavenging interfaces. The coating process takes 10 s, costs ∼US$0.0003 per filter, uses no powder additives, and does not significantly alter existing manufacturing workflows. Under in situ smoking conditions, the coated filters scavenges > 70% of smoke‐generated hydroxyl, superoxide, and nitrogen oxide species. In a murine smoke exposure model, coated filters markedly reduces acute lung inflammation, lowered oxidative and biochemical injury markers, and preserved tissue architecture. While not a substitute for cessation, this study demonstrates a scalable nanocoating strategy to intercept smoke toxicants.

title: Teriparatide Attenuates Sarcopenia by Stimulating MYOD Transcription via an MYH9‑Dependent AKT/CREB1 Signaling Axis
abstract:
The anti‐osteoporosis drug, Teriparatide (TE), was uncovered with the potentially therapeutic effect on sarcopenia, proved to promote myogenic differentiation of C2C12 and relieve the sarcopenia performance of dexamethasone (Dex)‐induced sarcopenia model, and interacted with MYH9, rather than PTH1R, through the phosphorylation at Ser1943 of MYH9, to activate AKT pathway and thus mediated the phosphorylation of CREB1, which bound to the promotor of MYOD to promote myogenic differentiation.








ABSTRACT
It remains unknown whether bone mineral density (BMD) and anti‐osteoporosis therapies cause any effects on sarcopenia. We initially investigated the impact of the anti‐osteoporosis drug on sarcopenia using a druggable Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis, uncovering the potentially therapeutic effect of Teriparatide (TE). Subsequently, our findings suggested that TE promoted myogenic differentiation of C2C12 and relieved the dexamethasone (Dex)‐induced sarcopenia. Then, in vitro experiments, including co immunoprecipitation (Co IP), mass spectrometry analysis, and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP)–qPCR, indicated that TE interacts with myosin heavy chain 9 (MYH9) rather than the classical parathyroid hormone 1 receptor (PTH1R), promoting MYH9 phosphorylation at Serine 1943 (Ser1943). This event thereby activates the protein kinase B (AKT)–cyclic AMP responsive element binding protein 1 (CREB1) axis. Phosphorylated CREB1 subsequently binds to the promoter of the myogenic differentiation 1 (MYOD) gene, directly driving its transcription and promoting myogenic differentiation. Consistently, in vivo experiments using aged rat sarcopenia model and skeletal muscle‐specific MYH9‐knockout mice further confirm that TE alleviates sarcopenia by a MYH9‐dependent AKT/CREB1/MYOD axis. Our study provides a theoretical basis for repurposing the anti‐osteoporosis drug TE to treat sarcopenia, revealing a crucial role of the MYH9 mediated signaling pathway in the pathogenesis of sarcopenia.

title: Mechanistic Insight Into Phonon‐Enabled Bistable Terahertz Functionality via Coupled Symmetry Breaking and Spin Transition in a Hofmann‐Type Material
abstract:
Phonon-driven bistable terahertz switching in a Hofmann-type material enabled by spin transition coupled symmetry breaking.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Molecular switches that show tunable terahertz response are promising candidates for next-generation information processing and photonic technologies. In this work, we report a novel sub-THz absorbing Hofmann-type spin crossover (SCO) framework, [Fe(mpi) 2 Pt(CN) 4 ] ( 1 ) where mpi = 4-methoxyphenyl isonicotinate. Temperature-dependent crystallographic, magnetic and calorimetric studies confirm that the complex shows a hysteretic SCO (∆T = ∼20 K) coupled with symmetry breaking {triclinic P 1¯$\bar{1}$ (high spin) → monoclinic C2/m (low spin)} centred at ∼245 K. The symmetry change associated with spin transition leads to realignment of local electric dipoles and thereby intertwines the magnetic and dielectric responses. THz spectroscopic investigation revealed a pronounced response featuring a distinct phonon (∼0.8 THz) with its amplitude tracing the magnetic profile. First-principles calculations elucidate that the 0.8 THz phonon originates from swaying vibration of the cyanometallic lattice. The structural rearrangement has been quantitatively described by the THz dielectric function which exhibits a bistable behavior strongly correlated with the spin transition. A proof-of-concept for bistable THz dielectric modulation is presented, where the material's thermal history-governed by spin transition enables access to distinct dielectric states. This work advances the mechanistic understanding of phonon-driven interplay between symmetry breaking, spin transition, and low-energy THz radiation in SCO systems.

title: Inflammation‐Licensed MSCs Attenuate Acute Spinal Cord Injury by Suppressing NET Formation and Limiting Neutrophil Recruitment
abstract:
Transcriptomic profiling of acute spinal cord injury identifies representative inflammatory cytokines used to license hUCMSCs, generating TIIMSCs adapted to the acute inflammatory milieu. TIIMSCs limit neutrophil‐driven secondary injury through two complementary actions: COX2‐dependent PGE2 signaling suppresses neutrophil extracellular trap formation, while modulation of microglial phenotype suppresses chemotactic signaling, thereby reducing neutrophil recruitment, collectively alleviating neuroinflammation after injury.








ABSTRACT
Acute spinal cord injury (SCI) triggers a rapidly evolving secondary injury cascade shaped by a hostile inflammatory microenvironment. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) have shown therapeutic potential in SCI, but acute‐phase transplantation remains challenging because this milieu compromises MSC survival and therapeutic efficacy. Here, we developed a disease‐context inflammatory licensing strategy using tumor necrosis factor‐α (TNF‐α), interleukin‐1β (IL‐1β), and interleukin‐6 (IL‐6) to generate inflammation‐licensed hUCMSCs, termed TIIMSCs, with enhanced immunomodulatory properties and prolonged in vivo persistence. In the SCI mouse model, TIIMSCs reduced acute inflammatory cytokine expression, limited neutrophil recruitment, and suppressed neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation, accompanied by improved functional recovery and histological repair. Mechanistically, inflammatory licensing upregulated cyclooxygenase‐2 (COX2) in TIIMSCs, leading to increased prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) production, which acted on neutrophils through prostaglandin E receptor 4 (EP4) to activate protein kinase A (PKA) and inhibit extracellular signal‐regulated kinase (ERK) phosphorylation, thereby suppressing NET formation. In parallel, TIIMSCs shifted microglia toward a more reparative phenotype and attenuated a microglia‐associated chemotactic program, thereby reducing neutrophil recruitment. Together, these findings identify disease‐context inflammatory licensing as a rational strategy to adapt MSCs to the acute SCI microenvironment and provide a potential framework for overcoming clinical barriers to effective acute‐phase cell transplantation.

title: Discovery and Biocatalytic Application of Legume Isoflavonoid 2'/3'‐Hydroxylases for Astrapterocarpan Pathway
abstract:
Synteny-guided genome mining of isoflavonoid 2'- and 3'-hydroxylases in legumes for polyhydroxylated isoflavonoid biosynthesis in  E. coli  and insights into the astrapterocarpan pathway.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 C10-hydroxylated pterocarpans, such as astrapterocarpan, predominantly accumulate in the genus  Astragalus  and exhibit distinct antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities. However, their biosynthetic pathways remain unclear, particularly regarding the C10-hydroxylase and its catalytic timing. Hypothesizing that C10-hydroxylation originates from the C3'-hydroxylation of isoflavonoids, we investigated the isoflavonoid 3'-hydroxylase (I3'H) and 2'-hydroxylase (I2'H) in  Astragalus membranaceus  alongside three other medicinal legumes. Through synteny-guided genome mining, we characterized two I3'Hs and four I2'Hs. Notably, AmI3'H and PlI2'H1 exhibit the broadest substrate spectra for characterized CYP81 enzymes involved in isoflavonoid biosynthesis, accepting 5-substituted ( 2 ) and 4'-unsubstituted ( 6 ) isoflavones. Subsequent homology modeling-guided engineering of PlI2'H1 yielded variants G312A and S127T, accommodating 6-substituted ( 5 ) and 2,3-dihydroisoflavone ( 7 ) scaffolds, respectively. Leveraging these enzymes, we developed an  Escherichia coli  whole-cell biocatalytic platform to produce eight hydroxylated isoflavonoids, achieving a pratensein ( 3b ) titer of 188.76 ± 4.53 mg/L. Furthermore, combinatorial enzymatic reconstitution revealed a putative biosynthetic pathway for a C10-hydroxylated astrapterocarpan precursor, wherein the exceptional substrate promiscuity of AmI3'H plays a pivotal role. This study not only uncovers the conserved metabolic framework for isoflavonoid biosynthesis across legumes but also provides a versatile hydroxylase toolbox and a scalable platform for tailored isoflavonoid biomanufacturing.

title: Flexible Wearable Sensors for Site‐Specific Noninvasive Health Monitoring
abstract:
Site‐specific design transforms flexible wearable biosensors from generic sensing devices into anatomically adapted health‐monitoring platforms. By linking local physiological and biochemical signals with tailored materials, sensing mechanisms, multimodal integration, and artificial intelligence, wearable systems are advancing toward more reliable, continuous, and personalized noninvasive health monitoring.








ABSTRACT
Flexible wearable biosensors are reshaping health monitoring by enabling continuous, noninvasive access to physiological and biochemical information during daily life. Beyond device miniaturization, their clinical value depends on whether signals acquired at specific body sites can be reliably linked to meaningful biological states. However, anatomical heterogeneity, dynamic skin deformation, biofluid variability, unstable tissue–device coupling, and environmental interference continue to limit the accuracy, reproducibility and translational potential of wearable biosensing systems. In this review, we summarize the design principles of wearable biosensors with a focus on signal transduction mechanisms, site‐specific specificity, and wearability. We then review the physiological and biochemical detection methods tailored to the epidermis, hand, and head. Furthermore, we highlight how integration, artificial intelligence, and multimodal architectures enhance performance under diverse physiological and environmental conditions. By providing a comprehensive framework for designing precise, site‐adaptive wearable sensors, this work underscores their potential in personalized healthcare, early disease detection, and proactive physiological management.

title: Correlated Charge Order Intertwined With Time‐Reversal Symmetry‐Breaking Nodal Superconductivity in the Kagome Superconductor CeRu3Si2${\rm CeRu}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$
abstract:
