CeRu3Si2${\rm CeRu}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$ uniquely combines kagome-derived Ru-d and Ce-4f flat bands with correlated charge order persisting to room temperature. It exhibits field-induced magnetism and nodal superconductivity accompanied by spontaneous internal fields, suggestive of time-reversal symmetry breaking. Across the ARu3Si2$A{\rm Ru}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$ family, superconductivity correlates positively with normal-state symmetry breaking, establishing CeRu3Si2${\rm CeRu}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$ as a distinctive platform for intertwined correlated quantum states.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Kagome materials provide a platform for exploring flat-band-driven symmetry-breaking quantum states. Here, we introduce CeRu 3 Si 2 , a kagome superconductor in which our first-principles calculations show the coexistence of Ru d$d$-orbital kagome flat bands and flat bands derived from Ce4+4f${\rm Ce}^{4+} 4f$-states. X-ray diffraction reveals a dominant 1/2 charge order with a much weaker 1/3 component persisting up to room temperature. Deep within the charge-ordered state, magnetoresistance emerges below 80 K and strengthens further below 30 K. Zero-field muon spin-rotation measurements show no time-reversal symmetry (TRS) breaking in the normal state, in contrast to LaRu3Si2${\rm LaRu}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$ and YRu3Si2${\rm YRu}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$. However, an applied magnetic field induces weak magnetism. Across the ARu3Si2$A{\rm Ru}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$ family (A$A$=La, Y, Ce), the superconducting transition temperature Tc$T_{\rm c}$ scales linearly with the onset temperature of normal-state TRS breaking TTRSB$T_{\rm {TRSB}}$ and the magnitude of the field-induced magnetic response, revealing a direct positive correlation between normal-state symmetry breaking and superconductivity. Furthermore, we identify that CeRu3Si2${\rm CeRu}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$ is the first 132-type kagome compound to host nodal superconductivity together with spontaneous internal magnetic fields, suggestive of intrinsic TRS breaking in the superconducting state. These results establish CeRu3Si2${\rm CeRu}_{3}{\rm Si}_{2}$ as a unique platform where kagome-derived d$d$- and f$f$-electron flat bands coexist with rich hierarchy of electronic orders.

title: Palmitoylation of DLAT Licenses Cuproptosis by Antagonizing SYVN1‐Dependent Ubiquitination in Colorectal Cancer
abstract:
The molecular determinants that set the threshold for cuproptosis execution remain largely unexplored. We discover a lipid‐based protective switch: ZDHHC1 attaches a palmitate “shield” to the cuproptosis executioner DLAT, blocking its degradation by SYVN1. Copper itself activates TFE3 to drive ZDHHC1 production, forming a feedforward loop. AAV delivery of ZDHHC1 overcomes this degradation barrier, sensitizing colorectal PDX tumors to cuproptosis.








ABSTRACT
Cuproptosis is a copper‐dependent form of cell death with therapeutic potential in cancer; yet the mechanisms controlling cellular susceptibility to this process remain poorly understood. Here, through a PTM inhibitor screen in colorectal cancer (CRC), we identify S‐palmitoylation as a required determinant of cuproptosis sensitivity and DLAT as the principal substrate, modified at the conserved C488 residue. Palmitoylation at C488 stabilizes DLAT by preventing its proteasomal degradation. Mechanistically, this lipidation sterically blocks the E3 ubiquitin ligase SYVN1 from catalyzing K48‐linked polyubiquitination of DLAT. We identify ZDHHC1 as the cognate palmitoyltransferase for DLAT and show that copper stress stabilizes TFE3, which then translocates to the nucleus and directly activates ZDHHC1 transcription by binding its promoter. Therapeutically, AAV‐mediated ZDHHC1 delivery sensitizes patient‐derived xenograft (PDX) tumors to the copper ionophore elesclomol, suppressing tumor growth. Our findings reveal a copper‐sensing signaling cascade—from TFE3 through ZDHHC1 to DLAT palmitoylation—that governs cuproptosis vulnerability, and establish ZDHHC1‐mediated lipidation as a therapeutic target for sensitizing CRC to copper‐based therapies.

title: AI‐Driven Discovery of Nodakenin as a Novel Molecular Glue Targeting the TRIM28‐NR4A1‐LCN2 Axis to Induce Ferroptosis in Melanoma
abstract:
AI‐driven screening identifies nodakenin as a molecular glue that promotes TRIM28‐dependent K48‐linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of NR4A1. Loss of NR4A1 suppresses LCN2 transcription, disrupts iron homeostasis, and triggers ferroptosis. This mechanism links targeted protein degradation to reduced melanoma growth, liver metastasis, and patient‐derived organoid viability, revealing a potential therapeutic vulnerability in melanoma.








ABSTRACT
Melanoma remains a malignancy requiring novel interventions. While triggering ferroptosis has emerged as a promising anti‐tumor strategy, the targetable molecular vulnerabilities governing this process remain incompletely understood. Here, through artificial intelligence (AI)‐driven virtual screening, we identified the coumarin derivative Nodakenin (NK) as a potent inhibitor of nuclear receptor subfamily 4 group A member 1 (NR4A1), an orphan nuclear receptor highly expressed in malignant melanoma cells. Transcriptomic, biochemical, and structural analyses revealed that NK triggers ferroptosis in melanoma cells. Mechanistically, NK functions as a molecular glue that enforces proximity between NR4A1 and the E3 ubiquitin ligase tripartite motif‐containing protein 28 (TRIM28). This recruitment promotes K48‐linked polyubiquitination of NR4A1 at the K381 residue, leading to its rapid proteasomal degradation. Consequently, the targeted depletion of NR4A1 abolishes its transcriptional transactivation of the defense gene the defense gene lipocalin 2 (LCN2), resulting in intracellular free iron overload, lipid reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, and lethal ferroptosis. Crucially, NK dramatically suppresses tumor growth and liver metastasis in vivo and disrupts the viability of patient‐derived organoids (PDOs), with these therapeutic efficacies being dependent on the ferroptosis pathway. Collectively, this study identifies a novel molecular glue targeting NR4A1 and unveils the TRIM28/NR4A1/LCN2 axis as a promising therapeutic vulnerability for melanoma.

title: An Anti‐Adhesive Hydrogel Delivering Ginger‐Derived Exosome‐Like Nanoparticles Reshapes the Neuroinflammatory Microenvironment After Traumatic Brain Injury
abstract:
CG‐GELNs, an anti‐adhesive hydrogel incorporating ginger‐derived exosome‐like nanoparticles (GELNs), is developed for traumatic brain injury (TBI). By reducing brain–skull adhesion and enabling sustained local GELNs delivery, CG‐GELNs restores blood–brain barrier integrity, suppresses microglial inflammation via the microRNA‐396 (miR‐396)/secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1) axis, reduces reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, preserves synaptic function, and promotes behavioral recovery after TBI.








ABSTRACT
Traumatic brain injury (TBI) triggers secondary injury involving neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction, highlighting the need for multi‐target therapies. Ginger‐derived exosome‐like nanoparticles (GELNs) offer multi‐target therapeutic potential but are limited by insufficient local retention and rapid clearance. TBI‐induced brain‐skull adhesion may further aggravate the pathological environment. To address these limitations, an anti‐adhesive hydrogel (CG) composed of methacrylated chondroitin sulfate and 2‐methacryloyloxyethyl phosphorylcholine is loaded with GELNs to form CG‐GELNs. CG‐GELNs attenuates pathological brain‐skull adhesion and provides greater behavioral benefits than free GELNs, including reduced anxiety‐like behavior, improved social novelty discrimination, and enhanced spatial memory. At the pathological level, CG‐GELNs confers coordinated protection against secondary injury by preserving blood‐brain barrier integrity, suppressing pro‐inflammatory responses, mitigating mitochondrial damage and oxidative stress, and ultimately preserving synaptic function. Mechanistically, GELNs‐associated microRNA‐396 (miR‐396) suppresses secreted phosphoprotein 1 (SPP1) expression, and functional rescue experiments support the contribution of this miR‐396/SPP1 axis to the anti‐inflammatory effects of GELNs in microglial cells. Overall, CG‐GELNs simultaneously improves localized delivery of GELNs, attenuates pathological brain–skull adhesion, and suppresses neuroinflammation, offering a potentially translatable therapeutic platform for remodeling the neuroinflammatory microenvironment and promoting neurological recovery after TBI.

title: Biomimetic Carbonate Aerogel via γ‐Dicalcium Silicate Mineralization for Concurrent CO2 Sequestration and All‐Season Building Thermoregulation
abstract:
A biomimetic carbonate aerogel fabricated from γ-C 2 S via carbonation-directed assembly achieves concurrent CO 2  sequestration (334 mg g − 
 1 ), solar reflectance of 93.2%, and ultra-low thermal conductivity (0.046 W m −1  K −1 ). EnergyPlus simulations across 30 cities demonstrate 7.68%–67.75% annual building energy savings.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The decarbonization of the built environment demands strategies that simultaneously reduce operational energy and sequester atmospheric CO 2 , yet these functions remain decoupled in existing construction materials. Here, we demonstrate a biomimetic carbonate aerogel fabricated from γ-dicalcium silicate (γ-C 2 S)—a model system representative of carbonation-reactive calcium silicate phases in alkaline industrial wastes—via carbonation-directed assembly. In situ mineralization of γ-C 2 S under pressurized CO 2  (0.3 MPa, 75% RH, 24 h) sequesters 334 mg CO 2  g −1  whilst generating a hierarchical CaCO 3  nano-array architecture that functions as a broadband photonic platform. The resulting aerogel achieves a solar reflectance of 93.2% and mid-infrared emittance of 94.5%, delivering a daytime net cooling power of 76.3 W m −2 . An ultra-low thermal conductivity of 0.046 W m −1  K −1  mitigates the indoor overcooling impact in winter through superior envelope insulation. The inorganic-dominated composition confers excellent flame resistance under direct flame exposure exceeding 7 min and a 1476.5% carbonation-induced increase in compressive strength. EnergyPlus simulations across 30 cities spanning all Köppen-Geiger climate zones demonstrate annual building energy savings of 7.68%–67.75%. These results establish carbonation-directed assembly as a proof-of-concept materials strategy for coupling CO 2  mineralization with radiative and conductive thermal management.

title: Micro/Nanoplastics: Structural Transformations, Reactivity Migration, and Emerging Separation Strategies
abstract:
Micro/nanoplastics undergo complex environmental transformations involving aggregation, morphological evolution, surface modification, reactivity, and transport. This review critically examines their separation, detection, quantification, toxicological responses, and characterization, highlighting size‐, shape‐, and chemistry‐dependent selectivity. Emerging 3D manufacturing, recycling strategies, machine learning, and regulatory initiatives are discussed toward improved detection and sustainable management of plastic pollution.








ABSTRACT
Micro/nano plastics are ubiquitous in water, soil, and air, posing increasing risks to ecosystems. To mitigate their hazardous impact, it becomes imperative to understand how aggregation, morphology, surface chemistry, reactivity, and transport mechanisms evolve during environmental aging. Despite numerous studies on the occurrence and transport of microplastics, an integrated review of their structural transformation, reactivity, migration, and the selectivity of separation methods remains limited. Herein, we critically review recent advances in the separation and quantification of micro/nanoplastics (MNPs), focusing on their thermodynamic and kinetic properties, toxicological responses, aggregation phenomena, and surface adhesive characteristics. We examine how size, shape, and chemical composition govern the selectivity of separation methods and compare these methods with respect to their advantages and limitations. Emerging 3D manufacturing strategies for recycling and valorizing micro/nano plastic waste are also discussed as potential pathways for circular management. Furthermore, we summarize the state‐of‐the‐art characterization techniques, including spectroscopy, microscopy, thermal analysis, and machine learning, for the detection and quantification of MNPs. We also provide an overview of national and international initiatives to mitigate plastic pollution through regulation and technological innovation. Finally, we outline challenges and propose potential solutions to advance research and the sustainable management of plastic particulates.

title: Non‐Reciprocal Thermal Metamaterials With Programmable Functionality
abstract:
A non‐reciprocal thermal metamaterial is developed based on thermomechanically actuated bilayer structures. Direction‐dependent deformation reconfigures the interfacial contact state, producing distinct heat‐transfer responses under opposite thermal biases. The resulting thermal non‐reciprocity enables mechanically configurable thermal encoding and thermally gated electrical logic, providing a versatile platform for adaptive thermal management and thermal information processing.








ABSTRACT
Non‐reciprocal thermal transport provides a promising route toward active and multifunctional heat regulation, yet practical implementations are often limited by stringent material requirements and reliance on external energy inputs. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a class of non‐reciprocal thermal metamaterials (NTMs) that exploit thermally induced mechanical deformation to achieve direction‐dependent heat transfer. By leveraging the thermal expansion mismatch in bilayer beams, we constructed a thermally driven “on–off” switching mechanism that dynamically reconfigures the interfacial contact state. This mechanism enables the heat transfer pathway to switch between direct solid‐solid conduction and gap‐mediated heat transfer. Such deformation‐induced asymmetry gives rise to pronounced non‐reciprocity without needing phase‐change materials or spatiotemporal modulation. The deformation‐induced switching behavior can be tuned through material selection, geometry parameters, and thermal bias. Experiments further confirmed a pronounced direction‐dependent thermal response, where heat transfer in the forward direction were significantly enhanced relative to the reverse direction. By deliberately arranging the orientations of individual NTMs, we further demonstrate functionalities like mechanically reconfigurable thermal encoding and thermally gated electrical logic. These results establish a scalable and energy‐efficient strategy for non‐reciprocal thermal control using readily available materials, opening new opportunities for thermal management, information processing, and multifunctional metamaterial design.

title: Bimetallic Sites Cu/Co Alloy Targeting Quorum Sensing Reversing MRSA Ciprofloxacin Susceptibility
abstract:
Cu-bearing cobalt-based (CoCrMo-Cu) alloys with bimetallic active sites (Cu/Co) are designed to effectively restore MRSA sensitivity to ciprofloxacin, the most representative resistant antibiotic against MRSA. By combining CoCrMo-Cu with ciprofloxacin, proposing a synergistic dual-action platform addressing methicillin-resistant  Staphylococcus aureus  (MRSA)-infected osteomyelitis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The escalating global prevalence of infections caused by resistant pathogens emerge as a critical public health crisis, especially in implants. It underscores urgent imperative to advance novel and efficacious strategies combating antimicrobial resistance. Herein, Cu-bearing cobalt-based (CoCrMo-Cu) alloys with bimetallic active sites (Cu/Co) are designed to effectively restore methicillin-resistant  Staphylococcus aureus  (MRSA) sensitivity to ciprofloxacin, the most representative resistant antibiotic against MRSA. By combining CoCrMo-Cu with ciprofloxacin, proposing a synergistic dual-action platform addressing MRSA-infected osteomyelitis. Results show that CoCrMo-Cu exhibit anti-infection through two-stage process: disrupting biofilm, the extrinsic physical resistance barrier. Specifically, real-time bacterial motility trajectories reveal CoCrMo-Cu disrupt bacterial initial exploration behaviors, inhibiting biofilm development. Second, inhibiting intrinsic resistance barrier: efflux systems, enhancing effectiveness of antibiotics. Such comprehensive anti-infective mechanism is attributed to quorum quenching through satisfactory reactive oxygen species generation from bimetallic active sites. Eventually, MRSA resistance to ciprofloxacin is reversed and it results in an 87.5% reduction of minimum inhibitory concentration for ciprofloxacin. CoCrMo-Cu combining with ciprofloxacin significantly eradicates MRSA-infected osteomyelitis in vivo. Unlike stop-gap solutions focus on developing novel antibiotics, we prioritize restoring MRSA susceptibility to conventional antibiotics, providing a long-term strategy addressing resistant bacterial infection with enhanced sustainability.

title: The Lysine Metabolism–Protein Modification Axis in Tumor Immunity
abstract:
Dysregulated metabolism‐modification coupling & spatiotemporal imbalance. Lysine is metabolized through the saccharopine and pipecolic acid pathways. Perturbed metabolic flux disrupts lysine post‐translational modifications. This spatiotemporal imbalance induces immune cell exhaustion, drives tumor immune evasion and modulates dynamic homeostasis of lysine pool in the tumor microenvironment. Solid arrows represent experimentally validated pathways, and dashed arrows denote hypothetical pathways.








ABSTRACT
The metabolic‐epigenetic‐immune tripartite regulatory network within the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) serves as a central hub governing tumor immune evasion and therapeutic response. Long regarded merely as an essential nutritional substrate, lysine has now emerged as a pivotal signaling molecule bridging metabolic reprogramming, protein post‐translational modifications (PTMs), and immune cell fate determination. Tumor cells remodel immune cell function and foster an immunosuppressive microenvironment via three coordinated mechanisms: hijacking lysine transport, rewiring lysine catabolic metabolism, and disrupting acylation and methylation modifications at lysine residues. Herein, we propose a novel preclinical theoretical model coined “lysimetaboptenation,” which we define as lysine metabolism‐modification‐coupled T cell exhaustion. This review systematically delineates lysine transmembrane transport, rewired lysine catabolism, and the lysine‐centered PTM regulatory network, alongside the modulatory mechanisms underlying bidirectional crosstalk between tumor cells and immune cells. We further clarify the correlations between aberrant lysine axis signaling and patient prognosis, immunotherapeutic efficacy, and treatment resistance. Additionally, we summarize translational strategies targeting lysine transporters, catabolic enzymes, lysine PTM machinery, precision nutritional interventions, and combinatorial immunometabolic regimens. Finally, we highlight outstanding scientific questions, technical bottlenecks, and cutting‐edge research frontiers, aiming to furnish theoretical frameworks and innovative avenues for overcoming resistance to immunotherapy and developing precision combinatorial metabolome‐immunotherapy regimens.

title: TFAP2‐Dependent Super‐Enhancer Activation of PAX3 Drives Chondrogenic Fate in the Cranial Neural Crest
abstract:
A dominant element within the  pax3a -SE recruited Tfap2a and Tfap2c to assemble transcriptional condensates that amplify  pax3a  transcriptional activity.  Pax3a  directly activated the  tgfb1a  promoter to sustain TGF-β signaling to promote chondrogenesis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Defects in craniofacial cartilage development underlie a substantial proportion of severe human congenital birth defects. Cranial neural crest cells (CNCCs) generate the majority of craniofacial mesenchyme, yet how lineage-specific cis-regulatory programs couple progenitor homeostasis to chondrogenic fate, and how their disruption underlies human craniofacial malformations, remain poorly understood. Here, we found that CNCC super-enhancers (SEs) were significant reservoirs of regulatory genetic variants, enriched for craniofacial malformation-associated variants and functional expression and splicing quantitative trait loci. Pharmacological inhibition of BET bromodomains impaired CNCC proliferation and induced craniofacial abnormalities. By constructing a conserved CNCC-SE-associated gene set, we identified  PAX3  as a key SE-driven regulator of craniofacial development. Functionally, a dominant element within the  pax3a -SE recruited Tfap2a and Tfap2c. The condensate-like behavior of these transcription factors is required for normal  pax3a  transcription. Single-cell RNA sequencing of CNCCs isolated from  pax3a -deficient zebrafish revealed a depletion of ectomesenchymal progenitors and blunted chondrogenic trajectories leading to cartilage hypoplasia. Mechanistically,  Pax3a  directly activated the  tgfb1a  promoter to sustain TGF-β signaling and promote chondrogenesis, whereas restoration of  tgfb1a  partially rescued craniofacial defects in  pax3a -deficient embryos. Collectively, our findings define a conserved SE– PAX3 –TGF-β regulatory axis in CNCCs and provide a mechanistic framework linking enhancer dysregulation to craniofacial malformation.

title: Cationic Potential‐Guided Li/K Co‐Doping Enables Fast‐Charging Layered Oxide Cathodes for Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract:
Li + /K +  co-doping tailors the local coordination and structural evolution of an O3-type layered oxide cathode for sodium-ion batteries. Neutron diffraction reveals preferential Li +  occupation in transition-metal layers and K +  occupation in Na layers. Structural models illustrate the evolution of the layered framework during charging to 4.2 V. Complementary CI-NEB calculations indicate facilitated Na +  migration, linking Li + /K +  co-doping with improved structural reversibility and ion transport for fast-charging sodium-ion batteries.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Developing O3-type layered oxide cathodes combining fast charging, high capacity, and structural stability remains challenging for sodium-ion batteries. Here, a cationic-potential-guided Li + /K +  co-doping strategy is employed to synthesize Na 0.9 Li 0.05 K 0.05 N i0.317 Fe 0.317 Mn 0.317 O 2  (LKNFM) through a precursor-assisted solid-state ball-milling route. Neutron diffraction reveals preferential K +  occupation in alkali layers and Li +  distribution across alkali and transition-metal layers, regulating interlayer interactions and local coordination. LKNFM delivers 181.6 mAh g −1  at 0.1C and maintains 82.7 mAh g −1  after 1000 cycles at 20C, corresponding to 89.3% capacity retention. LKNFM/hard carbon full cell retains over 80% capacity after 1000 cycles. Operando XRD reveals a simplified, reversible O3↔P3 transition with reduced lattice strain. Ex situ XANES and WT-EXAFS indicate predominantly Ni/Fe-based charge compensation, while Mn mainly stabilizes the framework. DFT suggests cooperative cationic–anionic charge compensation at high voltage, while CI-NEB calculations show a reduction in the Na +  migration barrier from 1.21 to 0.80 eV along the investigated pathway. These findings highlight site-selective co-doping as a promising approach to structurally stable, fast-charging sodium-ion battery cathodes.

title: Membrane‐Embedded Antioxidant Lipids Overcome the Rapid Clearance Dilemma for Dry Eye Disease Treatment
abstract:
A membrane‐embedded antioxidant lipid (MEAL) strategy anchors α‐lipoic acid at corneal epithelial membranes, prolonging ocular‐surface retention and enabling localized reactive oxygen species (ROS) (scavenging. By establishing an antioxidant shield at the membrane interface, MEAL mitigates oxidative stress, epithelial damage, and inflammation, thereby improving ocular‐surface protection in dry eye disease.








ABSTRACT
Oxidative stress is a key driver in dry eye disease (DED), yet traditional antioxidant therapies show a mismatch between the spatiotemporal origin of oxidative damage and the distribution of antioxidants. Here, we report a membrane‐embedded antioxidant lipid (MEAL) strategy confining redox regulation activity on the cell membrane. Conjugation of α‐lipoic acid (LA) to lipid‐polyethylene glycol (PEG) amphiphiles converts a freely diffusive antioxidant into a membrane‐integrated entity providing persistent antioxidant protection. MEAL achieved prolonged ocular retention (up to 12 h) and effective suppression of lipid peroxidation and epithelial damage in a DED model. By covalently integrating LA with lipid‐PEG anchors, MEAL combines antioxidant activity, membrane‐embedding capacity, and prolonged ocular retention without requiring an additional carrier system. This molecular design provides a strategy for spatially localized and sustained antioxidant protection on the ocular surface.

title: MACE4IRmol: An Uncertainty‐Aware Foundation Model for Molecular Infrared Spectroscopy
abstract:
Trained on a chemically diverse quantum-chemical database, MACE4IRmol enables rapid and accurate infrared spectra prediction for molecules spanning broad chemical space, demonstrating robust transferability across multiple chemical families.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have shown significant promise in predicting infrared spectra with high fidelity. However, the absence of general-purpose MLIPs that simultaneously span broad chemical diversity and provide reliable uncertainty estimates has limited their wider applicability. In this work, we introduce  MACE4IRmol , an uncertainty-aware foundation model ensemble built on the  MACE  architecture.  MACE4IRmol  is trained on ∼$\sim$16 million molecular geometries and the corresponding density-functional theory (DFT) energies, forces, and dipole moments from the QCML dataset. The training data encompasses approximately 80 elements and a diverse set of molecules, including organic and inorganic compounds, and metal complexes. Importantly,  MACE4IRmol  is formulated as an ensemble of models to enable uncertainty quantification, which helps improve robustness in chemically diverse systems. Within this ensemble, separate models are trained with and without explicit dispersion corrections, allowing systematic assessment of van der Waals effects.  MACE4IRmol  delivers accurate predictions of energies, forces, dipole moments, and infrared spectra at a fraction of the computational cost of DFT, while enabling the explicit inclusion of nuclear quantum effects in infrared spectrum simulations. By combining generality, accuracy, efficiency, fine-tuning and uncertainty estimation,  MACE4IRmol  opens the door to rapid and reliable infrared spectra prediction for complex and diverse molecular systems.

title: Developmentally Informed Cell‐State Heterogeneity Reveals Targetable Cell‐State Plasticity in Multiple Myeloma
abstract:
A developmental reference map of normal plasma cells reveals that multiple myeloma is organized along a conserved differentiation continuum. LILRB4 identifies a subfraction of a primitive population that exhibits stem-like properties and unidirectionally generates more mature LILRB4 −  progeny. Targeting the EP300-TBX2 axis drives this primitive-to-mature transition, sensitizing LILRB4 +  myeloma cells to bortezomib.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Understanding the ontogeny of cancer in reference to parallel normal developmental processes has offered crucial insights into the biology and therapeutic discovery of many malignancies. However, this framework is significantly lacking for multiple myeloma (MM). Here, we constructed a malignant plasma cell (mPC) cell-state model for MM informed by normal plasma cell (nPC) development and demonstrated its clinical relevance. Applying this model, we identified developmentally primitive mPC cell states marked by LILRB4 expression, characterized by incomplete immunoglobulin production and enriched for stemness and therapeutic resistance. Single-cell colony assays revealed the unique capacity of LILRB4 +  MM cells to give rise to LILRB4 −  descendants. Xenograft assays confirmed the heightened disease-initiating capacity of LILRB4 +  MM cells. Integrative drug screening and molecular interrogation identified the EP300/TBX2 axis as a selective epigenetic vulnerability of the LILRB4 +  cell state that can be targeted by EP300 inhibitors. Collectively, our study systematically delineates previously underappreciated developmental heterogeneity in MM, suggesting that intratumoral heterogeneity may reflect a structured developmental process rather than a purely random phenomenon. This framework further enables the discovery of cell-state-specific vulnerabilities.

title: Ferroelectric Oxide–MOF Core–Shell Architectures for Coupled Adsorption and Ultrasound‐Driven Pollutant Removal
abstract:
A versatile core–shell synthesis strategy combines functional metal oxides with porous metal–organic framework (MOF) shells while preserving the properties of the oxide core. BaTiO 3  and TiO 2  cores are combined with ZIF-8 and ZIF-67 shells, while adsorption and ultrasound-driven transformation are systematically separated to reveal the interplay between ultrasound-driven adsorption and piezocatalytic degradation of methyl orange.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Metal oxide–metal–organic framework (MOF) core–shell architectures offer a promising strategy to enhance the surface area of inorganic oxides while preserving their intrinsic functionality. Here, we report a generalizable sequential solvothermal approach for the controlled fabrication of well-defined metal oxide–MOF core–shell composites with tunable shell thickness. Using BaTiO 3  as a representative ferroelectric oxide and TiO 2  as a non-ferroelectric benchmark, together with ZIF-8 and ZIF-67 as porous MOF shells, successive growth cycles enable uniform coating and systematic tuning of MOF loading, leading to increased surface area across multiple oxide–MOF combinations. Importantly, the MOF shell preserves the intrinsic properties of the oxide core, including the piezoelectric response of BaTiO 3 . As a proof of concept, BaTiO 3 –ZIF-8 was evaluated for methyl orange removal under ultrasonic exposure. The composite exhibited rapid adsorption, achieving ∼57% removal within 10 min of stirring and ∼62% total removal after sonication. TiO 2 -based controls revealed that the removal arises from coupled adsorption and ultrasound-driven degradation processes, including sono- and piezocatalytic effects highlighting the importance of disentangling the mechanisms responsible for pollutant removal. Although ZIF-8 exhibits limited stability under prolonged sonication, the modular synthesis enables integration of more robust MOFs or conversion into carbon–metal oxide derivatives with improved stability and added functionality.

title: Raman Scattering of Surface Phonon Polaritons Under Nanoscale Confinement: The Role of Structure and Environment
abstract:
Nanoscale confinement of surface phonon polaritons in polar nanocrystals enables structure‐ and environment‐sensitive Raman scattering, providing optical access to mid‐infrared polaritonic responses through visible‐light spectroscopy. The emergence, self‐hybridization, and ultrathin‐film control of these modes establish polar nanocrystals as a versatile platform for mid‐infrared sensing and nanoscale light‐matter engineering.








ABSTRACT
Strong light–matter coupling in polar materials gives rise to phonon polaritons—hybrid quasiparticles with mixed photonic and vibrational character. Here, we show that polar nanocrystals exhibit Raman scattering that depends sensitively on their structure and electromagnetic environment. This spectral dispersion enables refractive index sensing in the mid‐infrared via visible‐wavelength Raman spectroscopy. Importantly, Raman scattering emerges only under nanoscale confinement of surface phonon polaritons, within a particle size range of ∼$\sim$ 40–400 nm, bounded by volume limitations at smaller sizes and polariton coherence constraints at larger scales. In optimal structures, self‐hybridization arises between localized phonon modes and surface phonon polaritons hosted by the same nanoparticle. Finally, we show that depositing only a few nanometers of alumina (∼10−4$\sim 10^{-4}$ of the free‐space wavelength) enables tuning and complete suppression of surface phonon polaritons in this system, as probed by Raman scattering. Our findings establish polar nanocrystal Raman spectroscopy as a versatile probe of mid‐infrared polaritonics and open routes to optical sensing inaccessible to surface‐ and tip‐enhanced Raman scattering as well as noble‐metal and graphene plasmonic platforms.

title: Elevated ATP‐Citrate Lyase Links Hyperglycemic Metabolism to Maternal Diabetes‐Induced Neural Tube Defects
abstract:
Maternal diabetes induces neural tube defects (NTDs) primarily through excessive apoptosis. Using mouse models and human samples, we identify ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY) as a metabolic–epigenetic link between hyperglycemia and neural tube malformation. ACLY-mediated elevation of acetyl-CoA increases H3K27 acetylation (H3K27ac) and likely promotes TXNIP-mediated apoptosis. Notably, hydroxycitric acid (HCA) supplementation suppresses this pathway and reduces NTDs, providing proof of concept for a potential metabolic intervention. 

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The pathogenesis of neural tube defects (NTDs) precipitated by maternal diabetes mellitus (DM) encompasses a cascade of intricate cellular processes, prominently featuring excessive apoptosis. The critical metabolic mediators bridging hyperglycemic metabolism to apoptotic pathways remain unidentified, particularly in human contexts. Elevated expression of ATP-citrate lyase (ACLY), a metabolic enzyme catalyzing the synthesis of acetyl-CoA from glucose, was discerned in cranial neural tube exposed to maternal diabetes. Inhibition of ACLY effectively normalized hyperglycemia-induced augmented levels of acetyl-CoA and histone H3 lysine 27 acetylation (H3K27ac). ACLY inhibitor hydroxycitric acid (HCA) mitigated the elevated acetyl-CoA and H3K27ac levels and reduced the incidence of NTDs caused by maternal diabetes. Integrated analyses of H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation (CHIP)-seq and RNA-seq data unveiled a correlation between aberrant H3K27ac occupancy and genome-wide gene dysregulation. The most upregulated gene, thioredoxin-interacting protein ( Txnip ) coupled with downstream phosphorylation of ASK1 and heightened apoptosis, was prominently observed in cranial neural tube with maternal diabetes, which can be attenuated by inhibition of ACLY. Corroborative evidence from human subjects with diabetes-associated NTDs substantiated this pathogenicity. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of ACLY in linking hyperglycemic metabolism to NTDs, highlighting the potential prophylactic utility of HCA supplementation in preventing maternal diabetes-induced public health issues.

title: An open long non-coding RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
abstract: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play essential roles in transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization, yet predicting their functional properties from sequence remains challenging because informative signals span both local motifs and long-range base pairing across kilobase-scale transcripts. Current RNA foundation models are restricted to short sequences and existing lncRNA prediction models narrowly focus on isolated tasks, leaving a dedicated foundation model notably absent. Here we present LncRFM, a dedicated lncRNA foundation model, supported by the LncCorpus pretraining data and the LncBench evaluation suite, which stand for a systematic framework to decode lncRNAs. For foundation model pretraining, we develop a hybrid bidirectional state-space encoder trained with a structure-guided masking strategy to effectively capture both local sequence patterns and long-range contexts. For pretraining data, we contribute over 9.6 million lncRNA sequences to assemble LncCorpus, a pretraining corpus of 24.7 million sequences. For benchmarking evaluation, we construct a comprehensive benchmark, LncBench, comprising 15 datasets and totaling over 1,010,000 sequences across 10 prediction tasks: six core lncRNA functional and annotation tasks and four structural and regulatory RNA assay tasks. Evaluated against seven RNA foundation models under a unified frozen-encoder protocol, our LncRFM achieves the state-of-the-art primary-metric scores on 11 of the 13 datasets that allow downstream adaptation. On two external generalization benchmarks evaluated without further adaptation, LncRFM matches the best structure-specialized baseline in F1 (0.141) and achieves the highest AUROC (0.962) on lncRNA contact prediction, while maintaining competitive cross-species coding-potential transfer (F1 of 0.374) under severe multi-kingdom domain shift. To benefit the scientific community, we make all datasets, source code, and pretrained models publicly available.

title: Read&Tag enables antibody-independent combinatorial and multifactorial chromatin profiling
abstract: Genome-wide chromatin profiling methods based on in situ tagmentation have expanded access to epigenomic information but generally rely on antibodies, thereby limiting their multifactorial capacity and the direct measurement of combinatorial chromatin states. Here, we introduce Read&Tag, in which engineered chromatin reader domains or intrabodies are fused directly to the Tn5 transposase to target specific chromatin features in situ. Read&Tag profiles active and repressive histone modifications, DNA methylation, and elongating RNA polymerase II, with signal amplitude increasing with target abundance and remaining robust in frozen tissue and low-input samples. Because the targeting module is a protein of defined structure and affinity, two specificities can be combined within a single complex. Tagmentation by such a dual-specificity reader requires H3K4me3 and H3K27me3 to be present together in the same chromatin fragment. The co-occurrence of both marks thus becomes a precondition of the measurement rather than an inference drawn from independently measured profiles. Combining barcoded reader-Tn5 complexes with primer-timed signal augmentation enables the measurement of four chromatin features in a single reaction. Read&Tag therefore provides a modular, antibody-independent platform for combinatorial and multifactorial profiling.

title: Remarkable Biosynthetic Diversity in the Bionectriaceae: Uncovering the genomic basis of antipathogen bioactivity of cacao fungal endophytes Clonostachys rosea and Waltergamsia zeylanica.
abstract: Cacao (Theobroma cacao) production in tropical countries is threatened by fungal diseases caused by Moniliophthora roreri and M. perniciosa. Two cacao pod endophytes from Bionectriaceae, Clonostachys rosea TCF417 and Waltergamsia zeylanica TCF400, exhibit growth antagonism towards M. roreri; however, the genetic basis underlying the bioactivity of these strains has not been addressed. Here, we aimed to identify biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) potentially associated with the antifungal bioactivity of these two strains and performed a comparative analysis with 30 publicly available Bionectriaceae genomes using BiG-SCAPE. Whole-genome sequencing using Oxford Nanopore and Illumina technologies, resulted in assemblies of 52.9 Mb (C. rosea TCF417) and 31 Mb (W. zeylanica TCF400). Genome annotation was conducted using Funannotate, and secondary metabolite BGCs were predicted using antiSMASH. The two cacao endophytes harbored 92 BGCs (C. rosea: 67; W. zeylanica: 25), indicating remarkable biosynthetic diversity. Across all 32 genomes, 1,523 BGC-containing regions were identified, most belonging to T1PKS clusters. Network-based clustering revealed 209 gene cluster families (GCFs), of which 52 corresponded to previously characterized BGCs. Conserved BGCs for antifungal compounds, including sorbicillinoids and verticillins, were identified in cacao endophytes and across Bionectriaceae. Additionally, an antifungal assay conducted here demonstrated that verticillin D from C. rosea TCF417 exhibited growth inhibition of plant pathogens Moniliophthora roreri and Mycena citricolor. With about 75% of unassigned GCFs, our results reveal a largely untapped biosynthetic repertoire in the Bionectriaceae and identify verticillin D as a candidate contributor to the antagonism of C. rosea against plant pathogens.

title: Enabling Genotyping of Low-Biomass Zebra Mussel Samples via Multi-Displacement Amplification (MDA)
abstract: Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS)-based genotyping enables population genomic studies of the history of biological invasions, allowing for inference of source populations and routes of spread. Methods for genotyping include whole genome sequencing (WGS), as well as lower-cost targeted approaches, such as microarrays, hybrid capture, or Genotyping by Sequencing (GBS). Using GBS, we previously genotyped ~2,000 adult zebra mussels collected from over 100 populations across Minnesota, the Great Lakes, and the Upper Mississippi River. The need for sufficient template DNA restricts such genotyping approaches to adult animals, while genotyping lower biomass samples, such as zebra mussel veliger larvae remains challenging. Here, we applied Multiple Displacement Amplification (MDA) to increase DNA concentration from low-biomass samples. We demonstrate that MDA yields reproducible WGS and GBS data from as little as 1 ng of starting material and genotyped single veliger larvae from MDA amplified DNA, accurately assigning them to their known source populations. Furthermore, we showed that inheritance patterns can be tracked in MDA amplified DNA from veliger larvae and demonstrated an approach for forensic genetics of juvenile zebra mussels that were found contaminating "moss balls" and sold in the aquarium pet trade. Pairing MDA with high-resolution genomic workflows overcomes biomass limitations and represents a powerful toolkit to enhance early detection, trace invasion pathways, and mitigate the spread of the invasive zebra mussel. This approach is readily generalizable to other organisms or developmental stages where limiting quantities of DNA are available.

title: EPIC2: integrating single-cell chromatin accessibility with human genetics to identify trait-relevant cell types
abstract: Summary: EPIC2 is a computational and statistical framework for prioritizing trait-relevant cellular contexts by integrating genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics with single-cell chromatin accessibility data. It accounts for linkage disequilibrium when testing for association between GWAS association strength and cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility at both SNP and regulatory-peak resolutions. The resulting P-values are combined using the Cauchy combination test. Availability and Implementation: The core workflow is implemented in R, with source code, vignettes, and reproducible test data freely available at https://github.com/LingxuanZ/EPIC2. Supplementary Information: Supplementary material accompanies this preprint.

title: Chronically stable, frequency-selective auditory brainstem stimulation via ultra-flexible penetrating electrode arrays
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79747-4  Surface auditory brainstem implants have poor spatial resolution and limited tonotopic access. Here, the authors develop a high-density, ultra-flexible penetrating array for frequency-selective cochlear nucleus stimulation and use-dependent plasticity in downstream auditory circuits.

title: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79723-y  Late spring frost can damage plant tissues and disrupt reproduction. The authors show that frost damage to leaves shortens the fruit development period, whereas damage to flowers prolongs it, with limited carry-over effects into the following year.

title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79707-y  Despite notable progress, the development of novel and efficient glycosyl radical precursors that are readily accessible, synthetically versatile, and compatible with stereoselective coupling platforms remains an ongoing challenge. Here the authors report a nickel-catalysed stereoselective denitrogenative glycosylation of redox-neutral glycosyl sulfonohydrazides via anomeric C–N bond homolysis.

title: Electrically induced glass transition of polyelectrolyte complexes enables kinetic ionic diodes
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79559-6  The glass transition induces changes in material properties, transforming a rigid glass into a soft rubber. Here the authors demonstrate an electrically induced glass transition in a polyelectrolyte complex, sandwiched between two oppositely charged ionoelastomers and applying time-temperature-salt superposition principle.

title: The genetic and proteomic determinants of pediatric stature development and their link to adult height and type 2 diabetes
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79465-x  Childhood growth reflects complex genetic and biological processes, but their developmental timing is not fully understood. Here, the authors identify stage‑specific genetic and proteomic influences on growth from infancy through childhood, and reveal links between early growth patterns and later type 2 diabetes risk.

title: A quantitative deep-learning-based framework reveals a continuum of chromatin sensitivities across transcription factors
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79404-w  The authors develop a deep-learning-based framework revealing that TF binding sensitivity to chromatin is a continuum rather than a binary feature, and that binding patterns can be explained by a mixture of hierarchical and cooperative mechanisms.

title: Benzoxaboroles target CPSF3 for degradation through a SUMO-dependent pathway in trypanosomes
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79400-0  Benzoxaborole drugs, such as acoziborole, target CPSF3 and mRNA processing in multiple parasites. Here the authors find that these drugs rapidly and specifically target trypanosome CPSF3 for degradation, in a SUMO- and proteasome-dependent manner.

title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 22 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79344-5  Here, the authors use super-resolution microscopy to show that desmin filaments extend beyond Z-lines and align with actin inside mouse skeletal muscle sarcomeres, where they help support force generation when sarcomeres are stretched.

title: Single-base 5mC and 5hmC profiling identifies a dynamic 5hmC-to-5mC transition at gene bodies and transcription end sites during neuronal differentiation of mouse embryonic stem cells.
abstract: 5-methylcytosine (5mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) are genome-wide epigenetic modifications involved in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation. Although Enzymatic Methyl-seq (EM-seq) can enable the combined profiling of 5mC and 5hmC, Enzymatic 5hmC-seq (E5hmC-seq) can provide selective profiling of 5hmC at single-base resolution. In this context, we systematically validated E5hmC-seq using diverse genomic DNA samples. Next, we integrated E5hmC-seq with EM-seq to distinguish between 5mC and 5hmC landscapes during neuronal differentiation of mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we observed dynamic remodeling of both modifications throughout differentiation, with pronounced changes during the transition from embryoid bodies (EBs) to neural progenitor cells (NPCs), characterized by a global decrease in 5hmC accompanied by an increase in 5mC. Subsequently, differentially hydroxymethylated regions (DhMRs) exhibiting 5hmC depletion frequently showed a concurrent increase in 5mC, whereas regions gaining 5hmC displayed an opposing trend, reflecting the genome-wide relationship. Mapping these modifications to transcriptional profiles revealed an association between cytosine modification dynamics and gene expression, where transcriptional downregulation correlated with 5hmC depletion with concomitant 5mC enrichment. In summary, combined mapping of EM-seq and E5hmC-seq can decipher the dynamic interplay between 5mC and 5hmC at single-base resolution and provide insights into the relationships among cytosine modification dynamics, genomic context and transcriptional regulation during differentiation.

title: RADSuite: Improving Species-Level Identification in Microbiome Research
abstract: In the last twenty years, the microbiome has become a central focus of biomedical research, with amplicon sequencing of the 16S rRNA gene considered the industry standard for taxon identification of prokaryotes due to its cost-effectiveness. However, common target regions in 16S amplicons often do not uniquely distinguish closely related species, restricting many analyses to the genus level. Additionally, curated databases such as NCBI's 16S curated database often do not contain all intragenomic variants of the 16S gene and lack annotation of the 16S genomic composition and gene structure. To address these limitations, our team created RADSuite, a collection of tools which includes a more robust database of 16S gene copies (RADlib), an application that identifies which V regions will allow for species level identification (RADx), and a step-by-step guide for how to integrate RADlib within existing metagenomic profiling software tools. Here we demonstrate the utility of using RADSuite as a guide for designing 16S amplicon sequencing experiments. For example, RADx can be used to recommend 16S components that enable species-level resolution for most microbes of interest, even when industry-standard default amplicon choices (V3/V4) are insufficient. These findings suggest that targeted variable region selection is critical for reliable species identification. As researchers use RADSuite to improve the quality of their experiments, we anticipate improved experimental accuracy in fields of microbiome research from human health to environmental conservation.

title: MicroBioAgent: an AI agent for automated microbiome analysis
abstract: Microbiome data analysis demands customized workflows tailored to specific biological questions, sequencing modalities, and data properties. However, constructing and executing these workflows requires navigating heterogeneous software dependencies, reference databases, and multi-step parameter tuning. Here, we present MicroBioAgent, an autonomous, domain-specific agent framework that translates high-level biological queries into executable, study-specific pipelines across 16S rRNA amplicon, reference-based shotgun, and de novo assembly-based metagenomics. Rather than relying on static pipeline templates, MicroBioAgent employs a closed-loop execution architecture: it dynamically selects and runs bioinformatics tools within user-controlled environments while iteratively inspecting intermediate outputs to adapt downstream analytical decisions. Furthermore, to address the long-running nature of metagenomic computation, we introduce an asynchronous background task-management mechanism that reduces LLM token consumption by over 50% while enabling real-time plan adjustment and automated workflow resumption. We systematically evaluated MicroBioAgent across three benchmarks of increasing complexity: (1) paired amplicon and shotgun profiling of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes, (2) taxonomic and functional profiling coupled with machine-learning classification in a colorectal cancer cohort, and (3) de novo metagenomic assembly, metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) binning, and metabolic pathway reconstruction in a polyethylene degradation study. Across all benchmarks, MicroBioAgent faithfully recapitulated the primary biological findings of the original studies, exhibiting high analytical concordance despite expected tool- and database-dependent variations. In systematic robustness evaluations across 27 independent runs spanning three backbone large language models and three prompt-complexity tiers, MicroBioAgent achieved a 98.8% task completion rate and yielded highly reproducible diversity and differential-abundance estimates. MicroBioAgent establishes a scalable, adaptive paradigm for end-to-end computational microbiome research.

title: Transposable element copy number variation reveals demographic and environment-associated dynamics during apple domestication
abstract:
Background
                      Transposable elements (TEs) are major drivers of genome evolution, but the relative roles of demographic history and environmental factors in shaping TE copy number variation remain unclear, particularly in perennial crops with complex domestication histories. The cultivated apple ( Malus domestica  Borkh.) and its wild relatives provide an ideal system for investigating how demographic history, lineage differentiation, and environmental variation contribute to TE dynamics across domestication and diversification. 
                  
                     Results
                      By analyzing TE copy-number variation across 189 wild and cultivated  Malus  accessions, we find that TE variation is partitioned into two complementary components: structural TEs, whose variation tracks SNP-based population structure, and residual TEs, showing pronounced species- or geography-associated differentiation. Pangenome comparisons across five high-quality genome assemblies reveal that structural TEs have more conserved copy numbers among genomes and exhibit greater sequence divergence from consensus sequences, and show patterns consistent with older average insertion histories. Residual TEs are enriched for species-specific insertions with higher sequence identity, suggesting more recent turnover. In  Malus sylvestris , dense sampling across Europe identifies 34 residual candidate TEs whose copy numbers repeatedly covary with climatic gradients across three population subsets, although climate, geography, and ancestry are correlated across this range. These candidates are less CpG-depleted than other residual TEs, even after adjustment for TE superfamily. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      These results support a dual model of TE dynamics during apple domestication, combining demography-linked stability with lineage- and environment-associated heterogeneity. Our study provides a population-genomic framework for disentangling demographic and environmental contributions to TE variation in perennial fruit crops.

title: LmPro-Nano: a method for nanobody optimization using pretrained language and energy prediction models
abstract: Nanobodies are an important therapeutic scaffold for multiple diseases and have been shown to neutralize severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). However, optimizing affinity for a chosen antigen remains slow and expensive. Here, we present LmPro-Nano, a sequence-driven workflow coupling a pretrained nanobody language model with a structure-based binding-energy predictor and molecular dynamics. We demonstrate LmPro-Nano on 3-2A2-4 and VHH72, two nanobodies against the SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain. We find that LmPro-Nano improves antigen-binding-loop recovery by 4.37 points over a frequency reference, and for VHH72, sequence-only localization of the binding region raised the top-ten hit rate from two to seven tighter binders.

title: Using gene co-expression graph topological fingerprints to enhance pathway activity scoring via xGATE
abstract: Quantifying pathway activity in single-cell and spatial omics is error-prone when methods ignore how genes wire together. We present xGATE, a topology-aware pathway-scoring framework that reads activity from the topological fingerprints of gene co-expression graphs. xGATE summarizes graph structure into embeddings and calibrates significance against a random-subgraph null, yielding interpretable  p -values and continuous effect sizes. Across diverse omics datasets, xGATE outperforms marginal-expression and correlation-counting methods, recovering known active pathways and capturing dynamics that elude gene markers. xGATE yields mechanistic pathway readouts across tissues and platforms.

title: The PtrMYB82/PtrABF2‐PtrASMT1 module regulates melatonin biosynthesis to enhance Poncirus trifoliata drought tolerance via ABA‐dependent and ABA‐independent pathways
abstract:
SUMMARY 
 Drought stress poses a severe constraint on citrus growth and productivity, driving an urgent need to dissect drought resistance mechanisms for sustainable agriculture. Although melatonin (MT) acts as a pivotal regulator in plant abiotic stress responses, its specific role and mechanism in improving the drought resistance of trifoliate orange ( Poncirus trifoliata  L. Raf.) rootstock have not been fully resolved. In this study, we characterized a chloroplast-localized, key MT biosynthetic gene,  PtrASMT1 , which is significantly upregulated by drought, exogenous ABA, and exogenous MT. Overexpression of  PtrASMT1  enhanced drought tolerance by elevating MT levels and alleviating oxidative damage, whereas VIGS-mediated silencing increased drought sensitivity. Pharmacological treatments with CPA and exogenous MT further validated the MT-dependent function of  PtrASMT1 . Induced by dehydration and MT but not by ABA, PtrMYB82 directly binds to the  PtrASMT1  promoter and activates its transcription in an ABA-independent manner. In addition, the ABA-responsive transcription factor PtrABF2 also promotes  PtrASMT1  expression and is transcriptionally regulated by PtrMYB82. Furthermore, PtrMYB82 physically interacts with PtrABF2 to synergistically enhance  PtrASMT1  transcription, suggesting a molecular coordination between ABA-dependent and ABA-independent signaling pathways. Collectively, we uncover a novel PtrMYB82/PtrABF2- PtrASMT1  regulatory module that modulates melatonin biosynthesis to enhance drought tolerance, providing critical molecular targets for breeding drought-resistant citrus varieties.

title: Osmotic stress‐induced phase separation drives OsbZIP13 condensates to reprogram transcription from growth to stress adaptation
abstract:
Left (well-watered): nuclear OsbZIP13 is diffusely distributed and concurrently activates promoters of photosystem genes and OsNCED3 to sustain basal carbon fixation and ABA homeostasis. Right (acute osmotic stress): osmotic shock triggers liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) of OsbZIP13.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Osmotic stress forces plants to balance photosynthesis and abscisic acid (ABA) accumulation, but the molecular mechanisms coordinating these opposing responses remain unclear. We investigated the role of the rice ( Oryza sativa ) transcription factor OsbZIP13 in this trade-off.
To get insights into the mechanisms, we combined RNA-seq, ChIP-seq and live-cell imaging to dissect rice transcription factor OsbZIP13 as an osmotic sensor functional switch from photosynthetic growth to osmotic stress adaptation.
We show that  OsbZIP13  transcription is repressed by osmotic stress, while its protein is stabilized and undergoes liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) to form nuclear condensates. These condensates switch OsbZIP13 binding from photosynthetic gene promoters to the  OsNCED3  promoter, activating ABA biosynthesis and repressing photosynthesis. OsbZIP13 overexpression ( OsbZIP13-ox ) enhances drought and osmotic tolerance, higher photosynthetic rates and improved yield with delayed heading, whereas knockout mutants are hypersensitive.
Our findings reveal that osmotic stress-induced condensation of OsbZIP13 acts as a molecular switch to balance photosynthesis and osmotic stress adaptation, offering a promising target for breeding climate-resilient rice.

title: Dual Pathways Mediate Blue Light Signaling-Regulated Melatonin Accumulation in Tomato Fruits
abstract: Abstract Melatonin is an antioxidant and growth regulator in plants that directly or indirectly influences the yield and quality of vegetable crops. Melatonin accumulation is highly sensitive to light signals. Nevertheless, the biosynthetic route responsible for light response, along with its underlying regulatory architecture, remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that blue light stimulates the expression of  SlASMT7 , which encodes an enzyme in the "serotonin–5-methoxytryptamine" melatonin biosynthetic pathway, while also repressing melatonin catabolism via SlM2H. Both effects are mediated by the transcription factor SlHY5. SlHY5 activates  SlASMT7  by directly binding to its promoter, whereas it represses  SlM2H  expression by recruiting histone deacetylases SlHDA4 and SlHDA8. Melatonin accumulation is temporally phased—biosynthesis predominates at the breaker stage, whereas SlM2H-mediated catabolism drives its decline and is accompanied by a stage-dependent metabolic transition. The HY5–ASMT7–M2H module shows consistent directional trends across multiple fleshy fruit species, suggesting possible evolutionary conservation. Together, these findings define a blue light-regulated pathway that links transcriptional and epigenetic control to melatonin homeostasis and metabolic reprogramming, providing a molecular framework for improving fruit quality through breeding and light management.

title: The Plant Cell welcomes 2027 Assistant Features Editors
A Super-Enhancer-Like Element and a Positive Feedback Loop Drive Ultra-High Expression of CCS for Red Pepper Ripening
abstract: Abstract The  capsanthin-capsorubin synthase  ( CCS ) gene drives red pigment accumulation in pepper fruit through a ripening-specific transcriptional surge. In the pericarp of mature fruit, it is the second most highly expressed gene; however, the regulatory basis for this exceptional activation remains poorly understood. Here, we identified a super-enhancer-like (SE-like) element in the pepper ( Capsicum annuum )  CCS  gene ( CaCCS ) promoter, composed of 22 tandem repeats partitioned into three groups by two intervening miniature inverted-repeat transposable elements (MITEs) insertions. MITE-associated siRNAs and DNA methylation suggest a potential role for these insertions in  CaCCS  repression before ripening, whereas CaDML2-mediated demethylation alleviates promoter repression during ripening. CArG-box motifs present in all repeats mediate CaRIN–CaTAGL1 activation of  CaCCS  in a copy number-dependent manner. Mechanistically, CaRIN binds and stabilizes CaTAGL1, and the resulting heteromeric complex activates the  CaRIN  promoter, establishing an autoregulatory positive feedback loop that amplifies  CaRIN  accumulation during ripening. CaRIN further undergoes liquid–liquid phase separation through its C-terminal intrinsically disordered region, forming nuclear condensates that are enriched at the  CaCCS  promoter and contain CaTAGL1. This study reveals how an SE-like cis-element, MITEs-directed epigenetic dynamics, and a self-reinforcing CaRIN–CaTAGL1 transcriptional circuit and biomolecular condensates work together to drive the ripening-specific increase in  CaCCS  expression. Our findings reveal the regulatory mechanisms through which quantitative and temporal control of gene expression underlies metabolic innovation in  Capsicum  species.

title: MaldiSuite: a Python ecosystem for MALDI-TOF spectral processing and analysis in antimicrobial resistance research
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat requiring faster diagnostics than the 24-48 h needed for phenotypic antibiotic-susceptibility testing. Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry is widely used in clinical microbiology for species identification but does not directly capture AMR phenotypes. Machine learning on MALDI-TOF spectra offers a promising solution, yet existing software remains fragmented across legacy R preprocessing tools and ad hoc Python scripts, lacking standardized workflows, shared application programming interfaces (APIs), and safeguards against train-test leakage. Results We present MaldiSuite, a unified Python ecosystem built on a shared data model and a scikit-learn-compatible API. It integrates three packages: MaldiAMRKit (Bruker-native and open-format input/output, standardized composable preprocessing, spectral warping, and temporal drift monitoring); MaldiBatchKit (multi-site batch correction, including MALDI-specific methods, with batch-mixing diagnostics); and MaldiDeepKit (four deep-learning classifiers: multilayer perceptron, one-dimensional convolutional neural network, residual network, and Vision Transformer). All components compose within sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline with leak-safe fit/transform semantics. On the public multi-site Database of Resistance Information on Antimicrobials and MALDI-TOF Mass Spectra (DRIAMS), MaldiSuite achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of up to 0.92 on the DRIAMS-A  Staphylococcus aureus /oxacillin task, and a leakage experiment quantifies the optimistic bias that its leak-safe cross-validation removes. Availability and Implementation MaldiSuite is available on PyPI under the MIT licence (pip install maldisuite). Source code:  https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiSuite ,  https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiAMRKit ,  https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiBatchKit ,  https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiDeepKit . The package versions described here and the analysis code of this paper ( https://github.com/EttoreRocchi/MaldiSuite-paper ), with the pinned environments, are archived at 10.5281/zenodo.24199316. Documentation  https://ettorerocchi.github.io/MaldiSuite/ . Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at  Bioinformatics  online.

title: ARCADE: Controllable Codon Design from Foundation Models via Activation Engineering
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Coding sequence design requires optimizing multiple biological properties, which may be either aligned or in trade-off, and are typically measured as continuous-valued metrics. However, existing codon design methods lack explicit control over these objectives. Moreover, current controllable generation techniques are largely developed for discrete, human-interpretable attributes, leaving a gap in controllably steering continuous biological properties in genomic sequence design. Results We introduce ARCADE (Activation engineeRing for ControllAble coDon dEsign), a machine learning framework for flexible and controllable multi-objective codon design. ARCADE leverages pretrained genomic language models and extends activation engineering from discrete attribute control to continuous-valued biological metrics. By deriving biologically meaningful semantic steering vectors in the model’s activation space, ARCADE enables direct control over properties such as Codon Adaptation Index, minimum free energy, GC content, as well as their combinations. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that ARCADE supports robust single- and multi-objective steering, enabling simultaneous modulation of multiple properties without retraining model parameters. Availability Source code for the method and to reproduce the results is available at  https://github.com/Kingsford-Group/arcade  and archived on Zenodo (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21140668). Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at  Bioinformatics  online.

title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79685-1  This study shows that greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change depend on the original ecosystem and conversion pathway, highlighting the climate value of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

title: Shape conforming Janus hydrogel for preventing anastomotic leaks
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79644-w  Anastomotic leaks remain a major complication of gastrointestinal surgery, yet existing sealants often fail to provide durable coverage of irregular tissue surfaces. Here, the authors develop a Janus powder-derived dressing composed of an adhesive porous layer mechanically interlocked with a non-adhesive backing. The material conforms to anastomotic tissues, resists unwanted post-surgical adhesions, and provides sustained sealing, offering a promising strategy for leak prevention and repair.

title: Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79625-z  Strong polarization–strain coupling limits the energy density and reliability of lead-free dielectric capacitors. Here, the authors show that entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity weakens this coupling, enabling ultrahigh energy storage with minimal electrostrain.

title: [c2]Daisy-chain molecular turing machines with switchable fluorescence outputs
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79590-7  Synthetic small-molecule machines capable of bidirectionally reading and writing information on molecular tapes with visual output remain elusive due to the challenge in amplifying molecular-scale motions into macroscopic signals. Here, the authors report two [c2]daisy-chain molecular Turing machines that convert mechanical motions into fluorescence signals.

title: Deep ultraviolet gallium-oxide avalanche photodiodes reaching an impulse-response-derived gain-bandwidth record of 152 GHz
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79355-2  Solar-blind gallium oxide photodetectors enable secure deep-ultraviolet communication but face a trade-off between speed and gain. Dong et al. engineered a multilayer avalanche device achieving nanosecond response, high gain, and a record gain-bandwidth product.

title: Accelerating high-throughput catalyst screening by direct generation of equilibrium adsorption structures
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-79243-9  The authors develop DBCata, a generative model trained without energy or force labels to produce near-equilibrium adsorption structures, enabling faster screening of candidate catalysts.

title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78602-w  The authors map 1.1 million dermatology images to assess the diversity of data used to train AI and find major gaps in darker skin tones and children, highlighting the importance of representation for future data collection.

title: Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77502-3  Measuring nanoscale temperatures is hard: contact probes perturb samples and optical methods lack resolution. Here, authors develop Kikuchi diffraction thermometry, a non-contact electron microscopy method that maps nanoscale temperatures via tiny heat-induced lattice changes.

title: BepiColombo finally reaches Mercury after eight-year odyssey
abstract: Nature, Published online: 21 November 2026;  doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03803-8  European and Japanese probes will trace different paths around the planet to study its surface and its surroundings.

title: Period-Specific Remodeling of Luminal Lineages and the Mammary Microenvironment in Dairy Goats
abstract: Milk production requires coordinated remodeling of mammary epithelial lineages and their stromal and immune niches, but this process is incompletely resolved in dairy goats. We aim to define period specific cell states and epithelial niche interactions across the dry to lactation transition. We profile mammary tissue from three peak-lactation and three dry-period Saanen goats using 10x Genomics single-cell RNA sequencing and map one peak-lactation goat with Stereo-seq. Among 44,120 cells, we identify15 populations. Peak lactation is characterized by expansion of luminal alveolar cells and increased {beta}-casein and -lactalbumin expression, whereas luminal progenitors, hormone-sensing cells, fibroblasts, and B cells are enriched in the dry period. Trajectory inference place luminal progenitors near branches toward alveolar and hormone-sensing states, with sustained ELF5-associated activity along the alveolar branch. Myoepithelial, macrophage, natural killer T, and T cell states are also remodeled. SPP1 and MIF signaling networks become more connected and change their cellular targets. These data establish a period resolved atlas of dairy goat mammary remodeling and identify coordinated epithelial, stromal, immune, and communication programs associated with active lactation.

title: BEguided: Systematic guide and base editor evaluation for precision single-nucleotide editing
abstract: Base editing enables precise nucleotide substitutions without introducing DNA double-strand breaks, but identifying optimal editor-guide combinations remains challenging because PAM compatibility, editing-window positioning, bystander modifications, and off-target effects must be considered simultaneously. Here, we introduce BEguided, an integrated computational platform for variant-specific guide RNA design and systematic comparison across 38 predefined base-editor profiles, with support for user-defined editors. BEguided incorporates single-nucleotide variants directly into target sequences, eliminating the need for customized reference genomes, while its companion tool, BEguidedOFF, provides base-editing-aware off-target prediction. To demonstrate the utility of this approach, we systematically assessed the accessibility of the 1,000 most frequent ABE-editable cancer mutations to adenine base editing. Under stringent guide-quality, bystander-editing, and predicted off-target criteria, only 7 mutations could be targeted using SpCas9-ABE8e. Expanding the analysis to additional SpCas9-compatible adenine base editors increased this number to 30, while inclusion of SaCas9, relaxed-PAM Cas9-NG/SpG variants, and PAM-less SpRY further expanded the number of potentially targetable mutations to 100, 156, and 238, respectively. These findings highlight the substantial impact of editor selection on mutation accessibility and establish BEguided as a versatile framework for identifying and prioritizing base-editing strategies for disease-associated variants. BEguided is available at https://beguided.buchholzlab.org.

title: SIREN: Predicting RNA-Small Molecule Interaction using Language Models without Requiring Structure
abstract: RNA-targeted drug discovery is constrained by the scarcity of resolved RNA tertiary structures and the conformational flexibility of RNA, which limit the applicability of structure-based virtual screening. Here, SIREN (Small molecule Interaction with RNA via sEquence-based predictioN) is presented, a sequence-based framework that ranks small molecules for a given RNA target directly from its primary sequence without requiring tertiary structure. SIREN integrates a pretrained RNA language model with molecular language model embeddings and physicochemical descriptors through an interaction network that outputs a target-specific compound-ranking score. On four held-out ROBIN riboswitch targets, SIREN outperforms the structure-based methods RNAmigos2, RNAmigos++, and rDock in both enrichment and overall discrimination, and a cross-target derangement analysis confirms that its rankings depend on RNA identity rather than general ligand propensity alone. On an independent HIV-1 TAR benchmark, SIREN achieves strong discrimination without an experimentally derived RNA conformational ensemble. Prospective screening against IRES-derived RNA hairpins from cMyc and XIAP mRNAs further identifies multiple experimentally validated, micromolar-affinity binders from a diverse chemical library. These results demonstrate that SIREN generalizes to unseen RNA targets, transfers across independent benchmarks, and provides a scalable, structure-free framework for RNA-targeted compound prioritization that complements existing structure-based screening approaches.

title: Sequence-Derived Geometric Priors Enable Controllable Generation of Intrinsically Disordered Protein Ensembles
abstract: Predicting heterogeneous conformational ensembles from sequence remains a central challenge for intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs). Sequence-to-ensemble models often entangle geometric inference with coordinate generation, obscuring error sources and limiting control over ensemble properties. Here we introduce MANTA, a C-level framework that separates these stages. An encoder derives geometric priors from protein language-model representations, and a graph-Laplacian decoder converts these priors into conformational ensembles. On a homology-held-out test set, replacing predicted priors with reference-derived priors under the same decoder reduces the median absolute relative radius-of-gyration error from 8.78% to 1.89%, identifying geometric-prior estimation as the dominant bottleneck in MANTA. Across an external benchmark of 27 IDPs, MANTA generates broad, locally valid ensembles. Decoder controls modulate mean compactness and conformational breadth along partially separable axes, while compactness modulation alters motif exposure in tau and amyloid-{beta}. Meanwhile, -synuclein variants shift local exposure populations at nearly unchanged global size. MANTA provides a diagnostic and controllable framework for ensemble generation that captures both global dimensions and local conformational organization.

title: Combinatorial perturbation structure enables graded inference of signaling activity by CIRCE
abstract: Cells decode external inputs into intracellular activities of varying magnitude, and inferring both input identity and strength is crucial for cell-fate engineering. However, perturbation-response models typically treat all cells exposed to a given input as a discrete class, ignoring cell-to-cell variation in response magnitude. Here, we introduce a structured-label framework that infers both input identity and strength from combinatorial perturbation screens without dose-resolved training labels. We represent each perturbation combination in a binary combinatorial space and replace one-hot supervision with a Boltzmann distribution that decays with the Hamming distance between combinations.
