title: Ovatodiolide Suppresses NME1 Ubiquitination and Reactivates Tubular BRAT1–ATM DNA Repair Signaling in Diabetic Kidney Disease
abstract:
Ovatodiolide directly targets NME1 to restore BRAT1–ATM‐dependent DNA damage repair signaling in diabetic kidney disease. By disrupting TRIM47‐mediated NME1 ubiquitination and degradation, ovatodiolide stabilizes NME1, promotes tubular DNA repair, and alleviates renal injury and fibrosis, supporting NME1 stabilization as a potential therapeutic strategy for diabetic kidney disease.








ABSTRACT
Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) lacks effective therapies that halt disease progression. Although oxidative stress–induced DNA damage in tubular epithelial cells contributes to disease progression, its upstream regulatory mechanisms remain poorly defined. Here, we identify nucleoside diphosphate kinase 1 (NME1) as a key regulator of the DNA damage response (DDR) and a direct target of ovatodiolide (OVA). Proteome‐wide and structural analyses reveal that OVA binds NME1 at Lys12 and Arg114 and interferes with its interaction with the E3 ubiquitin ligase TRIM47, thereby suppressing NME1 ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation. Stabilized NME1 interacts with BRAT1 to facilitate assembly of the BRAT1–ATM complex, leading to activation of ATM‐dependent DNA repair signaling. Functionally, OVA reduces reactive oxygen species accumulation and DNA damage in tubular epithelial cells through an NME1‐dependent mechanism that requires BRAT1‐mediated ATM activation. In diabetic mice, OVA ameliorates renal injury independently of glycemic control, whereas tubular NME1 silencing abrogates these effects. Notably, the optimized derivative ACT004 retains NME1‐dependent cytoprotective activity with reduced cytotoxicity. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that OVA suppresses TRIM47‐mediated NME1 ubiquitination to restore BRAT1–ATM‐dependent DNA repair signaling and highlight pharmacological stabilization of NME1 as a potential therapeutic strategy for DKD.

title: Clean Thermolysis PMMA Top Layer Enables High‐Efficiency Kesterite Solar Cells
abstract:
A temperature-triggered PMMA blocking layer with clean thermolysis characteristics delays the early-stage selenization reaction, suppressing secondary phases and defect clusters, and enabling 14.69%-efficient (Ag,Cu) 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4  solar cells.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Regulating the phase evolution during selenization of kesterite (Ag,Cu) 2 ZnSn(S,Se) 4  (ACZTSSe) absorbers is essential for high-efficiency solar cells, yet it remains challenging because of uncontrolled contact reactions between the precursor film and selenium vapor. Herein, we introduce a poly (methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) blocking layer with clean-thermolysis characteristics onto the ACZTSSe precursor top surface to precisely control the onset of selenization. At low temperatures, the PMMA layer acts as a physical barrier that isolates the precursor from Se vapor, effectively suppressing premature reactions and secondary phase formation. Upon heating above 400°C, the PMMA decomposes almost residue-free, immediately exposing the precursor to high-concentration Se vapor and triggering a rapid one-step conversion into the desired kesterite phase. This temperature-triggered decomposition decouples early-stage intermediate reactions from final phase formation, significantly reducing secondary phases and the density of detrimental [2Cu Zn +Sn Zn ] defect clusters. Variable-wavelength photoluminescence confirms the simultaneous suppression of non-radiative recombination in both the bulk and the interfaces, yielding a prolonged minority carrier lifetime. The optimized device achieves a power conversion efficiency of 14.69% with an open-circuit voltage of 566 mV. This work demonstrates a simple yet effective interfacial engineering strategy for steering selenization pathways, offering a practical route toward higher-quality kesterite absorbers.

title: Nanotube‐Supported Pd–Ni/NiO Alloy–Oxide Heterointerfaces for Electro‐ and Thermocatalytic Hydrogen Transformations
abstract:
A silicate nanotube precursor-derived catalyst enables hydrogen production, storage, and release through electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution and thermocatalytic hydrogenation/dehydrogenation. Polyhedral misfit between NiO 6  octahedra and SiO 4  tetrahedra, together with contrasting redox thermodynamics, directs the formation of Pd–Ni/NiO alloy–oxide nanoparticles on a robust silicate framework, enabling balanced H* adsorption/desorption and efficient interfacial hydrogen transfer.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Electro- and thermocatalytic hydrogen transformations usually require separate catalysts because their operating environments impose different demands on active-site accessibility, redox control, and structural stability. Here we report a nanotube-supported Pd–Ni/NiO alloy–oxide catalyst for hydrogen production, storage, and release. The catalyst is derived from a lattice-mismatched Ni–Si nanotubular precursor, in which a silicate framework stabilizes the architecture while exposed Ni sites direct Pd anchoring, Ni exsolution, Pd–Ni alloying, and surface NiO formation. The heterostructure consists of Pd–Ni alloy nanoparticles decorated with NiO domains on a thermally robust silicate scaffold. This architecture promotes water activation, balanced hydrogen adsorption/desorption, interfacial hydrogen transfer, and resistance to aggregation. Consequently, it shows high activity and durability for electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution and thermocatalytic N-methylindole hydrogenation/dehydrogenation, including reversible hydrogen uptake and release in a single reactor. These results identify nanotube-directed alloy–oxide heterostructure formation as a strategy for linking hydrogen production, storage, and release across electro- and thermocatalytic regimes.

title: Human Activity Sensing and Sensing‐Assisted Adaptive Communication Based on an RIS‐Aided Single‐Channel System
abstract:
Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) are used in a single‐channel system for human activity sensing (HAS) and sensing‐assisted adaptive communications. Specifically, the RISs generate random patterns to acquire echo signals for recognizing location and posture of the human target. Based on the recognized results, the system tracks the human target and adaptively switch the communication content according to the target posture.








ABSTRACT
Multiple‐in‐multiple‐out (MIMO) systems have been commonly used in human activity sensing (HAS) to capture the characteristics in space, time, and frequency domains, but with complicated hardware architecture and high cost. Here, we propose to use reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) in a single‐channel system for human activity sensing (HAS) and sensing‐assisted adaptive communications. Specifically, the RISs generate random patterns to acquire echo signals of a human target, and then fully connected neural networks recognize the location and posture of the human target. Based on the recognized results, the RIS‐aided system can track the human target and adaptively switch the communication content according to the posture of the human target. The RIS‐aided single‐channel system provides a low‐cost and low‐complexity scheme for HAS and sensing‐assisted adaptive communications, thus showing enormous potential for applications in smart homes and smart cities.

title: Qualitative Change Effect of Defects on Carbon Regulates Interfacial Proton Kinetics for Efficient Nitrate Reduction Reaction
abstract:
A quantitative increase in carbon defect density in metal-free carbon induces a qualitative transformation of the electrocatalytic interface, reconstructing the interfacial water environment and shifting the hydrogenation pathway toward surface-adsorbed hydrogen. This kinetic transition enables highly efficient nitrate-to-ammonia conversion and outstanding performance in rechargeable Zn–nitrate batteries.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Metal-free carbon catalysts hold great promise for electrocatalysis but face formidable challenges in complex multi-electron reactions. Specifically, the dynamic behaviors of metal-free carbon catalysts at the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP) remain elusive, especially understanding how intrinsic carbon structures influence interfacial proton supply kinetics during multi-electron processes, such as electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) represents a critical knowledge gap. Herein, a series of carbons with tunable defect density was precisely regulated, revealing a linear positive correlation between the defect density of carbon and NO 3 RR activity. In situ characterizations and proton kinetic studies demonstrated that the quantitative change of carbon defects not only accelerates water dissociation via breaking the ordering interfacial hydrogen-bond network but also induces a new adsorbed-H mediated pathway to enhance hydrogenation of NO x  intermediates. Meanwhile, the defect-induced asymmetric charge distribution strengthens  * NO x  adsorption, synergistically lowering the hydrogenation barriers. The high-dense defective carbon (DC-1100) achieves a high NH 3  Faradaic efficiency of 99.1% and empowers a Zn-NO 3 
 −  battery with power density of 50.06 mW cm −2  and over 1000 h stability, outperforming all reported metal-free catalysts.

title: Golgi‐Linked Glucosylceramide Metabolism Regulates Cocaine‐Induced Dendritic Membrane Remodeling
abstract:
This study identifies a D1-MSN-selective GCS-GlcCer program linking Golgi remodeling and dendritic lipid redistribution to cocaine-induced structural and behavioral adaptations. GCS suppression attenuates cocaine-induced dendritic remodeling and behavioral responses, whereas GlcCer supplementation partially restores those effects after  Ugcg  knockdown, revealing a Golgi-centered lipid mechanism that contributes to cocaine-induced neuroplasticity in the nucleus accumbens.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Structural plasticity remodeling in the nucleus accumbens plays a critical role in the persistent addictive neurobehaviors induced by cocaine; however, the mechanisms underlying the supply of plasma membrane materials required for these adaptive changes have remained elusive. Here we identified a Golgi-centered lipid metabolic program that enables cocaine-induced structural plasticity in the nucleus accumbens. Cocaine increased glucosylceramide synthase (GCS) expression and glucosylceramide (GlcCer) abundance in dopamine D1 receptor-expressing medium spiny neurons (D1-MSNs) selectively, accompanied by Golgi remodeling and an increased abundance of Golgi-associated vesicles. GlcCer also accumulated in membrane-associated compartments, redistributed toward MAP2-positive dendritic structures, and altered the postsynaptic density architecture. Pharmacological GCS inhibition attenuated cocaine-induced Golgi remodeling and membrane-associated GlcCer accumulation, whereas  Ugcg  knockdown or D1-MSNs-specific deletion reduced cocaine-induced dendritic and behavioral adaptations. Conversely, exogenous GlcCer treatment restored dendritic remodeling and neurobehavioral responses following  Ugcg  knockdown. These findings define a D1-MSN-selective Golgi-lipid remodeling program that links GCS-GlcCer metabolism and membrane lipid redistribution to cocaine-induced neuroplasticity.

title: Microstructural Orientation Enables Mass‐Efficient Structural Batteries
abstract:
Magnetic-field-assisted electrophoretic deposition (MAG-EPD) aligns LiFePO 4  particles on carbon fibers, enhanced ion-transport pathways within structural electrodes. The resulting all-fiber structural battery simultaneously delivers high electrochemical performance and mechanical stiffness, demonstrating a scalable route toward lightweight multifunctional energy-storage materials.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Multifunctional energy materials are fundamentally constrained by the coupling between ionic transport and mechanical load-bearing, limiting performance and hindering practical implementation. In structural battery composites, this coupling has restricted energy density, rate capability and durability, keeping the field at a proof-of-concept stage despite its promise for system-level weight savings. Here we establish microstructural orientation as an architectural strategy to alleviate transport limitations while preserving the mechanical functionality of load-bearing energy materials. By aligning LiFePO 4  within a carbon fiber architecture, anisotropic transport pathways reduce tortuosity while preserving structural integrity. This enables all-fiber structural batteries with a cell-based energy density of 73 Wh kg −1 , power density of 78 W kg −1 , and an elastic modulus of 100 GPa. For the first time, multifunctional efficiency exceeds unity, reaching 1.6, enabling ∼37% system-level weight reduction. Sustained cycling at 5C over 1000 cycles and accelerated kinetic stress testing at 10C demonstrate improved high-rate performance, while calendar-life stability over 8760 h confirms long-term durability under mechanically constrained conditions.

title: Interfacial Kinetic Sink Confines the Oxygen Reduction Active Zone in Protonic Ceramic Fuel Cells
abstract:
A combination of in situ ME-DRIFTS, H/D isotope-resolved impedance, and ToF-SIMS analysis elucidates spatial confinement in PCFC cathodes, where rapid surface kinetics act as an interfacial kinetic sink. Mitigating this confinement provides a material design for maximizing the bulk potential of PBSCF and related 3D porous electrocatalysts.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) proceeds within H + /O 2− /e −  triple-conducting oxides. While facile bulk proton diffusion is conventionally assumed to spread the active reaction zone ( L 
 eff ) throughout the porous electrode, the precise link between molecular-level rate-determining steps and this macroscopic spatial extent remains elusive. Here, we reveal this interplay by bridging atomic-scale kinetics with macroscopic spatial utilization. By coupling in situ modulation-excitation infrared spectroscopy with hydrogen/deuterium isotope-resolved impedance analysis, we identify the vacancy-assisted dissociation of accumulated superoxide (O2−${\mathrm{O}}_2^ - $) into active O −  species as the molecular-scale rate-determining step. Integrating these surface kinetics with porous-electrode theory reveals that this O −  formation acts as an interfacial kinetic sink, consuming protons near the electrolyte interface before they penetrate the electrode bulk. Consequently, the overall ORR is confined to only a ∼110 nm zone in state-of-the-art PrBa 0.5 Sr 0.5 Co 1.5 Fe 0.5 O 5+δ  (PBSCF) cathodes at 600°C, leaving ∼98% of the porous scaffold electrochemically inert. This interfacial proton barrier is directly observed by time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry isotope tracking on dense model films. Overcoming the interfacial proton exchange barrier to expand  L 
 eff , rather than solely accelerating surface kinetics, defines a design principle for state-of-the-art PBSCF and potentially other porous mixed-conducting electrodes.

title: Decoding and Rewiring Neurovascular Communication in Spinal Cord Injury via Computational Extracellular Vesicle Dynamics
abstract:
This review reconceptualizes spinal cord injury as neurovascular unit disruption and examines the blood‐spinal cord barrier's biphasic remodeling, from acute hyperpermeability to chronic fibrosis. It describes computational molecular dynamics‐guided engineering of extracellular vesicles for receptor‐mediated transcytosis across the fibrotic barrier and integrates hydrogel scaffolds with neuromodulation to establish closed‐loop circuit repair, advancing toward patient‐specific digital twin therapy.








ABSTRACT
Spinal cord injury (SCI) disrupts the neurovascular unit (NVU), notably impairing the blood‐spinal cord barrier (BSCB), which undergoes a biphasic transformation from acute hyperpermeability to chronic fibrotic sclerosis. This dynamic remodeling creates a heterogeneous barrier that hinders effective drug delivery and limits therapeutic success. Here we integrate pathological characterization with computational molecular dynamics to rationally engineer extracellular vesicles (EVs) capable of receptor‐mediated transcytosis across the fibrotic BSCB. Coupled with computational fluid dynamics‐optimized hydrogel scaffolds and neuromodulation techniques, this approach promotes NVU repair, restores synaptic homeostasis, and facilitates neural circuit rewiring. This integrated framework advances precision SCI interventions by overcoming the evolving BSCB, offering a novel paradigm for enhancing functional recovery after traumatic SCI and informing therapeutic strategies for central nervous system disorders characterized by barrier dysfunction.

title: Anatomical Compartmentalization in Chickens Drives Divergent H9N2 Influenza Evolution Toward Human Receptor Binding and Immune Escape
abstract:
Avian influenza A(H9N2) viruses pose a potential pandemic threat, having evolved enhanced binding to human-type receptors and the capacity to escape pre-existing immunity in chickens. Using deep mutational scanning viruses, we demonstrate that tissue-specific microenvironments impose distinct selective pressures on viral populations in immunized chickens: the upper respiratory tract preferentially selects for variants with enhanced binding to human-type receptors, whereas the lower respiratory tract favors the emergence of antibody-escape variants.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Avian influenza A(H9N2) viruses pose a pandemic threat, having acquired preferential binding to human receptors and the ability to evade immunity in chickens. However, the selective forces driving these traits remain unclear. Here, we show how anatomical compartmentalization within chickens shapes hemagglutinin (HA) evolution. Using deep mutational scanning coupled with in  vivo  studies, we find that pre-existing immunity reduces viral load and blocks transmission, thereby imposing strong selection on viral diversity. Distinct tissues exert divergent selection pressures in immunized chickens. The upper respiratory tract mainly enriches viruses with high-affinity binding to human-type receptors, whereas the lower respiratory tract preferentially favors antibody-escape viruses. This functional difference was validated using variants carrying defined substitutions, which showed fitness aligned with their respective compartment. Our results demonstrate that tissue-specific selection within an avian host can concurrently shape viral diversity toward human adaptation and immune evasion, providing a mechanism for the emergence of variants with pandemic potential in poultry.

title: Colonic In Situ Microbiota Shows Greater Predictive Potential than Fecal Microbiota for Washed Microbiota Transplantation Response in Autism Spectrum Disorder
abstract:
Colonic in situ microbiota differ markedly from fecal microbiota in children with autism spectrum disorder and show stronger links with clinical severity. Washed microbiota transplantation remodels this intestinal microbial compartment toward donor‐like profiles, while models combining colonic microbiota and clinical features improve prediction of treatment response compared with fecal microbiota‐based models.








ABSTRACT
Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is increasingly linked to gut microbial dysbiosis, yet fecal microbiota may not adequately reflect host–microbe interactions at the intestinal mucosa. This study compares colonic in situ and fecal microbiota in children with ASD, evaluates their associations with clinical severity, and examines their responses to washed microbiota transplantation (WMT). Colonic in situ microbiota show marked structural and compositional divergence from fecal microbiota, with limited overlap between compartments. Despite lower microbial diversity, colonic microbiota exhibit broader and stronger associations with ASD severity, including Autism Behavior Checklist (ABC) and Childhood Autism Rating Scale (CARS) scores. In germ‐free ASD model mice, transplantation of healthy donor microbiota alleviates autism‐like behaviors. Consistently, WMT improves clinical symptoms in children with ASD and progressively shifts colonic microbiota toward donor‐like configurations. Colonic microbiota changes are associated with symptom improvement, and exploratory predictive analyses suggest that integrating colonic in situ microbiota with clinical features may provide additional predictive information compared with fecal microbiota‐based models. These findings suggest that clinically sampled colonic in situ microbiota may provide complementary information for understanding ASD heterogeneity and treatment response, although further validation is warranted.

title: CaSiO3‐Engineered Extracellular Vesicles Promote Diabetic Fracture Healing in Mice via the PGC‐1α–miR‐363‐3p–DKK3–β‐Catenin Axis
abstract:
In a mouse model of diabetic fracture, the hyperglycemic microenvironment promotes ubiquitin-mediated degradation of PGC-1α in BMSC, thereby inhibiting BMSC osteogenesis through the miR-363-3p-DKK3-β-catenin axis. Treatment with CaSiO 3  suppresses PGC-1α ubiquitination and degradation, leading to increased miR-363-3p expression. Concurrently, CaSiO 3  upregulates AGO2 protein expression, facilitating the assembly of miR-363-3p into miRISC complexes and their subsequent loading into EVs. A ROS-responsive hydrogel loaded with these CaSiO 3 -engineered EVs enables sustained EVs release specifically at sites with high ROS levels in the fractured area. The released EVs deliver miRISC complexes, which target the DKK3-β-catenin axis to promote BMSC osteogenesis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Diabetes impairs fracture healing. In diabetic mice, we found that PGC-1α expression is downregulated in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC). PGC-1α levels positively correlate with osteogenic capacity. Physiologically, reduced PGC-1α suppresses miR-363-3p expression; mechanistically, this further inhibits DKK3, thereby promoting β-catenin phosphorylation and degradation, which in turn inhibits osteogenesis in BMSCs. To target this pathway, we treated BMSC with calcium silicate (CaSiO 3 ). CaSiO 3  inhibited the ubiquitination-mediated degradation of PGC-1α, restoring miR-363-3p expression. It also upregulated AGO2, which facilitated the assembly of miR-363-3p into mi-RISC complexes and their loading into extracellular vesicles. We then engineered a ROS-responsive hydrogel (Gel ROS ) to deliver these CaSiO 3 -engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs). In diabetic mice with femoral fractures, the hydrogel enabled sustained, on-demand release of EVs specifically at sites with high ROS levels. The released EVs, enriched with miRISC complexes, suppressed the DKK3-β-catenin axis in recipient BMSC, enhanced osteogenesis, and accelerated fracture healing. This study identifies the PGC-1α–miR-363-3p–DKK3-β–catenin axis as a key pathway in diabetic fracture healing. It also presents a novel EVs-based strategy that avoids direct CaSiO 3  toxicity, offering a new translational approach for treating diabetic bone defects.

title: Bayesian Inference of Global Land Plant Diversification Dynamics Across the Phanerozoic
abstract:
Underlying diversification patterns and potential drivers of land plants remain puzzling, particularly at deep‐time and global scales. Here, we reconstruct the diversification dynamics of land plants using an updated time‐calibrated phylogeny comprising approximately 30,000 extant species, and nearly 40,000 fossil occurrences within the Bayesian birth‐death frameworks. Our findings highlight the combined roles of biotic interactions, global environmental change, and lineage‐specific responses in shaping land plant diversity through geological time.








ABSTRACT
The patterns and potential drivers of land plant diversification remain puzzling, particularly over deep time and at the global scale. Here, we reconstruct land plant diversification dynamics using an updated time‐calibrated phylogeny comprising 30,278 extant species and 39,857 fossil occurrences within the Bayesian birth‐death framework. Our analyses indicate that angiosperms exhibit the highest diversification rates, whereas ferns underwent a marked diversification increase during the Cretaceous, coincident with the rapid radiation of angiosperms. Among the major Phanerozoic mass extinctions, the Cretaceous‐Paleogene event has the most significant impact on land plant diversity, with estimated genus‐level losses of 13%, 14%, and 4% in bryophytes, pteridophytes, and gymnosperms. We also identify a pattern consistent with competitive displacement scenario, in which pteridophyte origination rates declined as gymnosperm diversity increased, accompanying the transition from pteridophyte‐ to gymnosperm‐dominated floras. Plant‐insect interactions can be traced to the emergence of pteridophytes, potentially promoting the diversification of pteridophytes and gymnosperms. During the Cretaceous, these associations shift toward angiosperms, as indicated by a positive relationship between insect diversity and angiosperm origination rates. Finally, continental fragmentation, fluctuations in aridity and atmospheric carbon, and sedimentary dynamics show stronger associations with the rise and decline of major land plant groups.

title: Integrating TiO2 Interlayers and NiFe Metal‐Organic Framework Cocatalysts for Enhanced Water Oxidation on Hematite Photoanodes
abstract:
A Ti-doped hematite photoanode combines a titanium dioxide interlayer with a nickel-iron metal-organic framework surface layer. Their complementary effects improve charge collection and water oxidation, giving 4.25 mA cm −2  at 1.23 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode. Spectroscopy and local interface calculations connect the improved response to interfacial charge management and more favorable oxygen-evolution energetics. 

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Charge recombination and sluggish oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics limit the collection and utilization of photogenerated holes in hematite photoanodes. Herein, we report a dual-interface strategy that combines a TiO 2  interfacial layer with a bimetallic nickel-iron metal-organic framework (NiFe-MOF) surface layer on Ti-doped Fe 2 O 3 . The TiO 2  interlayer modifies interfacial charge collection, while the NiFe-containing surface layer promotes hole utilization for water oxidation. The integrated NiFe-MOF/TiO 2 /Ti-Fe 2 O 3  photoanode delivers a photocurrent density of 4.25 mA cm −2  at 1.23 V vs. the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) and a maximum applied-bias photon-to-current efficiency (ABPE) of 0.51%. Complementary photoelectrochemical and spectroscopic measurements support improved charge collection and interfacial reaction behavior. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy resolves changes in carrier relaxation after each modification, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations on representative local interface models indicate charge redistribution and a lower reaction free-energy requirement for *O formation. These results link the performance improvement to the complementary effects of interface modification and surface catalysis, providing a strategy for improving hematite photoanodes.

title: Glutamine Fuels De Novo Sphingomyelin Synthesis to Drive Hepatocellular Carcinoma Development
abstract:
Dietary glutamine accelerates hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development by directly fueling de novo sphingomyelin (SM) synthesis. Elevated SM levels promote lipid raft assembly and induce the aggregation of TGF-β receptors. This structural enhancement activates downstream epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) signaling, thereby driving malignant transformation and hepatocarcinogenesis, revealing a critical metabolic-structural axis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Although metabolic reprogramming is a recognized hallmark of cancer, the specific metabolic pathways driving hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development remain incompletely understood. Through metabolomic profiling of human HCC specimens, we reveal that amino acids and their analogues are the most profoundly dysregulated metabolites, with glutamine being notably depleted within the tumor microenvironment. Despite its perception as a generic nutrient, we demonstrate that dietary glutamine supplementation promotes the malignant transformation of tumor progenitors and accelerates proliferation in oncogene-driven murine models, ultimately compromising overall survival. Metabolomic and  13 C-isotope tracing analyses indicate that glutamine is preferentially channeled into de novo sphingomyelin (SM) synthesis. Both genetic and pharmacological interventions establish SM as the primary downstream effector mediating glutamine's pro-tumorigenic effects. Mechanistically, SM accumulation promotes lipid raft formation, which subsequently activates TGF-β signaling to induce epithelial–mesenchymal transition. This cascade compromises the epithelial integrity of preneoplastic hepatocytes, thereby driving malignant transformation and fueling tumor progression. Collectively, these findings provide a mechanistic rationale cautioning against glutamine supplementation in high-risk populations and highlight potential novel metabolic vulnerabilities for the prevention and treatment of HCC.

title: A Dual‐Responsive Senolytic Hydrogel Remodels the Postsurgical Senescent Microenvironment to Suppress Glioblastoma Recurrence
abstract:
The senolytic hydrogel (ABT@Gal‐gel) was engineered using an injectable bacterial cellulose (BC)/chitosan‐based hydrogel that encapsulates galactose‐modified polydopamine nanoparticles loaded with ABT‐263, a selective BCL2 inhibitor. The postoperative injection of the hydrogel enabled β‐galactosidase‐responsive release of ABT‐263 to eliminate temozolomide (TMZ)‐induced senescent GBM cells, followed by immune activation to prevent GBM recurrence. This approach synergistically induced both senolytic pathways and GBM microenvironment remodeling to effectively inhibit GBM recurrence.








ABSTRACT
Tumor recurrence remains the predominant cause of mortality in patients with glioblastoma (GBM), and (chemo/radio‐) therapy‐induced senescence (TIS) has recently been recognized as a key driver by deteriorating the post‐surgical microenvironment. To exploit this “senescence trap”, we developed an injectable, bacterial cellulose (BC)‐based hydrogel system (ABT@Gal‐gel) designed for preferential elimination of senescent GBM cells. This platform encapsulates galactose‐modified polydopamine nanoparticles loaded with the senolytic agent ABT‐263 (ABT@Gal‐PDA). It enables programmed, β‐galactosidase (β‐Gal)‐responsive drug release to preferentially eliminate pro‐tumorigenic senescent cells. Moreover, the cellulose and chitosan in the hydrogel further remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment by inducing M1 macrophage polarization. In orthotopic GBM mouse models, this dual‐functional strategy significantly inhibits tumor recurrence and prolongs overall survival. Overall, this study presents a novel strategy by coupling senescence‐associated intracellular targeting with tumor‐associated macrophage (TAM) repolarization to suppress GBM relapses, providing a promising direction for the next generation of postoperative brain cancer therapies.

title: Mechanomedicine for Lung Transplantation: From Multiscale Forces to AI‐Assisted Translation
abstract:
This Review presents a multiscale mechanomedicine framework for lung transplantation, linking mechanical insults and cellular force sensing to measurable graft phenotypes, computational integration and clinically staged interventions. It critically evaluates evidence maturity across ex vivo lung perfusion, imaging, respiratory mechanics, mechanotherapeutics and digital‐twin concepts, and identifies validation priorities for safer, clinician‐supervised translation.








ABSTRACT
Long‐term outcomes after lung transplantation remain limited by primary graft dysfunction and chronic lung allograft dysfunction, despite improvements in surgery, immunosuppression and infection control. Mechanical injury is a complementary contributor that remains insufficiently integrated into transplant care. The lung allograft must accommodate cyclic ventilation, reperfusion shear, thoracic constraints and matrix remodeling. These forces can disrupt the alveolar‐capillary barrier, amplify inflammation and activate fibrotic programmes. Here we synthesize lung transplantation through a mechanomedicine framework that links organ‐scale loading, cellular mechanotransduction and clinical decision‐making. We discuss how computational models and artificial intelligence (AI) can integrate ex vivo lung perfusion waveforms, imaging‐derived ventilation or strain patterns, and molecular injury markers to support graft‐risk assessment. We then organize mechanotherapeutic strategies by clinical readiness, from protective ventilation, size matching and extracorporeal graft support to emerging interventions targeting mechanotransduction according to cell type and loading conditions. Finally, we outline a translational roadmap for standardized mechanical biomarkers, interpretable AI and clinician‐supervised digital‐twin models.

title: Commensal Bacteroides Strains Restrict Intestinal Colonization by Multidrug‐Resistant Campylobacter jejuni
abstract:
Strains of  Bacteroides acidifaciens  and  Bacteroides caecimuris  reduce multidrug-resistant  Campylobacter jejuni  colonization in mice, accompanied by changes in gut microbiota and metabolite profiles. Indole inhibits the pathogen in vitro, but its contribution to colonization resistance in vivo remains unproven. These findings identify commensal  Bacteroides  as candidates for further investigation in microbiome-based strategies against  C. jejuni .

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Multidrug-resistant (MDR)  Campylobacter jejuni  is a foodborne pathogen that threatens public health and food safety. Intestinal colonization is a prerequisite for infection, yet protective commensal bacteria and the potential contributions of microbial metabolites remain poorly defined. This study integrates in vitro co-culture assays, epithelial cell models, mouse infection experiments, and multi-omics analyses to identify protective gut commensals and explore potential mechanisms. Most commensal strains tested suppress  C. jejuni  growth in co-culture without impairing epithelial cell viability or markedly altering  C. jejuni  adhesion, indicating that epithelial attachment competition is unlikely to be the dominant protective mechanism.  Bacteroides acidifaciens  and  Bacteroides caecimuris  reduce intestinal  C. jejuni  colonization in mice, alleviate tissue injury, and limit inflammatory responses, with decreased expression of interleukin-1 beta, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha and increased expression of Occludin, zonula occludens-1, and mucin-2. Multi-omics analyses further show that these strains restore microbial community structure, restrain infection-associated taxa, and reshape intestinal metabolism. Indole exhibits antibacterial activity against  C. jejuni  in vitro, with additive effects when combined with propionic acid, syringic acid, or ferulic acid; its contribution to  Bacteroides -mediated protection in vivo remains unresolved. These findings support further investigation of commensal- and metabolite-based approaches against MDR  C. jejuni  infection.

title: Zerovalent Metallic Intermediates in the Synthesis of InSb Quantum Dots: From Precursor Reduction to Optical Tunability
abstract:
Cracking InSb Quantum Dot Synthesis: Room-temperature precursor reduction forms In 0  and Sb 0  intermediates, enabling intermetallic diffusion to produce monodisperse, size-tunable QDs (1160–2200 nm) with exceptional optical and colloidal stability—advancing SWIR-to-mid-IR technologies.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Indium antimonide (InSb) colloidal quantum dots (QDs) are transformative for short-wave to mid-infrared optoelectronics due to their narrow bandgap and exceptional electronic properties. This work refines the mechanistic framework of InSb QDs formation, demonstrating that the size of zerovalent In 0  and Sb 0  intermediate nanoparticles governs intermetallic diffusion and growth kinetics. By tuning precursor halides (Cl − , Br − , I − ), reducing agent ratios, In/Sb ratios (2:1–5:1), and reaction times (15–180 min), we achieved monodisperse InSb QDs with tunable absorption from 1100 to 2200 nm and exceptional stability. Temperature-dependent studies reveal that Sb 0  nanoparticles (3–4 nm) template nucleation at 140°C–160°C, while larger In 0  nanoparticles (50 nm) act as an indium reservoir, facilitating diffusion. Validation experiments with pre-synthesized In 0  and Sb 0  nanoparticles confirm that size-matched intermediates (14–17 nm) enable complete conversion to zincblende InSb QDs. Spectroscopic analysis identifies a dominant non-radiative decay channel (τ 1  ≈ 0.12 ns for 9.6 nm InSb QDs) at room temperature, attributed to surface trapping, with the radiative lifetime preserved due to surface oxides. These findings further elucidate the formation and transformation of metallic intermediates and provide practical guidance for controlling the size and optical properties of InSb QDs for SWIR applications.

title: DNA‐PKcs–DNMT3A Axis Triggers Aging‐Like Deteriorations in Mouse Pluripotent Stem Cells
abstract:
Lamin A-mediated phosphorylation of DNA-PKcs supports efficient DNA repair and proper SP1/3-mediated transcription of  Dnmt3a . During iPSC passaging, reduced Lamin A destabilizes the genome and lowers  Dnmt3a  expression by inactivating DNA-PKcs, leading to derepression of developmental and somatic programs that mimics aging and impairs iPSC differentiation potential.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-based regenerative medicine holds great promise for the treatment of age-related diseases. However, it still faces numerous challenges. One critical issue is whether iPSCs, which are commonly believed to be ageless and to indefinitely self-renew in an undifferentiated state, undergo a decline in cell quality during continuous passaging, ultimately compromising their therapeutic potential. Here, we show that long-term cultured iPSCs acquire aging-like molecular and functional deterioration, including impaired DNA repair via non-homologous end joining (NHEJ), loss of cellular identity, and diminished differentiation potential. Mechanistically, decreased levels of Lamin A trigger DNA-PKcs inactivation, leading to impaired NHEJ during prolonged culture. This DNA-PKcs inactivation then suppresses DNMT3A expression via SP1/3 and induces transcriptomic signatures characteristic of aging, ultimately impairing pluripotency. Our findings establish that iPSCs undergo aging-like deterioration during extended culture through DNA damage–epigenetics crosstalk, highlighting the critical need for genomic stability monitoring. Furthermore, we identify feasible targets to improve cell quality in iPSC-based clinical applications.

title: Microfabrication Route Shapes Morphology and Performance in PEDOT:PSS Organic Electrochemical Transistors
abstract:
PEDOT:PSS microfabrication critically determines organic electrochemical transistor channel morphology and performance. Comparing Parylene C peel‐off and germanium hard‐mask patterning reveals that peel‐off induces non‐uniform film thickness and variability, whereas Ge‐mask processing enables accurately controlled channel volumes, improving device reproducibility and reliable performance benchmarking while maintaining cytocompatibility with neuronal cultures.








ABSTRACT
Organic mixed ionic‐electronic conductors (OMIECs), and in particular PEDOT:PSS, have become central to the development of bioelectronic interfaces. Nonetheless, their integration with standard microfabrication remains challenging, as OMIECs are sensitive to processes commonly used in lithography. Here, we show that the method chosen to pattern PEDOT:PSS is a decisive design parameter that determines film morphology, active layer definition, device scaling, and biological interfacing. Under identical layouts and characterization conditions, we compare two fundamentally different fabrication strategies: the widely adopted Parylene C peel‐off process, based on the mechanical removal of a sacrificial layer, and a water‐removable germanium hard‐mask approach. Peel‐off patterning prevents chemical exposure of PEDOT:PSS, but introduces geometry‐dependent thickness gradients, edge accumulation, and poorly defined perimeters, making the PEDOT:PSS active volume difficult to define and increasing device‐to‐device variability. In contrast, germanium hard‐mask patterning ensures lithographic control and homogeneous film thickness, leading to a more reliable extraction of figures of merit. Lastly, primary cortical neurons were successfully cultured on both patterned substrates, displaying high viability. These results establish a central role for the fabrication route on the performance of organic bioelectronic platforms, highlighting the need to accurately control electrochemically active volumes for reproducible OECT benchmarking and scalable manufacturing.

title: Detecting Interventional Spatiotemporal Causality in Dynamical Systems
abstract:
Interventional spatiotemporal causality (ISTC) combines state embedding and reservoir computing to infer directed interactions and time delays from observed time series. Deviations between control and intervention surrogate trajectories quantify causal influence. Evaluations on synthetic benchmarks and diverse real‐world datasets support its utility for investigating causal connections, with delay recovery assessed in coupled dynamical systems.








ABSTRACT
Causal interactions in dynamical systems are structured not only across variables but also across time. However, conventional causal representations typically collapse this temporal organization into variable‐level links, obscuring when causal influences act. Here we introduce interventional spatiotemporal causality (ISTC), a framework that represents causal organization over the joint space of variables and temporal delays. ISTC reconstructs the high‐dimensional state space of a dynamical system from observations, learns a digital twin of the embedded dynamics, and performs targeted interventions within the learned dynamics to quantify intervention responses. Synthetic benchmarks show accurate recovery of causal topology and characteristic delays, while real‐world applications reveal interpretable spatiotemporal patterns of inferred causal influence consistent with domain knowledge. The framework integrates three key features: Joint modeling of causal relationships across spatial and temporal dimensions, intervention‐based inference grounded in reconstructed dynamical mechanisms, and a flexible state‐space reconstruction strategy that balances causal resolution with computational efficiency. By making the temporal organization of causal interactions directly accessible, ISTC provides a general framework for characterizing causal dependencies in complex spatiotemporal dynamical systems.

title: Histatin‐1 Restores ER‐Mitochondrial Coupling Through a Calreticulin–HSC70 Chaperone Axis to Promote Periodontal Bone Regeneration
abstract:
Histatin-1 restores endoplasmic reticulum-mitochondrial coordination in periodontal ligament stem cells under inflammatory conditions. By promoting calreticulin-HSC70 association, it improves calcium homeostasis and mitochondrial bioenergetics, alleviates endoplasmic reticulum stress, and supports osteogenic differentiation. These findings identify organelle coordination as a therapeutic target and highlight a salivary peptide strategy for enhancing periodontal bone regeneration. 

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-mitochondria contact sites (ERMCSs) are critical hubs for calcium homeostasis, metabolic coordination, and cell fate decisions, yet how inflammatory stress functionally destabilizes these interfaces remains poorly understood. Here, we show that inflammatory stimulation disrupts ERMCS integrity and bidirectional ER-mitochondrial calcium (Ca 2 
 + ) cycling in human mesenchymal stem cells, leading to unfolded protein response activation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired osteogenic differentiation. Mechanistically, inflammation compromises the functional engagement of the ER chaperone calreticulin at ERMCS, and we identify a previously unrecognized chaperone-mediated regulatory axis in which histatin-1 (Hst1) acts as a molecular scaffold bridging calreticulin and heat shock cognate protein 70 to stabilize ERMCS architecture and restore calcium cycling under inflammatory stress. Genetic disruption of any component of this axis phenocopies inflammatory defects in ERMCS stability, Ca 2 
 +  dynamics, and stem cell osteogenesis, whereas exogenous Hst1 reinstates ERMCS integrity, rescues osteogenic capacity, and accelerates bone regeneration in vivo. Together, these findings uncover a previously unappreciated, chaperone-mediated functional stabilization of ERMCS as a conserved mechanism linking inflammation to metabolic failure and regenerative impairment, and highlight ERMCS-targeted calcium rewiring as a potential therapeutic strategy.

title: Mechanistic Insight Into ROS‐Mediated Antibacterial Signaling Enables Hierarchical Hollow Polyhedral Nanozymes for Autonomous Bioelectronic Sensing and Synergetic Theranostics
abstract:
Hollow CuSe nanozymes integrate ROS-mediated catalytic activity with photothermal enhancement to achieve efficient bacterial inactivation. By coupling catalytic reactions with self-powered bioelectronic signal transduction, the developed platform enables sensitive dual-mode bacterial detection and synergistic antibacterial therapy, providing a versatile strategy for integrated bacterial sensing and treatment.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Postoperative bacterial infections remain a major clinical challenge, necessitating rapid and precise diagnosis alongside effective therapeutic intervention. Herein, we report a mechanism-driven platform integrating hierarchical hollow CuSe polyhedral nanozymes for autonomous bioelectronic sensing and synergistic antibacterial therapy. Guided by first-principles calculations, the engineered CuSe nanozymes facilitate interfacial electron transfer and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Integrated into an enzymatic biofuel cell (EBFC), the platform enables self-powered electrochemical and thermal dual-mode detection of  Salmonella  Typhimurium, achieving limits of detection (LOD) of 1.12 and 0.81 CFU mL −1 , respectively, over a linear range of 10–10 7  CFU mL −1 . Furthermore, CuSe exhibits a photothermal conversion efficiency of 45.53%, enabling enhanced ROS-mediated antibacterial activity under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation, with almost no visible bacterial colonies observed after 25 min of treatment. Transcriptomic analysis identified 88 differentially expressed genes, revealing alterations in metal ion homeostasis, oxidative stress responses, and bacterial metabolic pathways. Additionally, machine learning-assisted integration of electrochemical and thermal signals improves quantitative prediction performance compared with single-mode analysis. This study establishes an integrated strategy combining self-powered pathogen detection, synergistic antibacterial activity, and intelligent data analysis for potential point-of-care testing (POCT).

title: Phase‐Inverted Dual‐Resonant 2D Photonic Crystal Phosphor Enabling High Excitation‐Photon Absorptance (∼80%) and Enhanced Color Conversion
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
 Photonic crystal (PhC) phosphors have emerged as an effective platform for enhancing excitation-photon absorption through resonant light-matter interactions. In particular, an air-hole-based 2D PhC phosphor with a TiO 2  backbone layer enables strong light–matter interaction due to the significant refractive-index contrast between TiO 2  and colloidal quantum dots (CQDs). In this work, a phase-inverted, TiO 2  nanopillar-based 2D PhC phosphor is proposed to maximize the absorption of excitation photons. This achievement goal is further improved by intentionally overlapping both transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic guided Γ-point resonances with the excitation photon energy. Consequently, the fabricated PhC phosphor exhibits an absolute absorptance approaching A = 0.8 in the blue excitation wavelength region, accompanied by a significant CQD fluorescence enhancement factor (EF F ) of approximately 6.5. Therefore, the phase-inversion and dual-resonance overlap strategies provide a practical and effective route toward maximizing excitation-photon absorption in a structurally engineered PhC phosphor platform for high-performance color-conversion applications.

title: Spontaneous Intermolecular Cross‐Linking Produces Aβ Dimers With Multiple Alzheimer's Disease Relevant Activities
abstract:
SDS-stable Aβ dimers from AD brains exert disease relevant toxicity, but their formation mechanisms and contributions to AD pathogenesis remain incompletely understood. This work demonstrates that prolonged incubation of Aβ1-42 fibrils spontaneously produces dimers carrying the same covalent cross-links detected in AD brain. This time-dependent cross-linking is associated with changes in aggregate morphology and the emergence of multiple disease-relevant activities.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Despite success of therapies targeting the amyloid β-protein (Aβ), the molecular identity of the forms of Aβ which contribute to Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains poorly understood. SDS-stable Aβ dimers are present in higher-order aggregates and exert disease-relevant toxicity, but whether dimers form before or after large aggregates, or how dimers contribute to AD pathogenesis were previously unknown. Here, we report that covalently cross-linked Aβ1-42 dimers can form spontaneously upon prolonged incubation of Aβ fibrils and contain isopeptide bonds (Asp1-Glu22 and Asp1-Asp1), the same as those identified in dimers found in AD brain. Importantly, dimer-enriched Aβ aggregates (DEBA) are structurally distinct to dimer-poor aggregates (DPBA) and have enhanced resistance to proteolysis. Functionally, DEBA exhibit stronger binding to microglia, induce transcription of key pro-inflammatory cytokines, nucleate into plaque-like structures with microglia in vitro, and exacerbate amyloid deposition in  App 
 NL-F/NL-F  mice. DEBA do not appear to be overtly neurotoxic, whereas solubilized DEBA induce toxicities reminiscent of that caused by Aβ-containing AD brain extract. These findings demonstrate prolonged incubation of fibrillar Aβ aggregates results in spontaneous formation of cross-linked dimers, and this is associated with changes in aggregate morphology and emergence of multiple disease-relevant activities.

title: Anisotropic Energy Dissipation Governed by Phonon–Defect Interactions in Single‐Crystal Diamond
abstract:
We reveal pronounced crystallographic anisotropy in the mechanical dissipation of single‐crystal diamond cantilevers from 6.5 to 873 K. The orientation‐dependent Q factor peaks at a ratio of 3.5 near 200 K, consistent with a tetragonal elastic–dipole response of relaxing defects. These findings establish phonon–defect interactions as a route to engineering low‐loss diamond MEMS for quantum technologies.








ABSTRACT
The anisotropic mechanical dissipation of diamond MEMS resonators influence the performance of hybrid quantum systems. However, the anisotropic mechanical energy dissipation in diamond has never been examined. Here, the energy dissipation of single‐crystal diamond (SCD) microcantilever resonators oriented along the ⟨100⟩$\langle 100\rangle$ and ⟨110⟩$\langle 110\rangle$ directions is investigated over a broad temperature range of 6.5‐873 K. A pronounced orientation‐dependent Q$Q$ factor is observed: Q⟨110⟩/Q⟨100⟩$Q_{\langle 110\rangle }/Q_{\langle 100\rangle }$ is approximately 2 at room temperature, reaches a maximum of ≈3.5$\approx 3.5$ near 200 K, and approaches unity below 100 K. Through theoretical simulation, it is claimed that the full angular dependence of the mechanical dissipation is consistent with a tetragonal elastic–dipole response of the relaxing defects. These results establish crystallographic symmetry as a key factor governing mechanical energy dissipation in diamond, and identify both the tensorial elastic‐dipole response of lattice defects and anisotropic phonon–defect interactions as the underlying origins of the observed energy dissipation anisotropy. This work provides a framework for controlling mechanical energy losses through crystal orientation and defect engineering, and offers deep insight into strain‐mediated coupling between phonons and quantum defects in solid‐state quantum systems.

title: Machine‐Learning‐Driven Inverse Design of NURBS‐Parameterized Auxetic Piezoelectric Energy Harvesters for Self‐Powered Wireless Sensing
abstract:
A machine‐learning‐assisted inverse‐design framework enables stress‐aware optimization of NURBS‐parameterized auxetic piezoelectric energy harvesters. Continuous geometric control, neural‐network prediction, and NSGA‐II optimization discover high‐performance structures with enhanced power output and reduced stress concentration. The optimized device achieves 7.56 mW output power and integrates with a self‐powered LoRa sensing system for low‐frequency vibration monitoring.








ABSTRACT
Low‐frequency vibration energy is abundant in infrastructure, transportation, and industrial equipment, but piezoelectric harvesters face a power–stress‐concentration trade‐off: the large strain required for high output can intensify localized peak stress. In this paper, we develop a machine‐learning‐assisted inverse‐design framework for NURBS‐parameterized auxetic piezoelectric energy harvesters. NURBS control variables define a compact and continuous design space for curved re‐entrant lattices, expanding deformation and load‐transfer pathways beyond straight‐wall geometries. A finite‐element dataset generated by Latin hypercube sampling trains a neural‐network surrogate to predict maximum average output power and peak von Mises stress from geometric parameters. Coupling this surrogate with NSGA‐II enables co‐optimization of electrical output and stress concentration. The optimized geometry increases effective biaxial stress/strain in the piezoelectric layer while redistributing localized stress. Under 0.5 g excitation at resonance, the optimized harvester delivers 7.56mW$7.56\nobreakspace \mathrm{mW}$ maximum average output power and a normalized power density of 2.84×10−3mW/(mm3·g2·Hz)$2.84 \times 10^{-3}\nobreakspace \mathrm{mW}/(\mathrm{mm}^{3}\cdot \mathrm{g}^{2}\cdot \mathrm{Hz})$. Integrated with a self‐powered LoRa sensing node, the device transmits temperature data over 150m$150\nobreakspace \mathrm{m}$. This work offers a surrogate‐assisted route to high‐power, stress‐aware energy harvesters and energy‐autonomous IoT sensing.

title: Chronic Stress Associated Indoxyl Sulfate Upregulation Exhausts CD8+ T Cells to Decrease the Efficiency of Anti‐PD‐1 in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract:
Clinical data indicate that prolonged chronic stress is associated with inferior immunotherapy outcomes in HCC patients. Mechanistically, chronic stress upregulates hepatic SULT1A1, enhancing IS production. IS activates AHR signaling in tumor cells, inducing RNF115 transcription. Elevated RNF115 stabilizes HDAC8 through K27-linked ubiquitination-mediated inhibition of autophagic degradation, resulting in increased secretion of the immunosuppressive factor ANGPTL4, leading to CD8 +  T cells exhaustion.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Depressive symptoms are highly prevalent among patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet whether they influence the efficacy of immunotherapy and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Integrated analyses of a clinical cohort and murine models demonstrate that chronic stress-induced depressive-like states markedly attenuate the antitumor efficacy of anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) antibodies in HCC, accompanied by enhanced Tcell exhaustion. Mechanistically, chronic stress upregulates hepatic sulfotransferase 1A1 (SULT1A1) expression, thereby promoting the production of the tryptophan metabolite indoxyl sulfate (IS). IS does not directly act on CD8 +  T cells but activates the transcription factor aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) in HCC cells, upregulating the E3 ubiquitin ligase ring finger protein 115 (RNF115). RNF115 mediates lysine 27 (K27)-linked ubiquitination of histone deacetylase 8 (HDAC8) to inhibit its autophagic degradation. Stabilized HDAC8 enhances secretion of the immunosuppressive factor angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4), thereby contributing to CD8 +  Tcell exhaustion and reducing sensitivity to PD-1 inhibitors. Depletion or inhibition of HDAC8 significantly restores the antitumor efficacy of PD-1 therapy under chronic stress. Collectively, these findings support a chronic stress-SULT1A1-IS-AHR-RNF115-HDAC8 axis that drives immunotherapy resistance in HCC, suggesting a mechanistic link between emotional disturbance and tumor immune microenvironment remodeling.

title: A Nuclear Morphology‐Defined State Space Captures Cancer Cell Identity and State Transitions
abstract:
Nuclear shape reports cancer cell identity. In neuroblastoma, a nuclear morphology‐defined state space—built from nuclear features—non‐destructively annotates adrenergic and mesenchymal states at single‐cell resolution, concordant with transcriptomic and immunofluorescence readouts. It enables real‐time, single‐cell tracking of state transitions driven by ROCK and EZH2 inhibition.








ABSTRACT
Cancer cell identity and transitions among states reflect oncogenic mechanisms and predict clinical outcomes. These processes are typically defined through molecular profiling, yet such approaches remain limited in scalability and real‐time monitoring. In contrast, nuclear morphology provides a low‐dimensional state space that captures cellular identity and dynamic transitions. Using neuroblastoma as a model system, we establish a morphology‐based framework that maps individual cells within this state space and tracks their transitions as continuous trajectories. Morphology‐defined states show cell line‐level concordance with transcriptomic classifications and, at the single‐cell level, correspond to molecular and signaling features measured by immunofluorescence. Perturbations targeting Rho‐associated kinase signaling and enhancer of zeste homolog 2‐mediated epigenetic regulation drive convergent trajectories along a shared phenotypic axis. These results establish nuclear morphology as a state‐space representation of neuroblastoma cell identity, providing a practical framework for high‐throughput phenotyping and real‐time tracking of state transitions.

title: Hepatocyte Loss of TRMT61A Aggravates Liver Fibrosis by Driving ATF3‐Mediated Apoptosis and Macrophage Recruitment
abstract:
Hepatocyte-specific loss of  Trmt61a  exacerbates liver fibrosis by inducing the upregulation and nuclear translocation of ATF3. ATF3 transcriptionally activates CHOP and CCL2, triggering the endoplasmic reticulum stress-related apoptosis and CCL2-CCR2-dependent macrophage recruitment to amplify fibrotic progression.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Liver fibrosis is a common pathological consequence of chronic liver injury, but the hepatocyte-intrinsic mechanisms that initiate fibrogenic remodeling of the hepatic microenvironment remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify the RNA methyltransferase TRMT61A as a hepatocyte protective factor that is reduced in human fibrotic liver tissues and in experimental mouse models of liver fibrosis. Hepatocyte-specific deletion of  Trmt61a  was sufficient to trigger liver injury and progressive fibrosis, whereas restoration of enzymatically active TRMT61A restored m 1 A modification and ameliorated fibrosis. Mechanistically,  Trmt61a  deficiency activated the integrated stress response (ISR) marked by eIF2α phosphorylation and ATF3 induction, promoting hepatocyte apoptosis and CCL2 production. Transcriptomic and single-cell analyses revealed profound remodeling of the hepatic immune microenvironment, characterized by loss of embryonically derived Kupffer cells and accumulation of CCR2-positive monocyte-derived macrophages with pro-fibrotic inflammatory programs. Pharmacological CCR2/CCR5 blockade with cenicriviroc or hepatic  Atf3  knockdown reduced macrophage infiltration and attenuated fibrosis in  Trmt61a -deficient mice. These findings underscore the pivotal role of TRMT61A in regulating hepatocyte fate and remodeling the hepatic immune microenvironment during fibrosis progression, with the ISR–ATF3 axis serving as a central mechanistic hub. Restoring TRMT61A activity in hepatocytes thus represents a promising therapeutic strategy for preserving hepatocyte function and counteracting liver fibrosis.

title: Advancing MEMS Gas Sensors Through Intelligent Sensing Architectures and Stability Enhancement Strategies
abstract:
The next generation of MEMS gas sensors must combine accurate gas identification with long‐term operational stability. This review connects intelligent sensing architectures, machine learning, and degradation control to reveal how device design and signal interpretation shape performance, highlighting critical trade‐offs and emerging solutions for adaptive, low‐power gas sensors with sustained accuracy and real‐world reliability.








ABSTRACT
The growing demand for real‐time chemical monitoring has accelerated the development of micro‐electro‐mechanical systems (MEMS) gas sensors as compact, low‐power, and highly integrable sensing platforms. While remarkable progress in materials engineering and device miniaturization has enabled substantial improvements in sensing performance, challenges associated with gas selectivity, signal drift, and operational stability remain major barriers to real‐world deployment. Addressing these limitations increasingly requires the integration of intelligent sensing architectures with effective stability enhancement strategies. This review critically examines recent advances in MEMS gas sensors, focusing on the synergistic roles of intelligent sensing architectures and stability enhancement strategies. The major sensing architectures are discussed in terms of their operating principles, capabilities, and limitations, followed by intelligent sensing approaches that exploit dynamic sensing modes, sensor arrays, thermal modulation, and machine learning‐assisted analysis to enhance chemical discrimination and real‐time gas identification. The review further explores the mechanisms responsible for performance degradation and highlights engineering strategies for improving sensing accuracy, reproducibility, and long‐term reliability. By integrating device architecture, intelligent signal processing, and reliability‐oriented design, this review provides a unified framework for adaptive, scalable, and application‐ready MEMS gas sensors while identifying key challenges and opportunities that will shape the next generation of chemical sensing technologies.

title: Optoelectronic Decoupling Enables Synergistic Enhancement of Polarization Ratio and Sensitivity in on‐chip Photodetectors
abstract:
A spatially decoupled metasurface-Bi 2 O 2 Se photodetector separates polarization-selective surface plasmon excitation from photoconductive amplification. This filter-then-amplify strategy breaks the conventional trade-off between polarization ratio and polarization sensitivity, delivering a polarization ratio of ∼10 3  and a sensitivity exceeding 12 mA W −1 degree −1  at 1550 nm. Electrically tunable polarization-encoded imaging further demonstrates its applicability to integrated polarimetric sensing.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 On-chip polarization photodetectors are fundamental to integrated photonics, with the polarization ratio and polarization sensitivity as two critical metrics. However, conventional direct-excitation photodetectors inherently couple polarization selection with photoelectric conversion, preventing isolation of background photocurrent. Consequently, any attempt to enhance polarization sensitivity through electrical tuning indiscriminately amplifies this background together with the signal, degrading the polarization ratio and creating an inherent trade-off between the two metrics. Here, we propose an optoelectronic decoupling scheme that breaks this trade-off by implementing a filter-then-amplify indirect detection architecture. The metasurface suppresses unwanted background through polarization-selective surface plasmon excitation, theoretically enabling an infinite PR under ideal conditions, while the separated photoconductive unit amplifies the purified signal, boosting polarization sensitivity without background photocurrents. At 1550 nm, our photodetector achieves a polarization ratio of ∼10 3  and a two-order-of-magnitude enhancement in polarization sensitivity (> 12 mA∙W −1 ∙degree −1 ), and demonstrates electrically tunable polarization imaging contrast. This work provides an alternative paradigm for next-generation reconfigurable, high-information-density integrated systems.

title: M2 Macrophage‐Derived Galectin‐9 Enhances SLC1A5 Membrane Stability and Glutamine Metabolism to Promote Hepatocellular Carcinoma Progression
abstract:
Integrating scRNA‐seq, targeted metabolomics, proximity labeling, and clinical validation, we identify an M2 macrophage–HCC cell metabolic crosstalk axis. M2 macrophage‐derived Gal‐9 binds to the N‐glycans of the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 on HCC cells, thereby stabilizing its membrane localization and enhancing glutamine uptake and metabolism. This Gal‐9/SLC1A5 axis fuels the TCA cycle, ATP production, and mTORC1 activation, promoting HCC cell proliferation and migration while suppressing apoptosis. Targeting the Gal‐9‐SLC1A5 axis represents a potential therapeutic strategy for HCC.








ABSTRACT
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer‐related deaths globally. Current therapeutic options remain limited by poor efficacy, and there is an urgent need to identify new therapeutic targets and strategies. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of HCC progression, and intercellular crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment (TME) critically shapes tumor cell metabolism. However, the cell types and mechanisms regulating HCC cell metabolism remain largely unclear. In this study, by combining single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNA‐seq) and spatial transcriptomic data, we found that M2‐like tumor‐associated macrophages (TAMs) were associated with highly metabolic HCC cells. Using intercellular protein interaction detection (ICPID), a proximity‐labeling method developed in this study, we identified that Galectin‐9 (Gal‐9), highly expressed and secreted by M2 macrophages, is a ligand for the glutamine transporter SLC1A5 on HCC cells. This glycan‐dependent interaction promoted the membrane localization of SLC1A5, thereby enhancing glutamine uptake and metabolism to promote HCC growth. Gal‐9 neutralization or SLC1A5 inhibition suppressed glutamine metabolism and tumor‐promoting phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo. Our study shows that M2 macrophage‐derived Gal‐9 can promote HCC progression by directly enhancing glutamine metabolism in HCC cells, and that the Gal‐9‐SLC1A5 axis may serve as a new therapeutic target for HCC treatment.

title: Reusable and Reconfigurable Multistable Granular Mechanical Metamaterial for Programmable Energy Dissipation
abstract:
A granular mechanical metamaterial holds its cells by contact instead of bonds, so an assembly can be taken apart and recomposed after loading. Mixing cell types tunes peak force and stored energy together, and an inverted mixing rule returns the assembly that meets a chosen pair of targets.








ABSTRACT
Mechanical instabilities, when deliberately harnessed, offer a powerful route to reconfigurability and multifunctionality in architected materials. In multistable mechanical metamaterials, snap‐through instabilities of embedded structural elements are commonly used to access multiple distinct stable configurations under applied loading or actuation, modifying the bulk behavior. Here, we introduce granular multistable mechanical metamaterials and examine their behavior across two scales: a single unit cell and collective assemblies. At the unit cell level, we show how three identical arches embedded within a single unit cell can exhibit monostable or bistable sequential snap‐through responses, producing programmable, history‐dependent force‐displacement behavior. At the assembly scale, we demonstrate that many of these units interact to produce emergent cyclic responses. The macroscopic behavior is shaped by rearrangement and state evolution over repeated loading cycles, directly linking local snapping mechanisms to global mechanical properties. We map the range of responses across the full space of possible mixtures, and invert this map to design assemblies with prescribed responses. These materials show strong potential for applications in energy dissipation and shock absorption.

title: Chromatin Remodeling of RasGRP3 Underlies Temozolomide Sensitivity in Glioblastoma Organoids
abstract:
This work uncovers a previously unrecognized systematic decoding of the global regulatory axis of “enhancer-3D genome-transcriptome” in drug-resistant GBM by multi-omics sequencing and CRISPR screening. We utilized a convincing target screening method that aligns with the completely systematic logic of gene regulation, as 3D genome as a “direct contact map” between epigenetics and gene expression.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Acquired resistance to temozolomide (TMZ) constitutes a formidable clinical barrier in the management of glioblastoma (GBM). GBM organoid models (GBO) that faithfully mirror the parental tumor phenotype serve as powerful research instruments to overcome the limitations in this field. We established GBOs derived from primary glioma patients and their TMZ low-sensitivity counterparts. To unravel the intricate molecular underpinnings of this process, we performed an unbiased, integrated multi-omics analysis encompassing epigenomic, 3D genomic, and transcriptomic profiling, coupled with dual CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screening of TMZ-induced enhancers (TiEns) and their cognate target genes. Our findings demonstrate that enhancer-mediated 3D chromatin remodeling drives chemosensitivity predominantly by transcriptionally activating drug-sensitivity-associated genes, such as  RasGRP3, VEGFA, BTN3A2 , etc. Knockdown or knockout of these genes and enhancers renders glioma cells more sensitive to TMZ, especially  RasGRP3 . Our work unveils a druggable “enhancer-chromatin-target” signaling axis and proposes a novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy to surmount TMZ low sensitivity in GBM.

title: p‐PXN Downregulation Promotes Neovessel Stabilization and Improves Bone Defect Repair
abstract:
ECM stiffening induced an unstable, regression‐prone vascular phenotype via p‐PXN–Rac1‐mediated mechanotransduction, acting primarily by disrupting the balance between neovessel formation and vascular maturation. Downregulation of p‐PXN at the end of the angiogenic plateau promotes vessel stabilization.








ABSTRACT
Angiogenic‐osteogenic coupling occurs during bone regeneration. Vascularization during bone repair proceeds through three stages: sprouting, plateau, and regression. Insufficient vascularization due to vessel instability and premature regression underlies failed healing of critical‐sized bone defects. Maintaining neovessel stability is therefore crucial for achieving rapid bone regeneration. However, effectively sustaining vascular stability remains a major challenge. Here, we identify the p‐paxillin (p‐PXN)–RAC1 signaling pathway, activated by extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening, as a key mechanism driving vascular instability and regression. Bone matrix stiffness increases during the early phase of bone repair, accompanied by vigorous angiogenesis. Subsequently, as matrix stiffness continues to rise, vessel regression occurs. ECM stiffening increases angiogenic sprouting while decreasing pericyte recruitment and basement membrane component secretion, disrupting the balance between neovessel formation and vascular maturation, resulting in an unstable, regression‐prone vascular phenotype. Mechanistically, this process is driven by p‐PXN–RAC1‐mediated mechanotransduction. Downregulating p‐PXN at the end of the angiogenic plateau effectively promoted neovessel stabilization and boosted bone regeneration by 1.5‐fold. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of mechanotransduction in vascular stabilization, provide insights into the regulation of vascular homeostasis during bone regeneration, thereby establishing an innovative therapeutic strategy for bone defect repair.

title: Decorating Bacteria With Electrostatically Bound Liposomes as Programmable Extracellular Functional Compartments
abstract:
Bacteria are decorated with cationic liposomes via electrostatic self-assembly, creating modular biohybrid systems where synthetic compartments act as programmable extracellular modules. Liposome composition governs adsorption versus membrane fusion. Multicompartment architectures with tunable surface charge are demonstrated. Coated bacteria retain viability, motility, and gene expression while acquiring non-native capabilities including triggered cargo release and abiotic catalysis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Living cells are powerful programmable systems, yet efforts to engineer them are limited by the constraints of genetic modification, including metabolic burden, restricted chemical diversity of biomolecular systems, and slow, gene expression–driven responses. Complementary approaches augmenting cells without altering their genome offer an attractive route to expand their functionality. Here, we establish a strategy for equipping bacteria with synthetic extracellular organelle-like compartments by electrostatically assembling liposomes onto the surface of  Escherichia coli . This approach yields stable, multi-compartment, high-density coatings without genetic or covalent modification, while preserving bacterial growth, gene expression, and motility. We show that these surface-bound liposomes can function as modular compartments that operate alongside the cell, enabling capabilities that are difficult to realize genetically, including thermoresponsive cargo release and abiotic catalytic activity. Together, this work shows that bacteria–liposome biohybrids can be engineered with appended, tunable synthetic compartments to expand the functional repertoire of living cells.

title: An Intra‐BET Epigenetic Mechanism Driven by BRD4 Controls Pancreatic α‐Cell Expansion
abstract:
A targeted PROTAC screen identifies BET proteins as key regulators of pancreatic α‐cell biology. A KMT5B‐modulated BRD4‐BRD2 regulatory mechanism coordinates α‐cell proliferation and differentiation, while combined BRD4 activation and BRD2 suppression promote endocrine differentiation and enhance α‐cell features in human islet organoids, revealing a previously unrecognized mode of intra‐BET epigenetic regulation.








ABSTRACT
Pancreatic α cells play essential roles in maintaining glucose homeostasis. However, the epigenetic mechanisms governing α‐cell proliferation and differentiation remain poorly understood. Here, we performed a systematic screen of a targeted PROTAC library and identified BET proteins as key regulators of α‐cell proliferation and function. Single‐cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that BRD4 promotes the acquisition of an intermediate endocrine progenitor‐like state in progenitor cells. In vivo, α‐cell‐specific deletion of Brd4 markedly reduced α‐cell mass and suppressed Men1‐driven pathological α‐cell proliferation, demonstrating that BRD4 is required for the establishment and/or maintenance of α‐cell identity and abundance in vivo. Mechanistically, we identified the histone methyltransferase KMT5B as a BRD4‐interacting protein and demonstrated that BRD4 directly binds to and represses the BRD2 promoter, with this BRD4‐BRD2 regulation being modulated by KMT5B. Combined BRD4 overexpression and BRD2 suppression accelerated endocrine differentiation, reduced progenitor identity, enhanced α‐cell features, and increased glucagon secretion in human islet organoids. Collectively, our study identifies a previously unrecognized KMT5B‐modulated BRD4‐BRD2 regulatory mechanism that coordinates pancreatic α‐cell proliferation and differentiation, providing new insights into intra‐BET epigenetic regulation during α‐cell development and functional maturation.

title: Direct Electro‐Optic Transduction of Neurophysiological Signals for Multichannel Recording Using Ion‐Gated Graphene Integrated Photonics
abstract:
An ion‐gated graphene‐integrated photonic sensor directly converts extracellular neural potentials into optical signals through electrolyte gating and resonant enhancement, achieving ∼20 µV detectability and near‐direct current‐to‐90 kHz bandwidth. Ex vivo brain tissue recordings and 10‐channel wavelength‐division multiplexing on a single bus waveguide demonstrate a novel method of label‐free electro‐optic electrophysiology recording using a compact, scalable neural interface.








ABSTRACT
Large‐scale neural recording with high spatiotemporal resolution is essential for mapping distributed brain activity. However, scaling the number of simultaneously recorded channels in implantable electrical probes places growing demand on interconnects, multiplexing, and readout electronics. Functional optical imaging enables parallel readout but requires fluorescent labels or genetic modification. Emerging label‐free optical approaches rely on bulky free‐space configurations or surface‐level detection. Here, we introduce an ion‐gated graphene‐integrated photonic platform that directly transduces neurophysiological signals into wavelength‐multiplexed optical channels. The sensor integrates monolayer graphene with an on‐chip photonic microresonator. Extracellular potentials modulate graphene's electrochemical potential through the graphene–electrolyte electrical double layer. This change in graphene’s electrochemical potential modulates its absorption and thereby alters the optical  transmission through the resonator‐coupled waveguide. This mechanism enables optical encoding of neural signals without exogenous labels, genetic modification, or conventional electrode‐based electrical readout. Because each microresonator can operate at a distinct wavelength, arrays of sensors can share a single bus waveguide using wavelength‐division multiplexing. We demonstrate a detection limit of 20 µV at a signal‐to‐noise ratio of 3 dB and show label‐free recording of evoked neurophysiological signals from mouse brain tissue, including multiplexed recording from 10 sensors along a single waveguide. These results establish ion‐gated graphene‐integrated photonics as a compact and scalable platform for wavelength‐multiplexed, label‐free neural recording and future implantable photonic neural interfaces.

title: Biomimetic Ferroptosis‐Immunoreprogramming Nanotherapy Orchestrates Macrophage Polarization to Resolve Acute Lung Injury
abstract:
