Here, we develop a macrophage-membrane–camouflaged biomimetic nanoparticle (MM@HST–Mg NPs) to precisely target inflammatory macrophages and inhibit macrophage ferroptosis in acute lung injury. By integrating hesperetin–Mg 2 
 +  coordination with homologous membrane targeting, the nanoplatform synergistically scavenges ROS, chelates Fe 2 
 + , and activates the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 antioxidant pathway. This subsequently suppresses macrophage-associated ferroptotic stress, promotes anti-inflammatory macrophage polarization, and ultimately alleviates LPS-induced lung inflammation and injury. 

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Acute lung injury (ALI) is a severe inflammatory disorder with limited effective targeted therapies. Macrophage-associated ferroptotic stress contributes significantly to uncontrolled pulmonary inflammation, making it a promising therapeutic target for ALI treatment. Here, we report biomimetic macrophage membrane-coated hesperetin (HST)-magnesium (Mg 2 
 + ) nanoparticles (MM@HST-Mg NPs) that integrate inflammation-targeted delivery with ferroptosis modulation for the treatment of lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced ALI. The macrophage membrane coating enabled MM@HST-Mg NPs preferentially accumulate in inflamed lungs and be predominantly taken up by pulmonary macrophages. Compared with free HST or HST-Mg, MM@HST-Mg NPs exhibited superior therapeutic efficacy. They alleviated macrophage-associated ferroptotic stress by scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS), reducing intracellular Fe 2 
 +  accumulation, suppressing lipid peroxidation, and activating the Nrf2/HO-1/GPX4 antioxidant pathway. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) demonstrated that Mg 2 
 +  coordination enhanced the interaction between HST and Nrf2. Furthermore, Nrf2 knockdown and pharmacological inhibition confirmed that the anti-ferroptotic and macrophage-reprogramming effects of MM@HST-Mg NPs were largely dependent on Nrf2 signaling. These coordinated effects promoted macrophage polarization toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype, attenuated pulmonary inflammation, and effectively protected mice against LPS-induced ALI following early intervention. Overall, this study establishes a biomimetic macrophage-targeted nanoplatform for ferroptosis modulation and provides a rational strategy for developing immunoregulatory nanomedicines for acute inflammatory lung injury.

title: Nepenthes‐Inspired Superhydrophobic Porous Lightweight Concrete With a CO2‐Activated Dual‐Level Energy Barrier for Dynamic Anti‐Wetting
abstract:
Using CO 2  as a trigger transforms porous lightweight concrete into a water-repellent, anti-icing, and corrosion-resistant material. In coupled environments of moisture, shock temperature, and corrosive ions, a trapped-air pore network and a siloxane-modified calcite layer form a dual-energy barrier that blocks water invasion, slows heat transfer, and stabilizes dynamic anti-wetting under demanding service conditions for future smart infrastructure.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Bioinspired porous concrete with a superhydrophobic surface offers multifunctionality for anti-icing, anti-corrosion, and thermal insulation, meeting the adaptable demands of modern infrastructure. However, scalable fabrication of robust hydrophobic microstructures in porous cementitious materials remains challenging. Herein, inspired by the low-pinning dynamic anti-wetting of Nepenthes interfaces, an in situ carbonation strategy using CO 2  is developed to construct porous concretes with a dual-level superhydrophobic energy barrier. Intrinsic rough pores trap air to reduce solid–liquid contact as the first barrier, and siloxane-coated calcite layers mineralized on pore surfaces act as the second barrier, impeding wetting advance. Under optimal conditions: porous concrete with a density of 600 kg/m 3 , a poly (methyl hydrogen) siloxane (PMHS) usage of 600 g/m 2 , 48 h CO 2  curing (100% CO 2 , and 95% RH), exhibits a long-term Cassie-Baxter (CB) state with a water contact angle (CA) of ∼160°, low water absorption of 3.6%, icing delay time of 2350 s at −20°C, low ice adhesion of 15 kPa and anti-corrosion for reinforced rebar. The ∼1 µm calcite layer theoretically enhances water-droplet motion by six times compared with the uncarbonated surface. Under coupled water, icing, and elevated-temperature conditions, the dual energy barrier suppresses heat and mass transfer, making it a promising candidate for lightweight, durable, anti-icing, and thermally insulating material.

title: YAP/TAZ‐TEAD as an Executor of Focal Adhesion Mechanotransduction Suppressed by the Hippo Pathway
abstract:
The predicted working model illustrates that the YAP/TAZ-TEAD transcriptional complex is governed by the balanced action of the positive focal adhesion mechanotransduction pathway and the negative Hippo pathway.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Although the Hippo pathway is a well-established negative regulator of the YAP/TAZ–TEAD1–4 transcriptional complex, the molecular mechanisms that actively sustain YAP/TAZ–TEAD activation remain poorly defined. Integrating recent literature with systematic Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap) codependency analysis, we propose a working model wherein the TAZ/YAP–TEAD complex functions as a nuclear executor of the focal adhesion mechanotransduction cascade. This mechanotransduction arm is predicted to initiate at the plasma membrane by integrins α 
    v 
 β 5  (ITGAV/ITGB5), N-cadherin (CDH2), and lysophosphatidic acid receptor 1 (LPAR1), which likely engage PKN2 and MARK2/3 signaling kinases downstream of the focal adhesion complex. Conversely, a cell-surface triad comprising NRP1, PLXNA1, and KIRREL1 and EPHA2 may act as an upstream activator of the inhibitory Hippo pathway. Collectively, we propose that TAZ/YAP–TEAD activity is governed by a dynamic, reciprocal antagonism between the Hippo pathway and focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, with the latter serving as a positive driver sustaining YAP/TAZ functional activity.

title: Mapping Mesoscale Cardiac Architecture With Axially Swept Dithered Light‐Sheet Microscopy
abstract:
A dual‐actuator light‐sheet strategy integrates rapid beam dithering with synchronized axial sweeping to extend the effective confocal region and accelerate mesoscale volumetric imaging while maintaining micrometer‐scale optical sectioning across intact hearts. The platform enables efficient visualization, segmentation, and topological analysis of myocardial architecture and vascular networks from embryonic to adult stages.








ABSTRACT
Comprehensive characterization of cardiac microstructure and vascular networks is critical for assessing cardiovascular development, disease progression, and therapeutic interventions. While volumetric imaging combined with tissue clearing enables high‐resolution organ‐level analysis, the densely organized cardiac microenvironment, characterized by compacted and trabeculated myocardium, remains technically challenging to resolve in its entirety. To address these limitations, we exploit the temporal dynamics of illumination‐detection interplay to create a time‐averaged beam profile, thereby maximizing system throughput across multi‐scale specimens. Our dithered light‐sheet (DiLS) approach extends the confocal region by over 40% and improves the space‐bandwidth product while largely preserving optical sectioning capability. Building on this, the axially swept dithered light‐sheet (AS‐DiLS) employs a dual‐actuator strategy that combines rapid beam dithering and axial sweeping to further accelerate imaging speed while achieving micrometer‐scale resolution across centimeter‐scale scanning ranges, enabling detailed cardiovascular morphological and topological assessment from embryonic to adult stages. We anticipate that this scalable imaging scheme will advance in‐depth investigations of organ morphogenesis and disease pathogenesis across a broad spectrum of models.

title: Carbene Generation in Endoplasmic Reticulum for O2‐Independent Tumor Photo‐Immunotherapy via Synergism of Ferroptosis and Apoptosis
abstract:
Hypoxia severely limits conventional photodynamic therapy. This study presents  ER-N , an ER-targeting photosensitizer that operates independently of oxygen. By simultaneously triggering ferroptosis and apoptosis via severe ER stress,  ER-N  effectively eliminates resistant hypoxic tumors and stimulates potent antitumor immunity, offering a robust strategy for precision cancer photoimmunotherapy.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Hypoxia, a hallmark feature of the tumor microenvironment, not only compromises the effectiveness of conventional oxygen-dependent photosensitizers (PSs) but also contributes to enhanced tumor malignancy and immunosuppression. To address these challenges, we developed an endoplasmic reticulum (ER) targeting PS,  ER-N , which showed O 2 -independent photoinduced carbene formation, and could activate robust antitumor immune activation via synergistic induction of ferroptosis and apoptosis. Mechanistically,  ER-N  induces severe ER stress via activating the inositol-requiring enzyme 1 (IRE-1) and PKR-like ER-resident kinase (PERK) pathways, resulting in apoptotic cell death. Concurrently,  ER-N  significantly triggers ferroptosis through light-mediated downregulation of multiple ferroptosis-suppressing proteins, including glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), thioredoxin (TRX), solute carrier 7A11 (SLC7A11), and ferroptosis suppressor protein 1 (FSP1). This approach is particularly advantageous for overcoming intractable tumor cells that exhibit both apoptosis resistance and one or two mechanisms that suppress ferroptosis. Notably,  ER-N  not only maintains high phototoxicity under hypoxia comparable to that under normoxia, but also induces distinct immunogenic cell death (ICD) and promotes immune activation signatures in vivo. This study establishes a robust strategy for designing high-performance PSs against hypoxic tumors, offering significant potential for advancing precision cancer photoimmunotherapeutics.

title: Quantifying Homology and Length Bias in Antimicrobial Peptide Prediction
abstract: Bacteria are becoming resistant to existing antibiotics faster than new ones are found. Antimicrobial peptides are a promising alternative, but laboratory testing is slow and costly. Candidates are therefore ranked first by a classifier, and published classifiers report near-perfect accuracy. Two controls are missing from the benchmarks behind those numbers. Training and test peptides are not separated by sequence homology. The negative class is not matched to the positive class by length. We propose a controlled evaluation protocol that imposes both, plus a sample-size control that separates matching from the data it removes. We apply it to a four-model ensemble of our own and ten baselines on a benchmark of 16,168 sequences, holding the models fixed. A classifier given nothing but peptide length separates the benchmark far above chance. Homology control costs 0.067 MCC and length matching a further 0.115, taking the reported score from 0.834 to 0.661. Over ten redrawn partitions the length term holds while the homology term shrinks, so length is the effect that survives. The protocol also reorders the methods, and a frozen ESM-2 embedding overtakes the ensemble. Three published benchmarks show the same pattern. We recommend a minimum reporting standard that makes such losses visible.

title: The assembly and annotation of a new reference genome for the eastern mosquitofish (Gambusia holbrooki) reveal a new sex chromosome system in its invasive range
abstract: Gambusia species, especially eastern mosquitofish - Gambusia holbrooki - are of broad relevance to evolutionary biologists aiming at understanding genomic bases of adaptation during biological invasions and rapid response to selection to heterogeneous environments including pollution. Here we used HiFi and HiC to assemble a new, high quality, chromosome scale, genome sequence for G. holbrooki in its invasive range. Both haplotypes of the nuclear genome were assembled, comprising 657.64 Mb and 651.75 Mb respectively, in 24 chromosomes and had N50s of 28.97 Mb and 28.25 Mb. They had 94.87% and 94.29% BUSCO scores, illustrating a high completeness. Genome annotation yielded 25146 genes, which is comparable to other recent genome annotations of poecilid fish species. Repeat content was 25.69%, similar to what was previously reported for this species and for G. affinis. Synteny was highly conserved between the G. holbrooki assembly and the reference genome for G. affinis and Xiphophorus maculatus, shown here to be a genetically close species, with very few inter-chromosomal and little intra-chromosomal rearrangements. Mapping of resequenced males and females to the reference genome provided genomic evidence for a newly evolved homomorphic sex chromosome pair (W and Z, hence with female heterogamety) in G. holbrooki's invaded range, which is unlike the XY system of its native range. Also, the new sex chromosomes are homologous to the ZW sex chromosome pair (chromosome 1) of the sister species G. affinis. This assembly provides a high quality reference genome for Gambusia holbrooki, in its invasive range in Europe, that is serving as a key resource for research on the genomics of invasion and of rapid adaptation to environmental change, pollution adaptation and sex determination evolution.

title: A compartmentalised cochlear ageing programme: weak systemic concordance and a distinct macrophage compartment
abstract: Whether the ageing cochlea follows the systemic ageing programmes defined by multi-organ atlases is unknown. We integrated single-nucleus RNA-sequencing data for 13,988 mouse cochlear nuclei (3, 12 and 24 months) with the Tabula Muris Senis atlas (16 droplet-based and 12 Smart-seq2 fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) sources). Cross-organ alignment of ageing programmes was quantified by genome-wide vector correlation, pre-ranked gene-set enrichment and a systemic ageing score. Cochlear ageing showed weak but significant genome-wide concordance with systemic ageing (Spearman rho 0.01-0.12), with lineage-matched pairs ranking among the highest. In contrast, systemic tissue ageing-up signatures, dominated by immune and inflammatory programmes, were depleted from the ageing-up rankings of cochlear non-sensory epithelial cells (normalised enrichment score -1.45, adjusted p = 0.032) and, for the immune-organ signatures, from cochlear macrophages. The cochlear macrophage ageing vector correlated positively with tissue-resident macrophages of peripheral organs (kidney rho = 0.056, 95% confidence interval 0.016-0.063, p = 1.6 x 10^-13; microglia rho = 0.034, p = 1.4 x 10^-6), negatively with bone-marrow and splenic macrophages, and not with lymphocytes. A systemic ageing score increased with age in spiral ganglion neurons, Schwann cells, inner hair cells, epithelial cells, and fibrocytes, but not in cochlear macrophages. These cell-type-resolved analyses support a compartmentalised view of cochlear ageing: non-immune compartments track systemic ageing weakly, the immune arm is reversed, and cochlear macrophages age along a tissue-resident rather than haematopoietic programme.

title: MARRI: Mechanism-Aware Learning of RNA-RNA Interactions with Foundation Models
abstract: RNA-RNA interactions (RRIs) are central to post-transcriptional regulation, yet their prediction requires accounting for structural accessibility and intermolecular base pairing beyond sequence complementarity. Pretrained RNA foundation models provide representations of individual RNAs, but translating these representations into interaction predictions requires mechanistic knowledge of interaction recognition. Here, we introduce MARRI, a mechanism-aware multimodal framework that couples pretrained representations with domain knowledge by embedding learned opening penalties and hybridization gains into bidirectional cross-RNA attention. MARRI improves ROC--AUC and PR--AUC over the strongest baseline by 12.20% and 10.25%, respectively, and maintains strong discrimination for unseen RNA partnerships and interaction regions. Perturbation and repeat-context analyses identify prediction-relevant sequence regions. Integrating MARRI-derived interaction propensities with disease-associated expression profiles links molecular prediction to systems-level models of disease progression and network remodeling. MARRI thus illustrates a knowledge-guided strategy for coupling molecular foundation models with domain knowledge to support grounded prediction, interpretation and systems-level hypothesis generation.

title: Comparative metagenomics reveals diversity and metabolic heterogeneity of sediment microbes from the Great Barrier Reef
abstract: Microbial communities in coral reefs are highly connected through benthic-pelagic coupling. Pelagic and host-associated microbiomes have recently been characterised via genome-resolved metagenomics. However, similar characterisation of sediment communities has lagged behind due to their higher complexity. Here, using short- and long-read shotgun sequence data, we characterised sediment microbial communities of Australia's Great Barrier Reef. From 191 samples across 48 broadly distributed sites, we recovered 2,698 prokaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) representing 1,201 species-level clusters, most of which are novel. Compared against their sympatric counterparts in seawater, sediment MAGs exhibited greater phylogenetic diversity and flexibility in metabolic potential, implicating diverse respiration strategies and cycling of nitrogen, sulphur, and hydrogen. They also encode more abundant and novel biosynthetic capabilities, likely reflecting competition and adaptation to intermittent fluctuations in nutrient regimes, and between oxic and anoxic conditions. Our results provide foundational genomic resources for reef sediment microbes, uncovering biodiversity and function that together with planktonic microbes shape the ecological success and stability of coral reef ecosystems.

title: spicyR enables robust, well-powered co-localisation tests in large spatial omics cohorts
abstract: Spatial omics technologies can now profile finely resolved cell populations in patient tissue at scale, offering a way to link their arrangement to outcomes. Yet images often differ in size, shape and cell content, and existing tests between patient groups mistake these differences for co-localisation or weight every image equally. We present spicyR v2, which avoids both problems with a fast, permutation-free test that accounts for these differences and weights each image by how precisely it measures co-localisation. In simulations and 74 analyses of 42 public datasets, it controlled false discoveries, had more power than spicyR v1 and was robust to tears, holes and differences in cell number that misled other methods. These analyses also revealed that many studies relating co-localisation to clinical outcomes are underpowered, and spicyR v2 can estimate the number of patients a new study needs. spicyR v2 analyses 100 million cells in minutes, making robust, well-powered tests of co-localisation practical for large spatial omics cohorts.

title: The Caenorhabditis elegans pangenome elucidates hyper-divergent region gene content to reveal extensive gene copy-number variation and a novel anthelmintic resistance locus
abstract: Caenorhabditis elegans has been a keystone model in biological research since the early 1970s, and it was the first metazoan to have its genome sequenced and assembled in 1998. Over the last few decades, the genetic and genomic resources developed for C. elegans made it one of the most powerful models for understanding metazoan biology. Recently, the C. elegans community has collected over 2,000 globally distributed wild strains, which after whole-genome sequencing, were found to contain punctuated regions of extreme genetic variation, called hyper-divergent regions (HDRs). HDRs have been described in organisms across the tree of life, including plants and humans, and genes in HDRs appear to be involved in adaptation, such as environmental response genes, parasitism genes, or immunity genes. However, the extreme genetic divergence at these loci complicates short-read alignments, and the genomic content of these regions in non-reference strains is largely uncharacterized. To define the gene content in HDRs, we de novo assembled and annotated genomes of 140 genetically diverse strains. These data enabled the construction of the first gene-based pangenome for the species. Among these strains, we characterized the landscape of structural variation and developed novel methods to quantify gene content diversity. We found that both variable copy-number and stable-copy environmental response genes were enriched in HDRs. These results further suggest that these regions have an important evolutionary role in adaptation to heterogeneous environments. We leveraged this pangenome to elucidate gene content in previously identified quantitative trait loci associated with adaptive traits. In one HDR, we found large deletions, spanning multiple genes, that are correlated with resistance to the anthelmintic drug abamectin. The C. elegans pangenome provides novel insights into genome and gene family evolution in a genetically diverse animal species, and empowers deeper investigations of genotype-phenotype relationships underlying adaptive traits, particularly in the context of structural and gene copy-number variation.

title: Integrating disease and protein networks expands genetic support for therapeutic targets
abstract: Human genetics guides therapeutic target selection, but direct genetic support covers few clinically investigated target-indication pairs, each linking a target to a disease. Here we introduce BRIDGE (Biological Relation-Informed Diffusion of Genetic Evidence), which propagates genetic evidence through coupled protein-protein interaction and disease-similarity networks. Each candidate's score is calibrated against scores obtained after randomly substituting similarly connected genes for genes with direct genetic support. In a retrospective benchmark of 13,022 pairs that had reached at least phase I, BRIDGE supported 572 additional pairs, increasing coverage from 5.1% to 9.5%. Among eligible pairs lacking direct genetic support, 25.3% of network-added pairs had reached launch versus 8.6% of remaining candidates (relative success, 2.94; 95% confidence interval, 2.51-3.45). This enrichment extended to 158 pairs involving 101 genes with no direct genetic support in the benchmark. At a matched selection size of 1,310 pairs, BRIDGE ranking captured 265 launched pairs, compared with 223 under a rule transferring support across neighbouring targets or indications. These findings show that coupling disease relationships with protein connectivity expands the reach of human genetics to additional therapeutic targets and indications while retaining clinical relevance.

title: GenVinci reconstructs 3D molecular tissue scenes from histology to map senescence across aging and disease
abstract: Spatial omics has generated measurements at unprecedented scale, yet computational approaches remain largely confined to individual modalities and 2D representations. Here we assemble ImageOmicsNet-300M, a corpus of 300 million single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiles, including 24.9 million H&E-predicted virtual spatial transcriptomics profiles, and 4,623 H&E sections. Of these H&E sections, we generated 1,782 from aging mouse organs and serially sectioned human skin spanning five decades, with matched spatial transcriptomics and snRNA-seq. Building on this resource, we develop GenVinci, a multimodal tissue foundation model that reconstructs 3D tissue scenes from routine 2D histology. GenVinci predicts spatial gene expression from H&E with zero-shot generalization and maps senescence-associated states across 85.8 million cells, revealing cell-type-specific patterns and disease-associated remodeling. Integration with human genetics implicates suprabasal keratinocytes in atopic dermatitis and keratinocyte carcinomas, linked to higher and lower p16 and p21 expression, respectively. These findings establish GenVinci as a framework mapping senescence in 3D across scales.

title: Genome assembly for Amanita muscaria var. muscaria
abstract: Amanita muscaria is a charismatic and widely distributed mushroom-forming fungus. Amanita muscaria comprises a species complex, and genomic resources are unevenly distributed, which may bias genetic and genomic study of the species complex. This study produces a high quality hybrid genome assembly of a specimen from New Zealand. Phylogenetic analysis shows that this belongs to Amanita muscaria var. muscaria.

title: CIRCA learns identifiable cell- and niche-level programs and their interactions with tissue pathology from spatial transcriptomics
abstract: Interactions among cells and their local microenvironments shape tissue organization and function, while their dysregulation can contribute to disease. In Alzheimer's disease (AD), the complex responses of glial cells and neurons to amyloid-{beta} pathology can both mitigate and exacerbate neuronal injury. Spatial transcriptomics enables investigation of these relationships in situ, but recovering interpretable transcriptional programs and their interactions from spatial transcriptomics remains challenging, in part because conventional nonlinear models are non-identifiable. Here we present CIRCA (Causal Interaction Representation for Cellular Architectures), a self-supervised causal representation learning framework that jointly learns identifiable cell- and neighborhood-level transcriptional programs and the directed interactions among them under explicit assumptions. It can also be extended to incorporate additional modalities such as pathology. Benchmarked against five existing methods across seven cell-resolution datasets, CIRCA achieved the highest biological accuracy in six and the highest overall score in all five multi-section datasets, while recovering higher-order anatomical organization. In an AD mouse model, incorporating amyloid-{beta} pathology revealed four region-specific plaque niches enriched for microglia. Plaque-associated microglia shared a core disease-associated response whose strength varied by region, and AD genetic risk was preferentially enriched in hippocampal and cortical plaque-associated microglia. Reproducible latent factors linked to cell-level amyloid burden separated phagocytic from inflammatory microglial programs. Applied to a human colorectal cancer dataset, CIRCA resolved patient-specific tumor niches, conserved stromal remodeling niches, and distinct macrophage states, highlighting its versatility. Together, these results establish CIRCA as a methodological advance over existing approaches, enabling deeper insights into tissue organization and the molecular dependencies linking cells to their local environments.

title: Spatiotemporal profiling reveals emergence of cell type-specific molecular aging and senescence programs in the spinal cord
abstract: The spinal cord is the primary relay center between the periphery and the brain, playing a critical role in sensory, motor and autonomic function. Despite its functional importance, the cellular and molecular changes underlying spinal cord aging and their relationship to cellular senescence - a hallmark associated with aging - remain incompletely understood. Here, we generated a cross-species, multi-omic atlas of spinal cord aging in mice and humans by integrating a combination of liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, Visium spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing, and multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging. We identified converging age-associated increases in fibrinogen, laminin, and immune activation-associated proteins across the mouse and human spinal cord. Over the mouse lifespan, we further identified distinct spatiotemporal patterns of aging. Downregulated transcriptional programs, including synaptic signaling, mitochondrion organization, and autophagy, were most highly expressed in grey matter regions and in neurons. Upregulated transcriptional programs, including vascular and immune processes, were enriched in white matter regions and in endothelial cells and microglia, respectively. Notably, these increasing spatial modules were also enriched for senescence-associated genes. In the human spinal cord, endothelial cells and microglia were also most enriched for canonical senescence markers CDKN1A and CDKN2A, respectively. Overall, this study defines the shared, spatially-resolved, cell type-specific features associated with aging and senescence in the mouse and human spinal cord.

title: Fine-tuned DNA sequence language models for predicting gene expression in admixed population: A comparison with variant-based methods
abstract: Predicting gene expression from whole genome sequencing data is essential for elucidating regulatory mechanisms and interpreting functional consequences of non-coding variants to complex diseases. While traditional approaches rely on variant-based linear models, DNA sequence-based language models have gained increasing popularity for their ability to learn regulatory features directly from whole genome sequence data. Previous studies have evaluated models such as Enformer, but newer sequence-to-function models, including Borzoi and AlphaGenome, remain less well characterized for individual-level gene expression prediction, particularly in non-European and admixed populations. Here, we evaluated and fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome using personal genomes paired with whole-blood RNA-seq data from the Hispanic Community Health Study/Study of Latinos (HCHS/SOL). Fine-tuning substantially improved the performance of both sequence-based models compared with their pretrained versions; however, their performances remained similar to that of the variant-based linear models. Leveraging the ancestral diversity of HCHS/SOL, we found that Borzoi and AlphaGenome showed similar performance across Amerindian-, European-, and African-enriched groups. Fine-tuned Borzoi, fine-tuned AlphaGenome and elastic net performed modestly better when trained and evaluated in the same ancestry-enriched group. Finally, we explored strategies to improve prediction performance and found that incorporating predicted epigenetic features improved prediction near the promoter region. Significant progress remains needed before the full potential of sequence-based models is attained. Incorporating more biology-guided training approaches could be helpful to achieving better performance.

title: Transposase-mediated activity is associated with accessory gene turnover and positive-selection signals in Streptococcus pyogenes
abstract: Streptococcus pyogenes causes diseases ranging from mild pharyngitis to life-threatening invasive infection, yet the genomic determinants of this variation remain poorly understood. We analyzed 1,863 publicly available genomes, whose pangenome comprises 6,568 genes (1,392 core and soft-core, 656 shell, and 4,520 cloud), and grouped isolates into 15 genetic groups with FastBAPS. Ten groups were monophyletic on the global phylogeny, and non-monophyly of the remaining five largely reflected the placement of isolates from group 12, which is dispersed across the tree. A GenomegaMap scan identified 163 of 3,147 genes with {omega} > 1. These genes were depleted among core genes and enriched among cloud genes, a pattern consistent with positive selection on recently acquired genes but also with the retention of slightly deleterious variation in young genes. A putative IS transposase (K07497) was the most consistent functional enrichment signal, which led us to analyze insertion sequence (IS) elements directly. In group 12, complete IS copies within genomes were more often near-identical than in other groups (OR = 1.46), consistent with more recent IS activity, and genes with {omega} > 1 were 2.9 times more likely than other accessory genes to lie within 5 kb of an IS element (8.8% vs. 3.0%; permutation p = 0.0006) after excluding IS-encoded genes. We did not detect this association in any other group, and most genes under selection were not IS-proximal.

title: Multimodal Structural and Regulatory Architecture of Coding and Non-Coding Variants Across the Orofacial Clefting TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 Network
abstract: Pathogenic variation across the TP63-IRF6-GRHL3 transcriptional network causes syndromic and nonsyndromic orofacial clefts (OFCs), yet scalar sequence predictors collapse distinct failure modes and leave isoform-specific coding variants, splice-altering indels, and distal enhancer alleles unresolved. Here, we integrate 29 AlphaFold 3 (AF3) assemblies (10 wild-type, 19 mutant), thermodynamic stability ({Delta}{Delta}G) calculations, and AlphaGenome regulatory modeling across clinical, saturation-mutagenesis, and reporter benchmarks. In strict leave-one-gene-out (LOGO) coding benchmarks, replacing paralog crystal templates with full-length human AF3 structures improves IRF6 classification (biophysical AUROC rising from 0.7844 to 0.8967; {Delta}{Delta}G from 0.6461 to 0.8516) and resolves canonical isoform gaps in the 602-residue MANE Select GRHL3 homodimer. Projecting IRF6 missense variants onto a two-dimensional stability-versus-interface phase plane separates dominant-negative popliteal pterygium syndrome (PPS) poisons from haploinsufficient Van der Woude syndrome (VWS1) alleles (VWS1-versus-PPS Quadrant I odds ratio [OR] = 0.0263 [reciprocal OR = 38.0], p = 4.652 x 10-3) and distinguishes DNA-contact poisons from dimer-unfolding alleles across 12 zebrafish in vivo assays. Atomistic base-readout contacts in the AF3 TP63-MCS9.7 tetramer mirror loss-of-function profiles in MaveDB ({rho} = 0.6048, p = 6.52 x 10-4) and AlphaGenome keratinocyte DNase predictions ({rho} = 0.6040, p = 6.65 x 10-4). Across non-coding benchmarks, AlphaGenome splicing tracks reach an AUROC of 0.9876 while prioritizing cryptic splice variants of uncertain significance, and epithelial chromatin tracks capture enhancer grammar, plasmid-cloning artifacts, and context-dependent ARHGAP29, FOXE1, and local 8q24 chromatin effects within AlphaGenome's 1.049-Mb horizon.

title: CAS-X: A Probabilistic Multi-Tissue eQTL Framework for Prioritizing Candidate Effector Genes at Type 2 Diabetes Risk Loci
abstract: The genetic etiology of Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) involves regulatory mechanisms operating across multiple metabolic tissues. However, candidate effector gene prioritization can be limited by approaches that focus predominantly on pancreatic transcriptomics. To address this limitation, we developed CAS-X, a computational multi-tissue functional genomics framework for prioritizing candidate effector genes at T2D susceptibility loci. CAS-X integrates fine-mapped Posterior Inclusion Probabilities (PIP) and allelic fold changes (aFC) across five tissues: pancreas, skeletal muscle, subcutaneous adipose, visceral adipose, and whole blood. In the reported analysis, multi-tissue integration identified 28 candidate genes meeting the selected prioritization threshold, compared with 12 under the pancreas-only baseline, representing a 133.3% increase in candidate coverage. Prioritized candidates included JAZF1, FTO, GRB14, and CDKN2B. Framework robustness was examined through Leave-One-Tissue-Out sensitivity analysis and comparisons with non-metabolic GTEx Brain Cortex controls. Pathway enrichment analysis highlighted associations with insulin resistance, adipocytokine signaling, and lipolysis regulation. The analysis also incorporated phenome-wide associations and computational assessments of therapeutic tractability. CAS-X provides a computational approach for integrating regulatory evidence across metabolic tissues to support candidate effector gene prioritization in T2D research.

title: BI-SCUDO Regression - A novel algorithm to infer clinical variables from omics datasets
abstract: Regression analysis of high-throughput omics data is often made difficult by noise, batch effects, and the loss of information resulting from the discretization of continuous variables. Existing machine learning algorithms often struggle to extract stable biological signals under these heterogeneous conditions. We introduce BI-SCUDO Regression, a rank-based regression framework designed for omics data analysis. By leveraging within-sample rankings and network-based predictions, BI-SCUDO Regression bypasses the need for complex normalization and provides robust, interpretable results. In synthetic benchmarks, BI-SCUDO Regression demonstrated strong resilience to noise, maintaining predictive and feature-selection stability under conditions in which standard models exhibited performance degradation. When applied to cohorts from TCGA datasets, BI-SCUDO Regression consistently outperformed LASSO, Random Forest Regression, and XGBoost in predicting survival, with an average increase in Ratio of Performance to Deviation ranging from 43% to 86%, depending on the comparator. Furthermore, the algorithm consistently identified parsimonious, statistically significant, and biologically relevant biomarkers, with enrichment for cancer-related terms across all stage stratifications. Although BI-SCUDO Regression incurs higher training times due to its genetic optimization strategy, it offers a robust and interpretable approach to outcome prediction and biomarker discovery, with potential applications in precision medicine, where noisy data compromise the performance of conventional regression methods.

title: Accurate and interpretable protein complex stoichiometry prediction through agentic AI with StoiAgent
abstract: Accurate protein complex structure modeling requires knowledge of complex stoichiometry, yet the copy numbers of individual subunits are often unknown. Consequently, predicting protein complex stoichiometry has emerged as a major challenge in recent years. Here, we present StoiAgent, a large language model (LLM)-powered AI agent that automates the retrieval and integration of sequence, structural, and literature evidence to predict stoichiometry while preserving interpretable reasoning traces (chain of thoughts) of its evidence assessment and ranking decision. An open-weight LLM model, Qwen3.6-27B, is used by StoiAgent as the LLM backbone to combine sequences, structural templates, AlphaFold3 structure predictions, and literature evidence, and perform stoichiometry candidate generation and ranking. On 56 CASP17 protein complex targets, it achieves top-1 accuracy of 75.0%, which represents a 23.2 percentage-point improvement over PreStoi with AlphaFold3 ranking (51.8%) and matches the top-1 accuracy of StoPred. Moreover, StoiAgent has a higher top-3 and top-5 accuracy than StoPred (85.7% versus 80.4% and 87.5% versus 85.7%, respectively). Furthermore, it outperforms general-purpose frontier LLMs, including ChatGPT and Gemini, in stoichiometry prediction. Case studies further illustrate how StoiAgent evaluates competing assembly hypotheses by integrating complementary evidence, with recorded reasoning traces documenting its decision-making process. Overall, StoiAgent demonstrates the potential of LLM-powered AI agents to improve protein complex stoichiometry prediction through the automated integration of diverse sources of evidence while providing interpretable explanations to guide downstream structure modeling.

title: Benchmarking four large language models on generating and selecting hypotheses that match published findings in 50 studies of ageing biology
abstract: Objective We asked how often hypotheses generated by large language models for 50 research tasks matched the withheld finding of the published study, and whether model forecasts could identify the matching hypotheses. Methods We built tasks from 50 peer-reviewed studies in ageing biology published after the models' stated training cutoffs; each task gave the background and a research question and withheld the study's finding (the reference finding). GPT-6 Astra, Grok 4.5, Claude Opus 5.5, and Gemini 4 Argon each generated five hypotheses per task by three methods: a single request, a multistep pipeline, and the Omega Point method without literature search (2997 hypotheses). A hypothesis matched the reference finding if at least two of three judge models from other developers scored it at least 3 (primary threshold) or at least 4 (strict threshold) on a 0 to 5 scale; refusals counted as non-matches. A selection rule, chosen from 112 variants evaluated on the Grok 4.5 hypotheses, kept only the hypotheses for which all four predictor models forecast experimental confirmation; the predictors never saw the published finding. The controls were recorded random answers and each generator's first-listed hypothesis. Confidence intervals (95% CIs) were calculated by cluster bootstrap over tasks. Results Of the hypotheses generated by a single request, 13.2% to 18.0% matched the reference finding, compared with 11.2% to 18.8% for the multistep pipeline and 2.8% to 7.6% for the Omega Point method. With a single request, the hypothesis listed first matched in 37.5% of cases (75/200), and the hypotheses in positions 2 to 5 matched in 10.1% (81/800). Among the hypotheses selected unanimously, the match rate was 73.7% (14/19) for Grok 4.5, 47.4% (9/19) for Gemini 4 Argon, and 63.6% (14/22) for Claude Opus 5.5, compared with 12.1% to 17.9% for the random control and 37.5% to 40.0% for the first-listed hypotheses. The selected lists captured 27.3% to 35.0% of all matching hypotheses. Pooled across the three sets, the match rate among selected hypotheses exceeded that among first-listed hypotheses by 23.2 percentage points (pp; 95% CI [13.0, 32.6]). When Gemini 4 Argon re-extracted the reference findings, the match rate among selected hypotheses was 59.6% (34/57), compared with 61.4% (35/57) against the original reference findings for the same tasks. In a manual audit with the generator, judge scores, and selection status hidden, our classifications agreed with the judges' at the primary threshold in 81/100 cases (Cohen's kappa 0.62). Agreement was 89.7% after weighting the sample strata by their size in the corpus. We classified 19 of 30 sampled selected hypotheses as matches, and the judges classified 20 of 30. Conclusions In the evaluated sets, unanimous selection by the four predictors increased the match rate among selected hypotheses; the resulting match rate depended on the matching threshold. Generators listed a matching hypothesis first more often than in later positions, and 50 of the 60 selected hypotheses were listed first. The advantage over the first-listed hypotheses and over the best single predictor at equal list length was statistically significant for the Grok and Opus hypotheses but not for the Gemini hypotheses, and the pairwise differences of the advantage between generators were not statistically significant (p >= 0.16 after Holm correction). We selected the rule using the Grok hypotheses and evaluated it on the Gemini and Opus hypotheses for the same 50 tasks; it has not been tested on new tasks.

title: Elflow: Automated Quality Control and Self-Supervised Representation Learning for High-Dimensional Cytometry
abstract: High-dimensional flow and mass cytometry are foundational technologies for clinical immunophenotyping and hematological diagnostics, yet computational data analysis remains bottlenecked by operator-subjective manual gating. While computational tools have emerged, they remain fragmented across isolated tasks such as quality control or discrete clustering, leaving an unmet need for integrated, modular workflows that resolve continuous biological variation without manual supervision. Here, we introduce Elflow, a modular, self-supervised framework that links automated quality control, single-cell representation learning, and patient-level modeling without manual gating at inference. Elflow couples automated machine-learning quality control with Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization (VICReg) to learn continuous, batch-resilient single-cell representations without negative pairs or hand-labeled training sets. Across four diverse public benchmarks, Elflow adapts to distinct biological panels and clinical objectives. On 22-channel spectral flow cytometry (OMIP-030), self-supervised embeddings preserve fine functional T-cell gradations and outperform classical baselines in unsupervised clustering, while an anchor-guided extension accurately reproduces canonical manual gating hierarchies. On hand-curated CyTOF panels (Levine-13), linear PCA matches deep models, establishing an empirical boundary condition where linear methods suffice. Across multi-center clinical cohorts (FlowCAP-II), Elflow representations achieve high diagnostic sensitivity for acute myeloid leukemia across heterogeneous instruments despite severe class imbalance. In longitudinal immune monitoring (FlowCAP-IV), patient mean embeddings and micro-cluster differential histograms preserve rare antigen-specific responses, yielding significant AIDS-free survival stratification. By uniting automated quality control, self-supervised representation learning, and multi-scale patient aggregation, Elflow provides a modular, reproducibly benchmarked framework for high-parameter and multi-center translational cytometry.

title: Sc-HistoMorphomics: A General Framework for High-throughput, Multimodal Profiling of Nuclear Morphology in Tissues.
abstract: Quantitative cellular morphology provides a rich but underutilized window into cell identity and state. We introduce sc-HistoMorphomics, a scalable framework for profiling nuclear morphology in whole-slide H&E images and correlating these measurements with spatial transcriptomics data. Our pipeline combines deep-learning based segmentation with 194 interpretable morphometric features capturing nuclear shape, eosin and hematoxylin texture, and neighbourhood architecture, enabling high-throughput, multimodal characterization of tissue organization. Applied to endometrium, breast cancer tissue, and pancreas, sc-HistoMorphomics revealed conserved high-dimensional feature structure across tissues and reproducible association between morphology and gene expression. Eosin-based texture features were associated with senescence signatures in endometrium, and morphology-based clustering recapitulated broad stromal, lymphocyte, and epithelial tumor cell classes in breast cancer. In pancreas, negative correlations between CDKN1A and multiple morphological features were consistent across cell types and donors. Together, these results establish sc-HistoMorphomics as a generalizable and interpretable tool for linking morphology with spatially resolved molecular state across diverse tissues.

title: FULL-seq reveals isoform-specific regulatory architecture in single cells
abstract: Gene regulation is commonly modeled at the gene level, yet genes express multiple isoforms from distinct transcription start sites whose regulatory architecture is not resolved by current approaches. Here we introduce FULL-seq, a scalable single-cell multiomic platform that jointly profiles chromatin accessibility and full-length transcript coverage from the same cell, enabling direct coupling of regulatory elements to alternative first exon (AFE) usage. FULL-seq achieves high sensitivity for both transcriptome and chromatin accessibility while providing transcript-wide coverage across mRNAs up to 15 kb with precise exon-level mapping. We uncover diverse promoter-AFE regulatory architectures, revealing distinct transcription factor programs across alternative first exons of the same gene, and show that gene-level annotation frameworks can obscure regulatory relationships in multi-promoter genes. Applying FULL-seq to human cancer cells further reveals metastasis-associated AFE programs that are not apparent from gene-level expression. These AFE programs were reproduced in independent colorectal cancer cell-line datasets, and CALB1 AFE activation was observed in a subset of liver metastases from an independent patient cohort. Furthermore, CRISPRi-mediated repression of metastasis-associated CALB1 AFEs reduced colorectal cancer cell migration. Together, our findings establish alternative promoter and first-exon usage as a functionally relevant layer of gene regulation and demonstrate that FULL-seq enables regulatory relationships and cellular phenotypes to be connected at the promoter-isoform level.

title: scUNVEIL: Learning scRNA-seq Cell Embeddings Through Measurement Enrichment
abstract: Large-scale pretraining can improve scRNA-seq representations through measurement enrichment: estimating what the same measurement would reveal at greater UMI depth under the same measurement process. We introduce scUNVEIL, a self-supervised model trained through next-UMI prediction. We show that the Bayes-optimal next-UMI predictor is the posterior mean of the transcriptome composition that arbitrarily deep sequencing would reveal. Because UMI identities are exchangeable conditional on transcriptome composition, scUNVEIL operates directly on count vectors using a residual multilayer perceptron, without attention over gene tokens. The measurement-enriched transcriptome composition is predicted from a single low-dimensional hidden state, which therefore serves naturally as the cell embedding. The same model provides both reusable cell representations and measurement-enriched gene-expression estimates. scUNVEIL was pretrained without labels or auxiliary metadata on approximately 92 million human cells spanning diverse tissues. Under linear evaluation on fine-grained cell-type annotation, its zero-shot representations achieved the best performance among the evaluated methods, while providing over 1000-fold faster inference than the strongest evaluated transformer-based foundation model and matching that model's predictive performance using 88% fewer input UMIs per cell. Further evaluations show that these representations improve prediction of tumor reactivity, mitochondrial membrane potential, cell morphology, and lineage-associated treatment outcomes.

title: Most substitutions need more than one base change and an exact test tells which deposited scans measure the route
abstract: Design methods that reach a target through an intermediate take two substitutions at one position, and no deep mutational scan built from a single parental sequence reports the second. The detour is common, since 230 of the 380 ordered pairs of amino acids are more than one base change apart. Both substitutions are nevertheless present in the public record wherever one protein has been scanned on two parental backgrounds that differ at a position. We assemble every such comparison in MaveDB, 102,421 complete two-step routes over 65 protein clusters. The difference between a route and its two legs is a double difference, which is the epistasis between the tested position and the other positions at which the two backgrounds differ. Where the backgrounds differ nowhere else, that quantity is zero by construction. The rank correlation over the target residues must then return one, on any scale and against no null, which makes the comparison an exact test. Over the 741 qualifying pairs across 46 proteins the median is 0.965, and 34 of the 46 proteins return a median at or above 0.9. The arithmetic therefore holds across the population the record supplies, short natural domains drawn from families of near-identical sequences. Which pairs fail is not written in the record, since pairs drawn from one experiment set return 0.34 and pairs from unrelated submissions 0.97. The null such comparisons are read against fails the same test, returning +0.227 where it must return zero, more than the shift the comparison reports. Matching the control positions on the dispersion of the effects ranked halves that bias to +0.104. Two deposits of one protein agree at 0.642 where both score the same position. That bounds any predictor tested against one deposit at 0.80 for a position drawn at random, and at 0.90 and 0.98 where positions are scored more reliably. The test costs one correlation and settles, before any analysis, whether two deposits can be compared.

title: A de novo reference genome of the red seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis
abstract: Furcellaria lumbricalis is a red seaweed that occurs across a broad salinity gradient, ranging from the saline waters of the NE Atlantic to the brackish Baltic Sea. In the Baltic Sea, natural populations of F. lumbricalis are harvested commercially, primarily for furcellaran extraction, a sulphated polysaccharide used as a stabilizing, thickening, and gelling agent. Genomic resources for this species remain absent, constraining evolutionary, ecological, and applied research. Here, we present a de novo reference genome assembly of the seaweed Furcellaria lumbricalis using PacBio Hifi and Oxford Nanopore Technologies long-read sequencing. The final assembly, consisting of 149 contigs spanning 918.2 Mb, contains a high proportion of repetitive elements (90.5%), and has an N50 of 15,5 Mb. We further integrated RNA-seq data, protein homology evidence, and ab initio gene prediction to build a genome annotation comprising 6100 genes, of which 82.6% has a functional annotation. This genomic evidence contributes to a steadily growing body of genomic resources of red algae, with often expanded and highly repetitive genomes, and helps facilitate the study of genetic adaptation to their unique environments.

title: ARGeement: sequence-based, versioned mapping of antimicrobial resistance gene databases
abstract: Genomic studies of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) rely on several independently curated reference databases, which describe the same genes under different names, in different structures and with different classifications. This makes results obtained with different databases difficult to compare. ARGeement maps the entries of AMRFinderPlus, the Comprehensive Antibiotic Resistance Database (CARD) and ResFinder/DisinFinder to each other by protein sequence, independently of their names. It characterises every link by its relation type, difference count and coverage, tracks the database versions, and produces a documented, immutable mapping for every release. The 17,920 entries of the release described here encode 17,959 protein sequences, corresponding to 9,337 unique proteins. For 64.4% of the cross-database entry pairs that encode the same protein, the names differ even when letter case is ignored, and 447 pairs show a genuine naming conflict. Conversely, 2.0% of the pairs with the same allele name do not encode the same protein. For synthetic variants created with known modifications, the original protein was among the best hits in 99.6% of the cases. In 100 complete RefSeq genomes annotated with AMRFinderPlus, the Resistance Gene Identifier (RGI) and ResFinder, the gene names agreed at 55.3%-75.6% of the loci called by both tools of a pair, whereas after mapping the two reference proteins were identical, near-identical or length variants at 89.6%-94.2%. These results show that name-based comparison is unreliable even for identical sequences, and that a sequence-based, versioned mapping is needed.

title: DRAFT: graph-recurrent learning of dynamic gene regulatory networks along single-cell multi-omics trajectories
abstract: Single-cell multi-omics data offer an opportunity to resolve how gene regulatory networks (GRNs) are rewired during cell-fate transitions, but most existing methods infer static snapshots, ignore temporal dependencies or assume linear regulation. Here we present DRAFT, a deep learning framework that combines graph attention with recurrent temporal memory to infer dynamic GRNs from time-resolved single-cell multi-omics data. On simulated data, DRAFT outperforms existing methods in accuracy and temporal smoothness. In mouse cellular reprogramming and Drosophila adult spermatogenesis, it recovers interactions supported by independent ChIP-seq, perturbation and Hi-C data, together with known stage-specific regulators. By inferring regulatory activity from dynamic network structure rather than expression alone, DRAFT identifies regulators whose activity precedes their transcriptional peak, including the candidate early germline regulator Mondo. Germline-specific Mondo knockdown alters germline stem cell number and expression of the predicted targets kuz and mamo. DRAFT also enables nonlinear alignment of co-developing lineages and reveals stage-specific cell-cell communication.

title: ChIMe-seq enables multimodal epigenetic profiling in single molecules and single cells
abstract: Recent advances in single-cell and single-molecule sequencing have enabled high-resolution characterization of epigenetic states. However, methods that jointly measure multiple layers of epigenetic regulation within the same molecules and cells remain limited. Here, we developed Chromatin Immuno-Methylation sequencing (ChIMe-seq), a multimodal approach that simultaneously profiles histone modifications, DNA methylation, and nucleosome positioning genome-wide in single molecules and single cells. In contrast to recent approaches that rely on enzymatic fragmentation, ChIMe-seq preserves long DNA molecules by using a methyltransferase to deposit exogenous methylation marks that report on proximal histone modifications. This enables integration of multiple epigenetic features within individual molecules and supports short-read, long-read, and single-cell sequencing. These multimodal measurements are integrated into a novel mathematical framework that captures the coupling between nucleosome positioning, histone modifications, and DNA methylation. Both single-molecule and single-cell analyses reveal that DNA methylation is linked to nucleosome density in a manner modulated by local histone modifications, whilst differences in nucleosome:DNA structures are observed depending on epigenetic context and cell-type. Together, these results establish ChIMe-seq as a framework to investigate multifaceted epigenetic coordination across scales, from single-nucleotide resolution to long-range chromatin organization in single molecules and single cells.

title: Regulatory grammar design of tissue-specific enhancers across species
abstract: Enhancers encode tissue-specific gene expression through the combinatorial identity, number, and arrangement of transcription factor motifs, collectively known as regulatory grammar. However, existing deep-learning methods directly optimize nucleotide sequences, leaving enhancer regulatory grammar implicit. Here we introduce REgulatory Grammar Architecture via reinforcement Learning (REGAL), a framework that explicitly programs enhancer grammar under sequence-to-function oracles. REGAL generated tissue-specific enhancers across species using the same placement architecture with interchangeable oracles and motif vocabularies. Experimental validation and perturbation revealed that tissue specificity requires coordinated target-tissue activation and off-target repression, depends on both motif composition and spatial organization, and employs distinct regulatory strategies across tissues. REGAL-designed enhancers drove predicted lineage-specific expression in transgenic mouse embryos, outperformed a nucleotide-level optimizer in human cells, and matched or exceeded leading designs in zebrafish and Drosophila at notably shorter length. Together, these findings establish regulatory grammar as a programmable and experimentally testable substrate underlying enhancer design and specificity.

title: No detectable DNA methylation in the kelps (Laminariales): a conversion-free test of a predicted loss
abstract: Kelps (Laminariales) dominate temperate and polar rocky coasts and support a fast-growing aquaculture sector. Breeding and restoration programs need to know whether a line's performance follows its genotype or its culture history. DNA methylation has been reported in kelps, with differences by life stage, thermal history and population of origin now underpinning a literature on conditioning and priming in seaweed breeding. Recent comparative genomics work predicts otherwise, because brown algae lack the canonical DNA methyltransferases and should therefore carry little or no DNA methylation. We tested the prediction with native-DNA nanopore sequencing, which requires neither bisulfite conversion nor methylation-dependent digestion, in seven kelp datasets spanning three genera, four species and four S. latissima life stages. Nuclear 5-methylcytosine stayed at the measurement background in every sequence context (CG 0.021-0.034% of sites, against 0.023% on PCR copies that carry no methyl group by construction), while the same pipeline returned 58% of CG sites methylated in a diatom and recovered the transposon-targeted distribution a functioning system predicts. In native reads, thirteen of the fourteen best-covered chloroplast positions that bisulfite sequencing placed above 2% carry at most one methylated call, and those published levels track each library's conversion efficiency rather than its tissue. Gene content and direct measurement agree, so the heritable effects reported in cultivated kelp require a carrier other than DNA methylation: chromatin modifications or non-coding RNA.

title: Systematic evaluation using SigMatch reveals how sample tissues shape transcriptomic disease relationships
abstract: Motivation Diseases often share underlying molecular characteristics captured by transcriptional responses. Leveraging this knowledge transfer can aid in uncovering novel disease biology and drug repurposing. Large-scale transcriptomic datasets and disease signatures provide an opportunity to computationally identify these shared disease relationships based on shared genome-wide gene expression changes. However, disease signatures are strongly influenced by sample tissue, making it difficult to distinguish shared disease biology from shared tissue origin. Despite this challenge, existing computational approaches do not systematically take into account or evaluate the impact of tissue on their predictions. Results We present SigMatch, a systematic evaluation of the impact of sample tissue on transcriptomic-based disease relationship prioritization. We evaluate this impact on existing correlation- and rank-based methods, and on an alternative family called reconstruction-based methods. In particular, we examine (i) mechanistic disease relationships given the context of sample tissues and (ii) prediction agreement with external evidence of disease relatedness based on shared genes, symptoms, drugs, and comorbidities. We found that predicted disease relationships by all the methods are heavily influenced by sample tissue. Tissue-specific genes are not the sole driver of the prediction scores. Across methods, removal of tissue-specific genes did not reduce the observed tissue-dependent patterns or improve recovery of evidence-supported disease pairs. This work demonstrates substantial sample-tissue influence in transcriptomic similarities between diseases and that sample tissue should be considered when identifying and interpreting inferred transcriptomic disease relationships.

title: Robust Cluster Typing, a computationally accessible tool for species designation from whole genome data, exemplified with the genus Campylobacter
abstract: Bacterial genomic analysis is a cornerstone of modern epidemiology. Many genomic typing methods exist, and most are designed to work within a given species in a hierarchical fashion. However, designation of bacterial species can be problematic, making the higher resolution level of hierarchical typing difficult. Using the universally present ribosomal proteins, we have developed a pipeline for a robust typing system which can be used to assign an unknown organism to a species-level cluster or, sometimes, a sub-species cluster. As proof of principle, we have used bacterial genomes from the genus Campylobacter, the most common cause of human bacterial gastroenteritis within which new strains, and new species (C. infantis), are reported. Species assignment, of all but the two most common species C. jejuni and C. coli, is beyond the ability of most microbiology laboratories. Outbreak investigation, even with genomic data, is difficult and so a robust typing scheme would be useful. Using available sequence-based typing schemes, we attempted to differentiate between 39 published Campylobacter species; we determined that the ribosomal 16S sequence typing and SNP typing did not discriminate all 39 but a single gene phylogeny method (GyrA), BUSCO, Mash, Panaroo and use of the Hugg proteins differentiated all 39. We assessed computational accessibility (important for implementation) and biological applicability (one universal typing scheme is easier to validate). The application of Hugg proteins proved computationally efficient and should be widely applicable. We developed a workflow in snakemake and Python, capable of clustering thousands of bacterial genomes. This Robust Cluster (RC) typing workflow was made accessible via the Terra platform, with usage instructions provided through an online training course on YouTube. Ninety-eight Campylobacter isolates from Bangladesh were sequenced and analysed using the Terra workflow, resulting in the identification of several novel clusters not previously found among publicly available genomes. Our work establishes the availability of RC typing and demonstrates its capacity to identify new Campylobacter lineages, thereby facilitating reporting and supporting future research initiatives.

title: De novo Genome Assembly and Annotation of the Seep Tubeworm Lamellibrachia satsuma using Oxford Nanopore Sequencing
abstract: The tubeworm Lamelllibrachia satsuma inhabits seep region by forming a mutualistic symbiotic relationship with chemosynthetic bacteria residing in its trophosome. Genomic and symbiotic studies have been extensively conducted, primarily from a bacterial perspective. But rarely vice versa. Here we present a high-quality draft genome assembly of L. satsuma and its tissue-specific transcriptome data. This genome will be valuable for further understanding the mechanisms of adaptation in cold seep environments, host-microbe interactions, as well as genome variation among tubeworms. We generated ~103 Gb of genomic sequencing data using Illumina and Oxford Nanopore platforms, which assembled in a 665 Mb draft genome. The assembled genome consisted of 6,320 scaffolds with 95.7% genome completeness. Among 32,394 predicted protein-coding genes, 1,063 gene families have expanded, and 1,385 gene families were contracted. Among the expanded gene families, multiple copies of leukocyte elastase inhibitor, reverse transcriptase, arylesterase, and xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidase genes were found. Molecular clock analysis based on the phylogenomic dataset revealed that L. sastuma and L. luymesi were diverged from their common ancestor during the Early Cenozoic era, approximately 13 million years ago.

title: GENECraft: A Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System for Controllable Regulatory DNA Design
abstract: Designing regulatory DNA requires reconciling two complementary modeling paradigms: genomic language models (gLMs) capture evolutionary syntax without guaranteeing targeted regulatory activity, whereas sequence-to-function predictors provide explicit functional supervision without enforcing native-like sequence plausibility. We introduce GENECraft, a training-free Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System (FP-DDS) that couples a genomic language model (Carbon) and a functional oracle (AlphaGenome) during inference-time optimization to balance predicted regulatory activity and consistency with genomic sequence priors. GENECraft evolves continuous latent nucleotide logits while evaluating strictly decoded discrete DNA sequences under a time-dependent composite vector field that fuses normalized functional utility, bidirectional contextual prior guidance, and compositional quality penalties, followed by feasibility-first trajectory readout. Across 2,185 loci spanning promoters, multi-constraint enhancers, and 18 transcription factors (TFs), GENECraft achieves full-joint success rates of 62.70%, 65.23%, and 94.56% (macro-averaged), substantially outperforming seven optimization, evolutionary, and generative baselines (which reach at most 2.15% on enhancers). In matched 336-locus ablations, in-loop Carbon guidance reduces native-relative dinucleotide divergence by 7.8--11.5%, enhancer context sensitivity by 10.5%, and TF mutation sensitivity by 11.0%, establishing FP-DDS as a principled framework for controllable regulatory DNA design.

title: Flux Transformer learns intracellular metabolic fluxes from isotope labeling and measured reaction rates
abstract: Cells convert incoming nutrients into energy and biomass via metabolic fluxes. Quantifying these fluxes involves feeding cells isotope-labeled nutrients, quantifying metabolite labeling patterns, and inverting the labeling data to retrieve the underlying flux distribution. Traditional metabolic flux analysis (MFA) is both computationally expensive and frequently requires manual refinement of the cost function to obtain plausible results. For this reason, MFA has remained inaccessible to non-experts. Here we present Flux Transformer, an AI model that uses reaction-specific attention to integrate isotope-labeling data with available reaction-rate measurements, reconstructing mass-balanced steady-state fluxes. The model is trained on simulated data with added noise and identifies the underlying fluxes from these data more effectively than traditional MFA. Provided experimental data from wild-type and mutant bacteria, yeast, plants, and mammalian T cells, it efficiently and accurately recovers expert-curated MFA fluxes. By making flux analysis accessible, Flux Transformer is poised to accelerate metabolic research and engineering.

title: CATEomics: model selection and ensembling for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation from high-dimensional omics data
abstract: CATEomics addresses the lack of a standardized and reproducible process for choosing among conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimators in high-dimensional omics studies, where their estimation errors cannot be evaluated directly from observed outcomes. The R package accepts a SummarizedExperiment, applies common preprocessing and data partitions across R and Python estimators, compares their out-of-fold estimates using proxy losses, supports model selection and ensembling, and returns the resulting CATE estimates to the original object for downstream omics analysis. Availability and implementation: CATEomics is implemented in R and is freely available under the MIT license at https://github.com/matsui-lab/CATEomics. The software version described here (v0.99.0) is archived on Zenodo at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24189754. A vignette illustrates the complete workflow from a SummarizedExperiment to downstream analysis.

title: Gene set selection for classification with single-cell RNA-seq
abstract: Marker genes are important for analyzing and interpreting single-cell RNA-seq (scRNAseq) experiments. They are used to identify and categorize cell types and can also be useful for the design of downstream experiments. We present CellSieve, which tackles the problem of finding effective gene sets rather than distilling markers one at a time. While several "combinatorial" approaches to gene set selection have been proposed, we find that our approach, which leverages a combination of multinomial logistic regression and linear programming, is much more effective at finding small gene sets that can classify cell types.

title: The genetic regulation of thyroid hormones on immune and hematopoietic homeostasis: an integrative Mendelian randomization and colocalization study
abstract: Background: Hematological traits are closely linked to immune and inflammatory processes implicated in thyroid dysfunction. Although observational studies have reported associations between blood-cell traits and thyroid disorders, whether these relationships reflect causal mechanisms remains unclear. Methods: We performed a two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis to investigate the causal effects of 25 genetically predicted hematological traits on hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism using genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics from the UK Biobank. Independent single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) were selected as instrumental variables and harmonized before analysis. Causal estimates were primarily obtained using the inverse-variance weighted (IVW) method and complemented by MR-Egger, weighted median, weighted mode, simple mode, MR-PRESSO, and MR-robust adjusted profile score (MR-RAPS) analyses. Sensitivity analyses assessed heterogeneity, horizontal pleiotropy, reverse causality, and directionality. Significant findings were replicated using independent FinnGen summary statistics. Multivariable MR and Bayesian colocalization analyses were subsequently performed to investigate significant associations further. Results: Among the 25 hematological traits evaluated, eosinophil-related traits showed the strongest associations with hypothyroidism. Genetically predicted eosinophil counts were associated with an increased risk of hypothyroidism (odds ratio [OR] = 1.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.11-1.42, P = 4.0E-04, FDR = 0.002), while combined eosinophil-basophil counts showed similar associations (OR = 1.24, 95% CI: 1.10-1.40, P = 5.0E-04, FDR = 0.002). These findings were consistently replicated in FinnGen and remained significant after adjustment for basophil traits, body mass index, and C-reactive protein in multivariable MR analyses. No significant associations were observed for hyperthyroidism. Bayesian colocalization identified strong evidence of a shared genetic signal at the rs653178 locus on chromosome 12 (PP.H4 = 0.994). Conclusions: This study provides genetic evidence supporting a causal role for eosinophil-related traits in hypothyroidism susceptibility. The consistency of the findings across complementary Mendelian randomization approaches, independent replication, multivariable analyses, and colocalization strengthens the evidence that eosinophil-related immune mechanisms contribute to hypothyroidism susceptibility.

title: pbzarr: cohort-scale storage and analysis of per-base genomic data with Zarr
abstract: Genomic assays now produce per-base signals for cohorts comprising thousands of samples. However, existing genomic data storage formats (e.g., D4, bigWig) were designed primarily for single samples or individual datasets. Consequently, cohort-scale analyses across samples, populations, or species require opening, reading, and merging thousands of files before proceeding to downstream computational analyses. Here, we present pbzarr, a format and toolkit that stores per-base genomic data from many samples and assays as a single Zarr store. Across multiple datasets, pbzarr simplified cohort construction to a single command and created cohort-scale datasets up to 2.1x faster than existing approaches while simultaneously using 5-6x less memory. More importantly, pbzarr compresses signal tracks to only a fraction of the input data size, using only 3.3% of the input size to store per-base coverage for 1,024 short-read genomes. Despite this smaller storage footprint, pbzarr maintains fast access to underlying genomic data: region-based queries complete 61x faster than D4 and 6x faster than bigWig, and full-genome scans are as fast or faster than existing formats. Finally, because pbzarr stores are native Zarr arrays, it integrates directly with widely used array libraries (e.g., Xarray and Dask), allowing cohort-scale analyses to be expressed in a single line of Python code using standard array operations instead of a complex, custom pipeline. Together, our results suggest that pbzarr is dramatically smaller, substantially simpler, and faster than competing formats for biobank-scale analysis. pbzarr is open source and available at https://github.com/pbzarr/pbzarr.

title: Contrasting plasmid-host associations shape the distribution of enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC) colonization factors
abstract: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) causes a substantial burden of diarrhoeal disease, but how its virulence plasmids spread across E. coli populations remains unclear. We generated 479 complete ETEC genomes and combined them with 56 publicly available assemblies to produce the largest plasmid-resolved ETEC collection to date. Clustering of 903 virulence plasmids identified distinct plasmid lineages associated with individual colonization factors (CFs). Some CFs were carried by plasmids confined to a single ETEC lineage, consistent with long-term vertical maintenance, whereas others, including CS23 and CS12, were found on closely related conjugative plasmids distributed across multiple lineages, indicating horizontal transfer. Screening the AllTheBacteria dataset confirmed these patterns and revealed additional plasmid diversity for several CFs. Finally, we identified eight previously undescribed putative adhesion operons on toxin plasmids that may explain CF-negative ETEC isolates. These findings showed that plasmids, rather than bacterial lineages alone, shape the evolution and dissemination of ETEC virulence.

title: Vocabulary recurrence, rather than biological grounding, explains tokenization transfer in protein function prediction.
abstract: Sequence-based protein function prediction requires a choice of tokenization. K-mers, the common default, correspond to no biological unit; enzymatic digestion offers a principled alternative, since tryptic peptides are the fragments proteases generate and mass spectrometry measures. We asked whether this grounding improves transfer to unseen proteins. Using six Gene Ontology terms and 23,723 UniProt proteins, we compared tryptic peptides, peptide topics (groups of related peptides), 3-mers, and amino- acid composition, with ESM-2 embeddings and homology transfer as reference points. Peptide performance followed vocabulary coverage: 92.2% of peptide tokens in test proteins were never seen in training, whereas almost every 3-mer had been seen. As a result, 38.9% of test proteins contained no peptide the model had seen, and with nothing to work from, the classifier gave all of them the same answer. The remaining 61.1% of proteins were classified almost perfectly with a random forest; however, because of this uncovered fraction, tryptic peptides scored lower overall than 3-mers under all three classifiers tested (macro-F1 0.640 against 0.690). These results suggest that vocabulary recurrence matters more than biological grounding for tokenization transfer.

title: Identifying disease-associated dysbiosis in image-based spatial microbiome via MiSA
abstract: Background: Extensive studies have revealed the associations of microbiome dysbiosis with disease through compositional analysis of 16S rRNA amplicon or shotgun metagenomic sequencing data. However, dysbiosis in spatial organization of microbiome inhabiting the body sites and its implication for diseases remain understudied.
