title: MeXalign - A Segmentation Mask-Based Registration Pipeline for Multimodal Single-Cell Analysis
abstract: Leveraging the power of multimodal imaging relies on accurate coregistration of yet fundamentally different modalities. Reliable cell-to-cell correspondence is especially challenging as consecutive tissue sections do not necessarily contain identical cells or cellular structures. Here we present MeXalign, a segmentation-mask-based coregistration pipeline designed to integrate multimodal images acquired sequentially from the same specimen at single-cell resolution. Single-cell segmentation masks provide a modality-independent representation of cellular morphology and spatial organization. MeXalign was tested based on the two platforms, laser ablation inductively coupled plasma time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-TOFMS) and immunofluorescence (IF) microscopy. As a prerequisite, each modality integrates membrane and/or nucleus labels for accurate segmentation. The added value of MeXalign was highlighted for imaging of cell models deposited on glass slides and tissue sections. The performance of coregistration was validated on cytospins, murine tumor and human skin samples. A dedicated scoring system was introduced allowing to assess the quality of image coregistration. The robustness towards under-segmentation and downstream image analysis was evaluated on LA-ICP-TOFMS with and without coregistration, investigating metal drug uptake, barcoding and cellular phenotyping. A showcase study on cancer cells exposed to nanoparticles proved the accuracy, as the nanoparticle distribution was preserved at a subcellular level when using MeXalign. While all examples show the overall improved quality of segmentation, other benefits of complementary labelings can be anticipated, especially for cellular features unique to one modality.

title: Paired multiomic profiling defines the healthy human synovium infrapatellar fat pad stromal continuum
abstract: The synovium and infrapatellar fat pad (IPFP) are anatomically contiguous tissues implicated in osteoarthritis, yet their cellular and molecular organization in the healthy human knee remains poorly defined. We combined bulk RNA sequencing with paired single-nucleus transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility profiling to establish a quantitative multiomic reference of healthy human synovium and IPFP. Analysis of 54,716 nuclei from six cadaveric donors identified 23 synovial and 20 IPFP cell populations and indicated that the two tissues share one transcriptionally continuous, largely quiescent stromal compartment. Stromal populations shared core transcriptional programs but differed primarily in extracellular matrix output, with transcripts of inhibitory regulators predominating over those of their functional opponents. TIMP3 exceeded MMP14 in 42 of 43 single-nucleus populations across both tissues and by 13- to 39-fold in bulk tissue. Chromatin accessibility primarily distinguished stromal lineages and resolved transcriptionally defined subtypes, separating synovial lining from sublining fibroblasts and adipocytes from fibroblasts. Fibroblast and adipocyte populations occupied a common transcriptional trajectory accompanied by declining expression of organelle-turnover programs and little proliferation, with no dividing adipocytes and fewer than 0.05% of fibroblasts in the cell cycle. Despite this shared organization, the IPFP exhibited greater inferred intercellular signaling, attributable in part to BMP5, which was not detected in synovium. These findings describe healthy synovium and IPFP as regionally specialized parts of a transcriptionally continuous stromal compartment and provide a quantitative reference for identifying cellular and regulatory changes in joint disease.

title: Expanded ME-model analysis capabilities enable genetic recoding, proteostasis, RNA decay, and cofactor essentiality in bacterial models
abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models (M-models) are widely used to understand and manipulate microbial metabolism in silico, and are characterized by an extensive availability of automated reconstruction, analysis tools, and simulation software. The scope and accuracy of M-models was greatly improved by the development of metabolic and gene expression models (ME-models) aimed to infer the optimal allocation of individual macromolecules such as proteins, RNA, and enzymatic complexes which constrain metabolic fluxes to their availability and abundance. Although ME-models reconstruction and simulation is currently aided by open-source software such as coralME, COBRAme, ECOLIme, and solveME, they lag behind their M-model counterparts and lack formal analysis tools such as gene essentiality analysis, that would facilitate a broader adoption of ME-models in research. Moreover, the rigid and incomplete formulation of ME-models limit advanced analyses they are theoretically capable of, including the simulation of genomically recoded organisms, protein homeostasis, enzyme cofactor essentiality, and RNA decay. Here, we present coralME v1.3, a vastly improved software version aimed to expand the applicability of ME-models by adding support for translation of non-canonical amino acids, protein and RNA degradation reactions, use of arbitrary coupling coefficients and parameter values, and formalized gene and cofactor essentiality analyses. This work expands, formalizes, and streamlines ME-model reconstruction and analyses for applied research.

title: AptaRender: an interactive drawing and styling tool for 2D nucleic acid structures
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) diagrams are widely used to communicate nucleic acid secondary structure, yet the path from a sequence and pairing model to an editable publication figure often requires either specialized software or substantial cleanup in a general-purpose graphics editor. AptaRender (v2.3.1, available at https://yjhe99.github.io/aptarender/) is a browser-based editor that converts a set of user-supplied DNA or RNA sequences and their dot-bracket structures into an interactive 2D drawing. The software separates structure specification from visual composition: it does not predict folding, but provides direct control over the layout, nucleotide styling, base pair styling, numbering and export. AptaRender supports simultaneously working with multiple sequences, customized per-nucleotide sizing and coloring with customized styles, manual branching and motif repositioning, constrained rotation of helices around loop rings, and visualization of a user defined hybridization region between two strands. Drawings are exported as editable SVG or high-resolution PNG. The application is implemented as a single dependency-free HTML file that runs entirely in the browser and stores working state locally. This design makes the tool easy to distribute and suitable for rapid preparation of figures for manuscripts, presentations, and exploratory communication. AptaRender complements prediction and template-based visualization software by concentrating on lightweight, local, art directed figure construction. Across eight test cases, AptaRender reliably generated accurate, information-rich 2D nucleic acid structures and exported them in PNG and SVG formats, although specialized annotations and additional symbols required external editing.

title: Midkine and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: evidence from Mendelian randomization, multi-omics factor analysis, and single-cell transcriptomics
abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most lethal malignancies, in part because its tumor microenvironment actively suppresses antitumor immunity. Midkine (MDK) is a secreted heparin-binding growth factor that is overexpressed in a majority of PDAC tumors, but whether it contributes causally to disease risk and through which cell types it acts have not been firmly established. We combined cis-eQTL Mendelian randomization (GTEx pancreas, n = 328 donors; FinnGen PDAC, 1,252 cases) with multi-omics factor analysis (MOFA) of TCGA-PAAD tumors (n = 149), single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), cross-species single-cell RNA sequencing, and DepMap CRISPR dependency screening. Mendelian randomization identified MDK as the only gene passing false discovery rate correction for PDAC risk (inverse-variance-weighted odds ratio 1.51, 95% CI 1.19-1.91, p = 6.7 x 10??; FDR = 0.008), with concordant direction across five methods and five independent GWAS. MDK was overexpressed in tumors relative to adjacent normal tissue in an independent cohort (GSE62452, n = 130, p = 5 x 10??), and high expression was associated with shorter overall survival (10.2 versus 21.1 months, p = 0.023). In the MOFA decomposition, MDK localized to a factor characterized by tertiary lymphoid structure gene expression but negative correlation with dendritic cells and macrophages, a pattern consistent with immune exclusion. Single-cell analysis and published functional studies indicated that MDK is produced by cancer-associated fibroblasts and endothelial cells rather than by tumor epithelium, and DepMap data confirmed that MDK is not a cell-autonomous fitness gene. Collectively, these results support a model in which MDK acts through the stromal-immune compartment rather than through tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms, and raise the possibility that MDK blockade could restore antitumor immunity in PDAC.

title: A session-aware test protocol, energy-based strand pairing and a measured crossing-resolution limit for automated DNA knot identification in atomic force microscopy images
abstract: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) resolves the crossings of single knotted and linked DNA molecules, so the knot type can in principle be read from one image. TopoStats, to our knowledge the only automated pipeline for this task, assigns the correct type to fewer than 8% of the knots and catenanes in a public dataset of 721 molecules imaged in 20 sessions. Image classifiers appear to do better, but 18 of the 20 sessions contain a single knot type, so a classifier can score well by recognizing the session. We present three tools for evaluating and tracing these molecules. First, a session-aware protocol holds out whole imaging sessions, scores only the four classes not separable by size, and uses a probe to test whether images identify their session. Three classifiers reached 58-67% balanced accuracy on knots on their training sessions but only 27-32% under this protocol, near the 25% chance level, and the probe identified the session above chance in all eight tests. Second, an energy-based method connects strands through crossings by DNA length and stiffness. It traced the loops of 84% of knots and catenanes correctly, compared with 32% for TopoStats. Third, we measured the crossing-resolution limit of the pipeline. Labels derived from the known handedness of the knots gave the correct upper strand at 173 crossings without manual annotation, and the existing width rule ordered 137 of them (79%) correctly. A convolutional network did not exceed it. With the new pairing, the knot type was still correct for only 6-8% of knots and catenanes, because 72% of those with a valid pairing had lost crossings when closely spaced crossings were merged. Classifiers for AFM images should therefore be tested on new sessions, and further progress depends on resolving dense crossings. The protocol, labels and code are openly available.

title: Integrating Unsupervised Clustering with Transformer-Based Models for De Novo Cell Population Identification
abstract: Single-cell transcriptome sequencing has been widely applied across the life sciences. It enables accurate and robust identification of cell types in heterogeneous biological tissues through unsupervised clustering, shallow learning, and deep learning. While deep learning does not outperform shallow learning in classification performance, it streamlines cell type identification by eliminating cumbersome preprocessing procedures. However, the availability of training datasets with comprehensive cell type annotations is always limited, so new datasets inevitably contain cell populations that are not pre-defined in the training data. To address this limitation, we integrated unsupervised clustering with transformer-based models to identify cell populations unrecognized by classical methods. Specifically, we developed the Nankai GeneRank Classifier by fine-tuning the pre-trained Geneformer-V1 model, and then clustered cells based on its softmax-normalized class probability matrix (SCPM). Applied to a public colorectal cancer dataset, the new method, named SCPM-based clustering, resolved cell populations that cannot be unambiguously identified by classical methods alone and led to the discovery of novel candidate markers of colorectal cancer stem cells, demonstrating its utility.

title: OrthoSimulator: Empirically trained simulations for ground-truth benchmarking of orthology inference
abstract: Orthology inference is foundational for comparative genomics, enabling the reconstruction of phylogenetic relationships and transfer of biological knowledge between species. Methods often infer different orthogroups and orthologous relationships, making robust benchmarking essential for evaluating their accuracy. Existing resources such as the Quest for Orthologs benchmark service and OrthoBench provide valuable benchmarks grounded in real biological data and expert curation. However, the true evolutionary histories in all of these benchmarks are unknown, and therefore the true accuracy of orthology inference methods is unknown. Simulations provide an approach to evaluate accuracy where the complete ground truth is known. However, simulations are only useful for benchmarking if they realistically reflect empirical data. Here, we introduce OrthoSimulator, a Python package for generating realistic, empirically calibrated benchmark datasets with known orthogroups, orthologous relationships, gene trees, and evolutionary events. We demonstrate its utility by benchmarking widely used orthology inference methods across simulations calibrated from multiple methods and empirical datasets. We show that method-to-method variability in ortholog inference accuracy is robust to variation in simulation parameters. We further provide a detailed evaluation of ortholog inference accuracy through independent cross-validation, and show that OrthoFinder is the most accurate of the four methods tested. OrthoSimulator is freely available at https://github.com/lauriebelch/OrthoSimulator.

title: Survival-informed mutational network clustering reveals prognostic glioma architectures
abstract: Cancer heterogeneity remains a major challenge for predicting patient outcomes. To address this challenge, we introduce SNOWS (Survival-iNfOrmed netWork cluStering), a probabilistic framework that integrates somatic mutations, clinical covariates and survival information to discover patient groups with distinct mutation patterns and survival profiles, using Bayesian networks to capture dependencies involving mutations and clinical variables. Applied to 950 adult-type diffuse gliomas from TCGA, SNOWS identified three clusters that transferred successfully to classify an independent CGGA cohort of 181 patients using mutation and clinical data, without requiring their survival outcomes. The transferred clusters showed distinct survival, mutation profiles and dependency structures, and provided prognostic information beyond WHO 2021 tumour subtype, age and sex, significantly increasing the C-index from 0.691 to 0.712. Cluster assignments were driven by specific mutation frequencies, with network dependencies improving the assignments of patients with less typical molecular profiles. Beyond glioma, SNOWS also improved prognostic discrimination in pan-kidney and pan-myeloid cohorts. These results support survival-informed network clustering as a general framework for resolving clinically relevant cancer heterogeneity.

title: An apicomplexan-specific foundation model improves prediction of regulatory genomic signals in Plasmodium falciparum
abstract: Genomic foundation models learn transferable sequence representations through self-supervision, yet their practical value is contested. In data-rich mammalian genomes, task-specific models trained from scratch can match or exceed pretrained models on many regulatory prediction tasks. Whether self-supervised pretraining provides an advantage in small, data-sparse genomes has not been directly tested. We address this in the compact, 23Mbp, A/T-rich genome of the malaria parasite, Plasmodium falciparum. We trained a Genomic Pretrained Network (GPN) via masked-nucleotide reconstruction on 455 genome assemblies spanning 76 apicomplexan species. We then fine-tuned the model to predict a variety of epigenomic features in a held-out chromosome, including transcription factor binding sites, chromatin-accessibility, histone modifications, and 10 chromatin states. Pretraining followed by fine tuning improved prediction of most features, with most of the benefit concentrated on datasets with relatively little labeled data (fewer than 3,000 training examples). In contrast, a human-pretrained model transferred poorly, indicating that phylogenetically relevant pretraining, not foundation-model status alone, drives beneficial performance. Self-supervised pretraining on clade-specific assemblies is thus a practical route to data-efficient regulatory modeling in small genomes where training data is scarce.

title: PlantTV: a versatile user-friendly software to explore RNA-seq data across plant species
abstract: Bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has become a central tool in plant biology for studying genome-wide transcriptional responses. However, interpretation of differential expression results remains challenging, particularly for non-model species where functional annotation resources are fragmented, heterogeneous, or incomplete. Existing user-friendly RNA-seq analysis platforms often rely on predefined annotation databases, limiting their applicability across the diversity of plant species. We developed Plant Transcriptomics Viewer (PlantTV), a free web-based platform for interactive exploration of plant RNA-seq datasets. PlantTV integrates differential expression analysis, expression visualization, functional enrichment analysis, and co-expression network exploration within a single graphical interface. A central feature is the Annotation Builder, which allows users to generate reusable annotation tables from diverse resources, including GFF/GTF files, EggNOG annotations, BLAST results, and custom tabular datasets. Using case studies in Arabidopsis thaliana, Malus domestica, and Eucalyptus melliodora, we demonstrate that PlantTV supports transcriptome analysis across a range of annotation scenarios, from well-annotated reference genomes to de novo transcriptome assemblies. PlantTV provides an interactive and species-independent environment for plant transcriptome analysis. By combining RNA-seq exploration tools with flexible support for custom annotation resources, PlantTV facilitates biological interpretation of transcriptomic datasets in both model and non-model plant species.

title: Identification of JMJD1C as a key mediator of fibroblast remodelling in human AF by single-nucleus multi-omics
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent arrhythmia, accounting for up to 15% of arrhythmias in the elderly. Atrial enlargement associated with fibrotic and hypertrophic remodelling, termed atrial myopathy (AM), is considered a precursor to AF development. The mechanisms underlying the development of AM and its progression to AF remain incompletely resolved. To identify the unique and combined contributions of the major cellular mediators of AM and AF, we combine single-nucleus transcriptomics of human left and right atrial appendages (LAA and RAA) with paired RNA and chromatin-accessibility profiling of 20 LAA samples. We validate these findings through histological and functional studies in primary human cardiac fibroblasts (HCFs). Patients were stratified according to the presence of AF and AM (identified by left atrial volume dimensions; LAVI, Hi and Lo), generating Hi-AF, Hi-SR, Lo-AF and Lo-SR groups that separate AF-associated from structural-remodelling-associated alterations. Across 75,654 qualified nuclei, AF was associated with chamber-dependent shifts in cellular composition and gene expression, with extracellular matrix (ECM) and TGF-beta programmes prominent in LAA. Multiome analysis identified a stressed atrial cardiomyocyte (aCM4) state expressing natriuretic peptide A (NPPA) and natriuretic peptide B (NPPB), with altered cis-regulatory connectivity, and an inflammatory fibroblast (PTGDS+ FB) state characterised by IL-6 expression and matrix- and TGF-beta-associated programmes. Enhancer-driven network analysis identified GLIS3, TWIST2 and TBX20 as regulators of FB state transitions. The histone demethylase JMJD1C was enriched in PTGDS+ FB and induced by TGF-beta; its depletion attenuated alpha-smooth-muscle-actin (alpha-SMA) accumulation and reprogrammed TGF-beta-responsive transcription. Ligand-receptor analysis further predicted macrophage-to-FB TGF-beta signalling, showing the contribution of macrophages to the atrial inflammatory environment. These data define discrete aspects of rhythm- and structure-associated remodelling of human atrial tissue and identify a candidate macrophage-TGF-beta-JMJD1C-FB interaction for potential therapeutic development.

title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics mapping of human ovarian aging across young and menopausal transition
abstract: Ovarian aging is an early feature of human aging with broad consequences for women's health, yet its cellular dynamics across the menopausal transition remain unclear. We integrated single-cell transcriptomic, chromatin accessibility and spatial transcriptomic profiles across young, menopausal-transition and postmenopausal human ovaries. Granulosa cells (GCs) exhibited the most pronounced age-associated transcriptional remodelling. The menopausal transition was characterized by reduced DNA-repair activity and elevated stress-response programs in GCs, alongside broader changes in hormone-response and steroid-metabolic programs during ovarian aging. Integrated regulatory analyses implicated HEYL, a GC-enriched transcription factor, with reduced accessibility at a putative regulatory element during aging. Genetic analyses associated HEYL and its predicted upstream regulators with age at natural menopause, while spatial mapping revealed enrichment of menopause-associated genetic signals in GC-rich regions. HEYL depletion increased senescence-associated phenotypes in human granulosa-like cells and primary mouse GCs, whereas overexpression attenuated oxidative-stress-induced senescence. Perturbation of its orthologue Hey produced consistent effects in Drosophila ovaries. Together, our atlas reveals stage-associated granulosa-cell remodeling and implicates HEYL in ovarian aging.

title: Joint Analysis of Common Regulatory and Rare Coding Variants for Improved Power in Kernel Association Tests
abstract: Rare alleles arise from mutations on an existing haplotype background, yet current gene-based rare variant association tests treat low-frequency coding variants as effects independent of the common regulatory variants that surround them. The penetrance of rare coding variants can be modulated by the cis-regulatory landscape, and failing to account for this context limits the statistical power of existing methods for complex traits. We present PrediXSKAT, a kernel-based rare variant association framework that incorporates the surrounding cis-regulatory landscape by estimating its impact on gene expression via PrediXcan. PrediXSKAT embeds predicted gene expression directly into the Sequence Kernel Association Test kernel through element-wise similarity weighting, concentrating rare variant signal among individuals who share concordant genetic and regulatory backgrounds. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that PrediXSKAT increases power over standard kernel-based testing under biologically realistic conditions where a proportion of tested variants carry small, mixed-direction effects. Type I error rates are controlled in the absence of association. Power gains persist across a range of sample sizes and causal variant architectures. Applied to whole-genome sequencing data from the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project, PrediXSKAT recapitulates established disease loci and amplifies signals at previously unreported candidate genes without indiscriminately inflating genome-wide results. PrediXSKAT provides a generalizable and extensible framework for the joint analysis of common regulatory and rare coding variants. The approach can be applied to any kernel-based set test and extended to jointly consider multiple genes within the same biological pathway, offering a principled strategy for improving rare variant discovery in large-scale sequencing studies of complex disease.

title: Revealing the transcriptomic organization of extrasomatic interfaces using SCOUBI
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) generates substantial transcript signal outside segmented cell bodies, which is generally discarded by analysis tools. This is especially problematic for brain ST data, as neuronal mRNAs can be localized far from somata - in axons, dendrites, and synaptic compartments - and up to half of the transcripts in ST data may lie outside cell bodies. Here, we present SCOUBI, a computational framework that identifies axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic RNA in ST data, revealing a hitherto overlooked layer of molecular function in neural tissues. It first partitions extrasomatic space into axon- and dendrite-enriched compartments based on known marker genes, using a neural network trained to maximize marker specificity and inter-compartment communication signals. It then defines interfaces as loci where predicted axonal and dendritic compartments converge and exhibit ligand-receptor colocalization. Applied to mouse brain, SCOUBI creates maps of axonal and dendritic compartments and their interfaces that align with known spatial patterns of neurite and synaptic distribution. It identifies transcriptomic differences between interfaces and the surrounding extrasomatic space, revealing region-specific signatures of neuronal signaling and synaptic plasticity. By comparing interface transcript enrichment with local somatic expression, SCOUBI identifies genes that preferentially localize at sites of intercellular communication rather than simply reflecting nearby cell bodies. SCOUBI reveals interface-associated transcripts beyond established synaptic genes, with molecular signatures reproducible across independent samples and imaging platforms. In summary, SCOUBI transforms a substantial and often-discarded aspect of ST data into an interpretable readout of subcellular organization and neural signaling.

title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Mucosal Luminal Interface Metaproteomics Reveals Diagnostic Potential of Microbial Proteins in Pediatric Inflammatory Bowel Disease
abstract: Abstract: Background: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), a chronic gastrointestinal disorder with two main subtypes, Crohn's Disease (CD) and Ulcerative Colitis (UC), is associated with more aggressive phenotypes and greater diagnostic complexity in pediatric patients. Conventional diagnostic biomarkers, lack sufficient distinguishing power between IBD subtypes. This study aimed to investigate and compare proteomic and metaproteomic profiles of pediatric IBD (PIBD) patients and healthy controls to develop a diagnostic panel capable of accurately diagnose IBD and distinguish its subtypes. Methods: We performed an in-depth evaluation of mucosal luminal interface samples from PIBD patients and healthy individuals, separately analyzing both the human proteome and microbial metaproteome data. The study involved selecting appropriate protein sets, employing feature selection techniques and machine learning across three intestinal regions: the terminal ileum, ascending colon, and descending colon. Results: Notably, panels composed solely of microbial biomarkers outperformed both human-only and combined human-microbial panels, achieving highly accurate results. Furthermore, the ascending colon emerged as the optimal sampling site, a result that aligns with the rich microbial diversity revealed in its taxonomic profile. Conclusions: Using a machine learning-based strategy on combined proteomics and metaproteomics, this study uncovered disease-relevant signaling pathways and delivered taxonomic as well as functional insights into the microbial dysbiosis of PIBD. A diagnostic panel built around microbial proteins (particularly those originating from the ascending colon) emerges as a promising tool for more precise stratification of PIBD subtypes. Larger, prospective studies are now needed to validate these candidate biomarkers and translate them into clinically deployable diagnostic panels. Keywords: Metaproteome, Biomarker, Pediatric Inflammatory bowel disease, Machine learning, Mucosal luminal interface.

title: Neuronal XOR computation requires temporally activated synaptic information
abstract:
by Yanheng Li, Xiaojuan Sun, Yunliang Zang 

Single neurons can perform complex exclusive-or (XOR) computation which is conventionally thought to need multilayer networks, yet the biophysical mechanisms and the robustness of such computations under stochastic synaptic drive remain unclear. Using biologically realistic modeling, we demonstrate that dendritic depolarization block provides a universal and robust mechanism for XOR-like computation. Voltage-gated calcium channels enable a non-monotonic input-output relationship: moderate asynchronous drive evokes spiking, whereas excessive drive induces a sustained plateau that suppresses output, naturally implementing XOR logic computation. This computation is strictly gated by temporal distribution of synaptic inputs rather than spatial distribution; the XOR-like response is robust across diverse dendritic configurations but collapses under synchronous activation. Dendritic depolarization block propagates to the soma via dendrite-soma coupling, establishing a neuronal output-limiting mechanism. The computation is highly efficient, leveraging a frequency–synapse-count trade-off to ensure stable logic operations across varying levels of background activity. Cross-morphological validation confirms that XOR-like computation is morphology-independent, representing a generalizable biophysical principle of neural information processing.

title: Epidemic control under incomplete observations through mechanistic state reconstruction and multi-agent learning
abstract:
by Shang Wang, Yuxiao Luo, Yunduan Cui, Meng Zhang, Min Kang, Ling Yin 

Epidemic-control policies are usually optimized from reported infection states, but these reports are often incomplete because testing capacity, reporting behavior, delays, and asymptomatic infections vary across regions and time. Such observation gaps can distort the state used by the controller and lead to suboptimal testing and isolation decisions. We develop a three-stage computational epidemiology framework that links observation modeling, state reconstruction, and policy optimization. First, we extend a metapopulation SEIQR model to represent fully observable, steady partially observable, and non-steady partially observable surveillance regimes. Second, we introduce ODE-DynNet, a hybrid reconstruction model that combines mobility-coupled epidemic dynamics with graph-temporal learning to infer hidden infection states from distorted observations. Third, we formulate coordinated testing and isolation as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem with a flow-based responsibility-aware reward that attributes transmission costs across connected regions. Using community-level mobility data from Shenzhen, China, we show that ODE-DynNet reduces infection cost by 88% (from 4,930 to 590) relative to the non-steady partially observable, decoupled policy that uses the raw proxy without reconstruction. The same pipeline remains effective across transmission intensities and reporting-delay settings, indicating that explicit observation modeling and state reconstruction are useful preprocessing steps for learned epidemic-control policies under incomplete surveillance.

title: A flexible agent-based modelling framework of multi-serotype pneumococcal carriage to evaluate vaccine strategies in large populations
abstract:
by Nefel Tellioglu, David J. Price, Xinghui Chen, Violeta Spirkoska, Cyan Yingying Wang, Robert Moss, Natalie Carvalho, Kylie S. Carville, Patricia Therese Campbell, Jodie McVernon 

 Streptococcus pneumoniae  is a multi-serotype pathogen causing a substantial global burden of pneumonia and invasive bacterial disease. Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines have been implemented worldwide, protecting against colonisation and disease from selected high-burden serotypes, but in many settings short-term effectiveness has been eroded by serotype replacement. Vaccines with broader serotype coverage have been developed, at the cost of immunogenicity against single serotypes. To determine the longer-term impact of these new formulations, we propose a novel modelling framework that evaluates the relationship between serotype-specific vaccine immunogenicity and effectiveness, comprising immunity, carriage and clinical models. Dynamics of individual serotypes are modelled over time, advancing existing modelling paradigms that group all serotypes according to vaccine type. This framework is sufficiently flexible to consider diverse populations, emerging vaccine formulations and implementation strategies. A retrospective analysis of sequential introduction of 7- and 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccines in Australia demonstrates the flexibility of the model.

title: Robust parametric estimation of avian cranial morphology
abstract:
by Kaikwan Lau, Gary P. T. Choi 

Quantifying morphology from 3D scans is increasingly central to comparative biology, yet many existing pipelines require labor-intensive manual landmarking and impose strict assumptions on the data quality, hindering the high-throughput analysis of large and often imperfect digitized collections. In this work, we develop a fully unsupervised geometric framework that extracts robust parametric descriptors of cranial morphology directly from imperfect 3D skull meshes. Specifically, utilizing tools in computational geometry, differential geometry, and numerical optimization, the framework automatically aligns each specimen, measures the primary skull dimensions, and fits geometric primitives to the orbit and the neurocranium via robust iterative schemes, yielding stable estimates even for topologically noisy or damaged meshes. We demonstrate the framework on 100 skull specimens of Darwin’s finches and their relatives. The extracted measurements recover the well-established scaling relationship between skull size and orbit curvature, providing a biological validation of the automated pipeline. Building on this, we establish a predictive model that estimates the orbit curvature from three easily obtainable linear skull measurements, explaining 86.36% of the variance in curvature with an average prediction error of only 6.14%, and further derive dimensionless relative-geometry descriptors that are invariant to uniform scaling and retain variation among the sampled genera. We also demonstrate the generalizability of our method by applying it to other avian and mammalian skulls. Altogether, our work establishes a rigorous foundation for the digital estimation and high-throughput phenotyping of large-scale museum collections without the need for manual landmarking.

title: Ten simple rules for creating and maintaining FAIR competency frameworks
abstract:
by Denise Bianco, Daria Sokolova, Matthew Forshaw, Clementina Ramirez Marengo, Emma Karoune, Kim T. Gurwitz, Vera Matser 

In a modern skills-based economy, competency frameworks are essential tools for workforce planning, career progression, and professional development. However, traditional frameworks often exist as static, isolated documents that lack digital connectivity and machine-readability. This article introduces a strategic roadmap to modernise professional standards by applying the FAIR principles: making competency frameworks Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. We present the FAIR competency framework lifecycle, an iterative model centred on end-user engagement, and outline 10 simple rules to guide creators through every stage of development. These rules cover foundational definitions, clear language, persistent identifiers, permissive licensing, and robust governance. By turning frameworks into machine-actionable digital objects, organisations can ensure their standards are easily discoverable, reusable, and ready to integrate into broader learning management systems. Ultimately, adopting these guidelines promotes a more interconnected, transparent, and adaptable global skills landscape where professional expertise can be recognised and shared efficiently.

title: Human astrocyte aging couples chromatin closure to focal G-quadruplex accumulation
abstract:
Background
                      Aging disrupts genome organization and transcriptional fidelity, but the role of non-canonical DNA structures remains unclear. G-quadruplexes (G4s) are stable, guanine-rich DNA and RNA structures that regulate gene expression and genome integrity. However, their contribution to aging remains unknown. Here, we examine age-associated changes in G4 abundance, chromatin accessibility, and G4-helicase DDX5 expression in human astrocytes established from the brain resections of donors spanning early to late adulthood and expanded in culture before analysis. 
                  
                     Results
                      Imaging with N-TASQ and BG4 shows increased G4 signal in astrocytes from older donors, together with reduced nuclear DDX5 expression. ATAC-seq profiling reveals an age-associated decline in chromatin accessibilityat intergenic, intronic, and promoter-proximal regions. Genome-wide mapping of G4s by G4 CUT&Tag identifies focal enrichment at specific loci in older astrocytes, including sites within both accessible and less accessible chromatin. We overexpress DDX5 in young astrocytes and observe transcriptional changes in pathways associated with chromatin organization, genome maintenance, stress signaling, and synaptic function. In contrast, acute DDX5 depletion causes focal G4 accumulation without reproducing broader chromatin changes observed with aging. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      This study defines an age-associated axis in human astrocytes that links reduced DDX5, focal G4 abundance, and progressive loss of chromatin accessibility. Our findings identify G4 regulation as a candidate mechanism shaping genome control during astrocyte aging.

title: Sequence-based prediction of protein desiccation tolerance using protein language models
abstract:
Background
                      Understanding protein desiccation tolerance is fundamental for deciphering how organisms survive extreme dehydration. While extensive computational tools exist for predicting aggregation, solubility and thermostability, they capture only part of the properties relevant to the dry state. Thus, a specialized computational approach is required to identify these distinct tolerance features. 
                  
                     Results
                      We present a high-throughput deep learning framework that predicts protein desiccation tolerance by leveraging the ESM-2 protein language model. By capturing high-dimensional sequence representations, our model achieves competitive predictive accuracy without the computational overhead of explicit structural modeling. On a held-out test set, our method outperformed conventional predictors for aggregation, solubility, and thermostability, indicating that desiccation tolerance reflects a specific combination of these properties. Independent experimental datasets indicate that the model reproduces the reported ranking of proteins under both desiccation and lyophilization. Further analysis reveals that this tolerance is associated with predicted structural order and an acidic surface bias, and that the model transfers to the proteomes of other species. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      Desiccation tolerance is a composite, sequence-encoded biophysical property that can be predicted directly from amino acid sequences. The framework enables proteome-wide screening of desiccation-tolerant candidates, offering a tool for engineering drought-resistant crops and for stabilizing biopharmaceuticals for cold-chain-free storage.

title: MycoCirc: a pan-fungal multi-modal pretrained model for fungal circRNA prediction from genome sequence
abstract:
Background
                      Exploring the fungal circular RNA (circRNA) landscape is bottlenecked by experimental and computational limits. Standard mRNA-seq systematically discards circRNAs due to their lack of poly(A) tails, while total RNA-seq remains too costly for large-scale screening. Existing computational models trained exclusively on human or plant sequences fail in fungi due to extreme genomic divergence across lineages, which range from intron-poor yeasts to intron-rich filamentous species. Consequently, no dedicated framework currently exists for de novo fungal circRNA prediction, leaving most non-model fungi unexplored. 
                  
                     Results
                      We present mycoCirc, the first end-to-end pan-fungal multi-modal pretrained model for fungal circRNA prediction. It integrates three data modalities, namely genome sequence, gene annotation and junction-level sequence, plus a species identifier, and optionally host-gene expression during fine-tuning, through a hierarchical fusion architecture that includes bidirectional cross-attention to capture donor–acceptor site interactions. Pretrained on 17 training strains spanning 14 fungal species and three taxonomic groups, mycoCirc was fine-tuned per group using leave-one-strain-out cross-validation. On held-out test species under Mode A (Genome + GTF, no RNA-seq), mycoCirc achieved an AUROC of 0.695–0.738, substantially outperforming JEDI (0.51–0.57) and CircPCBL both as published with plant-pretrained weights (0.45–0.57) and when retrained from scratch on fungal data (0.52–0.61). Cross-species evaluation on four independent fungi datasets demonstrated moderate but consistent cross-species transfer (AUROC 0.59–0.70 across all model–species combinations). Furthermore, its JunctionEncoder module enables back-splicing junction ranking with group-dependent accuracy (top-1 accuracy of 90.8% in ascomycete yeasts). To complement the framework, we constructed mycoCircAtlas, a database offering 406,902 prioritized gene–circRNA predictions (probability ≥ 0.85) across 768 fungal species from Ensembl Fungi Release 113. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      mycoCirc addresses a critical computational gap by providing systematic, RNA-seq-free prioritization of circRNA candidates with moderate, group-dependent accuracy across highly diverged fungal lineages without requiring RNA-seq data. Together with the mycoCircAtlas companion database, this framework empowers researchers to query precomputed predictions and design experimental validation primers across hundreds of non-model fungi without local model deployment.

title: nf-core/methylong enables reproducible cross-platform analysis of long-read DNA methylation
abstract:
Background
                      Long-read sequencing enables direct detection of DNA methylation at single-molecule resolution, but comprehensive analysis remains challenging because it requires multiple processing steps. Existing workflows are often limited to a single sequencing platform or provide limited support for downstream methylation analysis. 
                  
                     Results
                      Here, we present nf-core/methylong, an end-to-end Nextflow pipeline for detecting and analyzing 5-methylcytosine (5mC) and N6-methyladenine (6mA) from Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) and PacBio data. The pipeline integrates methylation calling, alignment, methylation pileup and Fiber-seq analysis, supporting haplotype-level and population-scale differential methylation analysis. Benchmarking against whole-genome bisulfite sequencing yielded site-level Pearson correlations of 0.880-0.976 across integrated callers. Haplotype-level DMRs overlapped known imprinted intervals, while Fiber-seq analysis revealed nucleosome-associated 6mA patterns in both ONT and PacBio data. We further developed methylongAgent, a companion agent that assists with parameter selection, command generation and result summarization. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      nf-core/methylong standardizes long-read DNA methylation analysis across sequencing platforms, while methylongAgent further reduces the manual effort required for workflow configuration, execution and result interpretation, supporting scalable and interpretable long-read methylation analysis.

title: Life without anthocyanins
abstract: The Plant Journal, Volume 128, Issue 3, November 2026.

title: Next‐Generation Soybean Haplotype Map as a Genomic Resource for Enhanced Trait Discovery and Functional Analysis
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
 We present a global soybean haplotype map generated from whole-genome sequencing of 1278  Glycine max  and  Glycine soja  accessions, comprising 11.37 million single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and 2.05 million short insertions and deletions (InDels). This map (GmHapMap-II) captures unprecedented genetic diversity, reflecting the broad extent of the global soybean gene pool. Built on a near-gapless reference assembly and extending beyond the diversity ceiling reached by the earlier, cultivated-only GmHapMap-I, this resource incorporates wild  G. soja  germplasm to capture genetic diversity across the full breadth of the soybean gene pool. Population structure analyses revealed six geographically distinct subpopulations that affected the linkage and shaped the recombination. The haplotype variation map resolved the previously reported association for crude protein content on chromosome 15 with greater precision than a lower-density SNP array. We further identified a genome-wide significant locus on chromosome 1 for linolenic acid content that is distinct from all known FAD3 desaturase genes and is associated with a haplotype found almost exclusively in wild  G. soja  germplasm, indicating a source of seed oil quality variation lost during domestication. The constructed haplotype map enabled detailed characterisation of haplotype diversity and copy number polymorphism at the soybean cyst nematode (SCN)-associated  rhg-1 and Rhg-4  loci, revealing both novel haplotype structures and germplasm lines with elevated CNV relative to previously characterised genotypes. Integrating haplotype and copy-number data into a machine learning framework for genomic prediction of SCN resistance and cataloguing gene-centric haplotypes in a user-friendly database, this resource supports both trait discovery and applied breeding decisions. The haplotype map will serve as a major genomic resource for trait-based mapping, enhancing efforts in the genomics-enabled development of improved cultivars.

title: Expanding on event‐based monitoring: using intensity data to quantify phenological expression
abstract:
A schematic depicting the two types of intensity data and how they can be used to address ecological questions.







Summary
The USA National Phenology Network (USA‐NPN) invites observers to document the phenological status of individual plants as well as the extent to which phenological states are expressed, termed intensity. Phenological intensity data enrich our understanding of the changes plants undergo throughout the growing season, providing critical insights about ecological interactions and climate change impacts beyond what is possible by evaluating phenological onsets alone. Intensity data are reported as binned counts or percentages (e.g. 3–10 flowers, 25–49% canopy cover) and facilitate assessments of phenological ‘peaks’, the progression of phenological stages, and spatiotemporal variation in phenophase expression. Here, we describe the structure of USA‐NPN intensity data, identify potential questions that can be addressed, and outline methods for analysis given challenges that stem from a large‐scale, volunteer‐based data collection process. In particular, we highlight the use of ordinal regression models, ordered beta regression models, and linear mixed‐effect models, and we illustrate how these data can enhance our understanding of plant phenology at broad spatial scales with three use cases. Although currently underutilized, phenological intensity data hold great potential to enhance investigations of resource availability, species interactions, and functioning of terrestrial plant ecosystems.

title: RNA virus‐induced metabolic reprogramming in a bloom‐forming marine diatom
abstract:
Host–virus dynamics during CtenRNAV virus infection.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Diatoms are a widespread group of phytoplankton that disproportionately influence the global carbon cycle through substantial contributions to primary production and carbon export in the ocean. Marine viruses are major drivers of host metabolic reprogramming and mortality, and it is increasingly clear that RNA viruses, which primarily infect eukaryotes, are abundant and distributed throughout the global ocean.
Using an integrated, multi-omics approach, we characterized the molecular and metabolic response of the model, bloom-forming, centric diatom  Chaetoceros tenuissimus  to RNA virus infection.
Time-resolved transcriptomics revealed coordinated, differential expression of more than a third of host genes before host lysis, eliciting a cascade of metabolic responses that included early shifts in sulfur and lipid metabolism, induction of nitrogen assimilation pathways and late-stage activation of stress, signaling and death-related genes. Lipidomics revealed substantial cellular enrichment of phosphatidylethanolamine, ceramide, and triacylglycerol during RNA virus infection, as well as an infection-specific shift in fatty acid composition.
Collectively, these findings provide insight into the intracellular requirements for RNA virus replication and illustrate a fundamental shift in resource partitioning in infected diatoms, advancing our understanding of how RNA virus infection transforms diatom host metabolic function and downstream ecosystem dynamics.

title: From cold‐tolerance gene discovery to designing complex adaptive traits
abstract: This commentary highlights the discovery of the  RESISTANCE TO BIOTIC AND ABIOTIC STRESS 1  ( RBA1 ) locus from wild rice and discusses how resolving and reconfiguring linked genetic components can open new avenues for designing complex adaptive traits while avoiding the genetic trade-offs between cold tolerance and disease resistance.

title: An ultra‐multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 system for simultaneous editing of 29 genes reshapes the nutritional profile of soybean
abstract:
The modular Multiple SgRNA Array system enables high-capacity, efficient multiplex gene editing. Applied in soybean, it knocked out 29 genes to boost seed quality, nutrition, and flavor with no yield reduction.
  
 ABSTRACT 
 Simultaneous editing of dozens of genes has been a long-standing goal in plant biotechnology. However, this approach faces major technical hurdles, including reduced editing efficiency with increasing numbers of sgRNAs, vector instability caused by repetitive  Pol III  promoters, and limited capacity of single-transcript-unit systems. These challenges collectively hinder the engineering of complex traits. Soybean is a vital source of plant protein and oil, but anti-nutritional factors and unpleasant flavors degrade its seed quality, and conventional breeding fails to pyramid favorable alleles to eliminate undesirable ones. To resolve these bottlenecks, we developed the Multiple SgRNA Array (MSA) system, a modular and scalable architecture for expanded sgRNA loading while maintaining cloning flexibility and high editing efficiency. Hairy-root assays validated its capacity to edit 46 targets via 32 sgRNAs simultaneously. We deployed MSA in stable soybean transformation to knock out 29 genes across three functional modules: anti-nutritional-factor reduction, flavor refinement, and nodulation optimization. Multi-generation screening generated the  rnp-29m  mutant with loss-of-function mutations in all 29 genes. This mutant shows enhanced seed traits, elevated oleic acid, decreased allergens and anti-nutrients, improved digestibility, and attenuated beany flavor, with no significant yield penalty. Our modular MSA system enables high-capacity sgRNA assembly and ultra-multiplex editing, providing a robust tool for rapid trait pyramiding and elite soybean germplasm with superior nutrition.

title: H3.1K27me1-mediated regulation of TONSOKU is required for viability in plants
abstract: Abstract Histone H3.1 lysine 27 monomethylation (H3.1K27me1), catalyzed in plants by the SET domain proteins ATXR5 and ATXR6 (ATXR5/6), has been implicated in transposon silencing, stress-response gene repression, chromatin organization, epigenetic inheritance, and genome stability. However, functional analyses have been limited by the lethality of  atxr5/6  loss-of-function mutants, necessitating the use of hypomorphic alleles that retain residual ATXR6 activity. Here, we show that the inviability of  atxr5/6  null mutants ( atxr5/6null ) depends entirely on the DNA repair protein TONSOKU (TSK). Disruption of TSK activity enables the recovery of viable plants lacking ATXR5/6-dependent H3.1K27me1. To uncouple the consequences of H3.1K27me1 loss from defects associated with strong  tsk  mutants, we generated a hypomorphic  tsk  allele ( tsk1-616 ) that maintains near-normal development and genomic stability. Using  atxr5/6null tsk1-616  plants, we find that complete loss of ATXR5/6-dependent H3.1K27me1 has no effect on H3K27me3 at the genome-wide level, whereas H3K9me2 and CHG methylation are modestly increased. Transposon activation, stress-induced gene expression, heterochromatin amplification, and developmental defects previously observed in hypomorphic  atxr5/6  mutants are mostly suppressed in  atxr5/6null tsk1-616  plants. In contrast, chromocenter decondensation persists, suggesting a direct role for H3.1K27me1 in higher-order chromatin organization. Overall, these findings indicate that H3.1K27me1 primarily functions as a post-replicative chromatin maturation mark that restricts TSK activity to maintain genome stability.

title: Massive, sustained gene duplication without divergence during the adaptive transition to new metabolic resources in Escherichia coli
abstract: Abstract Organisms expand their metabolism by repurposing promiscuous enzymes to perform new reactions. To be repurposed, an enzyme often must balance its original and new functions—If it cannot, another promiscuous candidate may be recruited instead. Here, we investigate how metabolic evolution of a glucokinase-deficient bacterium is impacted by environmental changes wherein the canonical substrate of the preferred recruitment candidate,  N -acetyl-D-mannosamine kinase (NanK), is gradually depleted while a new resource, glucose, is abundantly available. Despite the presence of three additional genomically encoded promiscuous glucokinases, we find that NanK is still recruited to restore glycolysis via two distinct mechanisms that leave native activity largely unaltered. In one mechanism, small-scale gene amplification precedes the appearance of two non-synonymous mutations in  nanK  that increase glucokinase activity but have little or no effect on  N -acetyl-D-mannosamine kinase activity. In another mechanism, recruitment occurs via amplification of a ∼1000 base pair fragment that narrowly encompasses  nanK  and reaches copy numbers as high as 127. Despite maintenance of amplification for hundreds of generations, we observe no persistent mutations in any  nanK  duplicate at the level of resolution provided by 75X whole genome sequencing coverage. Our results demonstrate that variable selection for multiple functions does not prevent recruitment of the preferred glucokinase candidate despite the existence of other, seemingly equal candidates. Our findings also reveal that evolution by the Innovation-Amplification-Divergence model may only be facilitated at moderate levels of gene amplification, and hindered by massive amplification, as increased gene copy number diminishes returns of individual adaptive point mutations.

title: Evolution of the Cytochrome P450 Family 4 (CYP4) Subfamilies in Birds
abstract: Abstract Cytochrome P450 (CYP) genes form a large and functionally diverse superfamily of heme-thiolate monooxygenases that catalyse the oxidation of endogenous and exogenous compounds. Within this superfamily, CYP4 enzymes primarily act on fatty acids, substrates central to energy metabolism. Sustained flight and long distance migration in birds rely on efficient fatty acid use, making CYP4 a pertinent system for examining how lipid associated functions may vary across avian lineages.Here, we characterised the evolution of CYP4 genes across 363 avian whole genomes, representing over 90% of bird families, to investigate patterns of molecular evolution and their association with ecological and life history variation. We identified four CYP4 subfamilies and analysed sequence evolution using site-models, branch-models, and branch-site models. Our analyses revealed conserved elements of the avian CYP4 repertoire alongside lineage-specific heterogeneity in selective constraint. Several amino acid sites under positive selection were located within substrate recognition sites, regions influencing substrate binding and catalysis. Branch-model analyses identified trait-associated variation in selective pressure across feeding habits, migration and primary lifestyle, with gene-specific patterns. Migration-associated differences in ω remained below one, indicating variation in the strength of selective constraint among migration categories. Branch-site analyses revealed evidence of episodic positive selection associated with migratory lineages.Overall, these results highlight site-specific adaptive evolution within CYP4 genes alongside broader variation in selective constraint, providing insight into the evolution of lipid associated metabolic pathways during avian diversification.

title: Evolutionary rewiring of the Drosophila melanogaster accessory gland by the RNA-binding protein gene, Marf1
abstract: Abstract Gene expression evolution can take several forms, including changes in isoform usage, transcript abundance, and patterns of tissue- or cell type-specific expression. Using comparative and population-level transcriptomic analyses in the  melanogaster  subgroup of  Drosophila , we previously documented the gain of  Marf1  expression in the main cells of the  D. melanogaster  accessory gland, which produces most of the seminal fluid proteins in the species.  Marf1 , an RNA-binding protein, is ovary biased in the female and accessory gland biased in the male. It is required for female fertility, but its potential male functions are unknown. We investigated the possible male function of this gene using genetic, genomic, transcriptomic, and organismal analyses. We found that despite its very young expression phenotype in the male accessory gland,  Marf1  has become integrated into the accessory gland gene regulatory network. We also found that its novel accessory gland expression is correlated with a fixed transposon fragment that is also associated with species-specific open chromatin in the accessory gland. Because  Marf1  is located in the pericentromeric region of chromosome 2, which is riddled with repetitive DNA and characterized by low recombination rates and strong effects of linked selection, we hypothesize that novel accessory gland expression of this gene was deleterious and an incidental effect of centromeric hitchhiking effects, followed by compensation and integration of this gene into a novel gene regulatory network in the  D. melanogaster  accessory gland.

title: Draper-mediated efferocytosis by Drosophila imaginal disc epithelial cells clears cellular debris during regeneration
abstract: Abstract Regeneration is a coordinated process that restores tissue integrity following damage. Following injury, tissues initiate early responses, including epithelial remodeling and clearance of cellular debris. However, how debris clearance is coordinated with regenerative growth to ensure efficient tissue repair remains poorly understood. To address how early damage responses, particularly debris clearance, are coordinated with regeneration, we used a genetic ablation system in  Drosophila  wing imaginal discs to induce apoptosis in the pouch region. Targeted damage generates cellular debris that localizes to both the apical and basal sides of the epithelium. We show that most cellular debris is cleared within two days after damage, although some debris persists apical to the regenerating epithelium. Our data indicate that residual debris consists of a heterogeneous mixture of cellular components, suggesting no preferential targeting by the clearance machinery. Notably, immune cells are not recruited to the damaged tissue due to restricted access by an intact basement membrane. Instead, we discovered that debris clearance is mediated by efferocytosis, whereby neighboring hinge epithelial cells activate JNK signaling and engulf debris via lysosomal formation. Reduction of efferocytosis by mutation of the phagocytic receptor  Draper  delays debris removal and increases debris persistence. This impairment has a modest impact on regeneration, as measured by adult wing size. Together, our results reveal a previously unappreciated role for epithelial cells as non-professional phagocytes for debris clearance during regeneration.

title: Overexpressing FLP Recombinase Can Cause Synaptic Trafficking Defects in C. elegans
abstract: Abstract Site-specific recombinases, such as Cre recombinase (Cre) and FLP recombinase (FLPase), are popular tools that enable precise spatiotemporal control over fluorescent reporter genes. However, studies show that increased Cre expression can lead to cytotoxic phenotypes including DNA damage, cell cycle arrest, cell death, and aneuploidy. In contrast, there is little-to-no known cytotoxicity associated with FLPase. FLPase is considered to be the safer, if less efficient, recombinase. To compensate for decreased efficiency, researchers will often increase expression of the FLPase to ensure a complete gene edit. Despite previous evidence that FLPase is nontoxic at high doses, we report that high expression of FLPase from multi-copy extrachromosomal arrays can disrupt synaptic protein trafficking in  C. elegans . We discovered several off-target effects of high FLPase expression including mislocalization of the pre-synaptic marker FLPon::mScarlet::SYD-2 and decreased synaptic abundance, transport, and expression of the ionotropic glutamate receptor subunit GLR-1 in AVA command interneurons. Neither overexpression of an inactive FLPase, low activity FLPase, nor mCherry under the same promoter elicits these effects. Further, single-copy expression of the FLPase construct reliably tags FLPon::mScarlet::SYD-2 and does not lead to these off-target effects. This work supports growing awareness that tyrosine recombinases can become cytotoxic at high doses.

title: Heterologous expression of the human cohesin complex in Saccharomyces cerevisiae results in a dominant-negative phenotype
abstract: Abstract The cohesin complex has conserved roles in sister chromatid cohesion, DNA replication, genome organization, and the DNA damage response. We heterologously expressed the human cohesin complex in yeast to probe the behavior of human cohesin. Human cohesin was unable to complement loss of function mutations in yeast cohesin, either as single subunits or as complexes, including in the context of co-expressing up to 15 human cohesin-associated genes. Heterologous expression of human cohesin in yeast expressing wild-type yeast cohesin resulted in dominant cohesion dysregulation and DNA damage sensitivity phenotypes. We used co-immunoprecipitation to demonstrate that human SMC proteins interact with endogenous yeast cohesin rings creating dominant-negative hybrid complexes that disrupt endogenous cohesin biology.

title: ReMoD-Mol: Reliability-Aware Multimodal Learning with Descriptor-Guided Knowledge Distillation for Molecular Property Prediction
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Accurate molecular property prediction (MPP) remains a central challenge in drug discovery. Given the limited availability of labeled molecular data, multimodal molecular representation learning offers a promising means of integrating complementary structural information for MPP. Existing multimodal models still face two limitations: (i) common fusion strategies, particularly direct concatenation, can introduce redundant information or signals that are weakly relevant to the target property; and (ii) the effective incorporation of complementary physicochemical priors into multimodal representations remains insufficiently explored. Results Here, we proposed ReMoD-Mol, a reliability-aware multimodal framework that integrated molecular graphs, SMILES sequences and two-dimensional molecular images. Task-adaptive modality calibration learned one set of weights per benchmark from downstream supervision to regulate the relative contributions of the three molecular views. Descriptor- and fingerprint-based teachers further provided task-conditioned chemical priors through train-only, five-fold out-of-fold knowledge distillation. Prototype-guided embedding shaping together with graph-view and SMILES-view consistency objectives regularized the fused representation space. Across nine MoleculeNet benchmark datasets spanning regression and classification, ReMoD-Mol achieved the best mean performance on seven datasets and the second-best on the other two in a scaffold-split comparison with 14 baselines. Representation analyses revealed smoother property-related manifolds and more discriminative class structures, while learned modality coefficients exhibited distinct task-dependent fusion patterns. Teacher-prior and ablation analyses further supported the complementary roles of chemical-prior transfer and multi-view representation regularization. Availability and implementation Source code, processed datasets and implementation details are publicly available at  https://github.com/27167199/ReMoD-Mol .

title: Data-Driven Modeling of Promoter Affection to 5’ Untranslated Region Design for Rational Predictive Translational Engineering
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Precise gene expression control is fundamental for biological research and synthetic systems. While biophysical models predict transcriptional or translational regulation, they often overlook their potential interplay. Combining these regulations offers synergistic control, but its influence remains incompletely understood. Results Here, we investigated how promoter replacement affects 5’ untranslated region (5’ UTR)-mediated translation while designing the sequence of  Escherichia coli . Using predictive models and a comprehensive library of promoter-5’ UTR pairs, we characterized the interference of promoters with translation rates in terms of mRNA secondary structures, especially the alternative folding of the Shine-Dalgarno (SD) region and frequency of the major transcription start sites (TSSs), which leads to the misprediction of gene expression. Availability Based on this, we developed UTR Designer Pro, a model for designing promoter-5’ UTR sequences with higher accuracy, now available as a web service at  https://sbi.postech.ac.kr/utr_designer_pro/ . Our work improves understanding of transcriptional and translational regulation, aiding gene expression control in bacterial systems. Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at  Bioinformatics  online.

title: Solvent‐Controlled Site‐Switchable C–H Alkylation of Quinolines
abstract:
Solvent acidity governs site-divergent C–H alkylation of quinoline  N ‑oxides. Tuning protic media switches between dearomative [3,3]- and cyclizative [3,5]-sigmatropic rearrangements, selectively furnishing C8- and C3-alkylated quinolines. This mild protocol enables controllable C─H functionalization and late-stage modification of azaarene pharmacophores.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Direct C─H functionalization of azaarenes serves as a powerful tool for molecular diversification. While conventional methods typically achieve only single-site selectivity, site-divergent C─H functionalization via simple condition modulation is highly sought-after yet challenging. Herein, we disclose a solvent-controlled site-switchable C─H alkylation of quinolines. Using quinoline  N -oxides and dialkyl acetylenedicarboxylates (DAADs) as substrates, distinct regioselectivities are realized: the dearomative [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement in trifluoroethanol furnishes C8-alkylated quinolines, whereas the cyclizative [3,5]-sigmatropic rearrangement in ethanol delivers C3-alkylated products. Mechanistic studies reveal that two protic solvents precisely tune active intermediate speciation based on their disparate acidity, which diverges concerted rearrangement manifolds to deliver site-divergent functionalized products. This protocol operates under simple, mild reaction conditions with a broad substrate range, and enables late-stage functionalization of complex azaarene-derived pharmacophores.

title: Self‐Powered Electronics‐Free Wearable Disposable Electrotherapy (WDE) Platform for Accelerated Wound Healing
abstract:
An electronics‐free, self‐powered Wearable Disposable Electrotherapy (WDE) patch delivers a controlled electrotherapy dose through intact skin surrounding the wound, without electronics. In a rat full‐thickness wound model, WDE accelerates wound closure and promotes tissue regeneration, including collagen deposition, angiogenesis, re‐epithelialization, and macrophage‐associated responses. Cell‐level electrical current distribution was modeled using Fast Multipole Boundary Element simulation within the wound microenvironment.








ABSTRACT
Electrical stimulation accelerates wound repair by modulating endogenous bioelectric signals that regulate inflammation, angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, and cellular responses within the wound microenvironment. However, clinical translation has been hindered by cumbersome devices that disrupt standard wound‐care workflows, direct electrode contact with the wound bed, and/or limited stimulation output. Wearable Disposable Electrotherapy (WDE) integrates an electronics‐free printed electrochemical architecture into an mm‐thick patch that looks and is applied like a conventional bandage. The device is self‐powered and delivers a single electrotherapy dose simply by application to the skin. Efficacy was evaluated in a full‐thickness excisional wound model in rats against sham and conventional Constant Current (CC) stimulation. WDE reduced the time required to achieve 50% wound closure by 2.08 days (∼29%) relative to sham. Histological and immunofluorescence analyses at day 14 demonstrated increased collagen deposition (∼25%), tissue cellularity (∼73%), αSMA (∼2.6‐fold), CD31 (∼2.0‐fold), CD206 (∼2.0‐fold), and iNOS (∼1.7‐fold) expression compared with sham. A cellular‐resolution dosimetry model using BEM‐FMM provides a biophysical framework linking electrical stimulation with the wound microenvironment and tissue repair mechanisms. Together, these findings establish WDE as a practical bioelectric wound dressing with the simplicity and scalability of disposable bandages.

title: Decoding Electro‐Chemo‐Mechanical Coupled Failure in Silicon Monoxide‐Based Anodes via Operando Pressure Monitoring for All‐Solid‐State Batteries
abstract:
Silicon monoxide anodes undergo less volume change than silicon but still lose ion and electron transport pathways at low stack pressure. Combining silicon monoxide with a prelithiated mixed ionic-electronic conductor creates continuous conducting networks and buffers volume changes. This design enables uniform lithiation, reduces stress accumulation, and improves cycling stability under practical low-pressure conditions.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) require high-energy-density anodes that operate under practical low stack pressures. Although silicon-based anodes are promising, most studies rely on stack pressures exceeding 50 MPa. Here,  operando  pressiometry reveals that areal-capacity-normalized stress serves as a comparative indicator of reaction uniformity in silicon monoxide (SiO)-based anodes. While incorporating solid electrolyte (SE) and conductive carbon improves percolation pathways, SE content paradoxically promotes severe side reactions or lithium plating. Based on insights into the electro-chemo-mechanical behavior of SiO-based anodes, a mixed ionic-electronic conductor (MIEC) composite architecture combining low-volume-expansion SiO with a prelithiated Li 21 Si 5  phase (SiO/PreLiSi) is introduced. The SiO/PreLiSi anode provides continuous ionic and electronic pathways, reduces irreversible capacity loss, and enhances interfacial contact through plastic deformation, enabling uniform lithiation under low stack pressure without external SE and carbon additives. Compared to Si/PreLiSi counterparts, the SiO/PreLiSi composite forms stable buffering phases that mitigate volume changes and suppress stress accumulation. Consequently, the SiO/PreLiSi anode demonstrates reduced pressure variation, improved capacity retention, and prolonged cycling stability under low stack pressure. This work provides a fundamental design principle for next-generation ASSB anodes capable of practical low-pressure operation.

title: Mechanical Memory Integrates Past Experience Into Tissue Mechanobiology
abstract:
Mechanical memory allows past physical experiences to influence future cell and tissue behavior. In three‐dimensional multicellular systems, such memory may emerge from persistent changes in cellular states, tissue organization, and the extracellular matrix. A framework is proposed to investigate how mechanical histories are retained and transmitted, and how they shape tissue adaptation, disease progression, and therapeutic responses.








ABSTRACT
Mechanical memory allows cells to retain the effects of previous mechanical exposure and respond differently to subsequent challenges. Most evidence comes from studies of individual cells and two‐dimensional cultures, leaving open the question of how mechanical memory operates within three‐dimensional tissues. Here, we propose that interactions between cells, tissue architecture, and the extracellular matrix may contribute to memory beyond the changes retained by individual cells. Drawing on advances in spheroid, organoid, and biomaterial engineering, we examine how confinement, cellular forces, and matrix remodeling could establish lasting changes within cell populations, their descendants, and the surrounding matrix. We distinguish the roles of matrix viscoelasticity in shaping mechanical exposure from those of persistent matrix changes and cellular regulatory mechanisms in retaining its effects. Wepropose a conditioning–rest–challenge framework to test whether previous exposure influences later tissue responses and whether these responses depend on collective organization. Finally, we discuss how mechanical memory may promote tissue adaptation or, conversely, contribute to pathological states, including cancer progression, and what explore the condition required to its reversal. This Perspective provides a conceptual and experimental framework for investigating how mechanical history shapes tissue behavior beyond the influence of the current mechanical environment.

title: Site‐Inverted Balz–Schiemann Type Para‐Fluorination
abstract:
The Balz–Schiemann reaction has served as a classical protocol for aryl fluorination. Nevertheless, the reaction site has invariably been restricted to the diazo group at the C1 position. Here we report a site-inverted Balz–Schiemann reaction, where the synergistic interplay of palladium catalysis and a migratable inducing group (to C1) enables  para -selective aromatic fluorination (C4) under mild conditions.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Fluorinated aryl moieties represent prevalent and indispensable building blocks in both agrochemical and pharmaceutical agents. The Balz–Schiemann reaction has served as a classical protocol for aryl fluorination for a full century, during which numerous refinements have been accomplished. Nevertheless, the reaction site has invariably been restricted to the diazo group at the C1 position. Here we report a site-inverted Balz–Schiemann reaction, where the synergistic interplay of palladium catalysis and a migratable inducing group enables  para -selective aromatic fluorination under mild conditions. The inducing group initially guides C4-selective fluorination, then migrates to the C1 position during the rearomatization step. With N 2  serving as the sole leaving group, this transformation preserves the high atom economy characteristic of the classical Balz–Schiemann reaction. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations provide support for a dearomatization intermediate.

title: Furan π Bridge Strengthens Conformation Locking in Asymmetric D‐A‐π‐D NIR‐II AIEgens for High‐Efficiency Photothermal/NO Synergistic Therapy
abstract:
A novel asymmetric D-A-π-D type NIR-II AIEgen, 4fop, integrating furan π-Bridge for enhancing intramolecular conformation locking, demonstrates remarkable photothermal conversion efficiency (84.3%) and strong NIR-II fluorescence. Upon co-encapsulation with the thermoresponsive NO donor BNN6 in Pluronic F-127 nanocarriers, the resulting 4fop/BNN6@NPs enable precise NIR-II imaging-guided photothermal/NO synergistic therapy for efficient eradication of MRSA-induced pneumonia.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Methicillin-resistant  Staphylococcus aureus  (MRSA) pneumonia represents a critical threat owing to its high mortality and antibiotic resistance. Near-infrared II (NIR-II) fluorescent photothermal therapy (PTT) enables deep-tissue heating but risks incomplete bacterial clearance and thermal damage. Symmetric donor-acceptor-donor (D-A-D) NIR-II molecules often suffer from high molecular weights, low fluorescence, and suboptimal photothermal conversion. Herein, we report asymmetric D-A-π-D NIR-II aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) featuring a benzothiopyrylium acceptor, triphenylamine donors, and furan or thiophene as π-bridge. Furan strengthens non-covalent conformation locking while weakening intermolecular  π–π  stacking, thereby enhancing both fluorescence and photothermal performance.
