AIEgen 4fop achieves an optimal photothermal conversion efficiency of 84.3% and a NIR-II photoluminescence quantum yield of 2.31% in toluene. To boost antibacterial activity, 4fop was co-encapsulated with the thermally responsive NO donor BNN6 into Pluronic F-127 nanoparticles. In a murine pneumonia model, this nanoplatform substantially reduces bacterial burden, suppresses inflammation through TNF pathway modulation, and promotes lung repair. This work establishes a rational D-A-π-D design strategy and an integrated nanoplatform for the precise treatment of deep-seated drug-resistant infections.

title: Hierarchically Porous COFs Enabled by Copolymer‐Mediated Mechanochemical Preassembly
abstract:
We propose a general, reproducible strategy that combines copolymer-mediated mechanochemical preassembly with recrystallization to construct crystalline, hierarchically porous covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with tunable large mesopores and diverse topologies. The confined microenvironments of low-solvent ball-milling strengthen hydrogen-bonding interactions between monomers and micelle assemblies, and lock mesostructures via stepwise kinetics, rationalizing the evolution of mesoscopic architectures.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The relatively small pore channels of conventional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) would impede mass transport and limit the accessibility of active sites therein, restricting their practical utility with bulky molecules. Here, we break this bottleneck by developing a copolymer-mediated mechanochemistry strategy that enables the construction of hierarchically porous COF (HPCOF) precursors with tunable large mesopores, which are then recrystallized to afford crystalline HPCOFs. The confined microenvironments of low-solvent ball-milling not only enhance hydrogen-bonding interactions between monomers and Pluronic F127 (PEO 106 PPO 70 PEO 106 ) micelles, but also eliminate the disruptive effects of excess solvent and acidic conditions on micelle assembly. Additionally, the mechanical pulses decompose the polycondensation into stepwise events, effectively buffering the incompatible rates between the polymerization of COF precursors and micelle assembly and allowing the mesostructures to be precisely “locked” under solid-state confined conditions. By varying monomer combinations, seven representative HPCOFs with different connectivities were constructed. Thanks to its simplicity and reproducibility, the proposed strategy demonstrates potential in large-scale production. Benefiting from the synergistic combination of large channels and rigid microporous crystalline walls, the resultant HPCOFs feature unique structural stability and favorable enzyme affinity, enabling efficient trypsin immobilization with retained catalytic activity for protein hydrolysis, prefiguring their application prospects in bioreactor construction.

title: Ultra‐Wide Temperature‐Stable High Piezoelectricity in Textured CaBi2Nb2O9 Ceramics via Defect‐enhanced Asymmetric Jahn‐Teller Distortion
abstract:
Synergistic integration of texture engineering and CuO doping overcomes the trade-off between piezoelectric activity and thermal stability in CaBi 2 Nb 2 O 9  ceramics. While a highly oriented grain arrangement maximizes the piezoelectric response, defect-enhanced Jahn-Teller distortion rigidifies the oxygen octahedral network. This effectively suppresses thermally induced depolarization, ensuring ultra-stable high-temperature piezoelectricity for extreme-environment applications.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 CaBi 2 Nb 2 O 9  is regarded as an eminently promising candidate for high-temperature piezoelectric devices due to its ultra-high Curie temperature and good insulation. Unfortunately, extremely low piezoelectric properties and poor temperature stability severely hinder its practical application. In this work, the CuO doping strengthens the structural rigidity of the octahedral network against temperature by coupling the Jahn-Teller effect of Cu 2+  with defect dipoles to form a defect-enhanced Jahn-Teller distortion, combined with the modulation of the polarization to the poling electric field direction via textural engineering, significant improvement of both piezoelectric response and temperature stability can be realized simultaneously. As a result, the sample with 0.1 wt.% CuO not only maintains an ultra-high Curie temperature ( T 
 C  ∼ 958°C) but also exhibits a  d 
 33  value of ∼27 pC/N and a low high-temperature (600°C) dielectric loss of 0.028. Simultaneously, its piezoelectric properties demonstrated excellent temperature stability by in-situ heating up to 600°C (Δ d 
 33 ∼4.96%) as well as undergoing 10 cycles of high-low temperature cycling tests (RT-750°C-RT, enduring approximately 240 h). This work represents a breakthrough for the practical application of high-temperature piezoelectric ceramics.

title: Trypsin Digestion Impacts Cellular Functions and Drug Efficacy Evaluation via PAR2/NLRP3 Signaling
abstract:
This study demonstrates that trypsin digestion alters cellular functions across multiple cell types and diminishes anti‐tumor drug efficacy in breast cancer via PAR2/NLRP3 signaling, whereas PAR2 knockout or inhibitors would abolish such effects. It provides critical insights for the rational application of trypsin as a digestive agent in cell culture and biomedical assays.








ABSTRACT
Trypsin acts as a standard digestive reagent for cell dissociation and passaging in biomedical research. In addition to its role in proteolytic detachment, trypsin activates protease‐activated receptor 2 (PAR2), a member of the G protein‐coupled receptor, thereby initiating downstream signaling. However, the impact of this unintended PAR2 activation on regulating cellular functions, and its consequent influence on drug candidate evaluation in cell‐based assays, has long been overlooked. Here, we demonstrated that trypsin‐mediated dissociation, unlike EDTA treatment or mechanical pipetting, potently enhanced cell adhesion, migration, and proliferation across multiple cell types in vitro, and accelerated tumor growth in vivo, primarily via PAR2 signaling. Moreover, trypsin digestion compromised the anti‐migratory and anti‐tumor efficacy of sorafenib, which could be effectively rescued by PAR2 knockout. Importantly, trypsin‐induced PAR2 activation acted as a cumulative proinflammatory stimulus, which peaked at 24 h post‐treatment, and facilitated EMT, adhesion, migration, and tumor growth, mechanistically through the NLRP3/caspase‐1/IL‐1β/IL‐18 pathway. Collectively, it revealed a previously unrecognized signaling mechanism by which routine trypsin digestion modulated fundamental cellular behaviors and biased drug efficacy evaluation. The potential confounding effects of PAR2 activation triggered by trypsin dissociation should be carefully considered—and minimized where possible—in experimental design and data analysis within biological and pharmaceutical research.

title: NRF2‐Associated ROS Clearance by PRP‐TPGN Hydrogel Accelerates Re‐Epithelialization in Diabetic Wounds
abstract:
TPGN nanoparticles are fabricated by covalent conjugation and self-assembly. Mixed with PRP, the blend forms an in situ gel on diabetic wounds. TPGN scavenges ROS and activates the NRF2/ARE pathway, while PRP releases growth factors. Their synergistic effects remodel the wound microenvironment and accelerate diabetic skin wound healing.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 In the diabetic wound microenvironment, excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) induces severe oxidative stress, thereby restricting re-epithelialization. Although platelet-rich plasma (PRP) gel can promote tissue repair by releasing platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), its bioactivity is substantially degraded by high ROS levels, which limits its clinical utility. To address this challenge, we designed a glucose-based molecular scaffold covalently conjugated with 4-Hydroxy-2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidin-1-oxyl (Tempol) and phenylboronic acid pinacol ester (PBAP), designated TPG. This molecule spontaneously self-assembles into monodisperse spherical nanoparticles (TPG-PBAP-Glucose nanoparticles, TPGN), which exhibit favorable biocompatibility and H 2 O 2 -triggered degradation, enabling on-demand payload release within oxidative microenvironments. We further incorporated TPGN into PRP to form an in situ forming PRP-TPGN composite gel. In vitro functional assays demonstrated that this composite gel accelerated keratinocyte migration under high-glucose conditions by activating the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) antioxidant signaling pathway; this protective effect was markedly attenuated by NRF2 knockdown or pharmacological inhibition. In streptozotocin-induced diabetic mice, PRP-TPGN expedited wound closure through NRF2-mediated ROS clearance, and this therapeutic benefit was largely diminished in NRF2-knockout animals. Collectively, the PRP-TPGN hydrogel constitutes a rationally designed, redox-synergistic therapeutic platform for the targeted management of refractory diabetic cutaneous ulcers.

title: CDK12 Inhibition Against Group 3 Medulloblastoma With PROTAC or Molecular Glue Degrader: Resistance Mediated by Distinct Transporters and Effective Countermeasures
abstract:
This study reveals novel cellular transmembrane transporters whose upregulation can confer resistance to PROTACs (ABCG2) or molecular glue degraders (SLC16A2 and ABCA2) in G3‐MB. Moreover, conventional BET inhibitors or CDK9 inhibitors can circumvent resistance to CDK12‐targeted PROTACs or CCNK‐targeted molecular glue degraders and exhibit synergistic inhibitory effects against G3‐MB when used in combination in vitro and in vivo.








ABSTRACT
PROTACs and molecular glue degraders represent novel approaches to developing therapeutic agents that target epigenetic and transcriptional regulators. It is crucial to understand their potential resistance mechanisms and countermeasures. In this study, we perform a parallel comparison of CDK12 inhibition therapy with CDK12‐targeted PROTAC, CCNK‐targeted molecular glue degrader, or conventional CDK12/13 inhibitor in treating group 3 medulloblastoma (G3‐MB). We verify loss of function of CRL4 E3 ligase via genomic or transcriptional aberrations that induce resistance to PROTACs and molecular glue degraders in G3‐MB, as previously reported in other cancers. More importantly, we reveal distinct sets of transmembrane transporters that regulate sensitivity to these agents: ABCG2 regulates sensitivity to the tested PROTACs in addition to the previously reported ABCB1 and ABCC1, whereas SLC16A2 and ABCA2 regulate sensitivity to the tested molecular glue degraders. Furthermore, we demonstrate that conventional function‐targeted inhibitors, such as BET inhibitors and CDK9 inhibitors, remain effective against G3‐MB models resistant to CDK12 inhibition therapy with PROTACs or molecular glue degraders and exhibit synergistic inhibitory effects against G3‐MB when used in combination. Together, these results not only advance our understanding of resistance to these agents in G3‐MB models but also provide insights into challenges during clinical translation of epigenetic/transcriptional targeted inhibitors.

title: ZDHHC20‐Mediated Palmitoylation of METTL16 Represses the m6A‐STEAP1 Axis and Confers Cell Resistance to Cuproptosis in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract:
In this study, we demonstrate that METTL16 plays a pivotal role in the cellular response to copper stress and cuproptosis by mediating the m6A modification of the STEAP1. However, the activity of the METTL16-STEAP1 axis is constrained by the cytoplasmic localization of METTL16, which is regulated by the protein ZDHHC20.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Methyltransferase-like 16 (METTL16), an m6A methyltransferase, regulates metal metabolism, but its role in copper homeostasis and cuproptosis in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unknown. Using ESCC cells exposed to CuCl 2  or cuproptosis inducers, RNA interference, multi-omics, reader screening, and protein-turnover assays, we dissected the ZDHHC20–METTL16–STEAP1 axis. Xenograft and 4NQO-induced models, TCGA/GTEx datasets, and tissue microarrays were used for in vivo and prognostic analyses. Copper stress upregulated METTL16 and m6A modifications. METTL16 silencing reduced sensitivity to elesclomol-Cu/disulfiram-induced cuproptosis, which was rescued by STEAP1 overexpression. Mechanistically, METTL16 stabilized STEAP1 mRNA via m6A modification at position 286 with YTHDC1, enhancing cuproptosis sensitivity. Conversely, ZDHHC20 mediated METTL16 palmitoylation and cytoplasmic retention, suppressing STEAP1 stabilization and increasing cuproptosis resistance; ZDHHC20 depletion altered METTL16 localization without affecting its abundance or turnover. In vivo, ZDHHC20 knockout reduced esophageal lesion burden, whereas METTL16-IN-1 or vandortuzumab vedotin administration was associated with increased lesion burden in knockout mice. The VDM-associated observations did not establish STEAP1-specific inhibition in vivo. High ZDHHC20 correlated with poor prognosis, while elevated METTL16/STEAP1 predicted better survival. Targeting the ZDHHC20–METTL16–STEAP1 axis may overcome cuproptosis resistance in ESCC.

title: Bioinspired Oxygen‐Bridged MIL‐100(Mn) Nanozymes Alleviate Chlorinated Paraffin‐Induced Lipid Disorders via the Gut‐Liver Axis
abstract:
Chlorinated paraffins (CPs) disrupt mitochondrial redox homeostasis, causing oxidative stress and gut-liver axis dysfunction that ultimately drives lipid metabolic disorders. Inspired by natural Mn-SOD, we developed oxygen-bridged MIL-100(Mn) nanozymes with enhanced SOD/CAT-like cascade activity. Oral administration restored CP-induced lipid metabolism by reprogramming gut microbiota and hepatic lipid-related genes, highlighting oxygen-bridged architectures as promising antioxidant designs.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Chlorinated paraffins (CPs) disrupt mitochondrial regulation of redox homeostasis, generating excessive reactive oxygen species. The resulting oxidative stress disturbs gut microbiota-liver crosstalk and ultimately induces lipid metabolic disorders, yet effective strategies to restore this metabolic communication remain limited. Inspired by the natural mitochondrial Mn-superoxide dismutase (Mn-SOD) and the biocompatibility of manganese, we constructed an octahedral MIL-100(Mn) nanozyme. Structurally, the unique  µ 
 3 -oxo-bridged trinuclear clusters within MIL-100 topology simulate the active center of natural Mn-SOD, offering more accessible metal active sites and hierarchical pores that enhance the adsorption of reaction intermediates and stabilize the thermodynamic environment, thereby improving catalytic efficiency compared with disordered Mn-BTC. Functionally, administration of MIL-100(Mn) enhanced the total SOD activity ∼8.75-fold, while the cascade of CAT activity prevented the potential toxic accumulation of H 2 O 2 . Following oral administration, MIL-100(Mn) reversed CP-induced lipid metabolic abnormalities in mice. Multi-omics integration revealed that this metabolic rescue is highly correlated with the coordinated reprogramming of the gut-liver axis, characterized by regulation of the dominant gut microbiota and normalization of key lipid metabolism-related genes. This work highlights an association between oxygen-bridged architecture and enhanced antioxidant nanozyme activity, while providing a potential design strategy for correcting lipid metabolic disorders through the gut-liver axis.

title: In Situ Multimodal Insights Into Hydration‐Driven MgO–Brucite Strength Build‐Up
abstract:
Hydrating MgO binders follow a non‐equilibrium, multiscale pathway. In this study, we used space‐time‐resolved correlative in situ multimodal characterization and atomistic‐level simulations to reveal how MgO‐to‐brucite transformation generates strength from the atomic to the macroscopic scale. Structural rigidity is governed by a discontinuous transition driven by morphological interlocking, which is temporally decoupled from bulk chemical conversion.








ABSTRACT
Decarbonizing the built environment demands scalable alternatives to Portland cement. Magnesium oxide (MgO) underpins a transformative class of low‐carbon binders, yet existing hydration mechanisms are primarily based on studies of dilute equilibrium systems, failing to capture the spatial confinement and local thermodynamic boundaries. By coupling a temporal and multimodal in situ analytical suite with density functional theory, we uncover a multiscale, non‐equilibrium hydration paradigm spanning orders of magnitude in length scale. We show that localized water activity acts as a dynamic switch: sufficient liquid water drives direct conversion to brucite, whereas water‐deficient conditions metastabilize a transient amorphous hydroxide intermediate. Water exposure triggers rapid MgO expansion, driving crystallite reorientation and particle rearrangement that reduce nucleation site spacing and promote hydration. At the single‐particle scale, inward front propagation induces sub‐surface hydrogen diffusion, where the hydrated overlayer accumulates tensile stress and generates local structural instability, sustaining cyclic renewal until progressive shell thickening arrests conversion. Similarly, at the particle‐cluster level, hydration products nucleate preferentially at the cluster perimeter. At the mesoscale, compaction organizes these core–shell architectures into an interlocked and load‐bearing brucite network. These insights into non‐equilibrium phase transformation and the structuration mechanisms of hydrating MgO pave the way for the next generation of potentially carbon‐negative cementitious materials.

title: MAGEA6 Phase Separation Suppresses Pyroptosis and Promotes Chemoprotection in Esophageal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract:
High MAGEA6 expression promotes condensate formation and sequestration of TP63 and GSDME, thereby suppressing the NLRP1–Caspase-1–GSDMD and Caspase-3–GSDME pyroptotic pathways. Cisplatin or the MAGEA6 ΔIDR  peptide disrupts this protective condensate state, releasing TP63 and increasing GSDME accessibility, which restores pyroptotic signaling and enhances cisplatin sensitivity.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Chemotherapy can trigger pyroptosis in cancer cells, yet the intrinsic regulatory mechanisms governing this process remain largely unclear. Here, we identify MAGEA6 as a phase-separating cancer-testis antigen that establishes a pyroptosis-suppressive condensate barrier in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) by coordinately restraining GSDMD and GSDME cleavage. Mechanistically, cytoplasm-anchored MAGEA6 undergoes phase separation, which impedes the nuclear translocation of TP63, thereby suppressing NLRP1 transcription and subsequent GSDMD activation. Concurrently, MAGEA6 recruits GSDME into dynamic condensates and restricts its Caspase-3-mediated cleavage in response to cisplatin. Disruption of MAGEA6 condensation relieved both inhibitory effects, whereas the MAGEA6 intrinsically disordered region was sufficient to sustain the chemoprotective condensate state. Perturbation of this condensate barrier restored pyroptotic signaling and increased cisplatin sensitivity across multiple ESCC models. These findings identify condensate-mediated spatial control of pyroptosis as a mechanism of chemoprotection and suggest MAGEA6 phase separation as a potential therapeutic target in cisplatin-resistant ESCC.

title: CRH‐CRHR1 Signaling in BNST‐vHPC Projections Mediates Trigeminal Neuropathic Pain‐Induced Anxiety‐ and Depression‐Like Behaviors
abstract:
CION increases the activity and excitability of BNST CRH  neurons. These neurons project to the vHPC, where CRH–CRHR1 signaling contributes to enhanced excitability of vHPC neurons and a shift in their response profile toward excitation. Manipulations targeting BNST CRH  neurons, BNST-derived CRH, BNST CRH -vHPC terminals, or vHPC CRHR1 attenuate anxiety- and depression-like behaviors, whereas local CRH infusion into the vHPC induces similar affective behavioral abnormalities.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Chronic pain is frequently accompanied by anxiety and depression, but the mechanisms linking nociceptive sensitization to affective dysfunction remain unclear. In a mouse model of chronic constriction injury of the infraorbital nerve (CION), we identified a corticotropin-releasing hormone (CRH)-dependent circuit through which trigeminal neuropathic pain promotes anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. CION induces hyperactivity of the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNST) neurons, particularly CRH-expressing neurons. Chemogenetic inhibition of BNST or BNST CRH  neurons alleviates CION-induced mechanical allodynia and improves anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. These effects are accompanied by increased  Crh  expression in the BNST, and local  Crh  deletion attenuates the behavioral abnormalities. BNST CRH  neurons directly innervate the ventral hippocampus (vHPC), where terminal inhibition reduces allodynia and affective deficits in CION mice. Postsynaptically, chronic pain shifts the functional output of this projection toward excitation. vHPC target neurons express  Crhr1 , and CRHR1 blockade prevents BNST CRH  terminal stimulation-induced excitation, reduces pathway-driven behavioral deficits, and ameliorates CION-induced anxiety- and depression-like behaviors. Conversely, intra-vHPC CRH infusion in naïve mice induces anxiety- and depression-like behaviors similar to those observed after CION. Together, these findings establish a BNST CRH -vHPC CRH-CRHR1 circuit linking trigeminal neuropathic pain to affective comorbidity and identify CRH-CRHR1 signaling as a potential therapeutic target.

title: IBA57 Functions as an Electron Transfer Activator in Mitochondrial [4Fe‐4S] Cluster Biogenesis
abstract:
This study defines the molecular function of IBA57 in mitochondrial Fe-S protein biogenesis. IBA57, in complex with ISCA2 ([2Fe-2S] IBA57-ISCA2), specifically recognizes [2Fe-2S] FDX2, thereby activating an electron transfer pathway involving NADPH, FDXR and FDX2. This pathway promotes the reduction of the [2Fe-2S] cluster bound to ISCA1-ISCA2.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The pathway responsible for mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] cluster assembly plays a crucial role in humans, as evidenced by numerous mitochondrial diseases linked to its dysfunction. GLRX5, FDX2, FDXR, ISCA1, ISCA2, and IBA57 are the proteins involved in the assembly of [4Fe-4S] clusters, but how they cooperate at the molecular level to accomplish this assembly remains unclear. Here, we provide a comprehensive investigation that elucidates the elusive molecular function of IBA57 in mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] cluster assembly. We found that the IBA57 subunit of the [2Fe-2S] IBA57-ISCA2 complex specifically recognizes [2Fe-2S] FDX2 in a transient manner. This interaction enables rapid electron transfer from NADPH to the [2Fe-2S] 2+  cluster of the IBA57-ISCA2 complex via the FDXR/FDX2 system, reducing the cluster to [2Fe-2S] + . An NMR data-driven structural model of the transient complex between [2Fe-2S] FDX2 and [2Fe-2S] IBA57-ISCA2 reveals a 17 Å electron transfer pathway connecting the [2Fe-2S] cluster of FDX2 to that of IBA57-ISCA2. Kinetic data showed that [2Fe-2S] +  IBA57-ISCA2, reduced by the NADPH/FDXR/FDX2 system, acts catalytically as an efficient electron donor, promoting reduction of the [2Fe-2S] cluster in the ISCA1-ISCA2 complex. These results highlight the role of IBA57 as an activator of the electron transfer pathway required for the formation of mitochondrial [4Fe-4S] clusters.

title: Tailoring Ion Exchange Efficiency in Synaptic Electrochemical Memtransistors Through Three‐Dimensional Artificial Crystal Engineering
abstract:
A 3D artificial crystal, fabricated by proximity-field nanopatterning, is integrated into an electrochemical memtransistor to expand the ion-exchange interfacial area without enlarging the horizontal device footprint. The resulting 3D device exhibits a dynamic range nearly 34-fold larger than its planar counterpart, robust endurance, and key biological synaptic dynamics, establishing deterministic 3D engineering as a scalable design strategy for neuromorphic hardware.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Electronic synapses featuring conduction modulation for synaptic weight update play a central role in implementing neuromorphic computing. Though memristors and memtransistors operating via ion exchange for conductance modulation have demonstrated synaptic functionality, their planar architectures suffer from a reduced interfacial area during lateral scaling, limiting their dynamic range of conductance modulation. Here, an electrochemical memtransistor is presented that replaces conventional planar layout with a precisely engineered 3D structure composed of an SU-8 organic reservoir and ZnO channel, fabricated using proximity-field nanopatterning. This design increases the effective oxygen ion-exchange interfacial area available for conductance modulation without enlarging the device footprint. The 3D device achieves a dynamic range nearly 34-fold larger than a planar counterpart, withstands over 10 4  updating pulses, and exhibits key biological synaptic dynamics. Deep neural network simulations based on the measured weight-update characteristics show improved classification accuracy over the planar control, and the inherent fading memory of the device supports reservoir computing. These findings establish deterministic 3D structural engineering as a scalable strategy for decoupling device footprint from synaptic modulation capability, thereby addressing a scaling bottleneck in neuromorphic hardware.

title: Deterministic Noncontact Release and Transfer Through Programmable Interfacial Stress Reconfiguration
abstract:
A bioinspired electroactive adhesive programs where its interface detaches. A perforated electrode couples a diving beetle‐inspired adhesive to a PVC‐gel actuator, imposing a displacement mismatch that promotes peel‐off at distributed interior sites. Resonance amplifies the mismatch and supplies inertial stress that completes noncontact separation, enabling deterministic placement of fragile microcomponents with 99.5% accuracy.








ABSTRACT
Deterministic placement of fragile microcomponents is a central challenge in advanced electronic manufacturing, including chiplet integration and micro‐LED assembly. Most switchable adhesives rely on contact‐mediated detachment, which concentrates stress at the perimeter and causes slip and misalignment. Here, we report a diving beetle‐inspired electroactive switchable adhesive (DESA) that achieves deterministic transfer through vibration‐driven noncontact release enabled by interfacial stress reconfiguration. A perforated electrode couples a bioinspired adhesive layer to an electroactive PVC gel actuator, defining electrically contracting electrode‐contact regions and mechanically linked gel‐continuous hole regions. Under actuation, differential displacement between these regions deforms the adhesive layer and promotes partial peel‐off at distributed interior sites rather than along a single perimeter front. At the 269 Hz resonance, vibration amplifies the displacement mismatch and spreads peel‐off across the contact area, progressively reducing the load‐bearing area. The resulting inertial stress completes noncontact separation, suppressing misalignment. The adhesive layer provides > 20 kPa dry and > 42 kPa wet adhesion across diverse substrates and retains stable performance over 1000 attachment–detachment cycles. On a robotic platform, the device transfers microcomponents with a lateral placement error of 318 ± 155 µm (≈99.5% placement accuracy). This interfacial stress reconfiguration offers a route to deterministic placement beyond adhesion‐strength control.

title: Advancements and Critical Evaluation of Wearable and Implantable Sensor Technologies in Joint Disease Management
abstract:
Bioelectronic sensors enable continuous, real‐time monitoring of joint disorders and injuries, overcoming the inherent snapshot limitation of conventional bulky imaging modalities. This Review critically evaluates the translational hurdles of bioelectronic sensors from biophysical and biochemical signal acquisition to clinical deployment, and outlines the key functional requirements for next‐generation devices. 








ABSTRACT
Joint diseases and injuries substantially impair daily activities. Continuous monitoring of joint function offers a powerful approach to assessing joint health and guiding therapeutic interventions. This Review begins with the pathophysiology of joint diseases and critically examines flexible bioelectronic sensors designed to monitor distinct physiological features associated with osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, gouty arthritis, and ligament injuries. We discuss the sensing mechanisms, developmental stages, and challenges in clinical translation of these devices. Currently, inertial sensing is the only technology that has entered clinical evaluation; most other sensors remain at an early developmental stage, with a considerable gap yet to be bridged before clinical application. Advances in flexible electronics, self‑powered operation and wireless transmission are steering these sensors toward personalized home‑based healthcare monitoring. However, the lack of standardized data protocols, low system integration, unverified long‑term reliability, and insufficient clinical sample sizes constitute major barriers to translation. Finally, we outline the functional requirements for next‑generation sensors designed for continuous, long‑term monitoring of joint diseases: future systems should prioritize high precision with unified data standards, high integration with robust fatigue resistance, and multimodality with proven biosafety.

title: Hyperactivated Macrophage‐Based Biohybrid Platform for Spatiotemporally Controlled Immunoregulatory and Sonodynamic Therapy of Cancer
abstract:
Schematic illustration . LCPs (Ce6-loaded, oxygen-carrying PFH nanoemulsion) are conjugated to hyperactivated macrophages (HMs; LPS/nigericin-stimulated under glycine protection) via a metal-phenolic network. After intratumoral injection, HM-LCPs act in two phases: sustained IL-1β release induces immunogenic cell death (ICD) and antitumor immunity; ultrasound-triggered ROS then amplify ICD and degrade the ECM, inhibiting primary tumor growth and inducing abscopal effects.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Reprogramming the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) is pivotal for enhancing cancer immunotherapy. This study introduces a biohybrid platform, HM-LCPs, which combines hyperactivated macrophages (HMs) with ultrasound (US)-responsive liposomal nanobubbles (LCPs) to sequentially remodel the immunosuppressive TME via spatiotemporally controlled immunomodulation and sonodynamic therapy (SDT). HMs consistently release IL-1β, independent of the immunosuppressive TME. Coupling oxygen-loaded, Ce6-containing LCPs with HMs yields stable HM-LCPs that preserve macrophage function and enable ROS generation upon US activation. Through immunoregulatory effects, HM-LCPs directly induce immunogenic cell death (ICD) in tumor cells, enhance dendritic cell maturation, and inhibit fibronectin production in fibroblasts. Subsequent US irradiation further amplifies these effects, leading to significant tumor growth inhibition, enhanced ICD, extracellular matrix remodeling, and increased CD8 +  T cell infiltration, thereby converting the TME from immunosuppressive to immunoactive. Additionally, treatment of the primary tumor with HM-LCPs and US induces a robust abscopal effect, effectively halting distant tumor progression. Collectively, HM-LCPs function as an intelligent platform that integrates immune activation and SDT to sequentially reprogram the TME and enhance antitumor immunity.

title: Heterogeneous Negative Gray Matter Volume Deviations Converge on a Shared Depression Circuit Associated With Symptoms and rTMS Response
abstract:
Subject‐specific negative gray matter volume deviations in major depressive disorder are revealed to converge on a reproducible functional circuit through normative modeling and connectome‐based mapping. This depression circuit links heterogeneous structural alterations with symptom severity, molecular signatures, and rTMS response, providing a network‐level framework for understanding disease heterogeneity and guiding circuit‐informed investigations.








ABSTRACT
Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by marked heterogeneity in regional negative gray matter volume (GMV) deviations, obscuring the network basis of the disorder. Here, subject‐specific normative GMV deviation maps are integrated with the human connectome using atrophy network mapping. Extreme negative GMV deviations in a medication‐naive, first‐episode MDD discovery cohort (n = 105) and an independent multisite validation cohort (n = 1265) converge on a reproducible depression circuit characterized by positive connectivity with subcortical‐limbic regions and negative connectivity with frontoparietal and default mode network hubs. Circuit coupling tracks depressive symptom severity, follows gradients of depression‐risk gene expression, and shows preliminary translational relevance: stronger negative connectivity at individualized rTMS targets is associated with greater clinical improvement. These findings reconcile heterogeneous structural deviations with the shared MDD phenotype and may inform future circuit‐based neuromodulation studies.

title: Synergizing Multiple Stress Induction and Mitophagy Blockade via a Single‐Atom Piezocatalyst for Enhanced Sono‐Immunotherapy
abstract:
A single-atom piezoelectric nanoplatform (HCQ@Ru@Cu 3 VS 4-x ) was constructed to integrate multiple stress induction and damage clearance blockade. In vivo evaluations demonstrate that this synergistic paradigm can not only eradicate primary tumors but also elicit a potent abscopal effect to suppress distant metastasis, providing a novel paradigm for overcoming immune tolerance and therapeutic resistance in complex solid tumors.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Piezoelectric sonodynamic therapy (SDT) holds great promise in the treatment of solid tumors, but its efficacy is severely limited by the rapid recombination of charge carriers, the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), and the protective mitophagy clearance of tumor cells. Herein, we constructed a single-atom piezoelectric nanoplatform (HCQ@Ru@Cu 3 VS 4-x ) that synergizes multiple stress induction with damage clearance blockade. Through defect engineering, ruthenium single atoms (Ru SA ) are precisely anchored on the sulfur vacancies (S V ) of Cu 3 VS 4-x , establishing a strong metal-support interaction (SMSI). This structure not only reduces the bandgap and amplifies the ultrasound-triggered piezoelectric polarization effect to achieve cascade amplification of ROS production, but also provides multiple enzyme-mimic activities for TME remodeling. Moreover, the tumor-specific release of Cu ions triggers cuproptosis-mediated metabolic stress, while the co-loaded hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) specifically disrupts lysosomal acidification thereby blocking the mitophagy clearance pathway of damaged mitochondria. This lethal combination of mitochondrial damage amplification and restricted clearance pathways leads to irreversible mitochondrial dysfunction and triggers immunogenic cell death (ICD). In vivo evaluations demonstrate that this synergistic paradigm can not only eradicate primary tumors but also elicit a potent abscopal effect to suppress distant metastasis, providing a novel paradigm for overcoming immune tolerance and therapeutic resistance in complex solid tumors.

title: Targeting Fibroblast Foxc2 Promotes Neurovascular Recovery by Suppressing Sdc4 After Ischemic Stroke
abstract:
YZD‐27, a Tanshinone IIA derivative, remains effective up to 24 h after ischemic stroke, reducing infarct volume and restoring motor and cognitive function. Single‐cell analysis identifies fibroblasts as a central signaling hub, where YZD‐27 binds Foxc2 to repress Sdc4 and attenuate Sdc4/Fn1‐mediated endothelial–fibroblast communication, promoting neurovascular repair.








ABSTRACT
Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long‐term disability, with current reperfusion therapies limited by narrow therapeutic windows and inability to promote sustained neurovascular repair. Here, we developed YZD‐27, a rationally designed Tanshinone IIA (TSA) derivative with improved druggability, and show that it remains therapeutically effective when administered up to 24 h after ischemic injury in transient and permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO and dMCAO) mouse models. Single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNA‐seq) and cell‐cell communication analysis revealed broad cellular responses to YZD‐27 and identified fibronectin‐1 (Fn1)/syndecan‐4 (Sdc4) as a predicted endothelia–fibroblast ligand‐receptor interaction. Mechanistically, YZD‐27 directly binds forkhead box protein C2 (Foxc2), enhances its protein stability by limiting proteasomal degradation, and increases its occupancy at the Sdc4 promoter, thereby repressing Sdc4 transcription in fibroblast. Fibroblast‐conditioned medium experiments further supported a role for Foxc2/Sdc4 regulation in modulating endothelial barrier‐related protein expression. These findings identify Foxc2/Sdc4 signaling as a regulatory mechanism associated with the therapeutic effects of YZD‐27, and establish YZD‐27 as a promising neurovascular therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.

title: Genome‐Resolved Metagenomics Uncovers Microbial Dark Matter and Complementary Modular Strategies for Lignocellulose‐Degradation in Forest Humus Soils
abstract:
A genome-resolved metagenomic resource from forest humus soils reveals diverse and underexplored lignocellulolysis microorganisms and modular CAZyme strategies. Integrated genomic and transcriptomic analyses identify responsive polysaccharide utilization loci and core glycoside hydrolases. These candidates are further validated by biochemical and structural characterization, establishing a genome-to-function framework for lignocellulose bioconversion.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Forest humus soil (FHS) harbors highly diverse microbial communities driving carbon transformation, yet genomic resources and strategies underlying lignocellulolysis remain poorly understood. A cross‑climatic FHS metagenome-assembled genome catalog (HSMAG) was constructed from 204 metagenomic FHS samples. HSMAG included 3338 species-level genome bins (96.1% undescribed species) out of 9776 MAGs. These taxa harbored > 669 000 CAZyme sequences. To decipher how they facilitate lignocellulolysis through functional organization, we performed multidomain identification. Results showed that CAZymes were extensively organized into multi-tiered modular degradation strategies, including free CAZymes (FCs), cellulosomes, and polysaccharide utilization loci (PULs). Cellulosome scaffoldins were enriched in nonclassical taxa (Blastocatellia and Gammaproteobacteria), whereas > 44.5% of PULs occurred in  Mucilaginibacter  and  Puia dinghuensis . FCs were enriched in endo- and exo-glucanases, while PULs harbored clustered xylan-degrading glycoside hydrolases (GHs). Thus, these modular strategies might cooperatively deconstruct lignocellulose through complementary GHs. Metatranscriptomics revealed PULs responsive to high lignocellulose levels and identified their core GHs. Recombinant expression and biochemical characterization confirmed the catalytic potential of these GHs. Notably, GH5 exhibited endoglucanase activity of 38.2 U/mg, and GH3 displayed xylanase activity of 20.3 U/mg. Taken together, HSMAG expanded FHS genomic resources and revealed synergistic modular strategies for lignocellulolysis, prioritizing targets for mechanistic investigation and lignocellulose bioconversion.

title: The OsERF39/OsNAC6 Transcription Factor Module Contributes to Rice Quality and Yield by Maintaining Methylglyoxal Homeostasis
abstract:
Two transcription factors, OsERF39 and OsNAC6, form a complex that activates the glyoxalase gene  OsGLYI7  for methylglyoxal detoxification in rice leaves and endosperm. This pathway maintains redox homeostasis and supports starch and protein biosynthesis for grain quality and yield. Its disruption causes methylglyoxal and ROS overaccumulation, impairing grain quality and yield.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The biosynthesis of starch largely determines rice quality and yield, and is regulated by numerous transcription factors (TFs). Methylglyoxal (MG), a toxic byproduct of glycolysis and the Calvin cycle, accumulates during starch biosynthesis and requires efficient glyoxalase-mediated detoxification for normal grain development. However, how TFs regulate MG homeostasis and modulate rice quality and yield remains largely unexplored. Here, we show that two transcription factors, OsERF39 and OsNAC6, physically interact to form a complex that directly binds to and activates  OsGLYI7 , encoding a plastid-localized glyoxalase I (GlyI). Loss-of-function mutations in  OsERF39 ,  OsNAC6 , or  OsGLYI7  markedly reduce GlyI activity, trigger MG overaccumulation and redox imbalance in leaves and developing endosperm. These metabolic perturbations compromise transitory and storage starch biosynthesis, reduce nitrogen (protein) accumulation, aggravate grain chalkiness, and decrease grain weight and yield. Collectively, our findings establish the OsERF39/OsNAC6–OsGLYI7 pathway as a critical regulatory node for MG detoxification, sustaining MG and reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis to support carbon and nitrogen assimilation in both source and sink organs, uncovering a TF-mediated mechanism linking MG metabolism to rice grain quality and yield and advancing our understanding of its underlying regulatory basis.

title: Layer‐by‐Layer Solvent‐Free Additive Manufacturing Enabling Controllable Ultrathick Electrode Coating for Lithium‐Ion Battery
abstract:
The layer-by-layer dry manufacturing enables the fabrication of ultra-thick NMC811 cathodes using an in situ-generated conducting binder network from rGO and PVDF. Sequential powder deposition and hot-roll compaction produce mechanically integrated multilayer electrodes with high active-material loading up to 90 mg/cm 2  and a high areal capacity of 9 mAh/cm 2 . This multilayer approach can be employed to dry process several cathode materials.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Dry electrode manufacturing is emerging as a transformative strategy for sustainable lithium-ion battery production, yet achieving ultrathick electrodes with homogeneous microstructures, efficient electron transport, and high electrochemical utilization remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a solvent-free, layer-by-layer additive manufacturing strategy that enables architecturally controlled ultrathick cathodes through molecular-level coupling between reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and binder. During roll-to-roll hot pressing, molten binder infiltrates the rGO framework to form a continuous conductive binder network, uniformly bridging NMC811 particles to enhance particle adhesion, suppress binder aggregation, and establish efficient electronic percolation. This strategy enables precise control of electrode thickness (300–1000 µm) and areal loading (20–100 mg cm − 
 2 ) while eliminating solvent-induced structural defects. The resulting multilayer cathodes, comprising up to five sequentially deposited layers, deliver a specific capacity of 230 mAh g − 
 1  at 0.1 C and an areal capacity of ∼10 mAh cm − 
 2 . The nearly linear increase in areal capacity with layer number demonstrates homogeneous conductive networks and efficient electrochemical utilization throughout the electrode thickness. Electrodes with ∼50 mg cm − 
 2  loading retain 9 mAh cm − 
 2  after 50 cycles. This work establishes a scalable platform for architecturally engineering ultrathick multilayer electrodes, overcoming heterogeneity of conventional thick electrodes and advancing next-generation high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries.

title: Tolerogenic Immunotherapy for Type 1 Diabetes Through Sustained Autoantigen Delivery in a Transient Inflammatory Niche
abstract:
Sustained co‐delivery of insulin autoantigen and low‐dose interleukin‐2 from an injectable hydrogel depot established a transient tolerogenic niche that expanded regulatory T cells and delayed median diabetes onset from 20 to >40 weeks in non‐obese diabetic mice. This strategy couples sustained autoantigen exposure with local immune modulation to promote durable tolerance, offering a promising approach to prevent type 1 diabetes.








ABSTRACT
Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a T‐cell‐mediated autoimmune disease characterized by destruction of pancreatic β‐cells, resulting in lifelong insulin therapy dependence and risk of severe complications. Tolerogenic immunotherapies offer a promising strategy to restore antigen‐specific immune tolerance and prevent T1D but have been limited by challenges in controlled spatiotemporal exposure of antigens and immunomodulators to achieve robust tolerance. Here, we report the development of injectable hydrogel depot formulations providing sustained co‐delivery of insulin autoantigen and low‐dose interleukin‐2 (IL‐2) and which form transient tolerogenic niches following subcutaneous administration. These treatments recruit and expand regulatory T cells both within the hydrogel niche and draining lymph nodes, inducing tolerance responses in the spleen and pancreas and increasing the median time to diabetes onset in non‐obese diabetic mice from 20 to >40 weeks. These studies suggest that sustained co‐exposure of autoantigen in the appropriate immune environment can promote durable tolerance for T1D prevention.

title: Breaking the Strength‐Deformability Tradeoff in Lattice Metamaterials by Mantis Shrimp Saddle‐Inspired Topological Design
abstract:
Inspired by the saddle architecture of the mantis shrimp, this study introduces a saddle‐based curved (SBC) lattice unit cell that strategically integrates saddle‐shaped surfaces with a conventional re‐entrant hexagonal (RH) lattice. The proposed SBC design simultaneously enhances strength, deformability, and energy absorption, thereby overcoming the classical strength‐deformability tradeoff in the design of metamaterials.








ABSTRACT
It is a long‐standing challenge to break the inherent trade‐off between strength and deformability in lightweight lattice materials for enhanced energy absorption. Here, we propose a bionic topological strategy to address this challenge. Inspired by the saddle geometry of the mantis shrimp, we propose a saddle‐based curved (SBC) lattice, built by integrating curved shells into a re‐entrant hexagonal (RH) lattice. The SBC lattice simultaneously achieves high strength, high energy absorption, large deformability, and stable deformation behavior. Specifically, the plateau stress reaches 5.28 MPa, and the densification strain reaches 0.518 at the structural scale. Compared with three typical lattice metamaterials, the SBC lattice demonstrates significant performance enhancements, with the strength improved by up to 1253.85% and the deformability by up to 11.09%. Moreover, the strength‐density performance of the SBC lattice unit cell is far superior to predictions from the Gibson–Ashby model, surpassing the empirical upper bound by 180.00%. The underlying mechanisms for the high strength and large deformability are systematically revealed. Overall, the bionic topological strategy in this work demonstrates the potential of utilizing idealized structures to achieve an optimal combination of strength and deformability and realize unprecedented enhancement in mechanical performance, providing new design guidelines for high‐performance metamaterials.

title: Vanadium Oxide Nanoregulator Modulates cGAS‐STING Pathway‐Associated Immune Dysregulation in Sepsis
abstract:
This work reveals a pathogenic mitochondrial DNA‐cGAS‐STING inflammatory axis in septic patients and demonstrates that vanadium oxide nanospheres with shape‐optimized catalytic surfaces can shut down this pathway by blocking mitochondrial DNA release. These nanospheres confer protection comparable to genetic STING deletion, establishing a preventive nanocatalytic strategy for sepsis management.








ABSTRACT
Sepsis is driven by cytosolic accumulation of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and consequent overactivation of the cGAS‐STING axis, which serves as a nodal upstream trigger for innate immune dysregulation. However, interventions directly targeting this subcellular event remain largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we synthesized a library of vanadium oxide nanostructures with distinct morphologies and identified nanospheres (VO NSs) as the optimal candidate. These VO NSs act through a multimodal mechanism, scavenging reactive oxygen species, stabilizing mitochondrial membrane potential, and blocking permeability transition pore opening, to physically constrain mtDNA egress from mitochondria, thereby ablating STING‐dependent inflammatory signaling. In murine models of sepsis, administration of VO NSs confers marked survival advantage and robust protection against multi‐organ injury. Mechanistically, using STING‐knockout mice, we demonstrate that STING ablation fully recapitulates the prophylactic efficacy of VO NSs, establishing STING as the pivotal downstream mediator. Beyond acute protection, VO NSs preserve mitochondrial genomic integrity and have the potential to disrupt the self‐reinforcing cycle between oxidative stress and immune exhaustion. This work offers an initial demonstration of a subcellular‐targeted intervention strategy for sepsis regulation, while also highlighting the potential of a modular nanoplatform for broader application in mitochondrial dysfunction‐associated diseases.

title: Histone Chaperone ASF1B Promotes Progenitor‐Like Cell States in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through H3.3‐Dependent SOX9 Transcriptional Activation
abstract:
ASF1B is reactivated as an oncofetal histone chaperone in hepatocellular carcinoma and promotes progenitor-like malignant cell states. Mechanistically, ASF1B cooperates with H3.3/HIRA-dependent chromatin regulation to activate SOX9 transcription. ASF1B and H3.3 also exhibit dynamic co-condensation behavior, suggesting an additional biophysical feature of this regulatory axis linked to tumor progression and sorafenib resistance.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Background and Aims 
 Tumor plasticity contributes to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression and therapy resistance, but chromatin mechanisms underlying progenitor-like malignant cell states remain incompletely defined. This study investigates whether ASF1B functions as an oncofetal chromatin regulator of these states in HCC. 
 Approach and Results 
 Integration of a human hepatocyte differentiation model with clinical and single-cell datasets identifies ASF1B as an oncofetal histone chaperone reactivated in HCC and associated with poor differentiation and unfavorable survival. Functional analyses show that ASF1B promotes progenitor- and stemness-associated properties, favors less-differentiated malignant cell states, and enhances tumor growth, metastatic phenotypes, and sorafenib resistance. Mechanistically, ASF1B interacts with histone H3.3, increases H3.3 enrichment and RNA polymerase II engagement at the SOX9 promoter, and enhances nascent SOX9 transcription, with HIRA contributing to replication-independent H3.3 deposition. ASF1B and H3.3 also exhibit dynamic co-condensation in live cells and a reconstituted system. Genetic epistasis establishes SOX9 as a major downstream effector. Liver-directed ASF1B depletion reduces tumor burden and enhances sorafenib responsiveness in an immunocompetent HCC model. 
 Conclusions 
 ASF1B promotes progenitor-like malignant cell states through an H3.3-SOX9 chromatin regulatory axis and represents a candidate therapeutic vulnerability in HCC. ASF1B and H3.3 additionally exhibit dynamic co-condensation, suggesting a possible biophysical feature.

title: GPCR‐Mediated Regulation of Cytochrome P450 Drives Sulfoxaflor Resistance in Aphis gossypii Glover
abstract:
DopR1  and  β-1A , whose transcripts are enriched in the epidermis and head, respectively, contribute to sulfoxaflor resistance in  Aphis gossypii . Genetic and biochemical evidence supports a working model linking these receptors to cAMP/PKA-associated signaling, with distinct contributions from  AC-2 ,  AC-5 ,  PKA-4 , and  PKA-7  to  CREB -associated regulation of  CYP6CY19  expression.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Rapid evolution of insecticide resistance threatens agricultural productivity. While the fundamental molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying resistance are well documented, the regulatory processes governing resistance-associated genes, particularly those involving signal-regulated transcription factors, remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated  trans -regulation of cytochrome P450 genes associated with sulfoxaflor resistance in  Aphis gossypii  Glover. Our findings suggest that G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-associated signaling and cAMP response element binding protein contribute to resistance-associated P450 gene regulation. FISH and RT-qPCR demonstrate that  DopR1  transcripts are enriched in the epidermis, and  β-1A  transcripts are enriched in the head. Molecular docking, heterologous expression, and biolayer interferometry assays demonstrate that DopR1 and β-1A participate in cellular recognition or response to sulfoxaflor and activate downstream cAMP signaling. Silencing  DopR1  and  β-1A  reduced cAMP content, PKA activity, P450 enzyme activity, and resistance-related P450 expression, thereby enhancing aphid sensitivity to sulfoxaflor. Inhibitor-based suppression, pathway gene silencing, and dual-luciferase reporter assays implicated  AC-2 ,  AC-5 ,  PKA-4 ,  PKA-7 ,  CRTC , and  CREB  in regulating critical resistance-related genes, especially  CYP6CY19 . Furthermore, functional validation using transgenic  Drosophila melanogaster  expressing  CYP6CY13  and  CYP6CY19  demonstrated increased sulfoxaflor tolerance. Collectively, these findings support a working model linking GPCR-associated signaling to the regulation of selected resistance-associated P450 genes in  A. gossypii .

title: Electrotunable Ultrafiltration via Electrochemically Controlled Pore Size and Charge
abstract:
Low‐voltage stimulation transforms cellulose nanofibril–carbon nanotube nanocomposites into electronically adaptive membranes. Stepwise electrochemical osmotic expansion tunes the apparent PEG transport window from approximately 13–21 kDa to above 70 kDa, while membrane polarization regulates the capture and release of charged molecules. Coupling size exclusion and ion exchange enables programmable ultrafiltration and opens a route toward adaptive separation.








ABSTRACT
Dynamic control of molecular transport remains a central challenge in membrane science, because most conventional membranes rely on fixed pore architectures or bulk stimuli such as pH and temperature. Electrotunable membranes offer more direct, programmable electronic control of transport properties. Here, we present electrochemical osmotic (ECO) actuator membranes based on cellulose nanofibril (CNF)–carbon nanotube (CNT) nanocomposites. The membranes undergo low‐voltage‐driven, uniaxial thickness expansion based on electrochemically induced ion redistribution and osmotic pressure gradients, while aldehyde‐mediated dynamic hemiacetal crosslinks restrict passive swelling and facilitate stepwise, state‐retentive ECO expansion. These membranes combine large actuation strains, electrical self‐sensing, and retention of expanded states after stimulus removal. Molecular transport is regulated by coupled structural and electrostatic mechanisms: ECO expansion modifies the accessible free volume and the effective pore size, while applied electrochemical polarization modulates charged‐solute partitioning. We demonstrate programmable capture and release of charged molecules and an electrically tunable molecular‐weight transport window for PEG spanning ~13 to >70 kDa, corresponding to an estimated effective transport diameter of approximately 4–16 nm. This range is relevant to biomolecular separations spanning small proteins to therapeutic macromolecules. These electrotunable ultrafiltration (eUF) membranes combine electrochemically driven pore‐size tuning with control of electrostatic solute partitioning, providing a basis for adaptive membrane separation.

title: tsRNA‐076 Promotes VSMC Autophagy and Vascular Remodeling by Activating IGF2BP2 Transcription
abstract:
Nuclear-enriched tsRNA-076 recruits ETV2 to the  IGF2BP2  promoter, activating  IGF2BP2  transcription in vascular smooth muscle cells. IGF2BP2 subsequently stabilizes m 6 A-modified  ATG5  mRNA, promoting autophagy and vascular remodeling. These findings identify tsRNA-076 as an endogenous small activating RNA and reveal a previously unrecognized mechanism linking transcriptional activation to vascular remodeling.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 tRNA-derived small RNAs (tsRNAs) are an emerging class of regulatory non-coding RNAs involved in diverse biological processes, yet their functions in the nucleus remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a nuclear-enriched tsRNA, tsRNA-076, that is markedly upregulated in synthetic vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and plays an important role in vascular remodeling. Mechanistically, tsRNA-076 functions as an endogenous small activating RNA (saRNA) by directly associating with the  IGF2BP2  (insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA binding protein 2) promoter and facilitating recruitment of the transcription factor ETV2 (ETS variant transcription factor 2), thereby driving transcriptional activation of  IGF2BP2 . Elevated IGF2BP2 enhances  ATG5  expression by stabilizing its mRNA in an m 6 A-dependent manner, thereby promoting VSMC autophagy. Inhibition of tsRNA-076 attenuates VSMC autophagy and alleviates vascular remodeling in vitro and in vivo. Together, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized RNA activation mechanism mediated by tsRNA-076 and provide new insights into vascular remodeling.

title: Hypofractionated Radiotherapy Elicits Tumor‐Derived APOC2 to Drive Inflammatory Monocyte Differentiation and Potentiate Anti‐Tumor Immunity in Colorectal Cancer
abstract:
Hypofractionated radiotherapy relieves ATF3-mediated repression of tumor-derived APOC2 in preclinical models, linking lipid remodeling to IFN-I-responsive Ly6A +  monocytes and CD8 +  T-cell responses. In patients receiving combined neoadjuvant therapy, rising serum APOC2 associates with pathological complete response. APOC2-loaded nanoliposomes enhance tumor control with radiotherapy and PD-1 blockade in mice, providing preclinical proof of concept.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Hypofractionated radiotherapy (HFRT) combined with immunochemotherapy holds promise for overcoming immune resistance in microsatellite-stable (MSS) locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). However, the mechanisms underlying its effects remain unclear. Using secretome profiling, ATAC-seq, bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing, we investigated how HFRT remodels the tumor immune microenvironment. APOC2 was induced by HFRT, and higher post-treatment serum APOC2 levels were associated with pathologic complete response (pCR) to HFRT-based neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy. Mechanistically, HFRT reduced ATF3 expression, relieving its repression of the APOC2 promoter and increasing tumor-cell APOC2 secretion. APOC2 activated lipoprotein lipase, increased free fatty acid production, enhanced type I interferon signaling, and promoted the differentiation of Ly6A +  inflammatory monocytes. These monocytes exhibit specialized MHC class I antigen-presentation programs that bolster CD8 +  T-cell effector functions. Clinically, the APOC2 nomogram demonstrated consistent discriminative ability for pCR across the discovery and internal validation cohorts. Therapeutic supplementation with recombinant APOC2 or APOC2-loaded nanoliposomes (APOC2@NL) sensitized murine tumors to HFRT plus PD-1 blockade. These findings position APOC2 as a functional mediator between radiotherapy-induced metabolism and antitumor immunity, offering a promising biomarker and a preclinical therapeutic proof of concept for LARC.

title: Unified Deep Learning Framework for Interpretable Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Lithium–Ion Batteries under Stochastic Group‐Behavioral Usage Scenarios
abstract:
This study presents a customized remaining useful life prediction framework for dynamic synthetic operating scenarios that emulate the usage variability of specific driving groups using Markov matrices. By combining mechanistic insight‐guided, data‐driven feature engineering with unified machine learning models, the approach delivers high accuracy and adaptability, offering strong potential for broad application to diverse batteries operating under complex real‐world profiles.








ABSTRACT
With the widespread use of lithium–ion batteries (LIBs) across various industries, accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is essential for end‐users. However, stochastic degradation patterns under unpredictable real‐world operations pose a fundamental challenge to conventional prognostic models. This study develops a unified deep learning‐based framework for RUL prediction under group‐behavioral usage scenarios. A group‐behavioral battery dataset is constructed using synthesized charging protocols characterized by a unique Markov transition matrix designed to capture distinct group usage patterns. Systematic feature engineering identifies 13 health indicators (HIs) with strong predictive relevance to RUL. By utilizing these HIs across multiple learning models, the framework offers a flexible paradigm where lightweight models provide high‐fidelity predictions or integrate into a weighted ensemble scheme to enhance accuracy and robustness. Across three heterogeneous datasets with varying cell chemistries and group behavioral patterns, the framework consistently yielded normalized root mean square errors (NRMSEs) ≤$\le$ 6.20%. Benchmarking against state‐of‐the‐art (SOTA) architectures showed that systematic feature selection paired with lightweight learning models remained highly competitive with the tested complex architectures. By elucidating the underlying mechanisms of the HIs, the proposed framework enables interpretable and specialized RUL prediction tailored to group‐specific driving patterns, highlighting its potential for real‐world applications.

title: Advances in Conductive Self‐Adhesive Interfaces for Epidermal Bioelectronics: Materials Design, Fabrication Strategies, and Future Directions
abstract:
This study comprehensively reviews conductive self‐adhesive interfaces for reliable epidermal bioelectronics. It synthesizes advanced material design (structural engineering, surface‐confined assembly, bulk blending molding) and fabrication strategies (prefabrication‐integration, in situ fabrication), detailing their role in balancing conductivity, adhesion, mechanical compliance, and biocompatibility. Applications in physiological sensing, therapeutic intervention, and human–machine interfacing are highlighted, together with emerging opportunities for advancing these interfaces toward practical epidermal bioelectronics.








ABSTRACT
Epidermal bioelectronics require a reliable, low‐impedance skin–electrode interface that maintains conformal contact under dynamic conditions. Conductive self‐adhesive interfaces, which integrate charge transport with interfacial adhesion, offer a compelling solution. However, optimizing conductivity, adhesion, mechanical compliance, and biocompatibility simultaneously remains challenging due to inherent trade‐offs among these properties. In this review, we first discuss the physicochemical properties of skin, then systematically examine the adhesion mechanisms, charge conduction pathways, and biocompatibility evaluation protocols for conductive self‐adhesive interfaces. We then comprehensively review recent advances in three primary material design strategies—structural engineering, surface‐confined assembly, and bulk blending molding—comparing their respective advantages and disadvantages in balancing the four core properties. Furthermore, we discuss the application of pre‐fabrication‐integration and in situ fabrication techniques in constructing stable and reliable interfaces. Building on these material platforms, we highlight their implementation in representative epidermal bioelectronics, including electrophysiological monitoring, physicochemical sensing, therapeutic intervention, and human–machine interfacing, with particular emphasis on how interface properties dictate device performance in each scenario. Finally, we identify remaining challenges and propose future directions for the continued development of conductive self‑adhesive interfaces toward practical epidermal bioelectronic applications.

title: MEC‐BioSense: Material‐Encoded Capillary Biointerface for Autonomous Whole‐Blood Biomarker Sensing
abstract:
A material-encoded capillary biointerface redefines whole-blood biosensing by programming plasma extraction, pressure-regulated transport, and electrochemical transduction into one autonomous architecture. Coupled microfiber separation, vent-assisted capillary flow, and a hydrophilic graphene/PEDOT:PSS/Prussian Blue nanoparticles MIP electrode enable >99% cellular exclusion, ∼80–93% protein recovery, and ∼9 min GFAP detection without centrifugation or external actuation from undiluted samples in a disposable point-of-care format.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Bioelectronic sensing in complex biological fluids is often constrained not by molecular recognition, but by poor coordination of transport, separation, and interfacial interactions at the material level. Here, we present a material-encoded capillary biointerface that integrates microporous media, microfluidic geometry, and a hydrophilic graphene/poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate)/Prussian Blue bioelectronic interface into a unified, self-regulated architecture. Capillary forces generated within a microfiber network are redistributed through vent-regulated pathways and stabilized at a hydrophilic mixed ionic–electronic interface, enabling controlled plasma extraction, transport, and analyte delivery without external actuation. System performance is governed by the balance between capillary driving pressure and distributed hydrodynamic resistance, defining an operating regime that simultaneously achieves >99% cellular exclusion, ∼80–93% protein recovery, and stable interfacial wetting. Within this regime, undiluted whole blood is autonomously converted into a reproducible electrochemical signal. Using glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) as a model biomarker, the platform enables direct sample-to-answer detection within ∼9 min, spanning 0.02 pg mL −1  to 200 ng mL −1  with an ultralow detection limit (∼0.01 fg mL −1 ) and reduced pre-analytical loss relative to centrifugation. These results establish that analytical performance is governed primarily by pre-analytical transport and interfacial regulation and introduce a generalizable nano/micro-engineered framework for autonomous, scalable point-of-care biointerfaces.

title: SVP Maps Spatially Variable Functional Programs and Their Coupling in Spatial Transcriptomics
abstract:
Spatial transcriptomics reveals where genes are expressed, yet functional interpretation usually remains indirect. SVP directly maps spatially variable cell states, pathways and transcription‐factor programs, and quantifies their spatial coupling through bivariate autocorrelation. Applied to pancreatic cancer, developing human heart and Alzheimer's disease models, it uncovers hypoxic matrix‐remodeling niches, coordinated cardiac maturation and plaque‐associated glial programs.








ABSTRACT
Spatial transcriptomics has made tissue architecture measurable at molecular resolution, yet most computational methods still identify spatially variable genes and infer biology only indirectly. We present SVP, a framework that directly maps spatially variable cell states, pathways and regulatory programs from spatial transcriptomic data. SVP combines location‐level functional activity inference with global and local spatial autocorrelation and extends these analyses to bivariate spatial coupling across heterogeneous features. Across simulations and real datasets, SVP recovered cell‐state‐associated activity patterns at individual captured locations, detected spatially variable features with calibrated statistics, and scaled efficiently to large datasets. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, SVP identified a spatially co‐organized hypoxic and extracellular‐matrix‐remodeling niche that co‐localized with regions of low immune activity. It further captured functional maturation in the developing human heart and plaque‐associated glial programs in Alzheimer's disease models. SVP enables direct analysis of functional spatial organization, moving beyond gene‐centric descriptions of tissue structure.

title: TRIM21 Drives MSR1 Degradation via K27 Ubiquitination in Macrophages to Deteriorate Postinfarction Cardiac Dysfunction
abstract:
Following MI, macrophage TRIM21 promotes ubiquitination at the K27 site of MSR1 and its degradation, reducing FA uptake, PPARγ-associated FAO and mitochondrial OXPHOS, thereby sustaining a pro-inflammatory state. Conversely, TRIM21 knockout or MSR1 K27R mutation stabilizes MSR1, reversing these metabolic changes, which shifts macrophages to a reparative phenotype and promotes cardiac repair. MI, myocardial infarction; BMDM, bone marrow-derived macrophage; KO, knockout; FA, fatty acid; FFA, free fatty acid; FAO, fatty acid oxidation; OXPHOS, oxidative phosphorylation.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) orchestrate the early inflammatory response following myocardial infarction (MI), yet the post‑translational mechanisms governing their phenotypic fate remain poorly understood. Although we previously demonstrated that global deletion of tripartite motif-containing 21 (TRIM21) attenuates post-MI inflammation, its macrophage-specific role and downstream targets are still undefined. Using bone marrow transplantation, we demonstrated that TRIM21 deficiency in BMDMs shifted macrophage polarization from pro‑inflammatory to reparative, limiting infarct size and preserving cardiac function post-MI. Mechanistically, ubiquitination proteomics identified macrophage scavenger receptor 1 (MSR1) as the substrate of TRIM21 in BMDMs, with TRIM21 catalyzing K48-linked polyubiquitination at lysine 27 (K27) to drive MSR1 degradation. Genetic disruption of this modification via the  Msr1  K27R knock-in mutation stabilized MSR1, recapitulating the cardioprotective and anti-inflammatory phenotype in vivo. At the molecular level, stabilized MSR1 enhanced fatty acid uptake and promoted a PPARγ-linked fatty acid oxidation program. This metabolic shift was accompanied by enhanced oxidative phosphorylation, effectively halting the transition toward a pro-inflammatory state. Collectively, our findings identify the TRIM21-MSR1 (K27) axis as a previously unrecognized post-translational regulator of BMDM-mediated post-infarction inflammation. Targeting MSR1 ubiquitination at K27 may represent a potential therapeutic target to resolve sterile inflammation and promote cardiac repair after MI.

title: Flexible Ultralow‐Power IGZO Multimodal Synaptic Transistors for Thermally Robust Neuromorphic Vision and Wearable Heatstroke Monitoring
abstract:
A flexible, energy-efficient amorphous IGZO-based optoelectronic synaptic transistor is developed for multimodal neuromorphic sensing, enabling simultaneous processing of optical and thermal stimuli. The device exhibits ultra-low power operation (1.6 fJ per synaptic event), stable performance under bending, and efficient optical signal processing. Its integration into dynamic vision sensing and heatstroke monitoring highlights its potential for wearable healthcare applications.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Multimodal synaptic devices are increasingly required to enable more reliable and informed decision-making in next-generation neuromorphic systems. A wafer-scale, energy-efficient flexible optoelectronic synaptic transistor based on an a-IGZO channel and ALD-deposited HfO 2  gate dielectric is demonstrated. The device is fabricated on a rigid silicon substrate and subsequently transformed into a flexible form, maintaining stable electrical characteristics under repeated bending (radius ∼3 cm). The device enables multimodal sensing by responding to optical stimulus and a wide temperature range (10-75°C), capturing signals such as body temperature, ambient conditions, and sunlight. Under optical stimulation, the transistor emulates key synaptic functions, including EPSC, PPF, and the transition from STM to LTM, as well as learning-forgetting-relearning behavior. Reliable synaptic responses are achieved at a low drain voltage of 0.01 V, with an energy consumption of 1.6 fJ per synaptic event. The behavior is governed by defect-mediated carrier trapping and detrapping in IGZO. System-level applications include heatstroke risk classification (99.6% accuracy, within the physiological temperature range 37°C–42°C) and neuromorphic vision sensing enabled by persistent photoconductivity. These multimodal capabilities enable both heatstroke monitoring and thermally robust vision processing within a unified platform. The results present a scalable platform for low-power neuromorphic and wearable healthcare applications.

title: Neutrophil‐Derived Biomimetic Nanoreactors Reprogram the Mitochondrial Metabolism‐Inflammation Axis to Alleviate Hepatic Ischemia‐Reperfusion Injury
abstract:
P. Shen and colleagues present a biomimetic nanoreactor coated with N2 neutrophil-derived vesicles for the targeted treatment of hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury. By exploiting inflammation-driven tropism, this curcumin-loaded platform synergistically scavenges ROS, protects mitochondrial function, and promotes macrophage reprogramming, providing a comprehensive therapeutic approach for liver repair.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a major cause of postoperative liver dysfunction after hepatectomy and liver transplantation; however, effective targeted therapies are unavailable. Here, we developed a biomimetic nanoplatform, Curcumin@CeO 2 @ZIF-8@N2 neutrophil-derived cellular vesicles (CCZ@N2-CVs), for targeted and multimodal protection against hepatic IRI. ZIF-8 enables acid-responsive curcumin release and localized Zn 2 
 +  delivery within the injury microenvironment, and CeO 2  provides sustained antioxidant activity via Ce 3 
 + /Ce 4 
 +  redox cycling. Surface coating with N2 neutrophil-derived vesicles endows the nanoplatform with inflammation-targeting capabilities and intrinsic immunomodulatory properties. In hepatocytes subjected to hypoxia-reoxygenation, CCZ@N2-CVs markedly attenuate oxidative stress, inflammatory cytokine production, and apoptosis, and restore mitochondrial membrane potential, respiratory function, and ATP generation. Moreover, the platform suppresses pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization and promotes a reparative phenotype, thereby enhancing hepatocyte proliferation and migration. In a rat hepatic IRI model, intravenously administered CCZ@N2-CVs preferentially accumulate in the liver and significantly mitigate tissue injury, as evidenced by reduced serum alanine aminotransferase and aspartate aminotransferase levels, decreased apoptosis, and improved histopathological outcomes. Enhanced mitochondrial metabolism and suppressed inflammatory pathways are observed in a transcriptomic analysis. Furthermore, CCZ@N2-CVs demonstrate favorable biosafety. Collectively, this biomimetic platform exhibits ion-mediated therapeutic nanozyme activity and establishes targeted delivery to achieve multi-mechanistic protection against hepatic IRI.

title: Tension‐Enhanced Impulsive Launching Using Partially Inflated Pneumatic Actuators
abstract:
The dynamics of blob launching is investigated, in which an impulsive output is produced simply by a partially inflated airbag. It is revealed that the impact‐induced stretch enhances the membrane tension and synergistically acts with the pressure impulse. A motor‐driven actuator is designed to strengthen the stretching effort, and soft robotic launchers are developed for high‐speed vertical and horizontal launching.








ABSTRACT
Impulsive actuation, exemplified by launching, has been pursued in engineered systems for centuries. To achieve such actuation, two primary strategies have long been employed: elastic mechanisms that gradually accumulate potential energy, and equipment that unleashes instantaneous bursts, such as explosive high pressure. In the activity of blob launching, an impact input is transmitted to launch the participant simply using a partially inflated airbag, and such soft transmission may inspire new design principles. However, those airbags' complicated deformation makes the underlying physics hard to understand and exploit. Here, we first investigated the launching dynamics based on multiple tabletop drop tests. In these tests, the launching speed exhibited two peaks at different inflation volumes. Through modeling and simulations, we revealed that the two peaks were respectively dominated by the impact‐induced stretch and the pressure impulse. The stretch enhances the membrane tension and synergistically acts with the pressure impulse, leading to the fastest peak. A motor‐driven actuator was then designed and proven to strengthen the stretching effort. Building on this mechanism, we developed robotic launchers capable of high‐speed vertical and horizontal launching. Beyond advancing the understanding of blob launching, this work offers a soft transmission strategy for achieving repeatable, programmable, and impulsive actuation.

title: Chiral‐Regulated Kresling Structure for Reconfigurable Multimodal Motion
abstract:
A reconfigurable dual‐layer Kresling origami structure with rigid‐flexible coupling is proposed to achieve physically programmable axis‐radial trajectories post‐configuration. By modulating internal chirality, a single module actively toggles between multimodal motion modes, bidirectional torsion, and a locked high‐stiffness state. This paradigm provides a versatile strategy for soft robotics.








ABSTRACT
Once geometrically defined, conventional Kresling structures typically exhibit a deterministic coupling path between axial displacement and radial deformation, which inherently limits their post‐assembly reconfigurability under identical actuation inputs. We propose a mechanically actuated double‐layer Kresling module, comprising a compliant inner layer with switchable chirality and a rigid outer shell featuring an expandable base boundary. By modulating the chiral state of the inner layer, the axial–radial coupling path of the assembled module can be dynamically reconfigured, achieving distinct rotational and radial responses under the same axial input without necessitating geometric replacement. The resulting coupling paths support compression, torsion, radial expansion, multidirectional bending, and a load‐resistant state under mechanical constraints.
