A multi‐module robotic system assembled from these units demonstrates locomotion in pipes with inner diameters from 84 to 140 mm and in a curved pipe, alongside inner‐anchoring grasping. Furthermore, the system uses radial deformation to estimate the pipe inner diameter; this measurement provides a basis for future adjustment of the inner‐layer configuration and driving parameters. By integrating reconfigurable axial–radial kinematics and radial measurement within a unified mechanical embodiment, this study establishes a mechanically programmable structural platform for future robotic systems with closed‐loop environmental adaptation.

title: Discovery of an NCoA4 Ligand That Suppresses Ferroptosis and Attenuates Kidney Injury by Limiting Ferritinophagy‐Mediated Iron Release
abstract:
Screening identifies a benzo[ d ]imidazo[1,2- a ]imidazole chemotype with ferroptosis-inhibitory activity, and structure–activity relationship studies yield  X27 , a potent NCoA4 ligand. Photoaffinity labeling identifies a modified NCoA4 peptide, supporting this scaffold as an NCoA4-binding chemotype.  X27  suppresses ferritinophagy-mediated iron release and protects against cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury and unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO)-induced renal injury and fibrosis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, is increasingly recognized as a key driver of renal tubular injury and kidney disease progression. Here, screening a focused library of nitrogen-containing heterocycles identifies benzo[ d ]imidazo[1,2- a ]imidazoles as a selective ferroptosis-inhibitory chemotype, with little or no protection against apoptosis, necrosis, cuproptosis, parthanatos, necroptosis, or pyroptosis. Structure–activity relationship analysis of 40 derivatives yields  X27 , which inhibits RSL3-induced ferroptosis in HT-1080 and renal tubular epithelial HK-2 cells with EC 50  values of 0.13 and 0.19 µ M , respectively, without detectable radical-scavenging or iron-chelating activity. Mechanistically,  X27  binds the NCoA4 383–522  fragment with a K D  of 0.28 µ M , suppresses ferritin degradation and labile iron accumulation, and attenuates lipid peroxidation. An activity-retaining photoaffinity probe,  X31 , enriches endogenous nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCoA4), while LC–MS/MS localizes probe modification to a peptide spanning Asp440–Lys452, defining a putative small-molecule interaction region. In mice,  X27  attenuates cisplatin-induced acute kidney injury and unilateral ureteral obstruction-induced renal injury and fibrosis. Together, these findings expand the chemical space of NCoA4 ligands, provide peptide-level insight into small-molecule recognition by NCoA4, and establish ferritinophagic iron mobilization as a chemically tractable node for controlling renal injury.

title: Reproductive History, Biological Indicators, and Pain Vulnerability in Aging Women: A Multi‐Cohort Study
abstract:
Female reproductive history is linked to pain vulnerability across cohorts of aging women through nonlinear, site‐specific, and context‐dependent associations. Reproductive timing, childbirth patterns, surgeries, and hormone use relate to chronic pain phenotypes, while inflammatory, hormonal, and metabolic indicators highlight potential biological correlates and future directions for women‐centered pain risk research.








ABSTRACT
Chronic pain disproportionately affects women, yet the relationship between female reproductive history and long‐term pain vulnerability remains insufficiently understood. Using three population‐based cohorts from the UK, China, and the US, we evaluated associations between reproductive factors and pain‐related phenotypes in aging women. Endogenous reproductive milestones showed nonlinear associations with pain risk. Specifically, both earlier and later ages at menarche and menopause, as well as shorter and longer reproductive lifespans, were linked to higher pain vulnerability. Childbirth‐related characteristics, such as higher parity, earlier age at first birth, and longer interbirth intervals, were also associated with increased pain vulnerability. Reproductive surgeries and exogenous hormone use were consistently associated with pain phenotypes, with timing‐dependent effects. In the UK Biobank, reproductive factors showed both shared and site‐specific associations across seven chronic pain sites. These reproductive‐pain associations were amplified among women with higher adiposity, greater socioeconomic deprivation, a history of depression or anxiety, and hypertension. Exploratory mediation analyses implicated inflammatory, hormonal, and metabolic indicators as potential biological correlates of several reproductive‐chronic pain associations. Together, these findings highlight reproductive history as an important life‐course factor associated with pain vulnerability and provide insights for future studies investigating mechanisms and risk stratification of chronic pain in women.

title: Covalent–Organic Frameworks for Food Waste Prevention: From Molecular Programming to Preservation, Sensing, and Packaging
abstract:
This review highlights covalent–organic frameworks (COFs) as versatile platforms for preventing food waste. By programming pore architectures and integrating fluorescent or nanozyme functionalities, COFs enable molecular capture, quality monitoring, and active packaging. These structure–function relationships offer design principles for preservation, sensing, and sustainable packaging, ultimately mitigating food loss and waste.








ABSTRACT
Food waste is a major global sustainability challenge, generating substantial economic losses and environmental burdens across production, distribution, and consumption. Covalent–organic frameworks (COFs), with their predictable composition and topology, tunable pore architectures, high crystallinity, and chemically addressable frameworks, provide a versatile platform for molecular‐level functional design. This review presents a function‐oriented perspective on COFs for food waste prevention. We first discuss how pore size, topology, surface chemistry, framework organization, and hierarchical transport pathways can be programmed to regulate molecular adsorption, confinement, release, and transport, thereby supporting preservation‐related functions. We then examine fluorescent COFs and COFs‐based nanozymes as complementary optical and catalytic signal‐transduction platforms for monitoring food quality deterioration and contamination markers, with emphasis on their construction strategies and underlying photophysical and catalytic mechanisms. These structure–function relationships are further discussed in the context of preservation and shelf‐life extension, food quality deterioration and contamination sensing and monitoring, and functional food packaging. Finally, key challenges associated with structural stability, mass transfer, functional integration, scalable synthesis, safety, and practical deployment are highlighted. By linking molecular programming with functional transduction and food‐system applications, this review provides design principles for advancing COFs toward more effective food waste prevention.

title: Label‐Free Assessment of Mesenchymal Stem Cell Quality by AI‐Driven Analysis of High‐Throughput Morphological Diversity
abstract:
This label‐free AI‐powered workflow evaluates mesenchymal stem cell quality using high‐throughput flow‐cytometry light‐scatter morphological signals. It predicts cell potency and enables real‐time harvest inspection, cell‐batch evaluation, and in vivo therapeutic efficacy forecasting.








ABSTRACT
The advancement of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) therapies is constrained by the absence of rapid, non‐destructive quality assessment methods. Here, we present FlowAIQ, an artificial intelligence (AI)‐driven platform for label‐free evaluation of MSCs potency. Our method quantitatively analyzes population‐wide morphological heterogeneity captured from millions of single cells via high‐throughput flow cytometry. We model each sample as a Gaussian mixture distribution to extract holistic biophysical descriptors. A constrained multilayer perceptron learns a nonlinear mapping from these descriptors to a quantitative functional potency index. This approach demonstrates high predictive accuracy, with outputs suggestive of therapeutic efficacy in osteoporosis and colitis mouse models. SHAP analysis identifies key morphological features underlying predictions, providing interpretability of cellular phenotypic diversity. We define AI‐derived morphological diversity as a digital biomarker of cell potency. Our work establishes an AI‐powered framework for label‐free stem cell quality control with translational potential.

title: WDR76 Drives Hepatocellular Carcinoma Stemness and Progression by Stabilizing CBX5 and Promoting Phase Separation‐Dependent Chromatin Remodeling
abstract:
Upregulated WDR76 recruits USP14 to stabilize CBX5, promoting nuclear liquid‐liquid phase separation and DNA co‐condensation. This drives heterochromatin‐associated chromatin remodeling and stemness‐related transcriptional programs, thereby enhancing HCC stemness, tumor progression, and reduced lenvatinib sensitivity. Conversely, siWDR7‐loaded nanoparticles disrupt this axis, suppress tumor growth, and enhance lenvatinib efficacy.








ABSTRACT
Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by high recurrence, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance, with cancer stem cells (CSCs) contributing substantially to these malignant features. In this study, we identify WD repeat‐containing protein 76 (WDR76) as a key oncofetal regulator of liver cancer stemness. Transcriptomic profiling of an in vitro hepatocyte differentiation model revealed that WDR76 is highly expressed in embryonic stem cells, suppressed during hepatocyte maturation, and aberrantly reactivated in HCC. Clinically, WDR76 upregulation correlated with poor differentiation, advanced stage, and reduced patient survival. Functional assays demonstrated that WDR76 enhances CSC‐like properties, including self‐renewal, invasion, and lenvatinib resistance, while suppressing hepatocytic differentiation. Mechanistically, WDR76 recruits the deubiquitinase USP14 to stabilize the chromatin‐binding protein CBX5 by preventing its ubiquitination and degradation. Stabilized CBX5 undergoes liquid‐liquid phase separation, promoting heterochromatin condensation and chromatin reprogramming, thereby activating stemness‐associated genes. Loss‐and gain‐of‐function studies confirmed CBX5 as an essential downstream effector of WDR76 in driving HCC stemness and tumor progression. Finally, siRNA‐loaded nanoparticles targeting WDR76 synergized with lenvatinib to suppress tumor growth in preclinical models. Together, these findings establish a WDR76‐USP14‐CBX5 axis as a pivotal pathway sustaining CSC phenotypes and nominate WDR76 as a promising diagnostic and therapeutic target in HCC.

title: Complementary Cardioprotection and Efferocytosis by Circulating Vesicle Recruitment and SIRPα Blockade after Myocardial Ischemia/Reperfusion
abstract:
Dual‐antibody‐conjugated, SIRPα‐overexpressing nanovesicles (SαV) hitchhike on circulating platelets (PLTs) to capture endogenous plasma extracellular vesicles (P‐EVs). In the ROS‐rich myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) zone, ROS‐cleavable linkages release P‐EVs and SαV. P‐EVs exert pro‐angiogenic and anti‐apoptotic effects, while SαV blocks CD47–SIRPα signaling, restoring efferocytosis and promoting clearance of irreversibly apoptotic cardiomyocytes.








ABSTRACT
Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) causes heart failure and mortality, driven by ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and CD47/Signal regulator protein α (SIRPα)‐impaired efferocytosis that together sustain tissue damage. Endogenous plasma small extracellular vesicles (P‐EVs) offer an endogenous, multifunctional option, yet their cardioprotective efficacy is limited by low cardiac accumulation. Herein, a nanosystem (SαV‐DAb) was developed by functionalizing SIRPα‐variant‐overexpressing nanovesicles (SαV) with dual antibodies (DAb) against CD42b (platelet marker) and CD63 (EV marker) via a reactive oxygen species (ROS)‐cleavable linkage. This configuration allows the nanovesicles to hitchhike on circulating platelets for targeted delivery to the ischemic heart, while simultaneously capturing and enriching protective circulating P‐EVs in the lesion. SαV could bind to CD47, avoiding the SIRPα activation on macrophages and promoting efferocytosis. SαV‐DAb demonstrated significantly enhanced cardiac accumulation and promoted targeted delivery of P‐EVs to the ischemic myocardium. Treatment with SαV‐DAb elicited a coordinated therapeutic response, including anti‐apoptosis, pro‐angiogenesis, and pro‐efferocytosis, ultimately leading to attenuated ventricular fibrosis and improved systolic function after I/R injury, with no observable toxicity. This strategy simplifies the preparation workflow by avoiding prior isolation of PLTs and protective vesicles, and provides a conceptual framework for endogenous‐system‐based nanomedicine in cardiac repair.

title: Molecular Engineering of Chiral–Polar One‐Dimensional Helical Perovskites for Circularly Polarized Light Detection and Zero‐Bias Photovoltaic Response
abstract:
Molecular engineering of chiral organic cations enables symmetry lowering from chiral–nonpolar to chiral–polar structures in one-dimensional helical perovskites. The resulting solution-processed thin films combine highly selective circularly polarized light detection with zero-bias photovoltaic responses, providing a versatile strategy for multifunctional chiral optoelectronic materials.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 One-dimensional (1D) helical hybrid perovskites provide an attractive platform for chiral optoelectronics because their helical inorganic frameworks support pronounced chiroptical responses. However, translating crystallographic control of 1D helical structures into solution-processable thin films while preserving their structural and optoelectronic characteristics remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate that rational substituent engineering of chiral naphthylethylammonium cations enables control over the crystal symmetry of 1D helical hybrid perovskites. Systematic structural analyses reveal that substituent-dependent intermolecular interactions and crystal packing are associated with changes in helical geometry, local octahedral distortion, and the formation of chiral–nonpolar  P 2 1 2 1 2 1  and chiral–polar  P 2 1  crystalline phases while retaining the characteristic 1D helical framework. Quantitative comparisons reveal correlations between chiroptical activity and multiple structural descriptors, while electronic-structure calculations suggest that organic–inorganic electronic interactions may also influence the chiroptical response. Solution-processed thin films exhibit highly selective circularly polarized light photodetection together with measurable zero-bias photocurrent and photovoltage, consistent with a possible contribution from the bulk photovoltaic effect. These findings highlight molecular substituent engineering as a promising approach to controlling crystal symmetry and integrating multiple optoelectronic responses in 1D helical hybrid semiconductors.

title: Sesamin Ameliorates Insulin Resistance in Association With Gut Microbiota Remodeling and ICA–AhR–GLP‐1 Signaling in Diabetic Mice
abstract:
Sesamin reshapes the diabetic gut microbiota and increases microbiota-associated indole-3-carboxaldehyde availability. ICA activates intestinal AhR signaling, enhances AhR occupancy at the  Gcg  promoter, and promotes GLP-1 production. GLP-1R signaling contributes to improved glucose tolerance and early insulin responses, linking microbial metabolism to systemic glucose homeostasis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is closely associated with insulin resistance and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Here, we identified a microbiota-associated indole-3-carboxaldehyde (ICA)–AhR–GLP-1 pathway that contributes to the glucose-lowering effect of sesamin (Ses), a major sesame lignan. In db/db mice, Ses improved hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, while remodeling the gut microbiota and enriching  Ligilactobacillus . Fecal microbiota transplantation from Ses-treated donors partially transferred these metabolic benefits. Integrated bacterial isolation, Ses-based fermentation, fecal metabolomics, and clinical LC-MS/MS analysis identified ICA as a Ses-responsive microbiota-associated metabolite. Serum ICA levels were reduced in newly diagnosed patients with T2DM and negatively correlated with FBG, HbA1c, and HOMA-IR. Oral ICA reproduced key metabolic effects of Ses and enhanced intestinal  Gcg  expression and GLP-1 production. Mechanistically, ICA bound to AhR, promoted AhR nuclear translocation, increased AhR occupancy at the XRE-containing region of the  Gcg  promoter, and stimulated GLP-1 secretion in STC-1 cells and intestinal organoids. AhR inhibition reduced Ses-induced GLP-1 production and partially attenuated its metabolic effects, whereas acute GLP-1R blockade blunted Ses- and ICA-induced improvements in glucose tolerance and early insulin secretion. Together, these findings support a model in which Ses improves glucose homeostasis in association with gut microbiota remodeling and engagement of an ICA–AhR–GLP-1 pathway.

title: Bacteroides Fragilis‐Derived Ceramide‐1‐phosphate Contributes to Depression Comorbidity in Irritable Bowel Syndrome Through Hippocampal SMPD4 and Myelin Disruption
abstract:
This study reveals that  Bacteroides fragilis  drives depression in IBS-D patients by producing ceramide-1-phosphate (C1P), which inhibits hippocampal SMPD4 and disrupts myelin integrity. Translationally, dietary branched-chain amino acid restriction or SMPD4 restoration rescues this demyelination and depressive behavior, highlighting a novel gut–brain therapeutic target.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Depression affects more than one-third of patients with diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D), yet the gut-brain mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identified enrichment of  Bacteroides fragilis  in IBS-D patients with comorbid depression, with relative abundance positively correlating with Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores.  B. fragilis  exposure induced depressive-like behaviors in antibiotic-treated and germ-free mice and was accompanied by reduced hippocampal sphingomyelin phosphodiesterase 4 (SMPD4), altered myelin-associated gene programs, and myelin loss. A combined hippocampal rescue strategy using Syn- and MBP-promoter AAV vectors restored SMPD4 expression and improved behavioral and myelin-related outcomes.  B. fragilis  cultures and a C1P-producing engineered bacterial strain supported an association between bacterial sphingolipid production and the phenotype, whereas peripheral C1P administration increased hippocampal C1P and reduced SMPD4 and myelin markers. Dietary branched-chain amino acid restriction reduced systemic C1P-associated signals, restored SMPD4 expression, and partially improved depressive-like phenotypes. Collectively, the findings support a  B. fragilis -associated C1P–SMPD4 pathway linking intestinal dysbiosis to hippocampal sphingolipid imbalance and myelin disruption, while leaving the route and molecular form by which peripheral lipid signals influence the brain unresolved.

title: Mitigation of Interfacial Phonon Scattering in Polyimine/Graphene Composites Through Controllable In Situ Construction of Liquid Crystal Networks
abstract:
A controllable in situ construction strategy introduces liquid crystal networks into TD 7 B 3  polyimines, forming strong interfacial π–π stacking Interfacial interactions (–242.62 kJ mol −1 ) and an ordered laminated microstructure with graphene nanoplatelets. Meanwhile, enhanced phonon density of states matching (56.9%) mitigates interfacial phonon scattering, providing a robust framework for high-performance thermally conductive polymer composites. 

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Thermally conductive polymer composites are promising candidates for advanced thermal management. However, their performance is often limited by severe interfacial phonon scattering and low intrinsic thermal conductivity ( λ ) of polymers. Herein, a strategy was proposed for mitigating interfacial phonon scattering via controllable in situ construction of liquid crystal polyimines and their composites with graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs). Ordered liquid crystalline domains with enhanced π–π stacking interactions are in situ introduced into the polyimines by tailoring the ratio of diamine crosslinkers, thereby improving intrinsic λ and interfacial affinity with GNPs. Optimized TD 7 B 3  polyimines exhibit a  λ  of 0.35 W m −1  K −1 , which is significantly higher than amorphous counterparts. When combined with 50 wt.% GNPs, as-prepared composite achieves superior in-plane and out-of-plane  λ  of 35.51 and 6.53 W m −1  K −1 , respectively, along with low thermal resistance of ∼0.70 K In 2  W −1 . Structural characterizations and molecular simulations reveal enhanced performance originates from the formation of ordered laminated structures, strong π–π interfacial interactions, and matched phonon spectra. Furthermore, TD 7 B 3 G 50  composites demonstrate superior thermal stability and heat dissipation capability in LED thermal management. This work provides an effective strategy for designing high-performance polymer composites by synergistically optimizing intrinsic thermal transport and interfacial phonon coupling.

title: An APOA5‐Derived Signature Bridges Cholesterol Homeostasis to T‐Cell Exhaustion and Directs Lung Adenocarcinoma Immunotherapy Response
abstract:
An APOA5‐correlated T‐cell signature (ACTsig) stratifies lung adenocarcinoma patients and predicts immunotherapy response. APOA5 deficiency drives cholesterol accumulation, elevates tumor‐derived MIF, and promotes CXCR4‐associated T‐cell exhaustion. Fenofibrate enhances anti‐PD‐1 efficacy in APOA5‐deficient models, linking tumor cholesterol dysregulation to immune resistance and providing a potential framework for patient stratification and therapeutic intervention.








ABSTRACT
Immune heterogeneity and metabolic remodeling frequently limit the efficacy of immunotherapy in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). To address this challenge, we integrated single‐cell and bulk RNA sequencing analyses, pairing machine learning with preclinical models to develop the APOA5‐correlated T‐cell Signature (ACTsig), which effectively stratifies LUAD patients and predicts immunotherapeutic response. Moreover, We identified apolipoprotein A‐V (APOA5) as a previously unrecognized tumor suppressor linking cholesterol homeostasis to the tumor immune ecosystem. Mechanistically, APOA5 deficiency induced intracellular cholesterol accumulation and MIF production. Cholesterol depletion and replenishment established a causal role for cholesterol accumulation in regulating MIF production, while MIF knockdown reversed APOA5‐loss‐induced T‐cell exhaustion and recombinant MIF restored the phenotype. Meanwhile, CXCR4 blockade rescued APOA5‐loss‐induced T‐cell exhaustion, supporting the functional involvement of the MIF receptor CXCR4 in this immunosuppressive phenotype. Finally, in silico drug screening identified fenofibrate, which, in combination with anti‐PD‐1 therapy, significantly suppressed tumor growth in APOA5‐deficient models. Together, these findings establish ACTsig as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy response and reveal an APOA5‐cholesterol‐MIF‐CXCR4 axis underlying T‐cell exhaustion.

title: Defeating Multidrug‐Resistant ESKAPEE Pathogens With Polymer Nanomaterials
abstract:
Antimicrobial resistance, particularly among ESKAPEE pathogens, represents a major global health threat and drives the need for innovative treatments. Polymer-based strategies offer promising alternatives to conventional antibiotics by overcoming resistance mechanisms. This review discusses polymer-based drug delivery systems, including nanoparticles and polymer prodrugs, intrinsically antibacterial polycations, and polymers exploiting photodynamic or photothermal effects against drug-resistant ESKAPEE infections.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The clinical efficacy of antibiotics has progressively declined over the past decades as a consequence of the global spread of antimicrobial resistance, a phenomenon that is particularly pronounced among the so-called ESKAPEE pathogens:  Enterococcus species ,  Staphylococcus aureus ,  Klebsiella pneumoniae ,  Acinetobacter baumannii ,  Pseudomonas aeruginosa ,  Enterobacter  species, and  Escherichia coli . Collectively, these bacteria are responsible for more than 50% of infection-related deaths worldwide, and multidrug-resistance is highly prevalent among them. This alarming trend poses a critical threat to global public health and underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. One such approach involves the use of polymers as drug delivery systems for both conventional antibiotics and novel antimicrobial compounds, in the form of nanoparticles or polymer prodrugs, to circumvent resistance mechanisms. Other promising strategies are polycations with intrinsic antibacterial activity that act through mechanisms not yet widely exploited and polymers exerting photodynamic and photothermal effects. In this review, we summarize and discuss the current evidence for the efficacy of polymer-based strategies against drug-resistant ESKAPEE infections.

title: Mitochondrial Dysfunction Driven by MARylation of GLUD1 as a Key Barrier to Sorafenib‐Induced Ferroptosis in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
abstract:
Sorafenib limits its ferroptotic efficacy in hepatocellular carcinoma by triggering a self‐limiting metabolic bottleneck. It drives SIRT4‐mediated mono‐ADP‐ribosylation of GLUD1 at R60, initiating mitophagy‐coupled, non‐canonical ubiquitination via the DTX3L DTC domain. This depletes α‐ketoglutarate, stalling TCA cycle‐driven lipid peroxidation. Replenishing α‐ketoglutarate bypasses this blockade, unleashing lethal ferroptosis to overcome drug resistance.








ABSTRACT
Restriction to Sorafenib‐induced ferroptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) involves poorly understood mitochondrial dysfunction. Using biochemical assays, orthotopic and patient‐derived xenograft (PDX) models, and clinical microarrays, we discover that Sorafenib triggers a metabolic self‐limiting effect. Mechanistically, Sorafenib inhibits mTOR to upregulate SIRT4, which mono‐ADP‐ribosylates (MARylates) GLUD1 at arginine 60 (R60), suppressing its enzymatic activity. Concurrently, mitophagy recruits MARylated GLUD1 to lysosomes, where the E3 ligase DTX3L specifically recognizes the modification via its DTC domain. DTX3L then non‐canonically ubiquitinates the 3′‐hydroxyl group of the ADP‐ribose moiety, driving GLUD1 proteasomal degradation. This dual suppression specifically blocks glutamate‐to‐α‐ketoglutarate (α‐KG) conversion, starving the TCA cycle and impairing Electron Transport Chain (ETC) activity, thereby preventing lipid peroxidation. Clinically, the GLUD1/SIRT4 expression profile predicts relapse‐free survival in HCC patients. Crucially, bypassing this blockade via α‐KG supplementation refuels the TCA cycle and restores ETC‐driven lipid ROS generation, yielding profound synergistic benefits with Sorafenib, particularly in PDX models with low GLUD1 enzymatic activity. Thus, R60 MARylation of GLUD1 constitutes a critical barrier to Sorafenib‐induced ferroptosis. Targeting this mTOR/SIRT4/DTX3L cascade or replenishing α‐KG represents a promising precision strategy to overcome Sorafenib resistance.

title: KRT16 From Diverse Tumors Induces Atrial Remodeling and Fibrillation via Endothelial‐to‐Mesenchymal Transition
abstract:
ABSTRACT 
 Anticancer therapy increases the incidence of atrial fibrillation (AF), the most common sustained cardiac arrhythmia worldwide. However, whether multiple cancers directly promote AF independently of anticancer therapy through shared mechanisms remains unclear. Here, retrospective clinical analyses revealed significantly increased AF prevalence in pre-treatment female patients with breast cancer (BC), lung cancer (LC), and colorectal cancer (CRC), independent of anticancer therapy. Consistently, orthotopic tumor-bearing mouse models exhibited enhanced AF inducibility accompanied by atrial enlargement, fibrosis, and electrical remodeling. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, combined with the TCGA datasets, identified endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) as a shared atrial remodeling pathway underlying tumor-associated AF across multiple cancers. Mechanistically, keratin 16 (KRT16) acted as a shared circulating factor across multiple malignancies. KRT16 accumulated in atrial endothelial cells and promoted EndMT through annexin A2 (AnxA2)-dependent activation of TGF-β1/Smad signaling. KRT16 promoted abnormal membrane retention of AnxA2 by suppressing Tyr23 phosphorylation, thereby sustaining profibrotic signaling and atrial remodeling. Genetic silencing of KRT16 in cancer cells or endothelial knockdown of AnxA2 markedly attenuated EndMT, atrial fibrosis, and AF susceptibility in tumor-bearing mice. Our findings demonstrate that multiple cancers directly induce atrial remodeling and AF through a shared mechanism centered on KRT16-driven EndMT, identifying this pathway as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Interfacial Interaction‐Engineered Dual Lithiophilic Ultrathin Interlayers for Dendrite‐Suppressed Lithium Metal Textile Anodes (Adv. Sci. 64/2026)
abstract:
Lithium Metal Textile Anodes  
 Ultrathin lithiophilic interlayers engineered on a three-dimensional textile electrode and separator synergistically regulate Li nucleation and Li +  transport, enabling homogeneous Li deposition while suppressing dendritic growth. This dual-interface architecture delivers prolonged cycling stability and enhanced full-cell durability, while providing a lightweight and scalable electrode platform for practical high-energy-density Li metal batteries. More details can be found in the Research Article by Seoin Back, Yongmin Ko, Jinhan Cho, and co-workers (DOI:  10.1002/advs.77494 ).

title: Synthesis‐Dependent Grain Boundary Density Governs Low‐Temperature Lithium Diffusion in Single‐Crystal NCM Cathodes (Adv. Sci. 64/2026)
abstract:
Low-Temperature Lithium Diffusion in Single-Crystal NCM Cathodes  
 This cover depicts the evolution of spray-pyrolyzed precursors into single-crystal NCM cathodes with a reduced grain boundary density. The formation of Li-containing precursors with a uniform elemental distribution provides favorable conditions for efficient single-crystal formation, resulting in fewer internal grain boundaries. This structural advantage promotes lithium diffusion and enables stable electrochemical performance under low-temperature conditions. More details can be found in the Research Article by Jihoon Choi, Sang Mun Jeong, Yun Chan Kang, Gi Dae Park, and co-workers (DOI:  10.1002/advs.77448 ).

title: The CXCL5/CXCR2 Axis Attenuates Ferroptosis in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma Through the Positive Feedback Loop Between PTGS2 Transcriptional Activation and Neutrophil Recruitment (Adv. Sci. 64/2026)
abstract:
Ferroptosis  
 The CXCL5/CXCR2 axis directly inhibits ferroptosis in ICC cells by activating the NF-κB/PTGS2 pathway. It also recruits N2 TANs, and the activated PTGS2 promotes the secretion of TNF-α from N2 TANs via the CCL2/CCL7 pathway, thereby activating the NF-κB/PTGS2 axis and forming a positive feedback loop, which further inhibits ferroptosis in ICC cells. More details can be found in the Research Article by Kefeng Lin, Qi Jiang, Qiong Li, Jian Ruan, and co-authors (DOI:  10.1002/advs.77185 ).

title: From Sensing Mechanisms to System Co‐Design: Graphene‐Based Sensors and Readout Circuits (Adv. Sci. 64/2026)
abstract:
Graphene-Based Sensors and Readout Circuits  
 This review presents a system-level perspective on graphene-based sensing by linking physical stimuli, electrical outputs, and readout features through the PS–EQ–RF framework. It classifies graphene sensors by electrical output type, analyzes corresponding readout architectures, and summarizes co-design strategies for low-noise, scalable integration, providing a roadmap from device-level sensing mechanisms toward practical intelligent sensing systems. More details can be found in the Review by Yingxin Wang, Ziran Zhao, and co-workers (DOI:  10.1002/advs.77374 ).

title: Root‐Inspired Microneedle Patch With Interlocked Rigid‐Soft Architecture for High Tissue‐Adaptiveness (Adv. Sci. 64/2026)
abstract:
Root-Inspired Microneedle Patch  
 Inspired by the robust mechanical interlocking of tree roots within soil, the root-inspired microneedle array patch mechanically integrates rigid microneedles with an ultrasoft substrate through interlocked lattice architectures. The cover illustrates how this biomimetic design bridges extreme mechanical mismatch, enabling tissue penetration, surface conformability, and stable attachment to dynamically moving, curved, and moist biological tissues. More details can be found in the Research Article by Dohyun Kwon, Brian Jun Lee, Sangyul Baik, and co-workers (DOI:  10.1002/advs.77211 ).

title: Bio‑Inspired Heterotypic Polymers Enable Independent Control of Distinct Coacervate Mesoscale Properties
abstract:
Mimicking biological proteins, we design synthetic heteropolymers with multiple functional groups that undergo associative phase separation via several distinct intermolecular interactions. These polymers permit independent tuning of mesoscale coacervate properties, such as stimulus responsiveness, material state, and morphology, over broad conditions. Notably, they overcome the common trade‐off between thermodynamic stability and liquid‐like dynamics in coacervates.








ABSTRACT
Many proteins undergo phase separation in biological systems, forming membraneless organelles known as biomolecular condensates. Their heterogeneous amino acid composition encodes multiple intermolecular interactions, enabling adaptable condensates that respond to diverse stimuli. By contrast, synthetic polymeric coacervates developed in materials science typically rely on a single dominant interaction, which couples key emergent properties. Inspired by biological macromolecules, we designed synthetic heteropolymers bearing multiple functional groups, that drive liquid–liquid phase separation through several intermolecular interactions with distinct sensitivities to temperature and ionic strength. We show that the heteropolymer composition enables simultaneous yet independent control over distinct emergent coacervate properties, including stimulus responsiveness, material state, and morphology. Specifically, we generated polymers that form coacervates within tailored ranges of ionic strength and temperature, across broad pH values and under biofluid‑compatible conditions, with behaviors spanning liquid‑like to arrested states. Notably, we engineered heteropolymers with excess net charge that broaden the phase diagram while preserving liquid‑like behavior, thereby overcoming the typical trade‑off between thermodynamic and dynamic properties observed in conventional coacervate systems. Our work introduces a design framework for synthetic coacervates that allows precise and independent modulation of multiple mesoscale properties, approaching the versatility of biological condensates while retaining the advantages of straightforward synthetic control.

title: Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 as a Programmable Bridge Chassis for Biomanufacturing and Host‐Responsive Living Systems
abstract:
A programmable EcN lineage spans four alternative deployment architectures: purified molecules, cell-derived architectures/materials, viable-cell products, and host-state-responsive living systems. This review links metabolic state, interface/material engineering, safety, and mode-specific evidence while distinguishing demonstrated EcN cases from transferable mechanisms and prospective design concepts.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Microbial biomanufacturing and engineered probiotics increasingly use related microbial lineages across distinct product architectures, but the associated engineering and evidence requirements are rarely compared. Here,  Escherichia coli  Nissle 1917 (EcN) is evaluated as a programmable bridge chassis across four alternative deployment modes: purified molecule, cell-derived architecture/material, living-cell product, and host-state-responsive living system. The review links carbon–nitrogen–energy–redox allocation and global regulation to cellular-state trajectories, interface capacity, safety refactoring, materials-assisted protection, containment, and mode-specific qualification. Direct evidence includes 100-L heparosan fermentation, antibiotic-free β-alanine production, engineered outer-membrane-vesicle delivery, human studies of phenylalanine-consuming EcN, and glucose-responsive GLP-1 delivery in diabetic mice and non-human primates. The terminated SYNB1934 Phase 3 program is considered alongside positive studies to distinguish proof of function, pharmacodynamic activity, tolerability, manufacturing readiness, and late-stage efficacy. Operational criteria for bridge-chassis designation, explicit rules for boundary cases, and a prospective design–build–test–learn agenda are proposed. As functional embodiment changes, engineering priorities shift among flux, state, interface, formulation, containment, and evidence—not necessarily toward a more advanced mode.

title: Matrix Softness and Fluid Shear Force Act Through TRPV4 to Promote Ovarian Cancer Stemness
abstract:
Extracellular matrix softness and ascitic shear stress are crucial mechanical microenvironmental factors enhancing ovarian cancer dissemination. This study shows that these cues activate TRPV4-dependent Ca 2 
 +  signaling, leading to PI3K/AKT activation and NFAT/AP1-mediated transcriptional regulation. The TRPV4 signaling pathway enhances cancer stemness and provides druggable targets for ovarian cancer therapy.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Matrix stiffness and fluid shear force are key mechanical cues in ovarian cancer microenvironment that can impact cancer stemness, tumorigenicity and metastasis. However, the molecular identity of related mechanosensors is unclear. In the present study, we used 3D soft fibrin gel to enrich ovarian cancer stem cell (OCSC)-like cells. Matrix softness increased the expression of a mechanosensitive Ca 2+ -permeable TRPV4 channel in these cells. TRPV4 stimulated the cell growth, increased the expression of OCSC markers, and promoted the growth of tumor xenografts in mice. Atomic force microscope measurement of patients’ samples and spatial transcriptome analysis demonstrated that softer tumor regions had higher TRPV4 expression. Light-induced photolysis of 3D CarHc hydrogel, which rapidly dissipates the gel stiffness, elicited a TRPV4-mediated Ca 2+  transient in the gel-encapsulated cells. Furthermore, TRPV4 activity promoted its own expression via NFAT and AP1, forming a positive feedback loop. Matrix softness also acted through integrin β3 to stimulate TRPV4. In addition, fluid shear force directly stimulated TRPV4, elevated the expression of OCSC markers, and promoted transwell migration in vitro and peritoneal tumor metastasis in vivo. Taken together, we conclude that soft matrix and fluid shear both act though TRPV4 to promote cancer stemness, consequently aggravating ovarian cancer malignancy.

title: Periprostatic Adipose Tissue Promotes Prostate Cancer Progression through Androgen Receptor‐Mediated Lipolysis
abstract:
Androgen receptor  (AR)  expression is induced in periprostatic adipose tissue (PPAT) from high-risk prostate cancer (PCa) patients. Enhancement of AR signaling suppresses expression of  Rnf213 , an E3 ubiquitin ligase, consequently leading to stabilization of hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) to promote lipolysis. PPAT-derived free fatty acids are taken up by PCa tumor to potentiate its growth. The anti-lipolytic drug Acipimox works efficiently to alleviate PCa growth in animal model.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Periprostatic adipose tissue (PPAT), a specialized fat depot surrounding the prostate gland, is linked to poor prostate cancer (PCa) prognosis. However, the mechanisms underlying the crosstalk between PPAT and PCa progression remain poorly understood. We found that PCa tumors, particularly aggressive ones, actively stimulated androgen receptor (AR) expression in PPAT, with elevated AR expression and signaling in PPAT being associated with aggressive PCa. Adipocyte-specific AR overexpression was sufficient to promote PCa growth in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, AR directly suppressed the E3 ligase RNF213, and RNF213 depletion increased hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) protein abundance. Consequently, AR-driven lipolysis liberated free fatty acids (FFA) and promoted PCa cell growth and tumor microenvironment remodeling. Clinically, PPAT in high-risk PCa patients exhibited elevated lipolytic activity and reduced RNF213 expression. The PPAT conditioned medium (CM) of high-risk PCa patients enhanced PCa cell proliferation, which was reversed by blocking fatty acid uptake. Targeting this axis with the antilipolytic drug Acipimox significantly attenuated PCa growth in vivo. Our findings support a feed-forward interaction between prostate tumors and adipocyte AR signaling that promotes disease progression. This self-reinforcing cycle accelerates disease progression, and targeting PPAT lipolysis may represent a promising therapeutic strategy.

title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important challenge. To address this challenge, we propose st2sc (Spatial Transcriptomics to Single-Cell), an end-to-end framework for inferring single-cell gene profiles from multicellular ST data. st2sc introduces a novel Attention Gradient Flow Tracking (AGFT) algorithm that extracts attention maps from a Vision-Gene Transformer to identify candidate cell instances without predefined background constraints. The detected instances are then used by a set of regressors trained under a multiple-instance, multiple-target regression setting to predict precise single-cell gene expression counts. Comprehensive evaluations on synthetic and Visium-like datasets demonstrate that st2sc significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accurately segmenting cellular instances and predicting gene counts. The method can further resolve contested 2um bin in Visium HD. Application to human IPF lung showed the model can recover the subtype marker level analysis. This advancement further improves single-cell resolution analysis in spatial transcriptomics, facilitating more accurate downstream biological analyses.

title: Point mutations in the FimH lectin domain: predicted folding stability versus conformational dynamics for R60P, Q133K and Y137A
abstract: Background. The adhesin FimH attaches uropathogenic Escherichia coli to the urinary epithelium through a force-regulated catch-bond that single lectin-domain substitutions can modulate. How such substitutions reshape the dynamics of the isolated lectin domain, and whether stability predictors anticipate them, is unclear. Methods. We compared the wild-type (WT) lectin domain (PDB 4XO8, apo) with R60P, Y137A and Q133K, using three 500 ns molecular dynamics (MD) replicates per system (6 microseconds total) and three folding-stability predictors (FoldX, a Cartesian-ddG-type Rosetta protocol, ERIS-2). The replicate was the unit of analysis (n = 3), with 95% confidence intervals and a WT replicate-to-replicate control. Results. FoldX and ERIS-2 ranked the variants consistently, R60P most destabilising and Q133K neutral; the Rosetta value for Q133K was anomalously high. All systems stayed folded. R60P gave the only reproduced local change, loss of beta-strand structure at residues 60-61 and of three local hydrogen bonds. Y137A did not bring Thr158 into the pocket, and the Q133K Gln133-Asp54 polar contact became a Lys133-Asp54 salt bridge. In the principal-component landscape, departures from the WT region came from individual replicates (Y137A replicate 1; Q133K replicates 2-3), not a systematic shift. Conclusions. A substitution perturbs local structure most clearly when it breaks a beta-strand (R60P), and the stability predictions and dynamics together give a consistent ranking of the variants, including the first dynamic characterisation of Q133K. The results characterise the apo lectin domain and give a reproducible basis for interpreting FimH mutations, not for inferring affinity. Keywords: FimH; lectin domain; point mutations; molecular dynamics; folding stability ({Delta}{Delta}G); protein stability prediction; principal component analysis; urinary tract infection.

title: DNA methylation assigns sequencing reads to closely related bacterial strains when their sequence cannot
abstract: Clinical and public-health questions often concern strains rather than species, yet co-resident strains of one species can be so closely related that a single long read carries no sequence difference between them. We measured how often this happens in 639 pairs of isolates of Enterococcus faecium, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus sequenced on one nanopore platform. Among the 297 pairs above 99% average nucleotide identity (ANI), 40.37% of read placements (a read counted against one strain's genome) carried no sequence difference between the two strains, and above 99.9% ANI about three quarters did. Strains of one species also differ in the DNA motifs they methylate. Our method, Epilect, assigns single nanopore reads to strains from the basecaller's methylation calls, given a methylation profile for each strain, and declines to call when the evidence is weak. In the pairs above 99% ANI it correctly assigned 21.8% of the read placements that sequence could not place, at a precision of 0.959. In computational mixtures of 65 pairs of distinct strains at or above 99.5% ANI that were predicted to differ in methylation, its per-read F1 score exceeded that of the best of three sequence-based read-phasing tools by 0.25 (95% CI 0.08 to 0.37); where equally related strains were predicted to share a methylome, the comparison reversed. DNA methylation therefore supplies strain evidence on reads whose sequence carries none, and whether it will do so for a given pair of strains can be estimated before sequencing.

title: Transcriptional regulatory landscape of plum (Prunus salicina) fruit ripening
abstract: Abstract Fruit ripening in plum ( Prunus salicina ) involves a complex transcriptional regulatory network, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study presents a comprehensive transcriptional regulatory landscape of plum fruit ripening by integrating multi-omics data, including transcriptome, chromatin accessibility (DNase-seq), and DNA affinity purification sequencing (DAP-seq) of multiple ripening responsive transcription factors (TFs) from EIL, NAC, bZIP, WRKY, MYB, and C2H2 families. We constructed a position-resolved regulatory network, revealing the dynamic modulation of multiple ripening processes, especially sugar accumulation. The key ethylene signaling TF PsEIN3-1 directly binds to the promoters of  PsbZIP44  and  PsNAC1 , which in turn, further bind to key enzyme genes involved in ethylene biosynthesis, starch degradation, and sugar accumulation. The regulatory effects of  PsbZIP44  on plum fruit ripening and sugar accumulation were preliminarily verified through transient transformation experiments. Through comparative analysis with other  Prunus  species (plum, peach, apricot, and sweet cherry), we uncovered both conserved regulatory circuits governing ripening. Additionally, we developed the  Prunus  Regulome Atlas  http://plantencode.fun/regulome/prunus/ that hosts multiple omics data and interactive regulatory networks of  Prunus . Our findings provide novel insights into the transcriptional regulation of plum fruit ripening and serve as a foundational resource for future functional studies and breeding improvement in  Prunus  species.

title: A transcriptomic atlas of grass senescence reveals divergent underground sink networks promote nitrogen recycling in perennials
abstract: Abstract Senescence enables plants to remobilize and recycle nutrients from aging organs to support growth, reproduction, and survival. In annual crops like maize, nitrogen remobilization from leaves to grain is incomplete, with 30-50% of nitrogen remaining in crop residue where it may be subject to environmental loss. Mitigating nitrogen loss in annual crops could be achieved by leveraging the physiological strategies of perennial grasses, which remobilize nitrogen and other nutrients into underground organs at the end of the growing season, thereby preventing environmental leakage. To uncover the molecular basis of perennial nitrogen recycling to underground organs, we built a transcriptomic atlas from field-grown plants, comprising 2,685 RNA-seq libraries from 14 grass species within the Panicoideae (Poaceae), utilizing maize and sorghum as annual references for comparative analyses. The atlas spans leaves, roots, stalks, and rhizomes across two seasons, from mid-growing season to senescence. Using a photosynthetic index to align the leaf’s transition from nitrogen sink to source across species, co-expression network analysis revealed that the subnetworks driving leaf nitrogen remobilization are preserved across annuals and perennials. However, we discovered that the subnetworks associated with underground sink establishment, specifically those associated with seed-like dormancy and desiccation tolerance pathways, have diverged among annual crop accessions. Our work identifies conserved gene candidates and networks that could reintroduce perennial-like nutrient recycling into annual crops to enhance long-term nutrient retention in the field.

title: A genome-guided multilocus sequence analysis scheme to detect and resolve diversity within the X-disease phytoplasma group (16SrIII)
abstract: Phytoplasmas of the X-disease group (16SrIII) cause economically important diseases of vegetables, forage and staple crops, fruit trees and ornamentals in South America, where they are diagnosed and classified only by 16S rRNA gene RFLP. Because this gene is highly conserved, strains that differ in host range, vectors and regulatory relevance cannot be distinguished. We developed a multilocus sequence analysis (MLSA) scheme for typing 16SrIII phytoplasmas, using genome data to select the markers and to define reference lineages. Five single-copy loci (tuf, secA, secY, mutM, cimH) were chosen from 16 curated genomes; primers matched all genomes in silico, and four of the five pairs did not amplify phytoplasmas of other groups co-occurring in the region (16SrI, 16SrVII, 16SrXIII). Genome comparisons resolved four lineages, including one restricted to South America that shared only 90.8-93.9% average nucleotide identity with the other lineages, despite > 98.8% 16S rRNA identity. The concatenated MLSA (2,870 nt) reproduced the genome-based lineages and assigned five Argentinian field isolates from weeds, fodder beet, cassava, plum and a native shrub. Identical 16SrIII-B RFLP patterns occurred in different lineages, and one 16SrIII-B isolate grouped within the 16SrIII-J clade, showing that subgroups are not reliable proxies for lineages. The South American lineage had the broadest host range, spanning six plant families. We also detected chimeric rRNA copies and sequencing artefacts that can cause misclassification. This MLSA provides a PCR-based tool to identify 16SrIII lineages in crops, weeds and insects, supporting epidemiological studies, disease management and phytosanitary decisions.

title: Cell atlases of schistosome human infective stages reveal larval tissue fates and innovations
abstract: Schistosomes infect over 250 million people, yet the cellular basis of their human-infective cercaria larva, that drives transmission and infection, remains poorly understood. We present single-cell atlases of Schistosoma mansoni cercariae, widely regarded as transcriptionally quiescent, and schistosomula, the first intra-mammalian stage. Twenty-two cercarial cell types either persist into schistosomula or are lost. The tail harbours several cercaria-specific innovations, including a novel tegument. Gene-age analysis supports the cercaria as the most recent addition to the life cycle and tail cells as younger than body cells. Persisting cell types undergo clear transcriptional transitions which give new insights into the dynamics of cercarial transformation into schistosomula. These findings link the recent origin of cercarial cell types to the evolution of active dispersal and transmission in digenean parasites.

title: Improved long-read sequencing technology reveals full genome architecture of Malian Plasmodium falciparum field isolates
abstract: Understanding genome plasticity in malaria parasites and the diversity of their repetitive gene families requires high-quality reference genomes derived from parasites recently isolated from patients. However, generating such genomes in Plasmodium falciparum remains challenging owing to the parasite's extreme AT content, extensive repetitive regions, and the frequent occurrence of multiclonal infections in endemic settings. As a result, most available reference genomes are derived from laboratory-adapted strains, that have experienced prolonged in vitro maintenance, and that incompletely represent natural parasite diversity. We developed and optimized a de novo assembly strategy based on PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and applied it to eight recently-isolated and cloned P. falciparum parasites from Mali. HiFi sequencing enabled highly accurate genome reconstruction, yielding assemblies with a mean of 18 contigs, 301 pseudogenes, and a frameshift rate of 0.04% following Liftoff annotation. Assemblies showed high structural integrity and near-complete chromosomes, including improved recovery of subtelomeric regions and multigene families, without requiring short-read correction. Despite overall conservation of chromosome organization, substantial variation was observed in chromosome-end architecture, subtelomeric structure, and telomeric repeat content among parasite genomes. Our approach simplifies the generation of high-quality P. falciparum genomes and reduces sequencing requirements fourfold. The resulting assemblies enabled characterization of natural variation in telomere plasticity and multicopy gene family diversity in field isolates. These findings establish PacBio HiFi sequencing as an effective and scalable strategy for producing highly contiguous and accurate de novo assemblies of P. falciparum, supporting the development of geographically-diverse, field-relevant malaria parasite reference genomes.

title: From Screening to Differential Diagnosis: Benchmarking 3D Facial Representations Across Craniofacial Conditions
abstract: Rare genetic disorders often present with highly heterogeneous physical features: some have distinctive craniofacial characteristics, whereas others produce subtler or more variable facial differences, making phenotype-based diagnosis challenging. Three-dimensional (3D) facial scanning is a noninvasive approach that captures facial shape and surface geometry, providing quantitative information on craniofacial morphology beyond conventional 2D photographs. Here, we investigated how well 3D facial representations support clinical tasks ranging from broad screening to fine-grained differential diagnosis without landmark registration, dense correspondence, or template fitting. We benchmarked four 3D models, including PointNet, PointNet++, DGCNN, and a geometric baseline, using 26,990 facial scans from 18,785 subjects across four prediction tasks. Across models, performance declined as greater diagnostic specificity was required. Broad affected-versus-unaffected screening achieved high performance (accuracy 0.893; AUC 0.956), although sensitivity analyses revealed substantial influences of cohort composition and demographic differences. Fine-grained syndrome diagnosis remained more challenging, with limited top-1 accuracy despite meaningful class-wise discrimination. Combining repeated scans improved patient-level diagnosis beyond differences in patient weighting. Prototype inference further improved diagnostic prioritization, placing the correct syndrome among the top five candidates for about 65% of held-out patients across 49 diagnoses. Patient-to-patient retrieval identified phenotypically similar confirmed cases, while useful syndrome prototypes could be constructed from relatively few reference patients. Anatomical region-occlusion analysis revealed syndrome-dependent patterns of facial importance broadly consistent with clinically recognized craniofacial features, although overlapping facial phenotypes contributed to diagnostic confusion. Overall, these findings support the potential of 3D facial representations for diagnostic candidate prioritization and retrieval, while emphasizing the influence of cohort composition on screening performance and the challenges of distinguishing phenotypically similar genetic syndromes.

title: The rise, evolution and future of whole genome projects in Asian populations
abstract: Asia contains over 60% of the global population and vast genetic diversity, yet its genomic resources remain underrepresented. Over the past decade or so, regional research has evolved from fragmented surveys into large-scale national precision medicine initiatives. Here, we examine how these sequencing efforts collectively form an emerging Asian genomic infrastructure. We discuss future directions to close critical gaps in Central Asia, minority populations, cross-project interoperability, and equitable access, highlighting the transition toward interoperable, clinical-grade genomic ecosystems supporting precision medicine across the continent.

title: AMP Challenge: towards a standardized, community-wide benchmark for AI-driven antimicrobial peptide design
SUN for scRNA-seq: stable-interval and embedding-based approximate silhouette guided Louvain resolution selection
abstract:
Background
                      In single-cell RNA-seq analysis, clustering resolution is often chosen by trial and error, yet it changes reported groups and downstream interpretation. Over-splitting or over-merging reduces reproducibility across teams. A transparent, practical approach to resolution choice is needed, including when over-clustering must be corrected before interpretation. 
                  
                     Methods
                      We introduce SUN (Stable-interval guided Unsupervised Neighborhood resolution selection), an unsupervised layer that selects one Louvain-style resolution on a fixed shared nearest-neighbour (SNN) graph. SUN scans a resolution grid with caching, identifies stable intervals as maximal runs of constant cluster count along cached resolutions (plateaus), and ranks intervals using a composite score of embedding-based approximate silhouette and interval width. 
                  
                     Results
                      We evaluated SUN on simulations, eight real scRNA-seq benchmarks, and a cortex over-clustering case. In simulation ( n  = 72 conditions), mean SUN ARI was 0.860 ± 0.230 (mean ± SD). Across eight benchmarks, dataset-level SUN achieved mean ± SD ARI 0.864 ± 0.099, FMI 0.886 ± 0.083, and NMI 0.873 ± 0.087. In the cortex over-clustering case study, SUN achieved ARI = 0.996 relative to the Manual Adjust partition used in the scSHC literature while recovering the expected UBC/MLI1 merge direction. Agreement used ARI, Fowlkes–Mallows index, and normalised mutual information, with internal indices as complementary evidence. 
                  
                     Conclusion
                      SUN converts undocumented trial-and-error on the Louvain resolution axis into an explicit, auditable recommendation—stable intervals plus quantitative ranking—within standard Seurat-style workflows. Across the included benchmarks, SUN showed generally high concordance with curated reference annotations, while remaining competitive with alternative unsupervised partitions; a cortex case study of over-clustering correction showed high agreement with the scSHC-associated Manual Adjust evaluation target. Seed sensitivity on some graphs and the heuristic nature of the ranking score are reported as practical caveats rather than fully eliminated sources of variability. 
                  
                     Availability
                      An online trial deployment is currently accessible at  http://8.166.114.84:3838/SUN_shiny_app_project/ . The SUN codebase is available at  https://github.com/BioinfoCenterSYSMH/SUN-Project .

title: ExP Heatmap: an ordered-pair workflow for regional cross-population genomic visualization
abstract:
Background
                      Population-genomic analyses often require the inspection of many population pairs across dense genomic intervals. Existing workflows usually compute cross-population statistics efficiently but leave interpretation to separate per-pair plots or generic matrix displays that do not preserve the directional structure of signed statistics. This creates a practical visualization problem when many populations must be compared along the same genomic coordinate axis. 
                  
                     Results
                      We developed ExP Heatmap ( https://github.com/bioinfocz/exp_heatmap ), a Python command-line and library workflow for ordered population-pair matrices. Starting from a Variant Call Format file and a population panel, ExP Heatmap can filter biallelic SNPs, convert genotypes to Zarr, compute pairwise statistics, transform values into empirical rank scores, and render heatmaps in which ordered population pairs define the y-axis and the same loci are aligned across rows; the native static output uses SNP-index spacing and the interactive HTML uses a base-pair axis. 
                      The software supports XP-EHH, XP-nSL, delta Tajima’s D, and Hudson’s FST, as well as plotting of precomputed pairwise tables. We demonstrate the workflow at the human lactase locus in 1000 Genomes Project phase 3 data, apply it to 589 ancient and historical individuals from 11 European archaeological populations in the Allen Ancient DNA Resource across a 25-Mb region of chromosome 15, and reproduce the analysis on chromosome 21 of the Gambian Genome Variation Project (GGVP). A controlled local benchmark on the GGVP chromosome 21 dataset showed that whole-chromosome statistic computation was the dominant runtime cost, while plotting remained comparatively fast once pairwise outputs were available. Additional pilot panels on Arabidopsis genotypes, Roadmap H3K27ac tracks, and SARS-CoV-2 lineage data support broader applicability of the ordered-pair representation when data are converted into the expected pairwise format. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      ExP Heatmap provides an integrated, reproducible workflow for regional visualization of many ordered population-pair comparisons. It is most useful when analysts need to preserve locus alignment, reciprocal direction, and pairwise structure in a single view. The current implementation is strongest for population-genomic data, while the pilot analyses indicate that the same display logic can also support carefully documented adjacent applications.

title: CNVision: a computational framework for functional interpretation of intragenic copy number variants
abstract:
Background
                      Intragenic copy number variants (CNVs), including exon-level deletions and duplications within a single gene, represent an important class of pathogenic genomic variation. Their functional consequences depend on the precise relationship between the CNV breakpoints, exon structure, coding sequence boundaries, transcript orientation, and reading frame. Although intragenic CNVs contribute substantially to Mendelian disease, their interpretation remains difficult because many existing workflows rely on manual transcript review or annotation pipelines that do not consistently resolve exon-level and base-pair-level consequences. 
                  
                     Results
                      We developed CNVision, a containerized computational framework for standardized interpretation of intragenic CNVs. CNVision accepts multiple input formats, including exon-based entries, genomic coordinates, and HGVS genomic notation, and converts each into a unified internal representation for transcript-aware analysis. The system maps CNVs to coding sequence regions, calculates affected coding sequence length at base-pair resolution, and classifies predicted reading-frame consequence. CNVision was evaluated using a dataset including 200 curated intragenic CNVs spanning multiple genes, genome builds, variant structures, and input types. Across the dataset, CNVision produced predictions concordant with manual transcript-level analysis and correctly processed exon-based, coordinate-based, and HGVS-formatted inputs. Beyond basic evaluation, CNVision also identified discrepancies in previously published CNVs. Of 131 reported CNVs evaluated, 15 yielded classifications that differed from the original published interpretation; independent manual transcript-level analysis using the UCSC Genome Browser supported CNVision’s classification in all 15 variants, indicating the discrepancies were attributable to differences in transcript interpretation or coordinate calculation rather than computational error. In terms of processing speed, CNVision was tested by two board-certified laboratory geneticists who compared the runtime of CNVision versus manual analysis across 18 CNVs, 6 of each input type. CNVision consistently outperformed manual analysis by both geneticists across all variants by a significant margin. 
                  
                     Conclusion
                      CNVision provides a reproducible framework for functional interpretation of intragenic CNVs by automating input parsing, transcript mapping, coding sequence overlap calculation, and reading-frame classification. The framework reduces manual burden, improves consistency, and provides a foundation for future expansion into batch CNV processing and graphical variant interpretation.

title: Comparison of interventional causal structure learning algorithms for gene regulatory network inference
abstract:
Background
                      Causal structure learning offers a promising approach to studying gene regulation in cells, aiming to provide deeper mechanistic insights than purely association-based methods. Theoretical groundwork indicating that interventions improve identifiability of causal structure motivates the use of causal structure learning methods in scenarios with interventional information. 
                  
                     Results
                      This benchmark investigates the ability of existing causal structure learning algorithms to leverage the information revealed by targeted interventions to infer gene regulatory networks (GRNs). In this study synthetic single-cell perturbation data and experimental data from a clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) screen are leveraged, and a suite of causal structure learning algorithms is evaluated on metrics tailored to synthetic ground truth and real biological data respectively. On synthetic data, accurate recovery of GRNs was achieved under favourable conditions: strong interventions, large sample sizes, and low measurement noise. For experimental data, no reliable ground truth is available, so inferred GRNs were assessed indirectly, using observed perturbation effects and curated regulatory annotations. Here, performance remained unreliable, with technical and biological noise and algorithmic scalability as limiting factors. This highlights a current gap between theoretical potential and practical application of causal structure learning for GRNs. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      The benchmark provides insight into algorithm strengths and limitations and offers groundwork for further methodological development. We also provide an accessible software package for applying modern causal structure learning to custom datasets and thereby foster future exploration of its potential.

title: Cell‐type‐specific dosage reprogramming reveals epidermal barrier‐based gray mold defense strategy in autotetraploid strawberry
abstract:
Whole-genome duplication enhances gray mold resistance in autotetraploid  Fragaria nilgerrensis  through coordinated gene-dosage effects, DNA methylation remodeling, and cell-type-specific transcriptional reprogramming.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Whole-genome duplication (WGD) triggers genetic and epigenetic remodeling that confers stress adaptation in plants, but how these responses act at single-cell resolution to shape adaptive phenotypes remains unclear. Here, we generated autotetraploid  Fragaria nilgerrensis  via colchicine treatment, which showed gigantism (enlarged leaves and stomata) and enhanced gray mold resistance.
Integrated multi-omics analysis showed that while the expression of many genes remained close to the diploid levels post-WGD, defense pathway genes displayed dosage sensitivity contributing to adaptive traits. Genome-wide transposable element (TE) hypermethylation stabilized the genome and may contribute to dosage by suppressing adjacent gene expression, and differential promoter/gene-body methylation may contribute to distinct gene-dosage responses.
Single-nucleus transcriptomics revealed cell-type heterogeneity in dosage responses, with epidermal cells undergoing regulatory network reprogramming toward enhanced physical barriers through increased expression of genes involved in cell wall and cuticle reinforcement. Functional validation confirmed  LAC9  as a core gene governing gray mold resistance: Its overexpression improved resistance in diploids, whereas its silencing weakened resistance in tetraploids.  LAC9  may increase lignin content to strengthen cell walls and restrain pathogen adhesion and penetration.
This work elucidates how WGD enhances adaptive potential through coordinated gene dosage, DNA methylation, and cell-specific reprogramming, offering mechanistic insights and targets for polyploid-based crop improvement.
 
 概括 
 全基因组加倍(WGD)能够驱动遗传和表观遗传重塑，赋予植物适应胁迫的能力，但这些响应如何在单细胞水平塑造适应性表型目前仍不清楚。本研究利用秋水仙素处理创制了黄毛草莓( Fragaria nilgerrensis )同源四倍体，该材料呈现器官巨大化特征(叶片和气孔增大)，同时灰霉病抗性显著增强。多组学整合分析表明，全基因组加倍后，大量基因的表达水平与二倍体基本持平，而防御通路相关基因表现出明显的剂量敏感性，可能推动适应性性状的形成。全基因组转座元件(TE)发生超甲基化，既维持了基因组稳定性，并可能通过抑制邻近基因的表达参与基因剂量调控；启动子和基因体甲基化的差异则可能驱动了剂量响应基因与剂量补偿基因的形成。单核转录组分析揭示，基因剂量响应存在细胞类型异质性: 表皮细胞发生明显的调控网络重编程，通过上调细胞壁和角质层强化相关基因的表达，增强物理屏障。功能验证证实， LAC9  是调控灰霉病抗性的核心基因: 在二倍体中过表达该基因可提高抗性，而在四倍体中沉默该基因则削弱抗性。 LAC9  可能通过提高木质素含量来强化细胞壁，进而限制病原菌的附着和侵入。本研究阐明了全基因组加倍如何通过基因剂量、DNA甲基化及细胞类型特异性重编程的协同作用，增强植物的适应潜力，为利用多倍体作物改良提供了理论机制与基因靶标。

title: Experimental context shapes interpretation of immune outputs in Arabidopsis
abstract:
Experimental context shapes the immune outputs measured after pattern recognition receptor activation. Rosettes were more sensitive than seedlings for reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and, as a non-significant trend, for mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) phosphorylation. By contrast, calcium reporter output was higher in seedlings, which reflects higher expression and functional availability of the aequorin reporter rather than intrinsic differences in calcium signaling. Although flg22 induced stronger early signaling outputs (ROS and calcium) than elf18, seedling growth inhibition (SGI) assays showed greater sensitivity to elf18. These results indicate that seedling and rosette experimental contexts cannot be used interchangeably.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Pattern recognition receptors (PRRs) activate plant immunity through recognition of extracellular immunogenic patterns, including microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). PRR activation is commonly assessed using different experimental systems, including sterile-grown seedlings and soil-grown rosettes.
We systematically compared Arabidopsis PRR immune outputs triggered by the bacterial MAMPs elf18 and flg22 across a range of concentrations in seedlings and rosettes using assays for reactive oxygen species (ROS), cytosolic calcium influx, mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) activation, and seedling growth inhibition (SGI).
Rosettes exhibited greater sensitivity than seedlings in ROS and MAPK assays, whereas calcium responses measured using the Aeq cyt /pMAQ2 reporter were stronger in seedlings, correlating with reduced reporter transcript accumulation in rosette tissue. Despite flg22 inducing stronger early signaling outputs, SGI assays showed greater sensitivity to elf18.
These findings demonstrate that canonical PRR-mediated immune outputs are differentially sensitive to experimental context and should not be interpreted as interchangeable measures of immune activation. This study provides a framework for selecting appropriate assay systems and MAMP concentrations in plant immunity studies.

title: Self-adaptive metasurface integrating sensing and active wave control for intelligent wireless communications
abstract: Abstract The vision for future wireless networks extends far beyond mere connectivity, fostering spaces that autonomously perceive and adapt to the radio environment. Reconfigurable metasurfaces (RMSs) are designed to tailor wireless propagation through programmable electromagnetic responses. However, conventional RMSs, while assisting communication, lack integrated sensing and self-adaptive control capabilities and suffer from severe path loss along the transmitter-RMS-receiver link. Here we report a self-adaptive metasurface (SA-MS) that integrates sensing and active wave control within a unified platform. Each meta-atom integrates dual-biased PIN diodes and an embedded port, enabling 1-bit programmable reflection and in-band sensing. The sensed waveform is fed to a lightweight convolutional neural network that infers the direction of arrival with robustness against array mismatches. The acquired spatial information is then mapped through a physics-informed surrogate model to an amplitude-phase configuration that works in conjunction with the amplifier to enhance the wireless link. Real-world wireless communication experiments in dynamic environments validate the sensing, decision, and execution loop of SA-MS, with an average signal enhancement of 14.6 dB. This work paves the way for intelligent wireless spaces, where sensing and communication co-evolve at the physical layer.

title: Tuned Fitness Landscapes for Benchmarking Model-Guided Protein Design
abstract: Abstract Machine learning-guided directed evolution (MLDE) is an emerging paradigm of protein design where ML models trained on experimental data are used to guide exploration of a protein fitness landscape. Building an MLDE pipeline involves many design choices across the design-build-test-learn loop ranging from data collection strategies to modeling. The cost of collecting experimental data makes benchmarking every component of these pipelines prohibitively difficult, necessitating the development of  synthetic  landscapes. In this work, we develop a framework called SLIP (“Synthetic Landscape Inference for Proteins”) for constructing synthetic landscapes with tunable difficulty based on Potts models. This framework can be extended to any protein family for which there is a sequence alignment. We show that our tuning framework provides landscapes sufficiently challenging to benchmark MLDE pipelines. SLIP is open-source and is available at  https://github.com/google-research/slip .

title: BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Protein-ligand scoring must address affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening, but these objectives are not necessarily optimized together. Geometric likelihood models may generalize poorly when training-set structural coverage is limited. We test whether pretrained biomolecular representations improve scoring under a controlled geometric baseline. Results BioLM-Score integrates frozen protein and molecular language-model embeddings into a residue-atom distance-likelihood framework via gated graph convolutions. We evaluate geometry-only, jointly trained, and two-stage fine-tuned variants, using the jointly trained variant for the primary controlled comparisons. All three DEKOIS 2.0 screening endpoints improve over the matched geometric baseline with target-level paired support, but affinity scoring and ranking do not improve uniformly. Under a time-split protocol, scoring is significantly lower and ranking is also lower than the geometric baseline, while screening gains persist. On BDB2020+, the difference in affinity correlation between BioLM-Score and GenScore narrows after LP-PDBBind-compatible retraining. Shuffling protein embeddings at inference reduces the screening advantage. However, retrained shuffle controls recover much of the performance, so correct alignment is not established as necessary. BioLM-Score strengthens geometric scoring on screening tasks without retraining the language models. Availability and implementation Code, dataset-split identifiers, preprocessing and evaluation scripts, and language-model embedding-generation utilities are available at  https://github.com/SZU-ADDG/BioLM-Score . An archival code snapshot and pretrained model weights are available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.21878818. Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
