We find pronounced platform-specific effects in low-complexity regions and trinucleotide contexts, including homopolymer-associated errors and context-dependent substitution skews that are directly relevant to rare-variant detection. In addition, we show that donor-specific references are essential for unbiased base-quality recalibration because they minimize reference bias and more faithfully support cross-platform comparison and low-frequency variant-calling thresholds. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      Donor-specific assembly-based benchmarking provides a robust framework for measuring true short-read sequencing errors and comparing platforms on a common, sample-matched basis. Our results establish a comprehensive reference for the community and show that authentic error profiles can guide platform selection, quality filtering, and improved detection of rare somatic variation.

title: CREMA: recovery of high clonal fraction mosaic chromosomal alterations missed by phase-based detection
abstract:
Background
                      Mosaic chromosomal alterations (mCAs), a type of clonal hematopoiesis, are large somatic gains, losses, and copy-neutral events associated with age-related genomic instability and cancer susceptibility. Phase-based mCA detection methods such as MoChA are highly sensitive for low clonal fraction events, including events present in approximately 1% of blood cells, because they leverage long-range haplotype imbalance. However, when clonal fraction is very high, heterozygous genotypes can be misclassified as homozygous because allelic imbalance becomes extreme. This misclassification of phase-informative heterozygous sites can reduce sensitivity, particularly for high clonal fraction copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity (CN-LOH), which retains near-normal log R ratio (LRR) and can resemble constitutional autozygosity. Sensitive detection approaches for high clonal fraction mCAs are needed as these events are more likely to manifest in phenotypic consequences and confer elevated risk of hematologic malignancies. 
                  
                     Results
                      We developed CREMA (Clonal Recovery using Expectation-Maximization Algorithms), a standalone post-processing framework that identifies and classifies high clonal fraction mCA candidates within runs of homozygosity (RoH) or other segmentation outputs. CREMA recenters LRR, models central B-allele frequency (BAF) distributions using expectation-maximization, selects one- or two-band models using Akaike information criterion, and applies a geometric classifier in BAF-derived clonal fraction and LRR space. Across test analyses, RoH nomination followed by CREMA post-processing identified high clonal fraction mCA candidates, predominately CN-LOH events, that were not present in the MoChA call set. The largest contribution was observed in a myelofibrosis cohort enriched for high clonal fraction 9p CN-LOH involving the JAK2 region, where RoH plus CREMA recovered 232 additional CN-LOH events, corresponding to 11.1% of autosomal mCAs of at least 2 Mb. In two population-based PLCO datasets, CREMA recovered smaller targeted sets of additional high clonal fraction CN-LOH events, adding 0.5% and 0.4% to the autosomal mCA call sets. 
                  
                     Conclusions
                      CREMA complements phase-based mCA detection by using RoH or other segmentation methods for candidate generation and BAF/LRR modeling for candidate-level classification. This workflow improves detection of high clonal fraction events, particularly CN-LOH, while remaining applicable to high clonal fraction gains and losses.

title: Auditing correlational gene regulatory networks through perturbation-grounded causal analysis for drug target prioritization
abstract: Gene regulatory network (GRN) inference for drug-target prioritization relies overwhelmingly on undirected co-expression, with highly connected “hub” genes routinely advanced as candidate regulators without independent causal verification. Although perturbation-based technologies now make direct causal validation feasible at genome scale, no study has directly tested whether correlational hub status reliably predicts causal regulatory importance or real-world druggability against an independent outcome rather than another network. This study evaluates that question and tests whether a simple, perturbation-free correction can recover any resulting predictive gap. Using the K562 essential-gene Perturb-seq dataset (2,285 pseudobulk CRISPR-interference profiles; 8,563 genes), an undirected correlational network and an independently constructed, perturbation-anchored causal network were built from identical data and compared across 1,868 shared genes via Spearman rank correlation and top-K overlap across three thresholds; both rankings were cross-referenced against Open Targets for documented drug mechanisms, and a logistic regression classifier quantified predictive value for known-drug status, with two specificity-adjustment refinements tested symmetrically on both networks. Rank agreement was weak and threshold-invariant (ρ = 0.091–0.158; zero top-20 overlap), yielding 77 correlational “false hubs” and 92 causal “hidden drivers.” Hidden drivers showed no category-level druggability enrichment (7.6% vs. 10.9% background) but included compelling, independently corroborated exceptions, CDK7 and AURKB, both invisible or near-invisible to correlation alone. Causal position outperformed correlational position for predicting known-drug status (AUC 0.655 vs. 0.625; combined 0.704), and specificity correction applied to the correlational network matched causal performance without perturbation data (AUC 0.655), reaching AUC 0.736 combined. These findings indicate correlational hub centrality is an unreliable proxy for causal importance and druggability, but a simple correction can recover much of the causal network’s advantage when tested empirically in both directions.

title: Deciphering the contributions of hybridization and genome dosage to vegetative vigor in perennial forage maize
abstract:
SUMMARY 
 Heterosis and genomic dosage each enhance plant vigor, yet their manifestation and underlying mechanisms in vegetative growth, particularly within polyploid systems, remain unclear. We synthesized and analyzed a series of  Zea – Tripsacum  allopolyploid trihybrids (MTPs) with varying genomic compositions to dissect the synergistic contributions of hybridization and polyploidy/aneuploidy effects to vegetative vigor. We demonstrate that increased  Z. perennis  genome dosage directly enhances fresh weight (FW) and photosynthetic capacity, whereas interspecific hybridization-triggered extensive transcriptome reprogramming. Heterotic hybrids exhibited transcriptional signatures of improved energy use efficiency, characterized by the downregulation of energy-costly protein quality control systems and upregulation of energy metabolism and carbon fixation pathways. Co-expression network analysis linked modules of fructose metabolism and glycolysis positively to FW heterosis, while protein folding modules were negatively correlated. Field trials confirmed the agronomic superiority of elite MTP-derived perennial forage cultivars, Yucao 6 and Yucao 9919, which achieved high yields (127.68–142.61 t ha −1 ) across diverse ecological zones, 156.28–186.25% higher than conventional silage maize. These perennial forage cultivars can be harvested for many years after a single planting, substantially lowering production costs and providing a practical option for utilizing sloping and abandoned lands in southern China. Our findings clarify how hybridization and genomic dosage, via transcriptional remodeling, jointly boost plant vigor, offering both a mechanistic framework and a practical breeding roadmap for integrating heterosis and genomic dosage strategies in crop improvement.

title: The evolutionary history of brackish specialization from marine ancestry in the seagrass Ruppia sinensis
abstract:
Conceptual model of waterfowl-mediated long-distance dispersal in  Ruppia sinensis .
 
 
 Summary 
 
 Ruppia sinensis , a unique seagrass species that originated in the marine environment yet successfully colonized extreme inland habitats, offers a rare window onto how plants cope with major habitat shifts and clarifies the mechanisms of adaptive evolution during marine-to-brackish transitions.
We assembled a chromosome-level genome, conducted comparative phylogenomic analyses, assessed salinity tolerance through physiological experiments, and analyzed whole-genome resequencing data from 103 individuals representing 19 coastal and inland populations.
 R. sinensis  falls in the core seagrass PRC (Posidoniaceae, Ruppiaceae, and Cymodoceaceae) clade with a Ruppiaceae-specific whole-genome duplication yet has lost tolerance to full-strength seawater and is an obligate brackish specialist. Coastal and inland lineages diverged  c.  25 000 yr ago; dramatic sea-level fluctuations since the Last Glacial Period repeatedly displaced coastal populations, causing reductions in effective population size, loss of genetic diversity, and elevated genetic load. Inland populations persisted in saline-lake refugia and retain nearly twice the genetic diversity.
The marine-to-brackish shift is an evolutionary trade-off rather than passive habitat tracking, with inland saline lakes serving as refugia that preserved diversity. Such shifts may be a recurrent adaptive strategy in seagrass evolution, and these diverse inland populations warrant conservation priority under climate change.

title: The cyanobacterium Anabaena uses pleomorphism as an acclimation strategy to high‐light stress
abstract:
The cyanobacterium  Anabaena  exhibits remarkable morphological plasticity in response to changes in light intensity. These reversible changes are associated with the repositioning of thylakoids within the cytoplasm. Here, we show that cell morphology is determined by the balance between the activities of two peptidoglycan assembly systems, the elongasome and class A penicillin-binding proteins, which respond oppositely to light intensity. By modulating light absorption and photosynthetic performance, changes in cell morphology enable large globular cells to mitigate the deleterious effects of high-light stress, revealing morphological plasticity as a previously unrecognized mechanism of acclimation to high light.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Phytoplankton species display characteristic morphologies that are generally assumed to confer adaptive advantages, yet the functional significance of cell shape remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated whether pleomorphism contributes to acclimation to changing light environments.
Using the cyanobacterium  Anabaena  sp. PCC 7120 as a model system, we combined molecular genetics, microscopy, physiological measurements and biophysical analyses to determine how morphology is regulated and how it affects photosynthetic performance under different light intensities.
We show that  Anabaena  undergoes a reversible light-dependent morphological transition from rod-shaped cells under low light to large globular cells under high-light stress. This transition is controlled by the relative activities of the elongasome and class A penicillin-binding proteins and is accompanied by thylakoid reorganization. The globular morphology reduces light absorption and enables cells to maintain photosynthetic activity under photoinhibitory conditions.
Our findings establish a mechanistic link between cell-wall remodeling, cellular optics and photosynthetic performance, revealing pleomorphism as a dynamic acclimation strategy to high-light stress. More broadly, this work provides experimental support for the packaging effect and highlights morphology as an active determinant of phytoplankton acclimation capacity.

title: Strigolactones modulate iron uptake in plants
abstract:
Model for strigolactone regulation of basal iron uptake in Arabidopsis and maize.
 
 
 Summary 
 
Strigolactone (SL) hormones influence a wide range of developmental and physiological processes but have not previously been linked to plant iron homeostasis. Here, we identify the gene underlying the iron-deficient maize mutant  interveinal yellow  ( ivy ) as  ZmCCD8 , a key enzyme in SL biosynthesis.
Maize  ivy/ccd8  mutants exhibit reduced expression of iron-regulated genes, including  IRO2  and genes involved in iron chelator and transporter biosynthesis. Application of the synthetic SL  rac -GR24 restores gene expression and alleviates chlorosis. Under iron-deficient conditions,  ccd8  mutants show normal upregulation of iron uptake genes, indicating that SLs are not required for the deficiency response but are essential for maintaining basal iron gene expression under sufficient iron.
Similar chlorosis in Arabidopsis and rice SL mutants under moderate iron suggests a conserved role for SLs in iron regulation, with potential agricultural applications.
We propose that strigolactone signaling acts as an upstream regulatory input to the established FIT/IRO2-centered iron-deficiency network, with SMXL/D53 proteins functioning as negative regulators and iron deficiency providing the principal activating cue.

title: Auxin-dependent miR167-ARF6/8.1-SAURs module coordinates local growth to shape floret diversification in Asteraceae
abstract: Abstract The corolla is a primary determinant of floral architecture and reproductive success. However, the processes that translate localized growth patterns into species-specific morphologies remain unclear. The complex inflorescences (capitula) of Asteraceae consist of different types of flowers. In  Chrysanthemum × morifolium , anemone-type varieties represent a distinct floral form characterized by dramatically elongated corolla tubes in bisexual disc florets. Using the anemone-type chrysanthemum, characterized by dramatically elongated disc florets, we demonstrate that sustained corolla formation depends on localized auxin enrichment. Two auxin response factors,  CmARF6  and  CmARF8.1 , have been identified as positive regulators of this process. These ARFs are post-transcriptionally regulated by miR167 in a dose-dependent manner, establishing a regulatory module that directly activates the auxin-biosynthesis gene  CmYUC2  and auxin-transport gene  CmPILS1 . Concurrently,  CmARF6  and  CmARF8.1  stimulate localized tissue proliferation by activating  CmSAUR64 and CmSAUR76 . Comparative analyses across diverse Asteraceae species suggest that auxin-associated regulatory mechanisms may contribute to region-specific corolla growth. Our findings demonstrate that auxin regulation contributes to region-specific corolla growth in the bisexual disc florets of chrysanthemum, providing a framework for investigating related morphological variation in other Asteraceae species.

title: Beyond acceptor emissivity: interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder regulate nonradiative voltage losses for organic solar cells
abstract: Abstract Suppressing non-radiative energy loss (Δ E  nr ) is critical for achieving high open-circuit voltage ( V  OC ) in organic solar cells (OSCs), yet it remains unclear whether intrinsic emissive properties of acceptors can reliably predict voltage losses. Here, we report a counterintuitive phenomenon in which a low-emissive acceptor (D6) delivers a significantly reduced Δ E  nr  compared with the benchmark L8-BO when blended with D18. Despite lower intrinsic emissivity of D6, the D18: D6 system exhibits a markedly higher electroluminescence efficiency and a reduced Δ E  nr  of 0.153 eV, leading to an enhanced  V  OC  of 0.980 V. Incorporation of D6 into the D18: L8-BO host yields a ternary device with a power conversion efficiency of 21.01%. Sensitive EQE analysis reveals that favorable CT-state energetics partially contribute to the reduced non-radiative loss of D18: D6, while temperature-dependent photoluminescence analysis further identifies suppressed interfacial dynamic disorder as a critical additional factor. While dynamic disorder is significantly increased in the D18: L8-BO blend, it is effectively suppressed in the D18: D6 system, resulting in preserved emissive interfacial states. Complementary structural and kinetic studies demonstrate that D6 modulates aggregation pathways and stabilizes nanoscale morphology, enabling efficient charge transport and reduced recombination. Furthermore, the beneficial role of D6 can be extended to multiple high-performance acceptor systems, demonstrating its general applicability as an interfacial regulator for improving photovoltaic performance. These results highlight that non-radiative voltage loss in OSCs is governed by the interplay between interfacial excited-state energetics and dynamic disorder rather than by the intrinsic emissivity of the acceptor alone, providing new insights into the design of low-energy-loss photovoltaic materials.

title: Rippled graphene pores as fluidic memristive devices with synaptic and neuromorphic functionalities
abstract: Abstract Nanofluidic memristive devices work with nanoscale pores (or channels) and ions dissolved in water, which harness the ionic memory effect aiming to store and process information. These devices share the same charge carriers as biological systems and bring hope for better emulating the neural functions and developing ionic circuits for neuromorphic applications. Specifically, theory and experiments suggest that nanoconfinement is essential for inducing a memory effect, which places a limit on the pore size to nm-scale or smaller. Such devices are, however, difficult to scale up with precision and operate with long-term stability. Here, we show that a micrometer size pore, generally expected to exhibit a linear ion transport, can display a pronounced memory effect, if its rim is wrapped by strongly curved and tightly stacked graphene. We attribute the observation to slow ion dynamics confined in the rippled graphene edges. The devices are easy to scale up and integrate into fluidic circuits. The memory effect is ion-selective and, crucially, exhibits long endurance, which enables reversible modification of the conductance states using programmable voltage spikes and various electrolytes over a long time, akin to biological synaptic plasticity. Thanks to this plasticity, our devices and their integrated circuits enable storing, transmitting and processing information with exceptionally high reliability, fidelity and accuracy, as evidenced by the effective processing of largescale and event-based information in the identification of both grayscale and color images, and in the real-time analysis of emulated neural signals. Our results highlight nanoscale morphology of the pore wall as an important parameter regulating ion transport, in addition to the well-documented pore’s charge and size, and indicate that the stringent nanoconfinement for ionic memory can be lifted from restricting the pore size to designing its rim structure. The devices and their integrated circuits may find use in ionic neuromorphic applications.

title: Conformational inversion mediated organic crystal actuator with extended stroke, self-healing, and optical switching
abstract: Abstract Dynamic molecular crystals with the capability to effectively convert thermal energy into mechanical work offer a compelling platform for microactuators. However, developing crystalline actuation materials that simultaneously achieve large and reversible deformation, rapid response, robust cyclability, and integrated optoelectronic functionality remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we take advantage of the conformational inversion of cyclohexyl groups and have rationally developed a dynamic organic crystal based on a dibenzothiophene sulfone derivative, BcDT, which exhibits exceptionally large, rapid, and reversible elongation. The thermally induced chair-to-boat conformational inversion of the introduced cyclohexyl moieties drives a cooperative phase transition that yields a linear elongation of ~14.3% along the crystal long axis, which delivers a work density of ~6.8 × 10 2  J m −3  and an efficiency of ~0.014%. Notably, the crystal features an uncommon self-healing capability, autonomously repairing macroscopic cracks during heating/cooling stages, ensuring its structural integrity and reliable actuation over multiple thermal cycles. The phase transition also enables reversible switching of linear and nonlinear optical properties, including a 4.2-fold modulation of two-photon excited fluorescence and tunable polarization anisotropy. Leveraging these properties, we demonstrate that BcDT crystals can function as microactuator devices to propel a heavy object and cooperatively lift a platform. This work establishes a molecular design strategy that integrates rapid, high-stroke actuation, self-healing, and optical switching within a single crystalline system, overcoming key functional limitations of current microactuators based on dynamic molecular crystals.

title: Back-end-of-line-integrated carbon nanotube modules for acceleration of silicon logic and clock networks
abstract: Abstract Geometric transistor scaling no longer delivers proportional timing gains in advanced silicon logic integrated circuits (ICs), where operating frequency is increasingly bounded by high-capacitance, fanout-limited logic paths and clock networks. The emerging  τ -scaling perspective reframes this limitation as a time-constant problem across the driver-interconnect-load system. Here we report  τ Drive, a monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) carbon-nanotube (CNT) active timing overlay that selectively compresses the dominant  τ  of silicon logic and clock paths. Unlike topology-folding approaches that primarily shorten interconnects,  τ Drive preserves the underlying silicon complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) fabric and inserts back-end-of-line (BEOL) integrated CNT timing cells only at load-critical driver stages. A 180-nm Si/500-nm CNT experimental platform verifies low-temperature CNT-on-Si integration, and will enable CNT-assisted Si ring oscillators to achieve a 294% output-swing improvement and 30% effective-current enhancement with a fanout (FO) of 5. In simulations of a 3-nm Si central processing unit (CPU) using calibrated 10-nm CNT CMOS standard cells, selective CNT insertion reduces FO = 39 local delay and transition by 87.5% and 89.5%, respectively, and a single-cell replacement improves the full-CPU logic-path maximum frequency ( F  max ) by 2.3%, while selective clock-tree enhancement raises the frequency bound from 2.85 to 2.93 GHz with only a 0.01 mW increase in clock-tree synthesis (CTS) power. These results establish CNT-on-Si M3D as a low-intrusion, vertically accessible drive resource for post-geometric  τ  compression, as well as a novel logic-folding approach.

title: Promoting photocatalytic methane oxidative coupling via gradient oxidation field engineering
abstract: Abstract The efficient and selective photocatalytic oxidative coupling of methane (OCM) into valuable chemicals remains an unresolved challenge in modern science. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of a robust photocatalyst by constructing photocatalytic gradient oxidation field on mesoporous TiO 2 , which demonstrates exceptional OCM performance and outperforms other benchmark photocatalysts. The optimized photocatalytic system exhibits a high CH 4  conversion rate of 1.2 mmol h −1 , a high C 2  hydrocarbon space-time yield of 82.7 mmol g −1  h −1  and 90.1% C 2  selectivity, accompanied by a remarkable apparent quantum efficiency of over 11.6%. Mechanism analyses reveal that the gradient oxidation field introduced by the Au nanoislands and Pd atomic satellites can optimize the oxidation activity and selectivity with hydroxide and superoxide radicals, respectively. The synergistic interaction between the Au and Pd sites facilitates favorable adsorption of O 2 /CH 4  reactants and promotes fast desorption of the C 2 H 6  product, thereby accelerating the overall OCM process. This work demonstrates the critical role of photocatalytic oxidation field, and opens a new avenue for developing efficient and selective catalysts for various photocatalytic applications.

title: Faster global mid-depth ocean connectivity in observations
abstract: Abstract Ocean circulation redistributes heat, carbon, and biogeochemical tracers through transport pathways connecting distant ocean regions, yet global connectivity of mid-depth transport pathways remains poorly constrained by observations. Here we establish an observational benchmark of global mid-depth water-mass connectivity, using more than 1.3 million displacements recorded by 9,920 Argo floats over the past two decades. The benchmark reveals that observed connectivity is generally faster than simulated, with mean connectivity timescales 23-29% shorter in the real ocean. This systematic discrepancy between observed and simulated mid-depth ocean connectivity arises from overestimated turnover timescales within subtropical gyre interiors and underrepresentation of rapid inter-basin exchanges along equatorial and western boundary pathways in the simulation-derived networks, particularly in the South Pacific and South Atlantic. These findings provide quantitative constraints on ocean interior transport, with broad implications for estimates of climate memory, tracer age, carbon sequestration, and marine biogeographic connectivity.

title: 4f-multiplet-enabled electron–phonon decoupling towards high thermoelectric performance in rare-earth topological semimetal TbPtBi
abstract: Abstract Topological materials exhibit strong magneto-thermoelectric effects owing to the ultrahigh mobility of electrons, yet bosonic phonon transport typically remains insensitive to magnetic fields. Crystal electric fields (CEF) combined with Zeeman splitting in rare-earth ions yielding discrete 4 f  excitation levels can in principle but have rarely been demonstrated to reduce phonon thermal conductivity by resonant phonon scattering. Therefore, rare-earth topological semimetals offer a unique platform in which electrical and phononic thermal transport can be intrinsically decoupled by magnetic fields. Herein, taking TbPtBi as an example, we demonstrate pronounced electron–phonon decoupling enabled by field-tunable 4 f  multiplets. High-mobility topological carriers give rise to high magneto-thermopowers and thermoelectric power factors. Meanwhile, multi-resonant phonon scattering by Zeeman-split Tb 3+  CEF levels suppresses the phonon thermal conductivity, leading to a complete quenching of the phonon peak and a reduction of nearly 90% at 13 K by applying a magnetic field of ∼9 T. Theoretical calculations indicate a redistribution of phonon lifetimes that can drive the lattice into a phonon-glass-like state. These results establish 4 f -multiplet engineering as a new way for electron-phonon decoupling and demonstrate the great potential of rare-earth topological materials for exceptional magneto-thermoelectric performance.

title: Multispecies Mixtures: An Individual-Centered Quantitative Genetic Framework for Complex Plant Neighborhoods
abstract: Abstract Mixing crop species or varieties in the same field can raise yield and stability, but performance varies widely among combinations that breeders cannot yet predict. What makes a good neighbor is partly heritable, and quantitative genetics models this as an indirect genetic effect describing a genotype's contribution to its neighbors' phenotypes. Here, we extend existing models with a complementary approach based on continuous neighborhoods, in which diverse genotypes of two species are mixed. In a continuous-neighborhood design, several genotypes of each species are grown in a single trial, with every plant georeferenced. Each plant's phenotype is decomposed into direct genetic effects, indirect genetic effects from neighbors of both species, and environmental effects. Breeding values are then assembled for each genotype by combining its three genetic effects. We derived analytical expressions for the variances and covariance of these effects, validated the model, and evaluated its statistical properties through simulations spanning a wide range of parameter settings. For the same number of plants, the continuous-neighborhood design estimated indirect effects far more accurately than a pairwise design and, in addition, allowed indirect environmental variance to be estimated. Applied to a wheat–alfalfa experiment comprising 3,840 plants, from 181 wheat pure lines and 106 alfalfa families, the model attributed 8.6\% and 8.2\% of the variance in wheat grain number and alfalfa biomass to direct genetic effects respectively, and 4.0\% and 4.6\% to indirect genetic effects from alfalfa. The framework therefore offers an individual-centered basis for analyzing multispecies neighborhoods and their breeding potential.

title: A review-based guide to selecting an appropriate strategy for transgene-free genome editing in plants
abstract: Abstract The field of plant genetic engineering has advanced considerably since the development of the first transgenic crop plants, and even though transgenic varieties of various crops are now commercially available, consumer reluctance and environmental concerns over transgene escape pose limits on their expansion. Gene editing offers the opportunity to selectively and precisely alter DNA sequences without reliance on stably integrated transgenes, assuaging both concerns. Considerable progress has been made with the advent of programmable nucleases such as Cas9 and its derivatives. The transgenes encoding the gene editing components can be expressed transiently without integration in the plant's genome or removed from the genome via outcrossing or haploid induction to result in gene-edited plants that are no longer considered transgenic. Nonetheless, gene editing systems remain challenging to implement in some plant species, notably those that have long generation times or are vegetatively propagated, precluding the removal of editing tools through crosses. In these cases, a transgene-free method for introduction of all components needed to enable gene editing will bring the promise of modern breeding tools within reach. Transgene-free genome editing can be accomplished through the delivery of editing components as DNA, RNA, or ribonucleoproteins with delivery via  Agrobacterium , microprojectiles, nanocarriers, DNA and RNA viruses, and grafting. Between technical constraints and scientific goals, it can be challenging to determine an appropriate transgene-free genome editing method. Following a review of the literature, a decision tree is provided to help select an appropriate method for a given plant species and to show how emerging tools, including smaller editors, can advance the field.

title: SeekRBP: leveraging sequence–structure integration with reinforcement learning for receptor-binding protein identification
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Receptor-binding proteins (RBPs) initiate viral infection and determine host specificity, serving as key targets for phage engineering and therapy. However, the identification of RBPs is complicated by their extreme sequence divergence, which often renders traditional homology-based alignment methods ineffective. While machine learning offers a promising alternative, such approaches struggle with severe class imbalance and the difficulty of selecting informative negative samples from heterogeneous tail proteins. Existing methods often fail to balance learning from these “hard negatives” while maintaining generalization. Results We present SeekRBP, a sequence–structure framework that models negative sampling as a sequential decision-making problem. By employing a multi-armed bandit strategy, SeekRBP dynamically prioritizes informative non-RBP sequences based on real-time training feedback, complemented by a multimodal fusion of protein language and structural embeddings. Benchmarking demonstrates that SeekRBP consistently outperforms static sampling strategies. Furthermore, a case study on  Vibrio  phages validates that SeekRBP effectively identifies RBPs to improve host prediction, highlighting its potential for large-scale annotation and synthetic biology applications. Availability and implementation The source code of SeekRBP is available via:  https://github.com/Saillxl/SeekRBP .

title: MIRAGE-DTA: conflict-aware multimodal evidence arbitration for drug–target affinity prediction
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Multimodal drug–target affinity (DTA) models can incorporate molecular, protein, assay and textual evidence whose availability and reliability vary under missing modalities, cold-start entities and assay distribution shift. Results We present MIRAGE-DTA, a reliability-oriented evidence-arbitration layer that complements DTA encoders by keeping current-sample and training-set retrieval evidence as two explicit chains, carrying modality masks into fusion, retrieving training-only neighbors, and resolving disagreement with an interaction gate and validation-selected anchor. Across BindingDB_Kd, DAVIS, KIBA and a 2010–2024 CHEMBL_ASSAY benchmark with 35,238 interactions, experiments tested cold-start, missing-modality and assay/temporal shift settings. Under 35% sequence/text missingness on CHEMBL_ASSAY, 10-seed paired evaluation showed that MIRAGE-DTA reduced expected calibration error relative to late fusion by 0.0524, 0.0923 and 0.1018 on assay-cold, target-cold and temporal splits. Risk at 80% coverage was significantly lower on target-cold and temporal splits and numerically lower on assay-cold. A complementary complete-evidence direct-pChEMBL regression analysis also showed lower RMSE for the two-branch model than for current-only and retrieval-only regressors across assay-cold, target-cold and temporal splits. Ranking remained broadly competitive, with a modest trade-off on the temporal split, indicating that the principal benefit lies in calibrated and selective prediction under incomplete or shifted evidence. Shortcut audits quantified neighbor-overlap effects and showed that temporal retrieval was not driven by repeated compounds or near-duplicate scaffolds. Availability and implementation Source code is available at  https://github.com/wushen1103-collab/mirage_drug_miniprototype  and archived on Zenodo at  https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22695984 ; data come from public sources.

title: PFM: perturbed flow matching for structure-based drug design
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Target-specific 3D molecular generation is a promising approach for structure-based drug design. However, existing diffusion-based methods are generally restricted to marginal distributions with closed-form solutions, limiting the flexibility of generative process design, especially for the forward noising process. As a result, these methods may be less effective in modeling the complex distributions underlying pocket-conditioned molecular generation. Results We develop Perturbed Flow Matching (PFM), a flow-matching-based framework for protein pocket–conditioned 3D molecular generation. PFM employs a perturbed conditional probability path that incorporates both pocket binding-site information and coupled atom type–coordinate information, enabling more effective generation of molecules in protein binding environments. On CrossDocked2020, PFM achieves competitive structural quality and the best average Vina score among the evaluated unguided methods (-7.12); PFM-G further improves the score to -8.70 with tailored classifier-free guidance. Experiments on additional molecular datasets further confirm the effectiveness and generalizability of the proposed framework. Availability and implementation  https://github.com/kurisu92725/PFM

title: DTBNet: multimodal 3D geometric perception with hierarchical attention for robust drug–target interaction and binding affinity prediction
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Accurate prediction of drug-target interactions (DTIs) and binding affinity (DTA) constitutes a core challenge in accelerating drug discovery. While existing computational methods have made progress, most models struggle to capture critical physicochemical interactions in 3D space due to reliance on 1D sequences or 2D graph structures, and exhibit limited generalization in cold-start scenarios. This study proposes DTBNet, a unified prediction framework integrating multimodal geometric perception and hierarchical attention. The framework constructs heterogeneous embeddings combining local chemical details with global biological information by incorporating protein 3D geometric features and multilevel drug representations. During cross-modal interaction, atom–residue cross-attention first captures pair-specific local associations, followed by group-level multi-head self-attention that integrates complementary chemical-semantic, global structural, and local geometric interaction representations. Results Experiments on benchmark datasets (Davis, KIBA, PDBBind) demonstrate that compared with the optimal baseline models, DTBNet achieves up to 19.8% reduction in mean squared error and 8.0% improvement in Pearson correlation coefficient, maintaining optimal performance in drug cold-start, target cold-start, and completely novel pairing scenarios, showcasing robust cross-domain adaptability. Independent validation on GPCR targets achieves RMSE 0.783, confirming real-world applicability. Visualization analyses reveal DTBNet precisely identifies interaction sites between key transmembrane helical domain residues and drug aromatic rings, with attention distribution highly consistent with experimentally resolved binding conformations. These results establish DTBNet as a new performance benchmark through 3D geometric perception and dynamic attention mechanisms, providing interpretable molecular insights for structure-based rational drug design and demonstrating broad potential in virtual screening and target discovery. Availability The source code and data are available at  https://github.com/wyx2012/DTB_Net . Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at  Bioinformatics  online.

title: CellSavior: an open-source framework for improved cell calling in targeted single-cell DNA sequencing
abstract: Abstract  Motivation Single-cell DNA sequencing (scDNA-seq) has emerged as a key approach for studying complex genomic variation, including tumor heterogeneity. Despite its increasing commercial availability, exemplified by the Tapestri platform, analytical reproducibility remains limited due to reliance on proprietary and non-transparent pipelines. Among preprocessing steps, cell calling is particularly critical, as it determines which barcodes correspond to true cells rather than background noise and directly shapes all downstream analyses. However, existing methods typically rely on empirical thresholding and exhibit inconsistent performance across datasets. These limitations underscore the need for a robust and generalizable cell calling framework for reliable scDNA-seq analysis. Results We developed CellSavior, an open-source cell calling algorithm with an integrated downstream pipeline that produces standardized outputs. CellSavior employs an ensemble clustering strategy across multiple distance metrics, combined with confidence-weighted merging, to generate a consensus classification that reduces bias and improves robustness. Across 33 public and in-house single-cell DNA sequencing datasets, CellSavior recapitulated cell annotations generated by commercial software (CellFinder) in 31 cases (93.9%). In the remaining discordant cases, CellSavior yielded more biologically interpretable annotations, rescuing previously undetected clusters enriched for key hotspot genomic alterations. Availability The source code for CellSavior is freely available at  https://github.com/dauer-tgilab/CellSavior ; DOI:  https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22744146 . Supplementary information Supplementary data are available at  Bioinformatics  online.

title: Roles of Interstitial Albumin in the Subcutaneous Delivery of Therapeutic Peptides
abstract:
A biomimetic extracellular matrix hydrogel platform reveals how interstitial albumin regulates peptide pharmacokinetics after subcutaneous administration. Albumin not only binds peptides but also shows a unique affinity for glycosaminoglycans, thereby reshaping peptide distribution and diffusion. In vivo, increasing albumin‐binding affinity prolongs tissue residence time, establishing competitive albumin‐matrix interactions as vital considerations for predictive in vitro biopharmaceutical models.








ABSTRACT
Subcutaneous administration of biotherapeutics is increasingly favored for better safety profile, improved stability, and patient compliance compared with intravenous administration. Despite these advantages, the roles of extracellular matrix (ECM) components and interstitial proteins, particularly albumin, in the mechanisms governing therapeutic pharmacokinetics and bioavailability remain poorly understood. We present a versatile and customizable hydrogel platform resembling native ECM in composition, charge density, and microstructure, enabling systematic investigation of transport mechanisms in the subcutaneous space. Using this platform, we studied peptides with different net charges and albumin affinities. Based on results from confocal microscopy combined with measurements of diffusivities by means of FRAP, we propose a role for albumin beyond that of a transport vehicle for drugs. We show that reversible peptide‐albumin binding can both remove peptides bound to the ECM biopolymers and modulate peptide diffusivity and distribution, as albumin was found to have an affinity for matrix glycosaminoglycans. For cationic peptides, albumin had a major influence on diffusivity and distribution in the matrix, with more pronounced effects over time in vitro. These findings, complemented by exploratory in vivo observations in a limited cohort, highlight realistic ECM structure and albumin inclusion as key considerations for predictive in vitro subcutaneous models.

title: Hypoxic Preconditioning Restores NK Cell Metabolic Fitness by Attenuating MAPK Signaling to Potentiate Antitumor Immunity in Lung Cancer
abstract:
Solid tumor hypoxia severely compromises natural killer cell function. This study demonstrates that hypoxic preconditioning preserves NK cell antitumor activity by limiting excessive stress -MAPK signaling and promoting mitochondrial metabolic fitness. Pharmacological MAPK attenuation reproduces this protective phenotype in NK92 and iPSC -derived NK cells, identifying the MAPK‒mitochondrial axis as a potential strategy for improving NK cell therapy in hypoxic tumors.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Solid tumor hypoxia is a major barrier to NK cell-based immunotherapy. To address this challenge, we establish a hypoxic preconditioning (HPC) model. We find that acute hypoxia (AH; 1% O 2 ) significantly impairs NK92 cell cytotoxicity—such as granzyme B secretion and infiltration into lung cancer cell spheroids. In contrast, HPC pretreatment (gradual reduction from 5% to 1% O 2 ) remarkably restores these functions. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis reveals that HPC markedly attenuates hypoxia -induced aberrant MAPK pathway activation. MAPK attenuation under normoxia recapitulates HPC -like protection by promoting mitochondrial biogenesis and metabolic remodeling, thereby enhancing the antitumor activity of NK92 cells both in vitro and in vivo. Notably, systemic MAPK inhibitor injection increases NKp46 expression on endogenous NK cells in BALB/c mice. Importantly, this strategy is also effective in human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived induced NK (iNK) cells, supporting broader evaluation across NK cell platforms. Collectively, this study identifies the MAPK–mitochondrial metabolic axis as a critical regulator of hypoxia-induced NK cell dysfunction and proposes metabolic preconditioning as a strategy to overcome solid tumor hypoxia.

title: Spray‐Dried mRNA‐LNP Powder Enabling Multi‐Route Delivery With 3‐Year Refrigerated Stability
abstract:
Spray‐dried mRNA‐LNP powder with trehalose matrix enables reconstitution for parenteral delivery or direct administration via pulmonary and sublingual routes, maintaining protein expression comparable to liquid controls. The thermostable powder preserves colloidal stability, mRNA integrity, and biological activity for over 3 years at 2°C–8°C, while liquid formulations degrade within 6–9 months, eliminating cold‐chain requirements.








ABSTRACT
The clinical translation of mRNA‐lipid nanoparticle (mRNA‐LNP) therapeutics is constrained by limited stability of liquid formulations, necessitating ultra‐cold storage and restricting global accessibility. Here, we report a spray‐dried dry powder platform for mRNA‐LNPs that overcomes these limitations while enabling flexible routes of administration. Systematic evaluation of pharmaceutically relevant sugars identifies trehalose as an optimal matrix former, yielding high‐recovery mRNA‐LNP dry powder product (DPP) with controlled particle size, low residual moisture, and preserved LNP physicochemical properties upon reconstitution. Mechanistic studies combining solid‐state characterization, fluorescence tracking, and solvent extraction demonstrate that mRNA‐LNPs are entrapped within an amorphous trehalose matrix core, providing protection against dehydration and rehydration stress. Reconstituted DPP (RDPP) maintains in vivo protein expression comparable to liquid control (LC) following intravenous and intramuscular administration, while supporting effective mucosal delivery via pulmonary and sublingual routes. Direct administration of DPP without reconstitution enables lung‐targeted protein expression, highlighting potential for cold‐chain–independent therapies. Critically, DPP preserves colloidal stability, mRNA integrity, ionizable lipid stability, and biological activity for over 3 years under refrigerated conditions, whereas liquid formulation exhibits substantial degradation within 6–9 months. These findings establish spray‐dried mRNA‐LNP DPPs as a robust platform integrating long‐term stability with multi‐route delivery for improved accessibility of mRNA therapeutics.

title: Targeting a Calcium‐Associated Mitochondrial Vulnerability in TET2‐Deficient Myeloid Cells
abstract:
Reduced TET2 function creates a calcium-associated mitochondrial vulnerability in macrophages that is preferentially exploited by Lanatoside C. The resulting stress promotes apoptosis of TET2-deficient macrophages, reduces inflammatory and fibrotic injury in human cardiac organoids, and highlights a genotype-associated myeloid liability that may be therapeutically tractable in clonal hematopoiesis-associated cardiovascular disease.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) driven by loss-of-function mutations in TET2 is associated with increased cardiovascular risk, yet therapeutic strategies capable of preferentially targeting pathogenic  TET2 -deficient myeloid effector cells remain poorly defined. Here, we identify a TET2 loss-of-function-associated ion-mitochondrial vulnerability that enables preferential pharmacological suppression of  TET2 -deficient macrophages. Using chemical-genetic profiling, we find that perturbation of ion homeostasis preferentially compromises survival of  TET2 -deficient macrophages through increased mitochondrial-enriched Ca 2+ -sensitive signaling and activation of intrinsic apoptotic pathways. The cardiac glycoside Lanatoside C preferentially induces mitochondrial depolarization and apoptosis in  TET2 -deficient macrophages, with substantially smaller effects in control cells. In multicellular human cardiac organoids, preferential reduction of  TET2 -knockdown macrophages suppresses inflammatory remodeling, reduces cardiomyocyte apoptosis and fibrosis, and improves abnormal calcium-handling dynamics. In a murine partial donor-cell reconstitution model, Lanatoside C reduced relative donor-derived monocyte and neutrophil frequencies in Tet2-deficient donor-cell recipients; these findings do not establish effects on stem-cell fitness. Together, these findings identify a pharmacologically exploitable ion-mitochondrial vulnerability associated with TET2 loss-of-function and establish human cardiac organoids as a platform for causal interrogation of immune-driven cardiovascular pathology.

title: Pharmacokinetic Tuning Redirects β‐Lapachone From NQO1 Bioactivation to Vimentin‐Targeted Oxidation in Cancer
abstract:
Pharmacokinetic tuning acts as a programmable mechanistic switch for β-lap. Sustained low-concentration exposure redirects β-lap from NQO1 bioactivation to direct oxidation of vimentin, driving disulfide crosslinking, proteasomal overload and ferroptosis. The sustained treatment also expands the therapeutic window by enabling efficacy at lower concentrations. These benefits provide new insight for indication and patient selection in clinical translation of β-lap.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The “single molecule, multi-target” paradigm is increasingly recognized among bioactive small molecules, yet the role of pharmacokinetics as a determinant of mechanism selectivity remains unexplored. Here, we demonstrate that dosing schedule governs the dominant cell death mechanism of β-lapachone (β-lap), an  ortho -naphthoquinone antitumor natural product, switching it from NQO1-bioactivation to targeted oxidative modification of vimentin (VIM), a type III intermediate filament protein overexpressed in aggressive cancers. Using a photoaffinity probe and mass spectrometry-based proteomics, we identified VIM as a direct binding target driving the dominant cell death mechanism under sustained low-concentration exposure. Vimentin directly binds β-lap with a dissociation constant at micromolar levels, and VIM essentiality for β-lap cytotoxicity was established via knockdown and overexpression in cancer cell lines. Mechanistically, β-lap selectively oxidizes the C328 residue of VIM, triggering disulfide crosslinking of VIM filaments, proteasomal overload, and ferroptotic cell death, a cascade independent of NQO1. A sustained-release formulation of β-lap achieves tumor suppression comparable to gemcitabine at its maximum tolerated dose in MIA Paca-2 xenograft models. Taken together, these findings establish pharmacokinetic tuning as a programmable mechanistic switch, repurposing β-lap as a broader-spectrum, safer VIM-targeted therapy for NQO1-deficient malignancies and offering a generalizable strategy for natural product therapeutic expansion.

title: Solute‐Induced Modulation of Hydrogen Bonding, Ion Hydration, and Protonation in Hydrogels for Enhanced Microwave Absorption
abstract:
Systematic solute screening reveals how noncovalent interactions regulate dielectric loss in P(AA-co-AM) hydrogels. By tuning proton conduction, ion hydration, and hydrogen-bond interactions, the dielectric response can be precisely controlled, enabling tailored hydrogels with broadband microwave absorption and providing a general strategy for designing flexible electromagnetic absorbers.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Hydrogels have emerged as promising candidates for microwave absorption in next-generation flexible electronics and soft robotics, whose rapid development demands increasingly sophisticated and tunable dielectric properties from microwave-absorbing materials. However, the coupling of hydrogen bonding, ionic coordination, and protonation involving water creates a complex noncovalent interaction network, making it difficult to explore the main contribution of each interaction to the dielectric response, which hinders modulation of dielectric performance. Here, we propose a solute-mediated regulation strategy based on acrylic acid (AA) and acrylamide (AM) backbones by introducing polar groups, metal salts (M + ), and acidic solutions (H + ) to systematically investigate hydrogen bonding, metal-ion hydration, and protonation in regulating dielectric properties. The results reveal that hydrogen bonding and ionic coordination suppress proton hopping while generating new dipolar polarization units, thereby reducing reflection and shifting the dielectric response from conduction-dominated to polarization-dominated, whereas protonation balances conduction and polarization by regulating water conduction and suppressing hydrogen-bond-induced orientational polarization. Notably, hydrogen bonding coupled with Co(NO 3 ) 2 -induced hydrated ions and tartaric acid-induced protonation both enabled a broad effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 7.1 GHz at thicknesses of 1.88 and 1.85 mm, respectively.

title: A Biomimetic Elastic SEI Film Enables Micron‐Sized Bismuth Anodes for Wide‐Temperature Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract:
Inspired by natural seashells' hard-soft layered structure, a biomimetic elastic SEI is in situ constructed on micron-sized Bi via a G2/NaBF 4  electrolyte. The flexible polyether-based organic layer and rigid NaF nanocrystals synergistically dissipate volumetric stress, enabling a low Young's modulus. This µ-Bi anode delivers 100% capacity retention after 450 cycles at 5C and excellent −40°C performance.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Micron-sized bismuth (µ-Bi) is a promising high-capacity alloy anode for sodium-ion batteries, but its ∼250% volume expansion causes particle pulverization and continuous SEI destruction, especially at low temperatures. Inspired by the alternating hard inorganic/soft organic layers of seashells, this work in situ constructs a biomimetic elastic SEI on µ-Bi via microscopic solvation engineering. The G2/NaBF 4  electrolyte is designed to promote the formation of a flexible polyether-like organic component and reinforcing NaF-containing inorganic domains through complementary interfacial decomposition pathways, thereby constructing a mechanically adaptive organic–inorganic SEI. The biomimetic SEI has a low Young's modulus of 334 MPa and a broad elastic transition, efficiently dissipating volumetric stress. Consequently, the µ-Bi anode delivers 100% capacity retention after 450 cycles at 5C and 25°C, stable cycling at 9.49 mg cm −2 , and excellent wide-temperature rate/cycling performance at −40°C. This biomimetic interfacial design offers a new strategy to overcome volume-expansion failure in micron-sized alloy anodes.

title: SynAtlas: A Safe and Versatile Platform for Rapid Organ‐Scale Tissue Clearing and 3D Atlas Mapping
abstract:
An orthogonal synergy design principle integrates lipid solubilization, protein hydration modulation, and refractive-index matching within a unified aqueous clearing system. This modular strategy enables rapid, low-hazard, and broadly compatible tissue clearing while preserving molecular signals, supporting multiscale three-dimensional imaging across diverse organs and biological applications.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Understanding the detailed three-dimensional organization of cells, molecules, and tissues in their natural state is essential for advancing knowledge of biology, disease, and neural circuits, yet traditional slicing methods are slow, destructive, and prone to artifacts, while existing tissue-clearing techniques often compromise speed, safety, signal preservation, or simplicity. By systematically analyzing the distinct optical barriers that impede tissue transparency, we propose an orthogonal synergy design principle. Guided by this framework, we developed SynAtlas (

    T

    l

    a

    S 
 
 ystem ), a rationally designed clearing method that combines safe, compatible chemicals to simultaneously overcome the main barriers to transparency—lipid scattering, protein hydration heterogeneity, and refractive index mismatch—creating a fast, modular, and low-hazard platform. SynAtlas clears thin sections in minutes and whole organs within two days while excellently preserving fluorescent proteins, nucleic acids, and antibody labels; it enables high-resolution 3D atlases of neurons, vasculature, gene expression patterns, and cell types in mouse organs and archival human brain tissue, supports multi-round labeling with minimal distortion, and allows non-destructive cryo-preservation for long-term storage. This versatile approach makes advanced volumetric imaging more accessible and impactful for research and clinical applications.

title: Matrix Stiffness Promotes Tumor Metastasis by Triggering Recycling Endosome‐Mediated YY1 Nuclear Translocation and Transcriptional Activity
abstract:
In stiff extracellular matrix (ECM), integrin αVβ3 transduces mechanical cues of ECM stiffness to promote recycling endosome formation, creating a signaling platform for yin yang 1 (YY1)/p21‐activated kinase 4 (PAK4) binding, but not in soft ECM. Then, this triggers PAK4‐mediated YY1 phosphorylation at S118, subsequent YY1 nuclear translocation and transcriptional activation, and ultimately, tumor metastasis. 








ABSTRACT
Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and aberrant stiffness represent hallmarks of cancer; however, the mechanism transmitting these biomechanical cues to biochemical signals influencing tumor progression remains largely unknown. Here, we showed that stiff ECM triggers yin yang 1 (YY1) nuclear translocation and transcriptional activation, establishing its role as a matrix stiffness‐responsive mechanotransducer that mediates stiff ECM‐driven tumor metastasis. Mechanistically, stiff ECM significantly enhances the integrin αVβ3‐mediated recycling endosome formation, providing signaling platforms that facilitate interaction between YY1 and p21‐activated kinase 4 (PAK4). This interaction triggers YY1 phosphorylation at S118 and its subsequent translocation to the nucleus, where it promotes the expression of genes driving tumor metastasis. This study not only demonstrates how matrix stiffness induces tumor metastasis, but also reveals the novel roles of YY1 and recycling endosomes in matrix stiffness‐driven mechanical signal transduction. Moreover, we elucidate the fundamental mechanism of YY1 as a transcription factor and identify it as a matrix stiffness‐responsive mechanotransducer with anti‐tumor therapeutic targeting potential.

title: Self‐Included Fluorescent Probes via Azocalix[4]arene–Dye Conjugation for Activatable and Stable NIR Imaging
abstract:
Self‐Included Fluorescent Probes (SIFPs), composed of self‐included macrocyclic carrier‐dye conjugates, encapsulate and protect covalently attached dyes, preventing leakage and enhancing stability. Azocalixarene‐based hypoxia activation enables precise tumor‐specific imaging. This strategy merges covalent and non‐covalent advantages, offering a versatile method to convert existing dyes into activatable, stable probes.








ABSTRACT
Near‐infrared (NIR) fluorescent probes are crucial tools in bioimaging; however, the challenge of improving their stability and targeting precision remains a key issue. In this work, we present a novel strategy for designing Self‐Included Fluorescent Probes (SIFPs) using a covalent macrocyclic host‐dye conjugate approach. By covalently linking NIR dyes, such as indole heptamethine cyanine fluorescent probes, to azocalix[4]arene carriers, we leverage the unique properties of the macrocyclic host to encapsulate and protect the dyes intramolecularly, while enhancing their stability and preventing off‐target leakage. Importantly, the azocalixarene's hypoxia‐responsive azo linkers enable targeted activation of the dye in tumor environments, improving imaging accuracy. Through comprehensive in vitro and in vivo experiments, we demonstrate that SIFPs significantly outperform conventional probes and their host‐guest binary complexes in terms of stability and imaging precision. This strategy not only combines the benefits of covalent and non‐covalent binding but also offers an effective method for enhancing the design of activatable, stable fluorescent probes.

title: Spin‐Polarized Metallic Metal−Organic Framework With High Conductivity and Half‐Metallic Behavior
abstract:
By establishing a progression from insulating to semiconducting and ultimately to metallic MOFs, this study not only introduces a new design paradigm based on quantum spin-polarized electronic structures, but also represents a significant breakthrough toward the realization of next-generation conductive materials.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The establishment of new concepts for next-generation conductive materials remains both highly desirable and scientifically challenging. Herein, we report a Cu-based metal–organic framework (MOF), ([Cu(6Hmna)] n  ( 1 , 6Hmna = 6-mercaptonicotinic acid)), featuring metal–sulfur chains that exhibit intrinsic metallic behavior. Compound  1  exhibits a high electrical conductivity of up to 120 S cm−1, indicating a high electrical conductivity for a MOF in its crystalline form. The metallic transport characteristics are confirmed by temperature-dependent conductivity measurements. In addition, this Cu-MOF demonstrates highly efficient photoconductivity, with an outstanding photocurrent responsivity reaching 8100 A W −1  under infrared light illumination. Our theoretical DFT calculations predict that compound  1  exhibits an exotic spin-polarized electronic structure, in which one spin channel is metallic while the other remains semiconducting. This unique electronic configuration is particularly attractive for applications in spintronics and quantum technologies, as well as in optoelectronic and photoelectrochemical devices.

title: Molecular Engineering of Multi‐Site Small‐Molecule Chelation for Highly Efficient and Stable n‐i‐p Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract:
Li +  ion migration in Li-TFSI-doped Spiro-OMeTAD impairs efficiency and device stability. Rather than replacing Li + , a multi-site chelator is designed and introduced into Spiro-OMeTAD to immobilize Li +  ions with high affinity. The synergistic effects of suppressing ion migration, inducing ordered molecular packing, boosting p-doping efficiency, and optimizing interface energetics enable an outstanding PCE of 26.03% with long-term stability.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Li-TFSI-doped Spiro-OMeTAD is the benchmark hole-transporting material for high-performance n-i-p perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Yet its intrinsic instability, arising from Li +  migration, has long been regarded as an inevitable trade-off for achieving high efficiency. Despite extensive efforts, no alternative dopant system has yet fully matched the Li-TFSI/ t -BP system in simultaneously achieving high doping efficiency and well-established processability. Instead, these alternatives often sacrifice efficiency for improved stability, or they are hampered by synthetic complexity that precludes large-scale application. Here we design a multifunctional small-molecule chelator, TPABT3, with multiple coordination sites to immobilize Li +  ions and stabilize doped Spiro-OMeTAD. This molecule concurrently suppresses ion migration, induces ordered molecular packing, and enhances p-type doping efficiency, while optimizing energy-level alignment at the perovskite/HTL interface. The resulting two-step-fabricated FAPbI 3  devices deliver an outstanding power conversion efficiency of 26.03% with negligible hysteresis. Moreover, the PSCs retain over 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h under ISOS-L-1 aging conditions. This work establishes multi-site molecular chelation as an effective, generalizable strategy for achieving highly efficient and stable n-i-p perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Ligand‐Ratio–Tuned DNA Nanocarriers Overcome Bladder Barriers for Ultralow‐Dose Intravesical Therapy
abstract:
A programmable DNA framework drug carrier coordinates barrier transport, tumor targeting, and drug delivery through ligand‐ratio engineering. Systematic exploration of the Sgc8/fluorocarbon design space reveals a nonlinear optimal balance between penetration and cellular engagement, translating multifunctional integration into durable bladder tumor remission at an ultralow intravesical gemcitabine dose.








ABSTRACT
Effective delivery to target cells across biological barriers requires coordinated integration of multiple surface functionalities, yet such integration remains difficult to control in nanoscale systems. This challenge is particularly evident in intravesical delivery, where selective tumor‐cell engagement must be coupled with efficient transport through the glycosaminoglycan/mucus‐associated luminal environment. Here we present a ratio‐tunable DNA framework drug carrier (dFDC) that enables precise control over two orthogonal surface modules: an Sgc8 aptamer for targeting and a fluorocarbon (F–C) chain for barrier transit. By programming their valency across 30 external sites of an icosahedral framework, we identify a nonlinear cooperative regime in which transport, uptake, and cytotoxicity are jointly optimized. Performance is governed by the relative proportion of functional modules rather than their absolute density. At the optimal Sgc8/fluorocarbon configuration, the carrier enhances diffusion in chondroitin sulfate, improves transport across a GAG‐associated epithelial barrier model, and increases tumor‐cell killing after barrier transit. In orthotopic models, this dFDC achieves complete tumor remission at ∼1/1500 of the clinical gemcitabine dose with no recurrence over 60 days. This work introduces ligand‐ratio engineering as a general strategy for balancing orthogonal transport requirements across hierarchical biological barriers.

title: Automated Conformational Clustering Reveals Desolvation Mechanisms in a Wide‐Temperature‐Range Sodium‐Ion Electrolytes
abstract:
Temperature-driven solvation conformational shift reduces the desolvation barrier and enhances sodium-ion mobility.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The desolvation kinetics of Na +  at the electrode-electrolyte interface critically limit the wide-temperature performance of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs). Conventional radial distribution function analyses, which rely on spherical symmetry averaging, inherently fail to capture the microscopic conformational inhomogeneity that governs this process. Herein, we develop an automated conformational clustering framework that integrates unsupervised machine learning with a multiscale DFT (Density Functional Theory) MD (Molecular Dynamics) approach to resolve the temperature-dependent solvation evolution in a model carbonate-based sodium-ion electrolyte. By mapping high-dimensional trajectory data, this approach quantitatively identifies solvent-separated ion pairs (SSIP) and contact ion pairs (CIP) conformations, revealing a temperature-driven population shift from SSIP-dominated (79.9% at 233.15 K) to CIP-dominated (61.7% at 333.15 K). Density functional theory vertical energy calculations demonstrate that elevated temperatures substantially lower the SSIP-to-CIP energy penalty (from 98.3 to 47.0 kcal/mol). Consequently, the increased CIP proportion reduces the system-averaged desolvation binding energy from 72.6 to 67.6 kcal/mol, which directly accounts for the order-of-magnitude enhancement in sodium cation mobility observed in molecular dynamics simulations. This work establishes a quantitative mechanistic closed loop linking microscopic conformational transitions to macroscopic transport kinetics, providing explicit molecular design principles for advanced wide-temperature SIB electrolytes.

title: Titin‐Mimetic Phase Separation Enables a High‐Performance Dielectric Elastomer for Artificial Muscles
abstract:
Inspired by the hierarchical mechanoresponsive structure of titin, a phase-separated fluorinated polyacrylate dielectric elastomer exhibits large actuation strain (235%), ultrahigh energy density (386 J kg −1 ), and excellent self-healing capability. A biomimetic swimming robot driven by this elastomer demonstrates efficient aquatic locomotion, highlighting its potential as a high-performance artificial muscle for soft robotics.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Dielectric elastomers (DEs) are promising candidates for soft robots to achieve efficient electromechanical conversion and lightweight integration. However, conventional homogeneous DE networks face multiple inherent contradictions among compliance, robustness, and dielectric performance due to the lack of differentiated structural design at the molecular scale. Inspired by the hierarchical responsiveness of titin, we present a phase-separated fluorinated polyacrylate DE that achieves synergistic optimization of electrical and mechanical properties while exhibiting excellent self-healing capability. The proposed elastomer achieves a maximum actuation strain of 235% and an ultrahigh specific energy density of 386 J kg −1  approximately 9.65 times that of natural muscle. As such, our work demonstrates a remarkably comprehensive performance among contemporary advancements. We further demonstrate a biomimetic swimming robot that achieves efficient aquatic locomotion, highlighting the potential of our DE as a suitable candidate for high-performance artificial muscle.

title: LepR‐Lineage Cells Represent the Main Target of the Nociceptive CGRP Pathway in White Adipose Tissue Browning
abstract:
Regulation of WAT Browning and UCP1 Expression in LepR‐MSCs of Inguinal WAT by Nociceptive CGRP and Sympathetic Nervous System (SNS) Noradrenaline (NE). 








ABSTRACT
Sympathetic innervation regulates white adipose tissue (WAT) browning; however, the roles of nociceptive neurons and their associated target cells remain unknown. Here, we used single‐nucleus RNA sequencing to profile adipose populations and genetic lineage tracing to identify LepR‐lineage stromal/progenitor cells contributing to cold‐induced WAT browning. Ablation of these cells using LepR‐Cre‐inducible DTR transgenic mice resulted in a decrease in the percentage of UCP1+ cells under cold conditions. The WAT browning process is controlled by peripheral nociceptive nerve‐derived calcitonin gene‐related peptide (CGRP), which was associated with reduced WAT browning and loss of LepR‐lineage cells during intermittent fasting (IF), but not during cold exposure. Local antagonist experiments targeting the transient receptor potential cation channels TRPV1 and TRPM8 were associated with opposing changes in CGRP immunoreactivity and WAT browning. These findings support a condition‐dependent role for nociceptive CGRP signaling in WAT remodeling.

title: Localized Hydrogen Release Driven by Mg–Pd Microgalvanic Cells from 3D‐Printed Microneedles Reverses Redox Homeostasis for Psoriasis Treatment
abstract:
A 3D printing microneedle (MP-MN), loading magnesium-based micro-galvanic cells (MP), is designed for improving psoriasis. H 2  generated from MP-MN scavenges ROS and •OH, actives NRF2-KEAP1 pathway, and decreases inflammation, thereby effectively restoring the oxidative stress homeostasis of psoriatic skin and suppressing the excessive proliferation of keratinocytes in the psoriasis mouse model. MP-MN system facilitated the transdermal delivery of H 2 , providing a basis for further investigation of hydrogen-based therapy for psoriasis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Psoriasis therapy faces multiple challenges, including refractory, recurrence, and various comorbidities, attributed to its complex pathogenesis driven by aberrant keratinocyte proliferation, oxidative stress imbalance, and inflammation. These three factors form a vicious cycle, and cycle disruption holds great therapeutic potential for psoriasis. However, current therapies merely focus on symptom relief or anti-inflammatory effects alone with ignoring the essential cycle. To address the issues, a magnesium (Mg)-palladium (Pd) micro-galvanic cell (MP) with spontaneous electrochemical corrosion was constructed. MP released hydrogen (H 2 ), inhibiting keratinocyte hyperproliferation, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) and •OH, activating KEAP1‑NRF2 antioxidant signaling pathway, while generated Mg 2+  exerted anti‑inflammatory effects. Furthermore, hollow microneedles loaded with MP (MP-MN) were fabricated via 3D printing to penetrate the stratum corneum for deep H 2  delivery. In the imiquimod-induced psoriatic mouse model, MP‑MN topical treatment restored skin thickness, ameliorated oxidative stress, decreased splenic Th17/Treg ratio, and lowered both local and systemic pro‑inflammatory cytokine levels. Collectively, MP‑MN presented a comprehensive strategy for anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immune-regulatory effects in psoriasis, broadening the applications of H 2  and micro-galvanic cells in skin disorders.

title: Triplet‐Triplet Annihilation‐Based Upconversion in Rod‐Like Silica Capsules
abstract:
Anisotropic rod-like silica capsules are engineered to securely contain triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC) media. Capping the mesoporous shell with a continuous silica layer provides structural stability, preventing internal oil leakage. This physical integrity maintains stable red-to-blue upconversion emission and facilitates the electric-field-directed spatial alignment of the microcarriers within hydrogels for patterned optical applications.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Most reported triplet-triplet annihilation upconversion (TTA-UC) platforms rely on isotropic spherical particles, leaving shape-derived functions of anisotropic carriers largely unexplored. Here, we developed rod-like silica capsules (UC RCs) by loading hollow mesoporous silica rods with a PdTPBP/perylene/squalene-based TTA-UC oil and sealing the mesopores with an additional silica layer, which effectively suppressed oil leakage during ethanol exposure and dry-powder storage. In aqueous suspension, UC RCs exhibited red-to-blue TTA-UC under low-intensity excitation, with a threshold intensity of 55 mW cm − 
 2  and an upconversion quantum yield of 1.47%. To add spatial controllability to these efficient upconverting microcarriers, we harnessed their rod-like geometry and investigated their electric-field response. Coupled-dipole calculations and rotational Monte Carlo simulations showed that shape-derived polarizability anisotropy favors field-parallel orientation, with an equilibrium mean angle of approximately 2.3° under the modeled electric field. Consistent with this prediction, UC RCs were aligned in a hydrogel matrix under an AC electric field while retaining their upconversion capability. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of field-aligned anisotropic TTA-UC silica capsules embedded in a hydrogel matrix. These anisotropic microcarriers hold great promise for developing patterned luminescent materials, anti-counterfeiting platforms, and advanced photonic architectures.

title: EZpred: Improving Deep Learning‐Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs
abstract:
Schematic of the EZpred pipeline, which provides high‐confidence predictions of enzyme function using a combination of sequence alignments, structural alignments, and deep learning. EZpred can be used to provide substantial increases in the richness of protein function annotations at genomic scales.








ABSTRACT
Features extracted from sequence homologs significantly enhance the accuracy of deep learning‐based protein structure prediction. Indeed, homolog‐aware models such as AlphaFold generally produce more accurate protein structures compared to single sequence‐based methods like ESMfold. In contrast, features from sequence homologs are seldom employed for deep learning‐based prediction of the biological functions of a protein, such as Gene Ontology terms or Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. Although a small number of models also incorporate function labels from sequence homologs, they cannot utilize features extracted from homologs that lack function labels. To address this gap, we developed EZpred, which is the first deep learning model to use sequence homologs by extracting their sequence features while ignoring any function labels. Starting with the target sequence and homologs identified by MMseqs2, EZpred extracts sequence features using the ESM‐C protein language model. These features are then fed into a deep learning model to predict the EC numbers of the target protein. For test enzymes with < 30% sequence identity to any training proteins, the F1‐score of EZpred EC number prediction is at least 34% higher than state‐of‐the‐art EC number prediction models. These results demonstrate the strong positive impact of sequence homologs in deep learning‐based enzyme function prediction.

title: Interface‐Mediated Self‐Rectifying CsCuCl3 Memristors With Tunable Thresholds for Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Computing
abstract:
Interface-mediated CsCuCl 3  memristors achieve self-rectification and tunable thresholds, enabling selector-free 8 × 8 arrays with > 10 5  ON/OFF and > 10 4  rectification. Supporting dual-mode neuromorphic computing, negative thresholds preserve low-light recognition accuracy (91%), while positive thresholds enable sparsity-aware edge computing. This work advances selector-free, sparsity-aware artificial intelligence hardware systems.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 We demonstrate a simple 1R self-rectifying halide perovskite memristor with dynamically tunable thresholds for selector-free crossbar arrays and programmable T-ReLU mapping. The memristors achieve an ON/OFF ratio > 10 5  and rectification ratio > 10 4 . The switching mechanism involves two synergistic processes: bulk ion migration within CsCuCl 3  provides and sustains the low-resistance state essential for a high ON/OFF ratio, while the Ag-Cl-containing oxidized interfacial layer introduces a Schottky barrier and trap filling/release mechanism that governs the HRS to LRS switching. Systematic simulations using CNN architectures reveal a dataset-dependent threshold sensitivity: MNIST accuracy remains robust (> 98%) regardless of threshold variations, whereas CIFAR-10 accuracy drops sharply as positive thresholds increase. Based on this complexity-dependent trend, we exploited the bi-directional tunability for dual-mode applications: (i) Negative threshold operation in CNNs maintains 91.0% accuracy for low-light image recognition (comparable to the ReLU baseline); (ii) Positive threshold modulation in a customized SparseResNet-18 architecture is explored for sparsity-aware edge computing, where thresholds τ ∈ [0, 0.3] are adjusted according to simulated battery levels to control the sparsity-accuracy trade-off. Under low-battery conditions (τ = 0.3), the simulated network achieves 76.3% activation sparsity while maintaining 90.1% accuracy without retraining. This work highlights the potential of tunable activation thresholds for reconfigurable neuromorphic systems.

title: Stretchable Electronic Skins Realized by Confined In Situ Silver Patterning on Siloxane‐Modified Polyimide
abstract:
Stretchable polyimide substrates support directly patterned silver circuits for skin-mounted motion-detection demonstrations. Device-level feasibility is further explored through strain-dependent resonance measurements and a separate smartphone-assisted near-field excitation experiment with rectified DC output, illustrating the potential of the platform for deformable circuits and near-field electronics.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 The rapid development of soft robotics and embodied intelligence demands electronic skins (E-skins) that are both mechanically self-adaptive and skin-conformal. However, the rigid aromatic backbones of conventional polyimides limit stretchability and hinder conformal integration with deformable surfaces.
