Here, elastically stretchable polyimide (es-PI) films are developed by incorporating aminopropyl-terminated siloxane spacers, while a confined-patterned in situ self-metallization strategy enables direct fabrication of patterned silver circuits. By spatially confining Ag +  coordination and reduction within predefined regions, this strategy produces continuous silver nanolayers with well-defined boundaries and robust metal–polymer interfaces, preserving electrical integrity during repeated deformation. The selected es-PI-0.5 substrate exhibits an estimated nominal elongation at break of approximately 96% and a tensile strength of approximately 25 MPa, while the corresponding metallized film retains electrical continuity during tensile deformation up to 50% strain. Device-level feasibility is demonstrated through a strain-dependent inductor–capacitor (LC) resonance response measured using a network analyzer and a separate smartphone-assisted near-field excitation experiment with rectified direct-current (DC) output detected using a multimeter. This work establishes a materials–circuit integration approach for stretchable electronic skins and skin-mounted sensing demonstrations.

title: Microenvironment‐Responsive Biomimetic Hydrogels Delivering Cistanche Deserticola‐Derived Nanovesicles for Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
abstract:
An injectable, microenvironment-responsive hydrogel (HAPOCS@CDNVs) is developed for sustained delivery of  Cistanche deserticola -derived nanovesicles (CDNVs). By scavenging ROS, restoring mitochondrial function, and attenuating SASP, this platform effectively suppresses nucleus pulposus cell senescence and facilitates extracellular matrix reconstruction, offering a minimally invasive strategy for intervertebral disc degeneration.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is driven by persistent oxidative stress and tissue acidosis, accelerating nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation. While plant-derived nanovesicles (PDNVs) hold therapeutic promise, rapid clearance and mechanical leakage constrain their translation. Here, natural nanovesicles from  Cistanche deserticola  (CDNVs) were incorporated into an injectable, microenvironment-responsive hydrogel (HAPOCS@CDNVs) for localized, sustained delivery. Dynamic Schiff base and phenylboronate ester crosslinks provide biomechanical buffering, scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS), and trigger on-demand CDNV release under acidic and oxidative conditions. Mechanistically, CDNVs alleviate oxidative stress, support mitochondrial function, and inhibit NF-κB activation, thereby suppressing the senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) and preserving ECM homeostasis. In a rat IVDD model, a single intradiscal injection of HAPOCS@CDNVs sustained disc height, preserved tissue hydration, and retarded degeneration over 8 weeks. This platform provides a promising, minimally invasive strategy for disc repair.

title: A Transcriptionally Distinct Intermediate Activation State Precedes Langerhans Cell Migration From the Epidermis
abstract:
A transcriptionally distinct intermediate Langerhans cell state is identified between steady and migratory populations during skin injury. Integrated single‐cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, and intravital imaging reveal state‐specific markers and implicate complement signaling, particularly C3, in regulating Langerhans cell accumulation near wounds, providing a framework for understanding epidermal immune‐cell activation and migration.








ABSTRACT
Langerhans cells (LC) are antigen‐presenting cells that form dense epidermal networks for immune surveillance. Upon antigen uptake, LCs are activated and subsequently orchestrate immune responses by migrating into the lymphatic system. However, the regulation of transcriptional programs during activation and the behavior of LCs in vivo during this transition remain poorly understood. Therefore, this study combines single‐cell transcriptomic analysis with intravital imaging to reconstruct the activation trajectory of epidermal LCs. In particular, the study generates a high‐resolution single‐cell transcriptomic dataset comprising over 22 000 high‐quality epidermal LCs under both homeostatic and injury conditions. Notably, a distinct intermediate activated state that precedes LC migration was identified and characterized at the level of signaling pathways and transcription factors. The integration of this dataset with external datasets from homeostatic and injured skin reveals wound‐specific fibroblasts as the major source of C3, which is the central component of the complement cascade. Moreover, intravital imaging of C3‐deficient mice and pegcetacoplan treatment demonstrates that C3 contributes to LC accumulation adjacent to wound sites. Collectively, the study findings identify an activated epidermal LC population and implicate complement signaling in the regulation of LC behavior during skin injury.

title: Bacillus Licheniformis‐Induced Cognitive Decline in Mice Linking Gut Microbiota Dysbiosis, Metabolic Perturbations, and Hippocampal Neuroinflammation
abstract:
Chronic oral administration of specific probiotic strains triggers gut microbiota dysbiosis and systemic metabolic perturbations in mice. Multi-omics profiling reveals subsequent hippocampal glial remodeling and neuroinflammation, which are linked to cognitive impairment. This work highlights potential neurological risks from long-term probiotic supplementation and underscores critical strain-dependent safety considerations.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 While often considered beneficial, the long-term effects of probiotic supplementation on brain function remain underexplored. This study demonstrates that prolonged oral administration of  Bacillus licheniformis  in mice induces significant cognitive decline, as evidenced by impaired social ability and social memory in the three-chamber test. This behavioral deficit was associated with hippocampal structural abnormalities, including reduced neuronal soma size, dendritic length, and spine density. Multi-omics analyses revealed that  B. licheniformis  disrupted gut microbiota homeostasis, driving specific shifts in microbial composition and function, notably enriching nucleotide metabolism pathways. Concomitant serum metabolomic profiling identified widespread perturbations, particularly in lipid, amino acid, and nucleotide metabolism. Single-cell RNA sequencing of the hippocampus unveiled a remodeled cellular landscape, characterized by a marked increase in microglia and a decrease in oligodendrocytes. Transcriptomic analysis further indicated a shift in oligodendrocytes and astrocytes toward a reactive, pro-inflammatory state, with significant activation of neuroinflammatory (e.g., NF-κB) and neurodegenerative pathways. Our findings reveal an association between chronic  B. licheniformis  intake and cognitive impairment, suggesting a potential gut-brain-axis-mediated pathogenic cascade involving intestinal dysbiosis, systemic metabolic disturbances, and hippocampal neuroinflammation. This work highlights the potential neurological risks of prolonged probiotic use and provides a framework for evaluating microbial impacts on brain health.

title: A Celastrol–Platinum(IV) Nanoprodrug Couples Ferroptosis With Caspase‐Independent Pyroptosis to Enhance Anti‐PD‐1 Therapy in Colorectal Cancer
abstract:
CPAN integrates celastrol-driven oxidative stress with Pt(IV)-induced DNA damage to couple ferroptosis with caspase-independent pyroptosis. Celastrol disrupts the GSH/GPX4 axis and promotes lipid peroxidation, while Pt(IV)-associated PARP/PARylation signaling facilitates full-length GSDME oligomerization. The resulting immunogenic cell death enhances CD8+ T-cell responses and sensitizes colorectal tumors to anti-PD-1 therapy.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Colorectal cancer (CRC) often responds incompletely to immunotherapy because tumor cells display limited immunogenicity and are embedded in an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Here, we engineered CPAN, a hyaluronic acid-modified celastrol-platinum(IV) nanoprodrug, to sensitize tumors to programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade by linking ferroptosis with caspase-independent pyroptosis. Following tumor-oriented delivery, CPAN perturbed redox balance through peroxiredoxin 1 (PRDX1) inhibition, glutathione (GSH) depletion, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) reduction, and heme oxygenase 1 (HO-1) upregulation, which together promoted ferrous iron (Fe 2 
 + )-associated lipid peroxidation. The platinum(IV) moiety concurrently activated poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP)/PARylation signaling. These lipid reactive oxygen species (ROS)- and PARylation-dependent events drove oligomerization of full-length gasdermin E (GSDME), producing caspase-independent pyroptotic death. The resulting immunogenic cell death (ICD) was evidenced by adenosine triphosphate (ATP) release, calreticulin (CRT) exposure, high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) translocation, and increased dendritic cell (DC) maturation. In CT26 tumor-bearing mice, CPAN restrained tumor progression, promoted CD8 +  T-cell infiltration, decreased the regulatory T-cell (Treg) fraction, and enriched M1 macrophages. Anti-PD-1 treatment further amplified the antitumor effect of CPAN. These results highlight a promising nanoprodrug-based strategy for improving CRC immunotherapy by coordinated activation of ferroptosis and caspase-independent pyroptosis.

title: Boron Crosslinking Enables Anion‐Lean Solvation and Stable Interfaces for Dendrite‐Free Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract:
The boron-crosslinked gel polymer electrolyte (GPE_TMAB) enhances Li +  transport through Lewis-acidic boron centers that selectively immobilize TFSI −  anions, thereby enabling single-ion conduction and promoting dendrite-free lithium deposition. The engineered solvation structure drives the formation of an inorganic-rich, mechanically robust SEI, resulting in exceptional interfacial stability and outstanding cycling performance, establishing GPE_TMAB as a promising platform for next-generation safe all-solid-state batteries.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Achieving high-performance and safe lithium metal batteries (LMBs) requires electrolytes that simultaneously optimize solvation chemistry, interfacial stability, ionic conductivity, and mechanical robustness. Conventional gel polymer electrolytes (GPEs) often suffer from low lithium-ion transference numbers and sluggish interfacial kinetics because mobile anions and strong Li +  solvation induce concentration polarization and dendritic Li growth. Herein, we design a sp 2 -hybridized boron-crosslinked gel polymer electrolyte (GPE_TMAB) that integrates anion-lean solvation and interfacial engineering within a single platform. GPE_TMAB is constructed from a boron-containing multi-arm crosslinker (TMAB), methyl ether acrylate, and isobornyl acrylate, together with a binary ethyl methyl carbonate/fluoroethylene carbonate solvent system that balances strong coordination and facile desolvation, thereby establishing soft, Li + -dominant solvation environments. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that the boron-mediated TFSI −  trapping weakens Li +  solvation and enhanced Li +  diffusion. Accordingly, Lewis-acidic boron centers enable Li +  single-ion conduction and promote formation of a mechanically robust, inorganic-rich SEI. GPE_TMAB achieves high ionic conductivity, intrinsic non-flammability, dendrite-free Li plating/stripping for over 1200 h, and durable LFP∥Li full-cell cycling with 86% capacity retention after 800 cycles, with improved transport kinetics and stable interfacial chemistry. This work establishes a boron-enabled solvation and interfacial design strategy for high-voltage, dendrite-free, and safe all-solid-state LMBs.

title: Label‐Free Super‐Resolution Imaging Using Non‐Linear Exogenous Photon Avalanche Backlight
abstract:
Transmission avalanche backlight (TAB) microscopy turns a photon-avalanching Tm 3 
 + :LiYF 4  crystal into a nonlinear luminescent backlight. Weak attenuation by a transparent sample is amplified into strong emission modulation: image contrast increases with sample attenuation and avalanche nonlinearity ( N ), while the effective point spread function narrows as 1/√ N , enabling label-free, reconstruction-free sub-diffraction imaging with a single scanned near-infrared beam.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Optical imaging beyond the diffraction limit of light enables direct investigation of the structure, organization and functioning of sub-micrometer, highly transparent objects such as subcellular components, thin films and nano-engineered devices. However, most existing super-resolution optical techniques rely on fluorescent labels, which can alter sample properties, suffer from phototoxicity and photobleaching, and require complex instrumentation. At the same time, alternative label-free super-resolution methods remain technically complex, demanding, costly and often difficult to implement. Here we propose and experimentally demonstrate a new concept of label-free super-resolution optical imaging termed transmission avalanche backlight (TAB) microscopy. TAB microscopy exploits strong optical nonlinearities in exogenous photon-avalanche materials, which act as a far-field created, luminescent backlight forming a near-field virtual, fluorescent nano-aperture. Weak attenuation and scattering by highly transparent samples are translated into strongly amplified luminescence modulation of the avalanche backlight substrate, resulting in enhanced image contrast. Using a single-beam laser-scanning configuration, TAB microscopy achieves far-field, reconstruction-free imaging with optical resolution of approximately 180 nm. This approach provides a relatively technically simple, label-free route to sub-diffraction imaging and may complement existing techniques across biology, materials science, nanophotonics and nanoengineering.

title: Single‐Cell Map of Early Lung Adenocarcinoma Uncovers Invasion‐Associated Tertiary Lymphoid Structures
abstract:
Early thoracic lesions are already heavily infiltrated by immune cells, yet these infiltrates largely consist of bystander T lymphocytes within an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Pathological invasion is strikingly associated with the neogenesis of T/B cell‐rich TLSs that predominantly remain immature. LTβR ligand overexpression or PD‐1 blockade promotes TLS neogenesis and maturation while constraining allograft growth, suggesting a link between TLS developmental state and tumor progression in early lung adenocarcinoma.








ABSTRACT
Early lung adenocarcinoma presenting as ground‐glass nodules (GGNs) is increasingly detected in clinical practice. However, robust biomarkers reflecting progression from in situ to invasive disease are incompletely defined. Here, we integrated single‐cell RNA sequencing, T‐cell receptor repertoire profiling, whole‐slide immunohistochemistry, multiplex immunohistochemistry, and an orthotopic murine lung adenocarcinoma model to dissect the immune landscape of primary GGNs. We found that these early thoracic lesions harbored abundant infiltrates of innate and adaptive immune cells, but intratumoral T lymphocytes included putative polyclonal bystander clones embedded in an immunosuppressive microenvironment. We further observed a marked stage‐dependent increase in T and B cell‐rich tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs), dominated by immature configurations, whereas mature TLSs remained relatively infrequent. In mouse allografts, spontaneously arising TLSs were likewise underdeveloped, and LTαβ or LIGHT overexpression, as well as PD‐1 blockade, promoted TLS neogenesis and maturation, accompanied by reduced tumor growth. Collectively, our study delineates the immunologic features associated with pathological invasion, identifies a predominance of structurally immature TLS niches, and provides a rationale for further investigating the therapeutic potential of promoting TLS maturation to intercept early lung adenocarcinoma.

title: A Bioengineered Mitochondrial Respiration‐Mimetic Copper‐Based Metal‐Organic Framework Reprogramming Oxidative Phosphorylation to Enhance Tumor Cuproptosis
abstract:
A bioengineered mitochondrial respiration‐mimetic nanoplatform (TC@OMG) renews tumor mitochondrial metabolism to enhance cuproptosis. TC@OMG integrates a copper‐based metal‐organic framework co‐loaded with glucose oxidase and a lactate dehydrogenase inhibitor, and is cloaked with a hybrid membrane derived from tumor cells and plant thylakoids, enabling tumor targeting and photosynthetic oxygen generation.








ABSTRACT
Mitochondrial metabolism‐dependent cuproptosis has emerged as a promising anticancer modality, yet its efficacy is constrained by the hypoxic and glycolysis‐dominant tumor microenvironment that suppresses oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS). Strategies that simultaneously overcome hypoxia and mitochondrial metabolic resistance remain underexplored. Herein, we report a bioengineered mitochondrial respiration‐mimetic nanoplatform (TC@OMG) that renews tumor mitochondrial metabolism to enhance cuproptosis. TC@OMG integrates a copper‐based metal‐organic framework co‐loaded with glucose oxidase and a lactate dehydrogenase inhibitor, and is cloaked with a hybrid membrane derived from tumor cells and plant thylakoids, enabling tumor targeting and photosynthetic oxygen generation. Mechanistically, photo‐triggered TC@OMG couples hypoxia alleviation with glycolysis inhibition to enforce a metabolic shift toward mitochondrial OXPHOS, thereby sensitizing tumor cells to cuproptosis. Concurrently, its microenvironment‐responsive copper release and glutathione depletion disrupt mitochondrial Fe‐S cluster homeostasis and induce aggregation of lipoylated proteins, ultimately promoting cuproptotic cell death. In vivo, photo‐triggered TC@OMG achieves efficient tumor targeting, hypoxia relieving, and tumor inhibiting effects across multiple melanoma models, including subcutaneous, metastatic, and intraocular tumors. Collectively, this work bioengineered a respiration‐mimetic nanotherapeutic strategy that integrates mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming with copper‐dependent cell death, providing a generalizable strategy for overcoming mitochondrial metabolic resistance in cancer therapy.

title: ALDH2 Deficiency Promotes Mitochondrial Oxidative Stress and Adverse Limb Outcomes via VDAC–HSP60 Signaling
abstract:
ALDH2 deficiency promotes 4‐HNE accumulation, resulting in covalent modification of HSP60, disruption of its oligomeric assembly, and VDAC1‐dependent release of HSP60 from mitochondria to the cytosol. Pharmacological activation of ALDH2 preserves HSP60 proteostasis and mitochondrial integrity, whereas the clinical association between the ALDH2 rs671 polymorphism and adverse limb outcomes supports the translational significance of this pathway.








ABSTRACT
The ALDH2 rs671 variant, which is frequent in East Asian populations, markedly reduces mitochondrial aldehyde‐detoxifying capacity and thereby increases vulnerability to reactive aldehydes, including 4‐hydroxynonenal (4‐HNE), during ischemic stress. We show that impaired ALDH2 activity perturbs endothelial mitochondrial proteostasis through an ALDH2–4‐HNE–HSP60–VDAC1 pathway. In Aldh2 knock‐in mice and endothelial cells exposed to oxygen–glucose deprivation, ALDH2 deficiency was accompanied by 4‐HNE accumulation, mitochondrial DNA injury, loss of membrane potential, increased mitochondrial ROS, mitochondrial fragmentation, and apoptosis. Analysis of transcriptomic data highlighted HSP60 (HSPD1) as a downstream candidate. LC–MS/MS, covalent docking, co‐immunoprecipitation, and proximity ligation analyses supported 4‐HNE modification of HSP60, while native electrophoresis indicated disruption of higher‐order HSP60 assembly. HSP60 redistribution to the cytosol was predominantly dependent on VDAC1. Activating ALDH2 with AD‐5591, or suppressing VDAC1 genetically or pharmacologically, preserved HSP60 homeostasis, mitochondrial integrity, and endothelial function. In a prospective cohort of 227 patients with peripheral artery disease, the rs671 variant was associated with a higher incidence of major adverse limb events. These data position HSP60 proteostasis downstream of ALDH2‐dependent aldehyde detoxification and identify the ALDH2–4‐HNE–HSP60–VDAC1 pathway as a potential therapeutic target in ischemic vascular disease.

title: Hierarchical Chemical Fluctuations Promote Exceptional Strength–Ductility–Modulus Synergy in Biomedical BCC Multi‐Principal‐Element Alloys
abstract:
Hierarchical chemical fluctuations are engineered in a biomedical BCC Ti 35 Zr 35 Nb 10 Hf 10 Ta 5 Sn 5  multi-principal-element alloy through contrasting Sn–element interactions. The resulting multiscale chemical–strain heterogeneity promotes dislocation interactions and kink-band-mediated partitioned plasticity, enabling the as-cast alloy to achieve a yield strength of 1.14 GPa, a tensile elongation of 20.3%, and a Young's modulus of 52.8 GPa.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Simultaneously achieving high strength, large tensile ductility, and low Young's modulus remains a central challenge in body-centered-cubic (BCC) multi-principal-element alloys (MPEAs) to be used as load-bearing biomedical materials. Here, we show a strategy of combining thermodynamic considerations and valence electron theory to address this issue. By means of the contrasting interactions of Sn with group-IV and group-V elements, hierarchical chemical fluctuations (CFs) spanning from <1 to ∼50 nm and corresponding alternating strain fields were introduced in the optimized Ti 35 Zr 35 Nb 10 Hf 10 Ta 5 Sn 5  alloy, favoring dislocation pinning, pile-up, and junction formation, thereby facilitating kink band formation early during uniform deformation and subsequent kink-band-mediated plasticity. Consequently, the as-cast alloy achieves a yield strength of ∼1.14 GPa, tensile elongation of 20.3%, and Young's modulus of 52.8 GPa, together with improved cytocompatibility relative to the Sn-free parent alloy. Kink bands represent a special plastic deformation mode, as their formation can accommodate localized strains, alleviate stress concentration, and avoid premature fracture. This work not only provides a novel pathway for realizing excellent strength–ductility–modulus synergy in BCC MPEAs, but also brings insight into the action of kink bands in partitioning plastic deformation that has not been well understood before.

title: SensEnhance: A Genetic Circuit for Converting Endogenous Mammalian Gene Signals Into High‐Dynamic‐Range Genetic Readouts
abstract:
Here, we present SensEnhance, a modular genetic circuit that converts leaky, low‐dynamic‐range promoter signals into tightly controlled, high‐dynamic‐range outputs. Applied to mechanosensing and IL‐6‐responsive promoters, SensEnhance increases fold changes from 2.6‐ and 2.5‐fold in promoter‐only configurations to over 20‐ and 14‐fold, respectively. SensEnhance may serve as a high‐performance genetic analog of a threshold amplifier for biosensing.








ABSTRACT
Integrating synthetic gene circuits with endogenous mammalian gene expression programs enables genetic readouts of physiologically relevant cellular states. However, the performance of these readouts is often constrained by sensing promoters with low maximal output, modest fold changes, and high basal activity. Here, we use mathematical modeling and analysis to devise SensEnhance, a generalizable genetic circuit architecture that converts leaky, low‐dynamic‐range promoter signals into tightly controlled, high‐dynamic‐range outputs. SensEnhance combines sequestration‐mediated suppression below a tunable response threshold with feedback‐supported amplification above it. We implement SensEnhance through split intein‐mediated protein trans‐splicing and experimentally validate its predicted input–output behavior and threshold tunability. We apply SensEnhance to a YAP/TAZ‐responsive mechanosensing promoter and stably integrate the circuit into NIH/3T3 fibroblasts, increasing output fold change between soft and stiff tissue‐like hydrogels from 2.6‐fold in the promoter‐only configuration to over 20‐fold using SensEnhance. When coupled to a STAT3‐responsive promoter showing a 2.5‐fold change in response to IL‐6, SensEnhance increases this fold change to 14‐fold, improving cytokine sensing and supporting its generic applicability across signaling pathways. These results establish SensEnhance as a modular strategy for improving the dynamic range and tunability of mammalian genetic biosensors.

title: Distinction Between Capping Agent and Self‐trapped Exciton in Emission Spectra
abstract: Advanced Science, EarlyView.

title: Cardiac Endothelial Enhancer RNA Tek‐e1 Restores Microvascular Homeostasis After Myocardial Infarction
abstract:
Hypoxia-induced KDM5A downregulation establishes a distinct endothelial repair programme, increasing H3K4me3 at the  Tek  promoter and intronic enhancer, enabling ISL1 to coordinately activate  Tek  transcription and induce enhancer-RNA Tek-e1. This cis-regulatory RNA is essential for additional  Tek /TIE2 induction through R-loop formation and reinforced enhancer–promoter communication. VCAM-1-targeted LNP@Tek-e1 further amplifies this response, restoring microvascular homeostasis and limiting adverse ventricular remodelling.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Microvascular repair after myocardial infarction involves both angiogenesis and re-establishment of vascular homeostasis. Here, we identify a distinct transcriptionally active state in hypoxic border-zone endothelial cells driven by KDM5A downregulation and biased towards endothelial stabilization and microvascular homeostatic repair. KDM5A loss increases H3K4me3 enrichment at the  Tek  promoter and an intronic enhancer, enabling ISL1 to coordinately activate transcription of  Tek  and the enhancer RNA Tek-e1. Tek-e1 acts as an essential cis-regulatory RNA that further amplifies  Tek /TIE2 expression through R-loop formation and reinforced enhancer–promoter communication, thereby converting  Kdm5a -loss-induced epigenetic activation into persistent transcriptional reinforcement. In mice with endothelial-specific deletion of  Kdm5a , this mechanism promotes the maturation and stabilization of nascent-microvascular networks after myocardial infarction. In a clinical cohort, serum soluble TIE2 independently stratified collateral status in 402 patients with chronic total occlusion. To further enable translation, we developed LNP@Tek-e1 modified with a VCAM-1-targeting peptide, combining VCAM-1-directed endothelial enrichment with enhancer-dependent Tek-e1 activity to selectively enhance  Tek /TIE2 expression in border-zone endothelium, improving microvascular function and limiting adverse left ventricular remodelling. Together, these findings define KDM5A downregulation as a hypoxia-triggered endothelial repair programme and establish Tek-e1 as an essential cis-regulatory amplifier that can be delivered in vivo to restore post-infarction microvascular homeostasis.

title: The Impact of Cobalt Substitution on the Electrochemical Properties of Cubic Li6.6La3Zr1.6Ta0.4O12 Solid Electrolyte for All‐Solid‐State Li‐Ion Batteries
abstract:
Cobalt is incorporated more readily into garnet Li 6.6 La 3 Z r1.6 Ta 0.4 O 12  when sintered in argon than in air. Under argon, Co in the garnet lattice lowers the total conductivity three- to fourfold; in air, Co segregates as LiCoO 2  and raises the electronic conductivity about 100-fold instead. These findings may explain why LiCoO 2 /Li 6.6 La 3 Z r1.6 Ta 0.4 O 12  cathodes processed under reducing conditions require a post-annealing in air.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Garnet-type Li 7 La 3 Zr 2 O 12  (LLZO) is a promising solid electrolyte for all-solid-state lithium batteries (SSLB). The diffusion of cobalt (Co) into LLZO in combination with LiCoO 2  (LCO) as the active cathode material (CAM) is widely reported in FAST/SPS-sintered LCO/LLZO composite cathodes, sintered under an argon (Ar) atmosphere, and associated with degradation. In contrast, air-sintered LCO/LLZO composite cathodes often demonstrate greater cycle stability, indicating an impact of the processing atmosphere. To address this issue, this study systematically investigates the effect of Co substitution in Li 6.6 La 3 Zr 1.6 Ta 0.4 O 12  (LLZTO) sintered under both atmospheres. The structural, microstructural, and electrochemical properties of the sintered materials were characterized using XRD, SEM-EDS, Raman spectroscopy, and EIS. DFT calculations were further performed to investigate the thermodynamic stability of Co substitution at different cation sites within the LLZO structure. Our results demonstrate that Co incorporation into the LLZTO lattice is significantly greater under Ar, with Co 2+  occupying Li-positions according to DFT, and total conductivity is reduced. When sintered in air, most of the Co segregated as a secondary phase of LCO and electronic conductivity is increased. These results identify one possible contribution to the degradation of LCO/LLZTO composite cathodes processed under reducing conditions and suggest that post-annealing in air may reverse it.

title: Dual Suppression of Oxidative Stress and JAK/STAT3 Signaling Attenuates Inflammation‐Driven Corneal Neovascularization
abstract:
Corneal neovascularization is sustained by oxidative stress and inflammatory STAT3 signaling. A macrophage membrane‐cloaked nanozyme, Sta@MSR, combines ruthenium‐mediated ROS scavenging with Stattic‐mediated STAT3 inhibition. Delivered as eye drops, Sta@MSR enhances ocular retention and corneal penetration, reduces inflammatory and angiogenic responses, and restores corneal transparency, offering a coordinated topical strategy for treating inflammation‐driven corneal neovascularization.








ABSTRACT
Corneal neovascularization (CoNV) is a vision‐threatening disorder driven by persistent oxidative stress and inflammation, yet effective therapies targeting these interconnected pathological processes remain limited. Here, we identify enhanced signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) phosphorylation and inflammatory signaling in corneal samples from patients with CoNV, as well as reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and macrophage infiltration were observed in an alkali burn‐induced mouse model. To address these pathological features, we developed Sta@MSR, a macrophage membrane‐cloaked biomimetic nanozyme integrating ruthenium‐mediated ROS scavenging with Stattic‐mediated STAT3 inhibition. Mechanistically, Sta@MSR attenuated oxidative stress and STAT3‐associated inflammatory signaling, thereby suppressing endothelial angiogenic activity and pathological neovascularization. Furthermore, macrophage membrane cloaking enhanced ocular retention and corneal penetration, facilitating topical delivery. Importantly, Sta@MSR markedly reduced pathological neovascularization and inflammatory injury, restored corneal transparency, and exhibited favorable ocular and systemic biocompatibility. Collectively, this work highlights coordinated regulation of oxidative stress and STAT3 signaling as a promising therapeutic strategy for inflammation‐driven CoNV.

title: Energy Matching in NV Spin‐Phonon Interaction Enabling High‐Temperature Quantum Sensing via Lifetime Readout
abstract:
Quantum sensing at high temperatures is challenging for the NV center. We overcome this by revealing an energy matching within NV spin-phonon interactions. This match preserves high sensitivity upon heating. By reading out the NV excited state lifetime, we demonstrate a shot-noise-limited sensitivity of 8.3 µK Hz − 
 1 
 / 
 2  at 490 K, paving the way for robust quantum sensing under extreme conditions.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 High-temperature quantum sensing with NV centers has long been hindered by the spin contrast degradation from the thermally accelerated intersystem crossing (ISC) and the thermally induced fluorescence instability in the conventional intensity-based readout. Here, we systematically investigate the NV spin-phonon interaction in the ISC transition and the zero-field splitting (ZFS) shift, which are two key aspects governing NV high-temperature sensing performance. We report an energy matching between their characteristic phonon modes, which enables the ISC-induced sensitivity degradation to be effectively compensated by the steepened slope of the ZFS shift, thereby preserving a high sensitivity even at high temperatures. This effect is particularly evident in the lifetime-based optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) measurements, as the lifetime readout remains robust against thermally induced fluorescence instability at high temperatures. We reach a shot-noise-limited temperature sensitivity of 8.3 µK Hz −1/2  at 490 K in the lifetime-based continuous-wave ODMR scheme. Our work has opened up opportunities for highly sensitive NV quantum sensors under extreme conditions.

title: Space‐Charge‐Driven Nonlinear Charge Transport in Silicon Reconfigurable Nonlinear‐Processing Units
authors: Wilfred G. van der van der Wiel
abstract:
Many approaches to AI hardware focus on accelerating linear operations, yet nonlinearity underpins computational expressivity. Reconfigurable nonlinear‐processing units (RNPUs) are promising computational primitives that provide nonlinear transformations directly in hardware. Using electrical measurements and semiconductor simulations, we show that their room‐temperature behavior is governed by space‐charge effects, establishing the operating principle of silicon RNPUs and design rules for CMOS‐compatible implementations.








ABSTRACT
Reconfigurable nonlinear‐processing units (RNPUs) are multi‐terminal electronic devices that act as computational primitives, exploiting intrinsic nonlinear charge transport combined with electrostatic tunability. Silicon‐based realizations provide a scalable and technologically relevant platform toward unconventional computing hardware, yet the physical origin of their room‐temperature nonlinearity has remained unresolved. Here, we demonstrate room‐temperature operation in both boron‐ and arsenic‐doped silicon RNPUs and show, using temperature‐ and length‐dependent measurements supported by TCAD simulations, that charge transport is governed by space‐charge effects. Interface trap states strongly suppress the equilibrium carrier density, while the functional nonlinearity arises from the competition between injected carriers and ionized dopants. The resulting transport evolves from Ohmic to strongly nonlinear and space‐charge‐limited current regimes, as evidenced by voltage and length scaling. The opposite‐polarity background doping is shown to control the onset and strength of the nonlinearity, producing behavior beyond the quadratic dependence of the classical Mott–Gurney law. Agreement between experiment and simulation supports that the spatial distribution of injected carriers and fixed charge governs the electric‐field profile and device response. These results establish a space‐charge‐based framework for RNPUs that does not require disorder or hopping transport, and provide design guidelines for scalable, CMOS‐compatible nonlinear computing hardware.

title: Hidden Giant Third‐Order Nonlinear Circular Dichroism in Chiral Two‐Dimensional Halide Perovskite
abstract:
We demonstrate hidden giant third-harmonic generation circular dichroism (THG-CD) in chiral two-dimensional halide perovskite. Although conventional polarization-integrated THG measurement shows almost no chiral optical response, polarization-resolved measurement reveals a hidden capability for nearly perfect discrimination of incident circularly polarized light helicity. This finding opens new opportunities for polarization encoded chiral optical application such as encryption and anti-counterfeiting system.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Chiral nonlinear optical (NLO) responses provide unique opportunities for manipulating circularly polarized light (CPL) and are attracting increasing interest for advanced photonic and optoelectronic technologies. However, investigations of chiral nonlinear optical materials have largely focused on second-order processes, while the role of chirality in third-order NLO responses, particularly in third-harmonic generation (THG), remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate hidden giant THG circular dichroism (THG-CD) in the chiral two-dimensional halide perovskite (R-MBACl) 2 PbI 4  through polarization-resolved THG measurements, and further examine the THG-CD in several structurally different Pb-based two-dimensional perovskites. Under excitonic resonant conditions, incident right- and left-handed CPL generates nearly orthogonally polarized THG emission, resulting in a reversal of the THG-CD response between the two orthogonal output polarization components. Consequently, nearly perfect CPL discrimination is achieved under polarization-resolved detection, with dissymmetry factors exceeding | g 
 
    THG  −  CD 
 | = 1.9. In contrast, these chiral NLO responses are largely canceled in conventional polarization-integrated THG measurements, resulting in apparently weak circular dichroism and masking the existence of giant chiral optical responses. These unique optical responses establish a versatile platform for polarization-encoded photonic technologies, including circularly polarized light detection, optical information encryption, and anti-counterfeiting systems operating at technologically relevant telecommunication wavelengths.

title: TIPIN Couples Epigenetic Rewiring to EGFR Stabilization and Lenvatinib Resistance in Liver Cancer
abstract:
DNA hypomethylation elevates TIPIN expression in liver cancer. TIPIN competes with E3 ligase c-Cbl for the EGFR intracellular domain, inhibiting EGFR ubiquitination and lysosomal degradation to sustain oncogenic EGFR- ERK signaling. High TIPIN confers lenvatinib resistance, while TIPIN depletion restores drug sensitivity in liver cancer.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
  Aims : Liver cancer is an aggressive tumor marked by substantial morbidity and mortality. Timeless-interacting protein (TIPIN) is dysregulated in multiple cancers, but its epigenetic regulation, biological function, and downstream pathways in liver cancer remain poorly defined. This study sought to explore TIPIN's function in liver cancer tumorigenesis, metastasis, and lenvatinib resistance. 
  Methods : We analyzed TCGA data and 94 paired clinical samples. DNA methylation sequencing, whole-body TIPIN knockout mouse hydrodynamic injection models, RNA-seq, immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry, co-immunoprecipitation, protein stability and ubiquitination assays, and patient‑derived xenograft and patient‑derived organoid models were used. 
  Results : TIPIN was upregulated by DNA hypomethylation in liver cancer and associated with poor prognosis. TIPIN promoted liver cancer initiation and progression in vivo. Mechanistically, TIPIN binds Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) and competes with E3 ligase c‑Cbl for the Tyr1045-containing interface, thereby repressing c‑Cbl-mediated EGFR ubiquitination and degradation and activating downstream ERK1/2 signaling to facilitate tumor proliferation and metastasis. TIPIN depletion accelerates EGFR turnover and sensitizes liver cancer cells to lenvatinib. 
  Conclusions : TIPIN stabilizes EGFR via competitive binding to the Tyr1045 interface, restricting its ubiquitin-dependent degradation to drive liver cancer progression and lenvatinib resistance. Targeting the TIPIN–EGFR axis could be an effective therapy for liver cancer.

title: Synthesis Route‐Controlled Atomic Ordering Optimizes Thermoelectric Transport in Bi2SbSe3
abstract:
Atomic ordering modulation enhancing the thermoelectric performance of Bi 2 SbSe 3 
 . The solid-state synthesis route redistributes Sb atoms between the Bi 2 Se 3  quintuple layers and the Bi bilayers in the BiSe structure, resulting in a more disordered Bi 2 SbSe 3  than the one-pot synthesized counterpart. Reduced atomic ordering decreased conduction band degeneracy and intensified phonon scattering, thereby optimizing electron and phonon transport.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Thermoelectrics have leveraged band and phonon engineering to optimize performance, typically realized through chemical composition control via one-pot doping or alloying. However, for compounds with complex atomic sites, the thermodynamic drive of conventional one-pot synthesis generally favors a thermodynamically preferred atomic occupation, thereby limiting atomic ordering control and obscuring its influence on thermoelectric transport. Herein, we constructed a synthetic pathway for composition-invariant band and phonon engineering via atomic ordering control in one-third Sb-alloyed BiSe (Bi 2 SbSe 3 ), a compound with multiple crystallographically distinct cation sites. Using BiSbSe 3  and Bi powders as precursors, we synthesized more disordered Bi 2 SbSe 3  than the one-pot synthesized counterpart, achieved by redistributing Sb atoms between the Bi 2 Se 3  quintuple layers and the Bi bilayers in the BiSe structure. Reduced atomic ordering suppresses the higher-lying conduction band contribution, lowering effective mass and enhancing carrier mobility, while simultaneously triggering lattice structure, slowing phonon velocities, and reducing lattice thermal conductivity. Finally, decreased atomic ordering enhances the  ZT  value of Bi 2 SbSe 3  by ∼15% to ∼0.61 at 423 K, with an energy conversion efficiency of ∼4.3% under a temperature difference of ∼323 K. These results reveal that synthesis-controlled atomic ordering is an effective strategy for enhancing thermoelectric performance in structurally complex materials.

title: A Citrulline‐Functionalized Patch Coordinates Macrophage NRF2 Signaling and Arginine Metabolism for Tendon‐to‐Bone Repair
abstract:
A locally implanted patch combines citrulline-functionalized carbon dots, a thioketal-containing membrane coating from tendon-derived stem cells, and aligned core–shell fibers. In macrophages, the patch reduces inflammatory markers and enhances antioxidant signaling through nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2); in rats and rabbits, it improves tendon-to-bone repair.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Structural retear remains common after rotator cuff repair. Persistent inflammation and metabolic dysfunction at the enthesis may impair healing, yet current augmentations rarely address this immunometabolic state. Exploratory single-cell profiling shows a higher proportion of M1-like cells among recovered macrophages in injured supraspinatus than in non-injured semitendinosus specimens (three donors per group). Metabolomics of polarized macrophages identifies glutathione redox imbalance and reduced arginine and proline abundance in the M1 state, supporting redox regulation and arginine metabolism as complementary targets. In ACGQD@pPLG, citrulline-functionalized, glutathione-derived carbon dots are encapsulated in an H 2 O 2 -responsive membrane coating from ultraviolet-treated tendon-derived stem cells and embedded in aligned core–shell electrospun fibers. In macrophages, the patch activates nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) signaling and increases argininosuccinate synthetase 1 (ASS1) expression and arginine-associated metabolite abundance. ASS1 knockdown attenuates CD206 induction, whereas NRF2 knockdown reduces HO-1 and NQO1 induction. In rats, the patch improves enthesis collagen organization and increases ultimate stress, stiffness, and load to failure to 1.6–2.5 times repair-only values at 8 weeks. Rabbit enthesis histology also improves at 10 weeks. These results support coordinated modulation of macrophage redox signaling and arginine metabolism as a local strategy for tendon-to-bone repair.

title: Bioorthogonal Click‐to‐Disassemble Phthalocyanine Nanoassemblies for Precise Chemo‐Photodynamic Therapy against Hypoxic Tumors
abstract:
A bioorthogonal “click‐to‐disassemble” strategy enables precise activation of self‐assembled phthalocyanine nanoassemblies for chemo‐photodynamic therapy. EGFR‐targeted activator triggers IEDDA‐mediated disruption of the quenched assemblies, restoring fluorescence and ROS generation while releasing tirapazamine. PDT‐induced oxygen depletion further activates tirapazamine, converting tumor hypoxia into a therapeutic advantage and enhancing antitumor efficacy.








ABSTRACT
Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers precise spatiotemporal control over cancer treatment but remains hampered by nonspecific photosensitizer activation, oxygen dependence, and some other limitations. Herein, we report a bioorthogonal “click‐to‐disassemble” strategy that enables tumor‐selective activation of self‐assembled phthalocyanine nanoassemblies for chemo‐photodynamic therapy against hypoxic tumors. An amphiphilic zinc(II) phthalocyanine bearing three triethylene glycol chains and a tetrazine‐functionalized substituent spontaneously self‐assembles into photodynamically silent nanoparticles through aggregation‐induced quenching while simultaneously encapsulating the hypoxia‐activated prodrug tirapazamine (TPZ). A bicyclo[6.1.0]non‐4‐yne (BCN) activator installed with an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)‐targeting peptide through a cathepsin B‐cleavable linker selectively delivers the bioorthogonal trigger to EGFR‐overexpressing cancer cells. Intracellular cleavage of the linker releases a small hydrophilic BCN moiety, which reacts rapidly with the tetrazine unit through an inverse electron‐demand Diels–Alder reaction, converting the amphiphilic photosensitizer into a hydrophilic product that disrupts the nanoassemblies. This process simultaneously restores photodynamic activity and releases TPZ, which is activated by PDT‐enhanced tumor hypoxia to achieve cooperative chemotherapy. The bioorthogonally triggered activation minimizes off‐target phototoxicity while markedly enhancing tumor‐selective therapeutic efficacy in vitro and in vivo. This work establishes bioorthogonal disassembly as a general strategy for spatiotemporal activation of self‐assembled therapeutic nanomaterials and expands the toolbox of precision photomedicine.

title: Beyond the Debye Temperature: A Unified Microscopic Framework for Designing Thermally Stable Red‐Emitting Phosphors
abstract:
Local symmetry engineering in noncentrosymmetric Na 3 EuGe 3 O 9  generates enhanced Eu 3+  local dipoles, enabling efficient light–matter interactions, high quantum efficiency, and exceptional thermal stability. A unified microscopic framework reveals the cooperative suppression of multiple thermal-quenching pathways, resulting in robust red emission in high-performance UV-driven color-converting devices and complex 3D-printed photonic architectures.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Symmetry-breaking luminescent materials enhance light–matter interactions and electric-dipole transitions, yet the links between local symmetry, dipole modulation, and thermal quenching remain elusive. Two new noncentrosymmetric Eu 3+ -activated oxide phosphors, Na 3 EuSi 3 O 9  (NESO) and Na 3 EuGe 3 O 9  (NEGO), are reported and serve to establish a unified microscopic framework that correlates local symmetry, dipole modulation, and thermal quenching behavior with luminescence performance. Despite sharing the nonpolar P2 1 2 1 2 1  structure, Ge substitution strengthens EuO 6  bonding, enhancing local dipoles and light–matter interactions. Consequently, NEGO exhibits a photoluminescence quantum yield of 88%, retains 95% of its emission after three days in water immersion, and retains 91% at 200°C, outperforming commercial K 2 SiF 6 :Mn 4+  and CaAlSiN 3 :Eu 2+  phosphors. Combined spectroscopy and DFT reveal that NESO has a stiffer lattice, while NEGO exhibits lower phonon energies, stronger Eu─O bonding, and greater Eu-centered structural and electronic stability. These findings identify local activator response, rather than bulk lattice rigidity alone, as a key descriptor of thermal robustness. Integrating local symmetry engineering with microscopic insights into thermal quenching provides a design principle for high-performance rare-earth phosphors, advancing color conversion, 3D-printed photonic devices, and solid-state lighting.

title: Fully Integrated Wearable Ultrasound System for Continuous Promotion of Wound Healing
abstract:
A wearable ultrasound system integrating a drug‐loaded patch and a miniaturized driving circuit is presented to achieve noninvasive, on‐demand stimulation, enabling programmable antibacterial activity, inflammation modulation, and accelerated wound closure through enhanced cell migration and collagen remodeling. It introduces a novel strategy for chronic wound management and shows great significance in advancing wearable medical devices in therapeutic applications.








ABSTRACT
Chronic wounds pose a significant global health burden due to their recalcitrance, high recurrence, and infection risks. Traditional treatments often lack consistent efficacy, multifunctionality, and dynamic adaptability to wound healing stages, prolonging patient distress and worsening outcomes. Here, we introduce an innovative intelligent Wearable Ultrasound System (iWUS) that seamlessly integrates a highly miniaturized ultrasound driving circuit, a drug‐loaded ultrasound patch for precisely controlled release of the antibacterial agent polyhexamethylene biguanide (PHMB), and a terminal for intuitive remote control, enabling noninvasive, on‐demand ultrasound stimulation to simultaneously promote tissue regeneration and combat infection. The iWUS combines biocompatibility, flexibility, and conformability for intelligent chronic wound management. It introduces an on‐demand dynamic therapy adapted to the wound microenvironment. In vitro assays showed sustained antibacterial action and enhanced cell migration. In vivo validation in a rat full‐thickness wound model demonstrated programmable bacterial inhibition, inflammation modulation, and improved collagen remodeling, significantly accelerating wound closure and promoting structural and functional skin regeneration. RNA sequencing analysis revealed that iWUS treatment upregulated pro‐healing genes (e.g., Bmp2, Egfr, Vegfd) while downregulating inflammatory pathways (e.g., NF‐κB, Tnf), elucidating its molecular mechanism in promoting tissue repair and resolving inflammation. The work paves the way for next‐generation wearable medical devices.

title: Development‐Informed Microsphere Assemblies Enable Spatiotemporally Programmed Bone–Vascular Organoid‐Like Constructs for Large Bone Defect Repair
abstract:
Single-cell-guided prioritization of BMP4 and VEGFA is combined with temporally programmed BMSCs and a Matrigel-free GelMA/PEO/bioactive-glass assembled-microsphere matrix to generate bone–vascular organoid-like constructs. The platform coordinates osteogenic differentiation, endothelial activation, vascular-like microchannel formation, and vascularized bone regeneration through temporally programmed BMP4 and VEGFA overexpression, providing a development-informed strategy for large bone defect repair.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Large segmental bone defects are difficult to repair because endogenous stem-cell activation, vascular ingrowth, and osteogenic maturation are insufficient to rebuild organized bone tissue. Bone organoids offer a promising regenerative strategy, but current systems are limited by Matrigel dependence, poor vascularization, low post-implantation survival, and inadequate reconstruction of hierarchical bone microarchitecture. Here, we report a development-informed, Matrigel-free bone–vascular organoid-like platform that integrates single-cell-guided gene programming with an osteoinductive and vascular-permissive microsphere matrix. Single-cell analysis identified  BMP4  and  VEGFA  as key genes linking osteogenic commitment with vascular morphogenesis. Engineered BMSCs were used to sequentially generate osteoinductive bone organoid-like constructs(OLCs) and bone–vascular OLCs with coordinated osteogenic and angiogenic activity. Microfluidic GelMA/PEO/bioactive glass(BG) microsphere clusters provided adhesive, mineralization-promoting, and space-making cues for cell migration, matrix deposition, and endothelial invasion. Within seven days, the OLCs developed mineralized matrix, vascular-like sprouting, and early vascular-like microchannels. After implantation into rabbit femoral defects, they enhanced vascularized bone formation, defect bridging, and trabecular remodeling. This work demonstrates the power of development-informed, Matrigel-free bone–vascular OLCs in accelerating vascularized bone regeneration for large segmental bone defect repair.

title: Coupling Fast Zn2+ Kinetics With V–O Framework Stabilization via Nitrogen‐Rich Interfacial Engineering of Spinel ZnV2O4
abstract:
Graphitic carbon nitride acts as a nitrogen-rich interfacial regulator for spinel ZnV 2 O 4  cathodes in aqueous zinc-ion batteries. Polar N sites promote interfacial Zn 2+  adsorption, migration, and charge transfer, while mitigating local framework distortion and reinforcing V─O bonding. This dual role couples fast surface-dominated Zn 2+  storage kinetics with reversible V 5+ /V 4+  redox, enabling durable, high-rate vanadate cathodes.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) offer intrinsic safety and cost advantages, yet spinel zinc vanadate cathodes remain limited by sluggish interfacial Zn 2+  storage kinetics, polarization, and structural degradation. Herein, graphitic carbon nitride (GCN) is employed as a nitrogen-rich interfacial regulator (NIR) to construct NIR-integrated spinel ZnV 2 O 4  (ZVO) cathodes (GZVO) through ultrasonication-assisted physical integration. The GCN-derived NIR provides polar N sites and regulated interfacial association with ZVO, promoting interfacial Zn 2+  adsorption/migration and charge transfer while mitigating local framework distortion. The optimized GZVO-7 wt.% cathode delivers 405 mAh g −1  after 150 cycles at 0.5 A g −1 , retains 258.93 mAh g −1  at 10 A g −1 , and maintains 218.24 mAh g −1  after 3000 cycles at 5 A g −1 . Cyclic voltammetry (CV), in situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy–distribution of relaxation times (EIS-DRT), and galvanostatic intermittent titration technique (GITT) reveal enhanced pseudocapacitive contribution, reduced polarization, and reversible Zn 2+  storage. Ex situ x-ray diffraction (XRD) and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) reveal persistence and partial recovery of ZVO-derived crystalline domains together with surface V 5+ /V 4+  redox evolution, oxygen-environment modulation, and N-site-mediated Zn 2+  interfacial regulation. Density functional theory (DFT) verifies favorable surface Zn-removal energetics and reinforced V─O bonding. This work establishes NIR as an effective strategy for durable, high-rate vanadate cathodes in AZIBs.

title: Rethinking Cochlear Implants: The Need for Precise Temporal Coding
authors: Nicole Rosskothen‐Kuhl, , Jan W. H. Schnupp
abstract:
Spatial hearing relies on sensitivity to interaural temporal cues, but this sensitivity is often poorly developed in patients with cochlear implants, particularly those with early‐onset hearing loss. Rats with cochlear implants, however, demonstrate excellent temporal sensitivity, suggesting that this limitation is not inevitable. Preserving temporal information in the pulse timing of cochlear implant stimulation could improve spatial hearing.








ABSTRACT
Hearing relies heavily on the encoding of rapid temporal patterns, yet contemporary cochlear implants (CIs) largely neglect precise temporal coding in favor of strategies that prioritize envelope information and minimize channel interactions. Here, we review the physiology of temporal coding in normal hearing, the limitations of current CI strategies, and emerging evidence that better temporal coding could substantially improve outcomes. Contemporary CIs face three major limitations: poor intensity coding, coarse place coding with only a modest number of resolvable frequency channels, and critically, the absence of precise pulse timing codes to support pitch perception and binaural hearing. Human bilateral CI patients generally show much worse interaural time difference (ITD) sensitivity than normally hearing individuals. However, rats fitted with bilateral CIs are no less sensitive to ITD than normally hearing rats or humans. These animals rely heavily and specifically on pulse timing cues for binaural hearing, with time‐intensity trading ratios around 20 µs/dB. We argue that prolonged exposure to random or misleading pulse timing from clinical processors may cause maladaptive suppression of innate ITD sensitivity. Developing novel coding strategies that exploit the auditory system's remarkable sensitivity to precise temporal patterns represents a promising but challenging path toward truly rich prosthetic hearing.

title: Activating Hidden Magnons With Anomalous Rotational Symmetry
abstract:
Unlocking high‐frequency magnons hidden by symmetry constraints is crucial for terahertz technologies. This work demonstrates that breaking local mirror symmetry via Mn‐substitution in the paradigmatic spin–orbit–coupled Mott insulator Ca2${\rm Ca}_2$RuO4${\rm RuO}_4$ activates previously inaccessible mixed‐parity magnons. Probed by polarized Raman spectroscopy, these excitations exhibit pronounced polarization nematicity. This strategy exploits spin–orbit–lattice entanglement to engineer advanced THz magnonic functionalities.








ABSTRACT
Correlated materials with competing spin–orbit and crystal‐field interactions can host composite spin–orbital magnons that are highly susceptible to structural and electronic perturbations, enabling the control of magnetic dynamics beyond spin‐only physics. Using Raman spectroscopy on Ca2${\rm Ca}_2$RuO4${\rm RuO}_4$, we show that the partial substitution of Ru with Mn reconstructs the magnon spectrum and reveals one–magnon modes that are hidden in the undoped state. We demonstrate that the transition‐metal substitution activates otherwise symmetry‐forbidden magnon modes through mirror‐symmetry breaking of the underlying spin–orbital configuration. This effect can be theoretically explained by the local structural distortions induced in the RuO6${\rm RuO}_6$ octahedra near the dopant, which enable the observation of mixed‐parity one–magnon modes. These excitations display a distinctive polarization dependence, with a lowering from fourfold to twofold rotational symmetry arising from the mixed‐parity character of the coupled magnons and interference between resonant and nonresonant scattering channels. Our results show that spin–orbit–lattice entanglement provides a route to tailoring collective magnetic excitations and their polarization response in spin–orbit–coupled correlated systems.

title: Anchoring Pd Single Atoms on N‐Doped MOF‐Derived TiO2 for Photocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution With an Ultra‐High Rate up to 185.8 mmol g−1 h−1
abstract:
N doping is adopted to introduce abundant binding sites within TiO 2  matrix, which enables firm immobilization of isolated Pd single atoms. The as-constructed PdN-TiO 2  single atom photocatalyst achieves greatly promoted solar-driven hydrogen evolution performance.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Photocatalytic hydrogen (H 2 ) evolution provides a sustainable pathway for clean energy production. However, conventional photocatalysts suffer from wide bandgaps and rapid charge recombination, leading to low photocatalytic efficiency. Herein, we construct an asymmetric N─Pd─O coordination environment by anchoring Pd single atoms (SAs) onto N‑doped MIL‑125‑derived TiO 2 . The optimized 1%PdN‑TiO 2  catalyst achieves a high H 2  evolution rate up to 185.8 mmol g −1  h −1  and an apparent quantum efficiency of 67.4% both measured under 365 nm monochromatic light irradiation. Synchrotron X‑ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy, ultrafast spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations reveal that the asymmetric N─Pd─O coordination promotes directional charge transfer and lowers the H 2  evolution reaction (HER) barrier. This work offers insights into the rational design of heteroatom‑modulated asymmetric coordination microenvironments toward high‑efficiency MOF‑derived single‑atom photocatalysts for sacrificial‑agent‑assisted photocatalytic H 2  production.

title: FADS2‐STING Signaling in Sertoli Cells Orchestrates Collagen Deposition and Germ Cell Necroptosis in Idiopathic Non‐Obstructive Azoospermia
abstract:
In Sertoli cells of iNOA testes, downregulation of FADS2 activates STING, promoting collagen deposition and peritubular fibrosis while increasing germ‐cell susceptibility to necroptosis. Supplementation with FADS2‐derived PUFAs (GLA and DHA) inhibits STING, alleviates collagen accumulation, and facilitates the recovery of spermatogenesis. (Figure was created with the help of BioRender.com).








ABSTRACT
Idiopathic non‐obstructive azoospermia (iNOA) is a severe form of male infertility with poorly defined etiology. While dysregulated lipid metabolism is a hallmark of spermatogenic failure, the molecular drivers linking lipid remodeling to testicular niche deterioration remain elusive. Here, integrated testicular lipidomics and single‐cell transcriptomics reveal a metabolic shift from polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA)‐enriched toward more saturated phospholipids in iNOA testes, accompanied by a selective downregulation of fatty acid desaturase 2 (FADS2) in Sertoli cells. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that FADS2 deficiency acts as a metabolic trigger for stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling, which orchestrates a transcriptional reprogramming in Sertoli cells. This process promotes aberrant collagen metabolic reprogramming and peritubular fibrosis while concurrently sensitizing germ cells to interferon‐mediated necroptosis. Importantly, restoring FADS2‐dependent metabolites (γ‐linolenic acid and docosahexaenoic acid) attenuates STING activation and collagen deposition and partially restores spermatogenesis in vivo. Collectively, these findings define the pathological relevance of Sertoli cell‐associated FADS2‐PUFA remodeling and STING‐associated inflammatory activation in iNOA, supporting PUFA replenishment as a potential strategy to mitigate structural niche pathology and germ‐cell vulnerability.

title: Superionic Al─O─H Compounds With Unconventional Stoichiometries Under Extreme Planetary Conditions
abstract:
First-principles calculations reveal stable AlOH and AlH 3 O 4  phases and protonic superionic behavior at high pressures and temperatures. Hydrogen diffuses rapidly through crystalline Al─O frameworks, while the two compounds exhibit different superionic transition trends with pressure. These results broaden high-pressure Al–O–H chemistry and suggest efficient proton transport under extreme planetary conditions.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Extreme pressure and temperature induce novel chemical behaviors, including unconventional stoichiometries and superionic states. Here, by combining crystal structure prediction with first-principles calculations, we identify two unconventional stoichiometries in the ternary Al─O─H system, AlOH and AlH 3 O 4 , which lie on the convex hull at 300 GPa. Representative formation reactions become thermodynamically stable above 65 and 245 GPa after including ZPE, respectively. Both compounds are wide-gap insulators and AlH 3 O 4  exhibits pronounced site-dependent charge differentiation between inequivalent oxygen environments under high pressure. Crucially, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations reveal protonic superionic transitions at elevated temperatures, where protons diffuse like a liquid through rigid Al─O sublattices. High-pressure and high-temperature dynamical-state diagrams further indicate that the solid, superionic, and liquid regimes overlap with conditions expected in deep planetary interiors, suggesting that they could play important roles in chemical behaviors inside planetary bodies. These findings significantly enrich the high-pressure phase diagram of Al─O─H system and provide valuable insights into chemical behaviors under extreme conditions.

title: Steps Toward Vitrification and Banking of Coral Larvae Using Field‐Friendly Cryomesh Technology
abstract:
Cryomesh enables a low-tech cryopreservation method, adding a valuable option to the coral reef conservation toolkit. The approach reveals how size, toxicity, and developmental stage govern larval survival, while modeling links cooling and rewarming rates to a theoretical upper volume limit. Shearing embryos reduces volume below this bound, offering a promising strategy for corals with larger-sized larvae.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Coral reefs are declining globally, and novel solutions, such as cryopreservation, can help secure coral biodiversity and genetic diversity. Factors that affect successful cryopreservation of coral larvae include cryoprotectant type and concentration, membrane permeability, larval developmental stage, lipid content, volume, and freezing and warming rates. This study examined conduction-dominated “cryomesh” technology across a range of coral species, distinguishing vitrification on cryomesh, 24 h swimming survival, and settlement competence as separate measures of success. Using a previously successful cryoprotectant solution, the exposure time, volume, and developmental stage most amenable to cryomesh cryopreservation were examined, and biophysical attributes were modeled to determine cooling and rewarming rates. Most species vitrified on the cryomesh and showed short-term motility, but robust 24 h swimming survival was limited to  Lobactis scutaria  and  Fungia fungites , the smallest species; other small-volume species did not survive. To improve heat transfer, subsets of embryos were sheared during early development, yielding sub-size larvae that did not swim post-thaw, but the sheared, untreated controls settled and matured normally. These findings show that volume alone does not ensure survival. Additional next steps must include toxicity and permeation studies of other cryoprotectants and long-term restoration potential evaluated by examining post-thaw settlement success.

title: Non‐Canonical Function of DDX21 in Fetal Hematopoiesis Antagonizes KDM5A‐Mediated Repression of Ribosomal and Hematopoietic Genes
abstract:
This study demonstrates a mechanism by which RNA helicase DDX21 coordinates the transcription of hematopoietic and ribosomal genes by interacting with the H3K4me3 demethylase KDM5A. The DDX21-KDM5A complex co-occupies active genes in hematopoietic progenitors, thereby ensuring their rapid proliferation during fetal hematopoiesis. Loss of DDX21 causes hematopoietic stem cell depletion and consequently hematopoietic failure, resembling the pathogenesis of ribosomopathies.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Ribosome biogenesis is crucial for meeting the elevated biosynthetic demands of rapidly expanding fetal hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) during fetal development. Ddx21 is a DEAD-box RNA helicase required for ribosome biogenesis, but its role in fetal hematopoiesis remains undefined. Here, we show that hematopoietic-specific deletion of  Ddx21  in mice results in severe fetal anemia, HSPC depletion, and loss of reconstitution capacity. Mechanistically, Ddx21 directly binds the histone demethylase Kdm5a via its helicase D2 domain in an RNA-dependent manner. Ddx21 and Kdm5a co-occupy active promoters of hematopoietic genes ( Gata1 ,  cKit ) and rDNA. Unexpectedly, Ddx21 loss does not displace Kdm5a from chromatin but reduces H3K4me3 at these loci, repressing both hematopoietic and ribosomal gene transcription. Although p53 activation drives apoptosis, p53 inhibition only partially rescues hematopoietic failure. Notably, combined pharmacological inhibition of Kdm5a and p53 synergistically restores H3K4me3, protein synthesis, and HSPC colony formation. Our findings reveal a non-canonical function of Ddx21 in epigenetic regulation by counteracting Kdm5a-mediated repression to sustain active transcription. The DDX21-KDM5A complex represents a previously unrecognized chromatin modulator balancing ribosome biogenesis and epigenetic repression, with implications for understanding the pathogenesis of ribosomopathies and developing therapeutic strategies targeting the epigenome-ribosome interface.

title: Multiband Optical Physical Unclonable Functions Based on Mixed‐Phase Multilevel Emissive Perovskites
abstract:
In this paper, sustainable multiband optical PUFs were developed by constructing heterostructures between lead‐free phase‐mixed perovskites and cellulose fibers via a water‐assisted drop‐casting process. Cesium manganese bromide perovskites provide an environmentally benign composition while exhibiting excitation‐dependent multilevel photophysical responses arising from mixed‐phase interactions. 








ABSTRACT
Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) are hardware‐based security primitives that exploit intrinsic physical randomness in materials or devices to prevent counterfeiting and enhance authentication across diverse applications. Among various sources of randomness, the optical signatures of luminescent materials represent a particularly robust and easily distinguishable feature. However, many optical PUF systems rely on environmentally hazardous materials or energy‐intensive fabrication processes while remaining vulnerable to counterfeiting due to deterministic and spectrally fixed emission characteristics. Here, we demonstrate sustainable multiband optical PUFs by forming heterostructures between lead‐free phase‐mixed perovskites and cellulose fibers via a water‐assisted drop‐casting process. Cesium manganese bromide perovskites provide an environmentally benign composition while exhibiting excitation‐dependent multilevel photophysical responses arising from mixed‐phase interactions. By leveraging these excitation‐dependent multilevel emission characteristics, we construct strong PUFs that significantly expand the challenge and response pairs from a single device through controlled optical feature extraction of the perovskites and the spatial randomness of cellulose fibers. Moreover, the multiband optical PUF platform is demonstrated for image encryption/decryption as well as currency authentication. These results establish an environmentally responsible optical PUF platform that combines sustainable materials and fabrication processes with distinctive photophysical characteristics for next‐generation hardware security technologies.

title: Oxygen‐Mediated Fe‐N3O Single‐Atom Sites Enabled by Lignin‐Derived Hierarchical Carbon for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
abstract:
A cooperative dual-template strategy transforms oxygen-rich lignin into hierarchical porous carbon hosting asymmetric Fe-N 3 O single-atom sites. The unique coordination downshifts the Fe d-band center, weakening *OOH adsorption and accelerating charge transfer. The optimized catalyst delivers exceptional oxygen reduction activity (E 1/2  = 0.87 V), outperforming commercial Pt/C.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Iron single-atom catalysts (Fe SACs) offer excellent performance for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). However, their catalytic activity remains limited by the coordination structure and the accessibility of the active sites. Optimizing the local coordination and pore structure of the catalyst is imperative. Herein, we report a dual-template strategy using oxygen-rich lignin to synthesize Fe single-atom catalysts with asymmetric Fe-N 3 O coordination embedded in hierarchical porous carbon (HPC). Lignin serves both as the carbon precursor and a coordination modulator, while Zn/MgO dual templates facilitate the creation of a tri-modal (micro/meso/macro) pore architecture. Operando spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveal that the asymmetric Fe-N 3 O configuration downshifts the d-band center of Fe, which weakens *OOH adsorption and accelerates charge transfer, leading to enhanced intrinsic activity. The optimized Fe-N 3 O@HPC catalyst exhibits exceptional ORR activity in 0.1 M KOH, with a half-wave potential of 0.87 V vs. RHE, surpassing Pt/C by 40 mV. Moreover, it exhibits significantly smaller decay over 30 h than commercial Pt/C. In zinc-air batteries, the catalyst delivers a peak power density of 174.2 mW cm −2  and a specific capacity of 807 mAh g Zn 
 −1 . This research offers a cost-effective methodology to design and fabricate high-performance catalysts for ORR.

title: Stage‐Adaptive Bilayer Hydrogel Coordinates Photodynamic Antibacterial Therapy with Engineered Extracellular Vesicle–Mediated Immunomodulation in Infected Diabetic Wounds
abstract:
Early photodynamic infection control and subsequent immunoregulatory repair are spatially separated within a stage‐adaptive bilayer hydrogel. Chlorin e6 is incorporated into the wound‐contacting layer to provide light‐triggered bactericidal therapy, whereas the upper layer regulates excessive reactive oxygen species before releasing microRNA‐146a‐enriched engineered small extracellular vesicles. Through this functional compartmentalization, antibacterial activity and oxidative‐stress regulation are temporally coordinated with macrophage immunomodulation, angiogenesis, and tissue reconstruction in infected diabetic wounds.








ABSTRACT
During the early phase of treatment, infected diabetic wounds require rapid bacterial control, whereas subsequent healing benefits from relief of persistent oxidative stress and inflammation, resulting in distinct and partly opposing redox demands over time. We therefore developed a stage‐adaptive bilayer hydrogel that separates photodynamic antibacterial therapy from engineered small extracellular vesicle (sEV) delivery. The wound‐contacting layer contains chlorin e6 (Ce6), while the ROS‐responsive upper layer scavenges ROS and retains miR‐146a‐enriched sEVs carrying a human CD64‐recognition module. The bilayer architecture limited premature release of sEV‐associated particles during photodynamic treatment but allowed substantial release thereafter, with key vesicle‐associated features preserved after irradiation. In human macrophages, engineered sEVs increased intracellular miR‐146a, reduced IRAK1 abundance and NF‐κB p65 phosphorylation, decreased CD86, and increased CD206. These effects were partly weakened by CD64 blockade. In infected diabetic wounds, Bil‐Gel@miR‐sEVs reduced bacterial burden and oxidative stress, suppressed IRAK1/NF‐κB‐associated inflammatory signaling, shifted macrophage‐associated markers toward a repair‐associated pattern, and improved epithelial, vascular, and matrix reconstruction. This bilayer design therefore links early infection control with later immunoregulation and tissue repair within one biomaterial.

title: Pyruvate Kinase M2‐Mediated H3K9 Lactylation and XBP1 Signaling Positive Feedback Loop Facilitates CD4+ T Cell Spinal Recruitment and Central Sensitization in Rheumatoid Arthritis
abstract:
In collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mice, increased CD4 +  T cell accumulation in the spinal dorsal horn induces pain hypersensitivity. Mechanistically, PKM2-mediated H3K9 lactylation and XBP1 signaling positive feedback loop facilitates CD4 +  T cell spinal migration and induces central sensitization-like behaviors in CIA mice. This clinically relevant pathway offers a promising therapeutic target for chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis.

 
 
 ABSTRACT 
 Central sensitization is a critical pathophysiological mechanism underlying chronic pain in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). CD4 +  T cells not only promote chronic inflammation in RA but may also migrate into the central nervous system to stimulate central sensitization. However, the regulatory mechanism by which CD4 +  T cells contribute to central sensitization in RA remains unclear. In this study, we report that CD4 +  T cells were significantly accumulated in the spinal dorsal horn (SDH) of collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mice and promoted their central sensitization-like behaviors. Mechanistically, PKM2-dependent lactate facilitated H3K9 lactylation (H3K9la) in CD4 +  T cells. H3K9la was highly enriched at the promoters of XBP1, which facilitated the transcription of  KIF4  and  MYO1B  and the accumulation of CD4 +  T cells in SDH. Furthermore, XBP1 may facilitate the transcription of PKM2, establishing a positive feedback loop between PKM2-induced H3K9la and XBP1 signaling in CIA mice. Crucially, the clinical relevance of this pathway was validated in patients with RA, where the expression of PKM2/H3K9la/XBP1 was significantly increased and positively correlated with central sensitization scores. Overall, our study indicates a positive feedback loop of PKM2/H3K9la/XBP1 in facilitating CD4 +  T cell spinal recruitment, which may provide a promising therapeutic strategy for mitigating central sensitization in RA.

title: Recent Advances in High‐Entropy Nanozymes: From Fabrication to Applications
abstract:
To highlight key achievements and clarify the current landscape of high‐entropy nanozymes (HEAzymes), this review summarizes state‐of‐the‐art developments ranging from thermodynamically and kinetically controlled synthetic strategies; enzyme‐like catalytic types, catalytic characteristics, and underlying mechanisms; to their antioxidative, therapeutic, biosensing, energy‐related, and other emerging applications. We think this review can spotlight the HEAzyme research frontier, inspire multidisciplinary researchers, and accelerate nanozymes development.








ABSTRACT
Nanozymes are artificial enzymes designed to circumvent the inherent limitations of natural enzymes. They have emerged as a transformative paradigm in biomimetic catalysis. High‐entropy nanozymes (HEAzymes) are nanomaterials that consist of high‐entropy alloys, oxides, sulfides, and other high‑entropy compounds that exhibit enzyme‐like catalytic activity. HEAzymes have recently garnered substantial attention as a next‐generation nanozyme. The rapid evolution of this field has been propelled by synergistic advances in nanotechnology, biotechnology, catalysis, and computational modeling, offering unprecedented opportunities for rational design and broad‐spectrum applications. This review provides a comprehensive and timely overview of state‐of‐the‐art developments in HEAzymes, systematically spanning synthetic methodologies, catalytic mechanisms, and multifunctional applications. We classify fabrication strategies into thermodynamically driven and kinetically controlled routes, elucidate enzyme‐mimetic catalytic behaviors and their underlying mechanistic principles, and critically examine recent advances in antioxidative, therapeutic, biosensing, energy‐related, and emerging applications. Finally, we discuss prevailing challenges and outline prospective directions to guide future research. By spotlighting the frontier of HEAzyme research, this review aims to foster interdisciplinary collaboration and catalyze continued innovation in nanozyme science.

title: Field Emission Enhancement in Graphene/Cu Cathodes Through Laser‐Shock‐Induced Modulation of Geometry and Work Function
abstract:
Laser shock microforming converts graphene/Cu foils into flexible cathodes without transfer while modulating their local work function. Lower barriers near protrusion tops and rims coincide with electric field concentration, favoring electron emission. The cathodes exhibit enhanced field emission, stable operation for 32 h, and durability after 3000 bending cycles, offering a route to flexible vacuum electronics.

 
 
 ABSTRACT
